final_records.name: Claude Code
final_records.deployment: local CLI/IDE/Desktop client with cloud inference; Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions; customer-run cloud-session runners (public beta, Team/Enterprise) keep execution on own hosts but not inference or transcripts
final_records.model_backend: Claude models only (Anthropic). Routes: Anthropic API or Claude subscription, Claude Platform on AWS (Anthropic-operated), Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) or Microsoft Foundry (the deployment's hosting option decides Azure or Anthropic infrastructure). LLM gateways may front these, including Anthropic's Claude apps gateway, which the customer runs from the claude binary in front of the same cloud upstreams; Anthropic does not support routing to non-Claude models. Covered Models (Claude Fable 5, Fable 5.1) keep prompts and outputs at least 30 days by default; ZDR applies to them only where Anthropic expressly authorizes it.
final_records.data_handling_note: Consumer plans (Pro, Max and Ultra; Free excludes Claude Code): model training is opt-out. Retention is 5 years with model improvement on and 30 days when it is off. Commercial use (Team, Enterprise, API and cloud providers) is not used for training by default unless the customer opts in, for example through the Development Partner Program. Team, Enterprise and API data has 30-day standard retention; cloud-provider routes follow that platform's policy. ZDR covers Claude Code inference only for Anthropic-approved organizations (Claude Enterprise or a commercial API-key organization), enabled per organization. Legal and misuse exceptions apply: flagged sessions may be kept up to 2 years, and safety-classifier results are retained. Covered Models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) keep prompts and outputs at least 30 days by default and are unavailable under ZDR unless Anthropic authorizes them. Under ZDR, cloud sessions, Claude Tag, Artifacts, feedback and Remote Control are disabled; Cowork, analytics, admin data and third-party integrations/MCP fall outside ZDR. Telemetry: usage metrics (no code, prompts or file paths) are on by default with the Anthropic API (DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 turns them off); /feedback transcripts are kept 5 years; redacted error reports are on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra sign-ins on v2.1.198+ connecting directly to the Claude API without a ZDR or HIPAA agreement; session-quality surveys run on every provider, and answering 'Yes' to the follow-up uploads transcripts and source code, kept up to 6 months (on Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry and Claude apps gateway sessions it writes a local archive instead); the WebFetch hostname check reaches Anthropic on every provider. Local plaintext transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/ expire after 30 days by default. ~/.claude/history.jsonl keeps every typed prompt until deleted (swept only under the HIPAA configuration). Sessions started or last continued in Desktop or Cowork are kept at any age unless desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays, a managed cleanupPeriodDays or the HIPAA configuration applies. With the Enterprise Compliance API on, Anthropic captures Claude Code session content, readable for 30 days (not while the organization has ZDR for Claude Code).

suitability_notes.personal: Use a commercial route (Team, Enterprise, API or a contracted cloud provider) under a DPA; Anthropic documents a processor role only for commercial plans, so consumer Pro/Max/Ultra accounts are not a route for other people's personal data (if used for own data, turn the training setting off; 30-day retention still applies). Confirm the exact surface and model are covered: ZDR disables cloud sessions and excludes Covered Models unless authorized. The HIPAA configuration covers only local CLI and Desktop Code-tab sessions, not the VS Code/JetBrains extensions, gateways (including the Claude apps gateway), cloud providers, connectors/MCP, plugins, desktop extensions or skills. Enforce organization login, allowed providers and transcript retention through managed settings, and protect local plaintext transcripts and history.jsonl. Data sent to MCP servers or other integrations is not covered by ZDR or the BAA; check each service's handling.
suitability_notes.special: Every documented inference route is cloud: the Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Agent Platform and Foundry. Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude (for example local) models, and its customer-run Claude apps gateway forwards only to those cloud upstreams. ZDR, the HIPAA configuration/BAA, self-hosted runners and the gateway do not keep inference or the session conversation on institution-controlled infrastructure. Under this index's strict rule, do not use it for identifiable or controlled-access health, genetic or clinical data.

compliance: Anthropic lists ISO 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and SOC 2 Type I and Type II (reports via the Trust Portal); the scope of each report for Claude Code requires confirmation.

A BAA is available to HIPAA-ready Enterprise organizations. It extends to Claude Code in the terminal and the Desktop Code tab either with the HIPAA configuration (Anthropic must turn it on through the account team and the Primary Owner applies it; Enterprise sign-in connecting directly to the Claude API; Claude Code v2.1.285 or later and Claude Desktop v2.19675.0 or later; server-side data then follows Anthropic's standard retention) or with ZDR for Claude Code. Console API-key use is covered only when that Console organization has ZDR. Under the HIPAA configuration, the VS Code/JetBrains extensions, cloud-provider, Claude apps gateway, other gateway or custom-base-URL sessions, connectors, MCP servers, plugins, desktop extensions, skills, Claude in Chrome, beta or research-preview features, cloud sessions, Remote Control and mobile are not covered.
final_records.pricing: Claude Code is included in all paid Claude plans (not Free) and shares the plan's usage limits; API/Console and cloud-provider use is metered separately. Listed 2026-11-06 (USD, excluding tax): Pro $20/month, or $17/month billed annually ($200 up front); Max $100/month; Ultra $200/month (Max and Ultra are billed monthly and include $100 and $200 of monthly API credits respectively); Team standard seat $25/month, or $20 billed annually; Team premium seat $125/month, or $100 billed annually; Enterprise $20/seat/month billed annually, 20-seat minimum, plus usage at API rates.
final_records.academic: Claude Team plan for scientists (promotional terms effective 2026-08-27, Supplemental Terms under the Commercial Terms): PIs or equivalent at accredited universities and nonprofit research institutes in the natural sciences, mathematics, computer science, engineering and related fields can apply; for-profits, CROs and industry R&D are excluded. For 12 months, Standard seats are $0 and Premium seats $15/month ($0/$180 per seat per year annually); 1-25 seats; initial group of 10,000 verified scientists; limited availability, final pricing confirmed after verification. A payment method is required, seats renew at the then-current price after 12 months, and 90 days without use can end the promotional pricing. Includes Claude Code. Institution-wide Claude for Education plans are available through Anthropic's Education team; confirm Claude Code inclusion.

final_records.name: OpenAI Codex
final_records.deployment: Local clients (Codex CLI, IDE extension, Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app) with OpenAI-hosted inference by default; Codex cloud tasks run remotely in OpenAI-managed cloud environments and require ChatGPT sign-in. Documented alternative model routes: custom providers or gateways (Responses API), built-in Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI providers, and CLI --oss mode with local Ollama or LM Studio.
final_records.model_backend: OpenAI-hosted models by default: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra (added 26 October 2026 for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu; not listed for the IDE extension; CLI 0.159.0 or later), GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (Free and Go: Luna in the desktop app). GPT-5.5 retired from Codex with ChatGPT sign-in on 14 October 2026 and remains available with API-key sign-in; GPT-5.6 models still appear on the credit rate card. API-key use follows the key's API model access. Custom providers and gateways need a Responses-compatible endpoint; built-in Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI providers and local open-weight models via Ollama or LM Studio (--oss) are documented alternatives.
final_records.data_handling_note: Business, Enterprise, Edu and API data are not used for training by default (API sharing is opt-in). Free, Plus and Pro personal workspaces share data for training by default, with an opt-out under Data Controls; Codex has a separate Include environments setting for training on Codex environment context, which the ChatGPT opt-out does not change, and Daybreak (Trusted Access) sessions on personal accounts may be used for training even when opted out. With ChatGPT sign-in, Codex follows the workspace's retention and residency settings; with an API key, the API organization's retention settings apply. API abuse-monitoring logs are kept for up to 30 days; ZDR or Modified Abuse Monitoring needs OpenAI approval, and OpenAI can make specific models ineligible after written notice. API ZDR does not define ChatGPT Work retention, and no Codex-cloud-specific deletion schedule was found; for Work cloud tasks, hosted execution state follows a lifecycle separate from chats. Local clients send anonymous usage and health metrics to OpenAI by default (opt-out via [analytics]); OTel log export is off by default, and explicit OTLP metrics exporters run independently of the analytics setting. With the Amazon Bedrock provider, requests go to Amazon Bedrock with AWS authentication and OpenAI's hosted Responses API is not in the request path; the Vertex AI provider sends requests to the Vertex AI endpoint for the configured Google Cloud project and location (default 'global'), authenticated with Google Application Default Credentials. AWS- and Google-side retention was not assessed.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a Business, Enterprise or Edu workspace or a contracted API organization with a DPA, not a Free, Go, Plus or Pro personal plan (personal plans train by default, Codex's Include environments training setting is separate from the ChatGPT opt-out, and Daybreak sessions may be used for training even when opted out). Confirm chat, file and cloud-task retention for the exact surface and any approved API ZDR scope, and disable analytics on managed machines.
suitability_notes.special: Only the open-source Codex CLI in --oss mode (or a custom no-auth provider) against Ollama in local-only mode (no :cloud models) or LM Studio on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware, with no ChatGPT or API sign-in, analytics, feedback and web search disabled, and egress verified. OpenAI-hosted, Codex cloud, ChatGPT Work, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI routes are not appropriate.

compliance: OpenAI states its business data practices align with SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 and CSA STAR, and offers a DPA; its Business pricing comparison lists SOC 2 Type 2 for both Business and Enterprise but the ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certifications for Enterprise only. Confirm that the Codex surface and plan are in scope.
A BAA is offered to ChatGPT for Healthcare and API healthcare customers; OpenAI's Work admin FAQ says HIPAA/BAA coverage depends on the features and agreement in use.
Data residency is available for eligible Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare and API customers; Codex with ChatGPT sign-in follows workspace residency settings.
final_records.pricing: Codex is included in ChatGPT plans (US list prices): Free and Go ($8/month) get GPT-6 Luna in the desktop app, subject to rollout; Plus $20/month; Pro $100, $200 or $500/month (among Pro tiers, Ultrafast only on Pro $500; also available on eligible Enterprise and Edu plans). ChatGPT Business (teams of 2-200): Standard seat $20/user/month billed annually or $25 monthly; Premium seat (more usage than Standard, no 5-hour limit) $100 annually or $125 monthly. Enterprise and Edu through sales. New Codex-only pay-as-you-go Business seats have not been offered since 24 June 2026 (existing seats unaffected). Codex and ChatGPT Work share usage; OpenAI says that from December 2026 Plus, Pro and Business usage will be shared across ChatGPT and Codex and measured in tokens. Purchased credits extend plan limits; API-key use is billed at API rates.
final_records.academic: ChatGPT Edu is sold through OpenAI sales. Verified university students in the US and Canada can claim $100 (2,500 ChatGPT credits) for Codex, valid 12 months; the offer is limited to those two countries. Maintainers of widely used open-source projects can apply to Codex for Open Source (API credits, six months of ChatGPT Pro with Codex, conditional Codex Security access).

final_records.notes: Multi-surface coding agent: Codex CLI, IDE extension, Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app and Codex cloud, plus code review, Codex Security and a GitHub Action. Current models are GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol (recommended for complex work at lower cost than Astra), GPT-6.1 Terra (added 26 October 2026), GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna; GPT-5.5 left Codex with ChatGPT sign-in on 14 October 2026. Codex and ChatGPT Work share usage limits. Licence scope: Apache-2.0 covers openai/codex (Codex CLI, SDK and app server); OpenAI lists the IDE extension and Codex cloud as not open source, and the ChatGPT desktop app is not among the listed open-source components. The special-category route covers only the local --oss CLI configuration; OpenAI-hosted, Bedrock and Vertex AI routes remain unsuitable for such data. Basis for that route: OpenAI's --oss and no-authentication local-provider documentation, a source review of codex-rs on 10 October 2026 (login skipped for non-OpenAI providers; model-catalog refresh only with the Codex backend, command auth or API-key discovery), and a 6 November 2026 check of model-provider-info showing the built-in Ollama and LM Studio providers default to localhost with requires_openai_auth = false. Network egress of an --oss session was not tested.
final_records.tier_gate: Personal data: Business/Enterprise/Edu workspace or contracted API org (not consumer plans); special-category data: local --oss CLI only, no OpenAI sign-in

required_controls: Run only the Apache-2.0 Codex CLI (including codex exec) with --oss, or a custom provider pointing to Ollama or LM Studio on hardware the researcher or institution controls; do not sign in with ChatGPT or an OpenAI API key, and remove stored OpenAI credentials (codex logout). Leave the experimental CODEX_OSS_BASE_URL and CODEX_OSS_PORT environment variables unset, or point them only at the local server.
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Set [analytics] enabled = false and [feedback] enabled = false; keep OTel export off and set otel.metrics_exporter = "none" (explicit OTLP metrics exporters run independently of the analytics flag), or send OTel only to an institution-controlled collector with log_user_prompt = false.
Set web_search = "disabled" and do not use Codex cloud, ChatGPT Work, the desktop app, remote connections, plugins, connectors or remote MCP servers.

Verify network egress on the deployed version (firewall allowlist), turn off startup update checks where updates are centrally managed, and apply institutional retention to local history under CODEX_HOME (or set history.persistence = "none").
residual_risks: OpenAI-hosted inference (ChatGPT sign-in or API key), Codex cloud and the Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI providers send data outside institution-controlled infrastructure; ZDR, data residency or a BAA do not change this.

A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so an --oss session pointed at local Ollama can still send prompts to Ollama's cloud unless local-only mode is enabled.
Analytics and feedback are on by default, and OpenAI's docs do not state that an --oss session makes no other network calls; egress has to be tested.
Codex needs a Responses-compatible endpoint (Chat Completions-only servers are unsupported), and local open-weight models are less capable than the hosted models.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Gemini CLI
final_records.deployment: local CLI / cloud inference
final_records.model_backend: Google Gemini models (the built-in model list covers mainly Gemini 2.5 and 3.x; the README says the CLI is not optimized for the Gemini 4 series) via Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licences, or via paid Gemini API and Vertex AI (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) keys, which the README now calls legacy routes; free-of-charge and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended 2026-06-18 and moved to the separate Antigravity CLI product
final_records.data_handling_note: The CLI is an Apache-2.0 client; data handling follows the backend route. The supported routes (Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise, and the paid Gemini API and Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform keys) do not use prompts or code for training by default. Retention differs by route. Paid Gemini API: Google logs prompts and responses for a limited period for abuse monitoring and points users who need guaranteed ZDR to Vertex. Separately, AI Studio API logging (developer-owned logs, private to the project, kept up to 55 days by default) is on by default for Generate Content calls in projects created on or after 2026-10-26; the project owner can turn it off, and these logs are not used for product improvement unless shared as datasets. Agent Platform: under the online Google Cloud Platform Terms, Google may log prompts flagged by its abuse classifiers (stored up to 90 days in the selected region); customers with a Google Cloud Master Agreement are exempt by default. Google states these terms for models not designated Frontier or Advanced AI; for designated models it describes prompt-and-response abuse logging for up to 30 days. Implicit caching (in memory and, by default, durable at rest) is deleted within 24 hours and can be disabled per project. Google describes Code Assist Standard/Enterprise as stateless services that do not store prompts and responses in Google Cloud. The CLI's built-in google_web_search tool uses Grounding with Google Search, whose logs cannot be disabled: 30 days on the Gemini API, up to 3 days on Agent Platform. Unpaid use is no longer a supported Gemini CLI route. If an API key without an active billing account still works, the unpaid terms let Google use content to improve products, except in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, where the paid-service data-use terms also cover unpaid quota. Anonymous usage statistics are on by default and do not include prompt content, per the docs; turn them off with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false. Free and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended on 2026-06-18.

suitability_notes.personal: Use only a paid route covered by a Google data processing addendum: a Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licence or Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Google Cloud terms), or a Gemini API key in a billed Cloud project (Gemini API Paid Services terms). For regional processing, use Agent Platform with GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION set to a regional location (not global) where the chosen model is offered; global endpoints give no data-residency guarantee. Code Assist processing is not guaranteed to stay in-region, and the paid Gemini API may cache data in any country. On Agent Platform, abuse-monitoring prompt logging is excluded by default only for customers with a Google Cloud Master Agreement, and only for models not designated Frontier or Advanced AI, so check the chosen model's designation; if your policy forbids storage at rest, disable durable caching (or all caching) for the project. On a Gemini API project created on or after 2026-10-26, turn off AI Studio logging, and share no log datasets with Google, because shared datasets are processed under the unpaid terms. Restrict the built-in tools (tools.core) so that google_web_search stays off, because grounding logs cannot be disabled. Turn off usage statistics, and enforce the authentication type in system settings (security.auth.enforcedType). If you enable OpenTelemetry, set telemetry.logPrompts to false, because it defaults to true. Confirm with your DPO.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. ZDR / HIPAA-BAA is a contractual assurance, but data still leaves your environment — not appropriate for identifiable or controlled-access (DUA) health/genetic data. Use a tool that runs on infrastructure you control, and confirm with your DPO / IRB.

compliance: Google Cloud or Code Assist contract and service scope must be verified; infrastructure certifications are not a blanket Gemini CLI certification
Google's Code Assist security page lists ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 and SOC 1, 2 and 3 for Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise; these cover the service, not the open-source CLI client
final_records.pricing: The open-source CLI is free. Model use is billed per token through a Gemini API key or Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, or through per-seat Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise subscriptions. The geminicli.com quota and plans pages still list free, Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra quotas, but per Google's banner and blog those routes were retired on 2026-06-18 and moved to the separate Antigravity CLI product.
final_records.academic: No dedicated academic or student discount for Gemini CLI was found on the current plans or quota pages. Since 2026-06-18 Gemini CLI itself has no free consumer route. Free consumer access is available only through the separate Antigravity CLI product.

final_records.name: Aider

final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: BYO key - local models (Ollama, LM Studio or other OpenAI-compatible servers) or most cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenRouter, etc.)
final_records.data_handling_note: With a local model (e.g. Ollama in local-only mode, or LM Studio on localhost) inference stays on controlled infrastructure; with a cloud API, prompts and code go to that provider under its terms. Aider states that analytics are opt-in and never collect code, chat messages or keys; a random subset of users is asked to opt in, the prompt defaults to Yes and, per source code, is auto-accepted under --yes-always; events go to PostHog (US host by default), and --analytics-disable turns analytics off permanently. By default Aider also checks PyPI for a new version on launch (at most once a day) and downloads LiteLLM's model-metadata file from GitHub (no code or chat content). Chat and input histories are written to .aider.chat.history.md and .aider.input.history in the project root by default; these files, repository contents and executed commands need access, retention and network controls.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a fully local model, or a cloud provider covered by an appropriate DPA and no-training terms; Aider itself is not the processor for cloud inference. Keep analytics permanently disabled (--analytics-disable).
suitability_notes.special: Requires a fully local model on controlled infrastructure (Ollama in local-only mode if used), analytics permanently disabled, the launch-time update check off and outbound traffic blocked except to the model endpoint. Any cloud-model configuration moves data outside that boundary and is not acceptable under this index's strict rule.

final_records.notes: Local-capable pair-programming CLI. The latest PyPI release is 0.86.2 (12 Feb 2026); the GitHub Releases page still lists v0.86.0 (Aug 2025) as latest. The last main-branch commit is dated 22 May 2026. As of 6 Nov 2026 no repository owner, member or collaborator has commented on an issue or pull request since 23 May 2026, and recent pull requests were closed unmerged by their own authors, while new issues keep arriving. The project is not declared discontinued; treat maintenance as stalled and check compatibility with the chosen model before adopting.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local model (e.g. Ollama in local-only mode), analytics permanently disabled, update check off and egress blocked except to the model endpoint for special-category data; a DPA-covered cloud provider with no-training terms for personal data

required_controls: Point Aider only at a model endpoint on the workstation or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network (e.g. Ollama via OLLAMA_API_BASE), and name every model role explicitly: --model, plus --weak-model and --editor-model, whose defaults depend on --model. Keep cloud API keys out of the environment, .env and Aider config files (without --model, Aider auto-selects a cloud model when a cloud key is present, or offers OpenRouter sign-in when none is).
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Disable analytics permanently with aider --analytics-disable (or AIDER_ANALYTICS_DISABLE=true) before any run with --yes-always.

Turn off the launch-time update check (--no-check-update) and block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the model endpoint, then verify the block; Aider downloads model metadata from GitHub by default.
Turn off URL detection (--no-detect-urls), do not use /web or /voice, and do not add web pages to the chat in sensitive sessions.

Check the effective configuration before sensitive sessions: Aider loads .aider.conf.yml and .env from the home directory, the git root and the current directory (later files take priority), plus any file named with --config or --env-file, so confirm that no such file sets a cloud model or API keys or undoes the controls above.

Restrict access to and set retention for local history files (.aider.chat.history.md, .aider.input.history, any --llm-history-file) and for the git commits Aider creates automatically; in sensitive repositories turn auto-commits off (--no-auto-commits) or review every Aider commit before it is pushed.
residual_risks: Any cloud-model configuration moves prompts and code outside the controlled boundary.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost OLLAMA_API_BASE alone does not guarantee local inference.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

Maintenance has stalled: no main-branch commits after 22 May 2026 and no owner, member or collaborator comments after 23 May 2026 (checked 6 Nov 2026). Two GitHub advisories published 31 May 2026 against aider-chat <= 0.86.2 (CVE-2026-10175, prompt injection to code in architect mode; CVE-2026-10177, scraper SSRF; both rated low) list no patched version, and the proposed scraper fix (PR #5137) is still unmerged.
Aider's documentation warns that it may not work well with less capable models, which limits the choice of small local models.

final_records.name: Goose
final_records.vendor: AAIF / Linux Foundation (originally Block; donated to Agentic AI Foundation in Dec 2025)
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: User-configured (Desktop model switcher, goose configure, GOOSE_PROVIDER or recipe). Local: built-in llama.cpp inference, or local servers such as Ollama, LM Studio and Docker Model Runner; OpenAI-compatible self-hosted endpoints (e.g. vLLM) are supported. Hosted: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini/Vertex AI, Azure, Bedrock, Databricks, OpenRouter and many others. final_records.data_handling_note: With a local model, prompts and code stay on the machine; with a hosted or ACP provider, content goes to that provider under its own retention and training terms. Goose stores full conversations and tool calls/results locally (sessions.db; no documented retention limit); CLI and server logs are deleted after two weeks, and llm_request logs keep the 10 most recent raw model requests and responses. Anonymous usage data (PostHog) is opt-in, off until the user agrees, and excludes conversations and code. OpenTelemetry export is off unless an endpoint is set; message-content capture defaults to false. Since v1.53.0 (2 Oct 2026) the default build (used for the macOS and Windows Desktop bundles) fetches public model metadata from models.dev at startup (no session content; bundled offline fallback); Desktop also runs an auto-update check by default. Opt-in Live voice in Desktop (v1.52.0) sends audio, recent conversation context and delegated tool results to OpenAI, whatever model provider the session uses; opt-in cloud dictation (OpenAI, Groq, ElevenLabs) sends audio to that service. No project-level DPA or certification.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer a local model; use a hosted or ACP provider only under an institutional DPA/no-training agreement for that provider. Keep anonymous usage data off; keep Live voice (OpenAI, whatever the session provider) and cloud dictation off unless an institutional agreement covers that service.
suitability_notes.special: Only with inference on the same machine or on institution-owned hardware, all cloud and ACP provider routes unused, usage data off, OTel export off or sent only to an institution-controlled collector, Live voice and cloud dictation off, Desktop updates centrally managed, and outbound egress blocked or allow-listed at host or network level (the default build contacts models.dev at startup, Desktop checks for updates, and the built-in goose-doc-guide skill reads goose-docs.ai unless GOOSE_DOCS_ROOT points to a local docs copy).

compliance: Customer-operated local route; Apache-2.0 client license does not certify a deployment.
final_records.pricing: Free open-source software (Apache-2.0); no paid Goose plan found on first-party pages. Hosted model, API or subscription costs depend on the chosen provider.

final_records.notes: Open-source desktop app, CLI and API under Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) governance. Privacy posture is set mainly by the configured model provider and enabled extensions. Actively maintained: three releases since the October review (v1.55.0 on 16 Oct, v1.56.0 on 23 Oct, v1.57.0 on 28 Oct 2026) and commits through 6 Nov 2026; repository not archived. Nostr session sharing was removed in v1.54.0; roaming (p2p remote access) remains an optional build feature outside the default build.
final_records.tier_gate: local model only (built-in llama.cpp, Ollama in local-only mode, or an institution-owned model server), usage data, OTel/Langfuse export, Live voice and cloud dictation off, Desktop auto-update managed and egress blocked for special-category data; a DPA-covered provider for personal data

required_controls: Run inference only on the same machine (built-in llama.cpp, or Ollama/LM Studio serving on localhost) or on an institution-owned model server inside the network (e.g. a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as vLLM); leave all hosted and ACP provider routes unconfigured, and point every model role Goose uses, not only the main session model, at that endpoint.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Keep no cloud provider API keys in the environment, .env files or Goose's stored configuration, and check the effective provider, model and extension settings before use (environment variables such as GOOSE_PROVIDER and recipes can also set the provider).

Keep anonymous usage data off (GOOSE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false or GOOSE_TELEMETRY_OFF=1); leave OpenTelemetry and Langfuse export unset, or send OTel only to an institution-controlled collector with content capture off.

Block or allow-list outbound network egress at the host or network level and test that the block holds. The default build fetches model metadata from models.dev at startup (since v1.53.0); a build without online-model-meta removes only that request. Set GOOSE_DOCS_ROOT to a local docs copy so the built-in goose-doc-guide skill does not read goose-docs.ai.
Manage Desktop updates centrally: the auto-updater is on by default, so disable or block it and roll out reviewed releases through institutional software management.

Keep opt-in cloud features and network tools off: Live voice (OpenAI), cloud dictation (OpenAI, Groq, ElevenLabs; local Whisper dictation is available), the Telegram gateway, web search or fetch tools, and remote or cloud-hosted MCP extensions. Restrict extensions with an institution-hosted GOOSE_ALLOWLIST (HTTPS-only and fail-closed since v1.57.0).
Protect the local session database, command history and logs (including llm_request logs) under institutional access, encryption and retention rules.
residual_risks: No documented runtime setting locks Goose to local providers; the project's custom-distribution guide only suggests a modified UI or an enforcing recipe. One mis-set provider, ACP agent, extension or voice/dictation setting can send data off-device.

sessions.db keeps full prompts, tool arguments and results with no documented retention limit; llm_request logs keep the raw payloads of the last 10 model requests; only CLI and server logs have a documented two-week cleanup.
Local models have smaller context windows and weaker tool calling (per Goose's own local-inference post), which can push users toward cloud routes mid-project.
Model weights downloaded from Hugging Face and third-party MCP extensions need provenance and security review.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

Updates can add new default network calls (v1.53.0 added the startup models.dev fetch), so a configuration checked once must be re-checked for each release. posthog.rs also keeps a path that would send Desktop onboarding events before the telemetry choice; the current Desktop frontend does not send them, but a later release could.

final_records.name: Cursor
final_records.deployment: cloud (local IDE/CLI client; inference, planning and the agent loop run in Cursor's cloud; Cloud Agent tool execution can move to customer-run machines, but tool outputs, which may contain code, and transcripts still flow to Cursor)
final_records.model_backend: Cursor models (Composer 2.5; Grok 4.5/4.6/4.7, documented as jointly trained by Cursor and SpaceXAI) + hosted third-party models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Moonshot, Z.ai, DeepSeek) + BYOK (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock); all requests routed through Cursor's backend
final_records.data_handling_note: Terms (3 Sep 2026) bar training on Content without explicit agreement; turning Privacy Mode off lets Cursor store and use code data to train its models, and some inference providers may temporarily store inputs and outputs. Privacy Mode is on by default for Teams and Enterprise and admin-enforceable; the individual-plan default is not stated (Cursor's MDM guidance warns personal accounts might not have it on). With Privacy Mode on, providers run under ZDR agreements, but abuse-flagged data may be stored for investigation, and the Privacy Policy (11 Oct 2026) allows analysis of security-flagged inputs. Standard Privacy Mode still lets Cursor store code for Cloud Agents and Grok Bot; Privacy Mode (Legacy) does not support Cloud Agents and blocks Grok Bot. Exceptions: BYOK is outside Cursor's ZDR and still transits Cursor's backend. Anthropic retains Claude Fable 5/5.1 inputs and outputs for harm review (deleted after 30 days unless under safety investigation or legal hold); these models need admin approval on Enterprise and wherever Privacy Mode is on, but the Fable 5.1 page says they are on by default for individual and Teams accounts with Privacy Mode off. Cursor temporarily caches encrypted file contents. Cloud Agents keep transcripts (prompts, responses, tool calls, diff context) indefinitely by default (deletable via API; Enterprise can cap retention at 90 days) and encrypted VM snapshots including cloned code for up to 30 days of inactivity, not deletable on demand (one governance page still says repository copies are deleted when the agent completes). Grok Bot, included with paid individual plans (Premium and above on The X Subscription) and on by default for Teams, keeps files, browser sessions and credentials on persistent US cloud computers and ignores model allowlists; its security page says team Privacy Mode applies, while Cursor's privacy FAQ calls it a separate product surface with its own data flows. The DPA bars sensitive/special-category data and does not cover individual plans. Since Oct 2026, new customers buy Cursor through The X Subscription (workspace and billing on grok.com, SpaceXSI Subscription Terms); Cursor's pages do not say whether its Privacy Policy, DPA and Privacy Mode terms apply unchanged to these workspaces.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Teams or Enterprise under the DPA (individual plans are not covered) with Privacy Mode enforced org-wide. BYOK blocking, model access control, the Grok Bot off switch and Cloud Agent retention caps are Enterprise-only. On Teams, Grok Bot is on with no off switch unless the team uses Privacy Mode (Legacy), Fable-class retention models stay off only while no admin approves them, and personal data should be kept out of Cloud Agents and Grok Bot. New teams now buy The X Subscription (managed on grok.com under SpaceXSI Subscription Terms); Cursor does not state whether its DPA applies unchanged there, so confirm the contracting entity and DPA before onboarding personal data. Enterprise is not moved automatically. US-only data residency is Enterprise-only; EU coverage is inference-only and on request.
suitability_notes.special: Inference and the agent loop always run in Cursor's cloud (Cursor states it is not an on-prem product), and the DPA bars special-category data. The Enterprise HIPAA BAA and Self-Hosted Machines do not create a customer-controlled inference boundary, so this catalog's rule excludes health/genetic/clinical data.

compliance: Cursor states AIUC-1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certifications and a SOC 2 Type II attestation; reports are on request via trust.cursor.com and were not reviewed.
HIPAA BAA on Enterprise only; PHI is limited to the Eligible Services and Models in Cursor's HIPAA Guide, with Privacy Mode locked org-wide.
DPA (last updated 5 Nov 2025) prohibits sensitive/special-category data and does not apply to individual plans.
final_records.pricing: New customers buy The X Subscription (Grok, Cursor and X in one plan; USD, excl. tax): Free $0; Plus $8/mo (Cursor models only at fixed settings; no Cloud Agents, third-party models or BYOK); Premium $30; Super $100; Ultra $200 per month (annual $80/$300/$1,000/$2,000); Teams $30, $100 or $200 per seat/month; Enterprise custom. Third-party models are not included: on Premium and above they bill at API list price from prepaid credit, and Teams/Enterprise also pay a Cursor Token Rate of $0.25/M tokens on eligible models, including BYOK requests. Legacy Cursor plans (Hobby free; Pro $20; Pro+ $60; Ultra $200; Teams Standard $40 and Premium $120 per user; Cursor Start INR 649 in India) continue for existing subscribers only. US-only data residency adds 10% to eligible model pricing.
final_records.academic: Legacy student discount closed to new sign-ups on 25 Jun 2026 (existing rates kept until the plan expires). Cursor's help centre invites Master's/PhD students, academic researchers and educators to request credits through an Anysphere-hosted Typeform (amounts and criteria not stated); undergraduates get credits or discounts through on-campus and online events.

final_records.name: GitHub Copilot
final_records.deployment: cloud (GitHub-hosted models via IDE extensions, Copilot CLI, the Copilot desktop app, GitHub.com, GitHub Mobile and Copilot in the cloud, which runs sessions in GitHub-hosted cloud sandboxes by default where an environment choice is offered; not available for GitHub Enterprise Server) / local-capable (Copilot CLI offline mode with a local BYOK model). Two further local-model features run inference on the device but are not offline: managed local-model download (MAI Code 1.1 Flash, Flint NVFP4; public preview), which is Windows-only and needs an NVIDIA GPU, and experimental Copilot Fusion local routing, which in Copilot CLI also works with manually configured local models on Windows, macOS and Linux. GitHub states that Fusion routing decisions are made in the cloud.
final_records.model_backend: GitHub-managed routing to models hosted by OpenAI and GitHub's Azure (OpenAI models); AWS Bedrock, Anthropic and Google Cloud (Anthropic models); Google Cloud (Gemini; GitHub uses Google durable caching, cached data held up to 24 hours); xAI (Grok); Azure AI Foundry in GitHub's tenant (Microsoft MAI Code 1.1 Flash, which can also run locally on qualifying Windows/NVIDIA machines); and Fireworks AI (open-weight models, and inline-suggestion models for Free and Student; Business/Enterprise inline suggestions run on Azure). Copilot Fusion (GA 28 Oct 2026) routes each prompt across the models enabled by policy. Free and Student use auto model selection only. Background utility models run on every plan and surface, and admins can disable them only by disabling Copilot. Local (client-side) BYOK is available in Copilot CLI, VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode, the Copilot app (public preview; requires GitHub sign-in) and the Copilot SDK (being renamed Microsoft Copilot SDK). The CLI reads providers from providers.json (legacy COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment variables still work when the file declares none) and supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints (incl. Ollama, vLLM, Foundry Local), Azure OpenAI, Anthropic and llama-server local models. Enterprise BYOK (public preview) runs server-side through GitHub's Copilot API.
final_records.data_handling_note: Business/Enterprise: GitHub states it does not use this data for training (GitHub DPA). GitHub's Copilot Trust Center FAQ (read 6 Nov 2026) gives default retention for Business/Enterprise: IDE chat and completions, the Copilot app and Copilot CLI inputs and outputs are not retained by default (GitHub may retain them for a limited time to investigate confirmed abuse or protect service security); all other Copilot access and use is retained for the life of the account (the Trust Center does not name these surfaces; GitHub's 'Copilot on GitHub' page indicates they include GitHub.com, Mobile and cloud sessions); engagement data is kept 2 years. The Trust Center also notes that certain Copilot CLI commands may write inputs or outputs to GitHub repositories, so 'not retained by default' does not cover content the CLI writes to repositories or sessions synced to GitHub. This replaces the earlier 28-day rule for CLI and GitHub.com. GitHub.com and Mobile chat now run as cloud sessions (GA 28 Oct 2026): cloud-sandbox sessions, the default where an environment choice is offered (GitHub says defaults can vary by workflow), keep chat data for the life of the account and can be deleted by the user; GitHub Actions-based sessions keep chat data 28 days and can be archived but not deleted. CLI and Copilot app sessions sync to the user's GitHub account by default (remoteExport); for Business/Enterprise users only if the 'Store local sessions in the Cloud' policy allows it. Copilot Memory (GA on paid plans) stores user-level preferences and repository-level facts on GitHub. User-level preferences are on by default for Pro, Pro+ and Max, off for Business/Enterprise until an admin enables them, and expire after the 90-day default. Repository-level facts have a separate default on all plans: they are allowed unless enterprise, organization or repository settings restrict them, with a configurable expiry of 7-180 days. Individual Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max: GitHub may use interaction data for training from 24 Apr 2026 unless the user opts out; Student is also an individual plan and should be treated the same. GitHub states that model providers operate under ZDR or no-training agreements. Exceptions: Claude Fable 5/5.1 (now listed on Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, Enterprise and Copilot access), where Anthropic retains prompts and outputs by default and ZDR is available only to approved enterprises under a time-bound exemption to end-2026; and some Anthropic beta/preview features. Provider ZDR does not remove GitHub's own retention.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Business/Enterprise under the GitHub DPA; direct volume-licence subscriptions and renewals from 5 Mar 2026 fall under the Generative AI Services Terms. The new 'Copilot access' model (GitHub Enterprise Cloud, sales-led from 28 Oct 2026) has Copilot Enterprise features; confirm contractually that the same data commitments apply. Prefer IDE, Copilot app and CLI surfaces, where GitHub states inputs and outputs are not retained by default for Business/Enterprise; GitHub.com, Mobile and cloud sessions are kept for the life of the account. Keep the session-sync policy off unless needed, keep the Copilot Memory policy off for user-level preferences and restrict repository-level facts at enterprise or organization level (organization 'Repository access' defaults to all repositories) or set a short repository-fact expiry (7-180 days); for Business/Enterprise, user-level preferences are owned by the billing organization or enterprise, whose owners can export or delete them; and keep Claude Fable 5/5.1 disabled unless a ZDR exemption is in place. Check the 'Default policy for new features', enforced from 22-26 Oct 2026, so new features do not switch on unreviewed. US/EU residency requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency and does not by itself establish compliance. Individual and education plans (Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max) are not a personal-data route; where they are used for non-sensitive work, turn off AI model training and Copilot Memory in Copilot settings.
suitability_notes.special: Only Copilot CLI with COPILOT_OFFLINE=true and a model served on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware qualifies, and only with every special_route control in place (auto-update off, egress blocked, remote MCP servers and web_fetch off, Ollama in local-only mode, no Copilot Fusion). GitHub documents that this mode contacts no GitHub servers and disables telemetry. Selecting or installing a local model, including MAI Code 1.1 Flash and Fusion local routing, does not make a session offline. IDE and Copilot-app BYOK routes were not appraised as fully offline (the app requires GitHub sign-in). GitHub.com, cloud sessions and all GitHub-hosted models remain unsuitable.

compliance: The GitHub Data Protection Agreement applies to GitHub Copilot. The GitHub Generative AI Services Terms (Version March 2026) apply to Generative AI Services purchased directly from GitHub under a volume licensing agreement, for new subscriptions and renewals from 5 March 2026 (no training on Inputs or Outputs without documented instructions). Earlier Business/Enterprise subscriptions stay under the archived Copilot Product Specific Terms until renewal. GitHub's Customer Terms update log shows no change after June 2026.

Customers without a volume licensing agreement are governed by the GitHub Terms of Service; GitHub's controller processing for individual plans is described in the GitHub General Privacy Statement. Purchases through Microsoft fall under the Microsoft agreement's Product Terms. Opted-in preview features fall under the GitHub Pre-Release License Terms.

US/EU data residency for Copilot is available only with GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency and is off by default; it restricts inference routing but is not by itself an institutional approval.

GitHub's Copilot Trust Center states that Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise are in scope of GitHub's latest SOC 2 Type 2 report and ISO 27001 certificate; the reports themselves were not reviewed.
final_records.pricing: Free ($0; limited chat/agent use, 2,000 completions/month) · Student (free, verified students) · Pro $10/mo (1,500 AI credits/mo: 1,000 base + 500 flex) · Pro+ $39/mo (7,000: 3,900 + 3,100 flex) · Max $100/mo (20,000: 10,000 + 10,000 flex); GitHub states flex allotments may change · Business $19/granted seat/mo (1,900 credits, pooled) · Enterprise $39/granted seat/mo (3,900 credits, pooled) · Copilot access (eligible GitHub Enterprise Cloud enterprises via a GitHub or Microsoft account team from 28 Oct 2026; self-serve not yet available): $0 seat for GitHub Enterprise Cloud licensees or $10/user/mo Copilot Standalone, no included credits, all usage metered. Usage-based billing since 1 June 2026, at 1 AI credit = $0.01. Chat, agents, CLI, the app and code review consume credits; code completions and next edit suggestions are unlimited on paid plans; code review also uses Actions minutes, and cloud-sandbox billing starts in November 2026 against the Actions compute entitlement. Data-residency enforcement adds 10% to AI-credit consumption. From 1 Oct 2026, Business/Enterprise seats paid by card or PayPal are charged upfront.
final_records.academic: Copilot Student is free for verified GitHub Education students. Verified teachers and maintainers of popular open-source projects can get Copilot Pro free. Eligibility is re-evaluated monthly. These are individual plans: GitHub's plans FAQ applies AI-model training to individual subscribers unless they opt out, and the plans docs list Student among the individual plans (the training-policy page names only Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max). Treat Student and free Pro as in the training program and set 'Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training' to Disabled.

final_records.notes: Individual Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max interaction data may be used for training unless the user opts out (treat Student the same); Business/Enterprise are excluded. Under Business/Enterprise defaults, GitHub's Trust Center now states that IDE, Copilot app and CLI inputs and outputs are not retained, while all other Copilot use, which GitHub's docs indicate includes GitHub.com, Mobile and cloud sessions, is retained for the life of the account (previously 28 days; the 'Chat in GitHub' how-to still says 28 days). Since 28 Oct 2026 GitHub.com and Mobile chat run as cloud sessions in GitHub-hosted sandboxes, and Copilot Memory is generally available. US/EU residency requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency and adds 10% AI-credit consumption; it does not by itself establish research-data approval. Copilot CLI offline mode (COPILOT_OFFLINE=true) with a local model is the only route this review appraised as documented to run without contacting GitHub; GitHub documents it, but this review did not test it, so confidence is medium. Local model routing through Copilot Fusion is not offline. Copilot is not available for GitHub Enterprise Server.
final_records.tier_gate: Business / Enterprise (or Copilot access on GitHub Enterprise Cloud) for organizational cloud use; Copilot CLI offline mode with a model on researcher/institution-controlled hardware for special-category data

required_controls: Use Copilot CLI with COPILOT_OFFLINE=true and a BYOK provider in providers.json (or a managed file named by COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG) whose baseUrl points to a model served on the same machine or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network (for example Ollama, vLLM, Foundry Local or llama-server). providers.json takes precedence over the legacy COPILOT_PROVIDER_* variables. The endpoint must serve only institution-hosted models and must not forward requests to external providers. Point every model the CLI uses at that endpoint and use no GitHub-hosted models.

Do not use Copilot Fusion or local model auto-routing: GitHub states that Fusion makes routing decisions in the cloud and that local inference does not make a session offline. Install local models through an institution-controlled channel, not the model picker's managed download.

If the model is served by Ollama, run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the server.json of the account that runs the Ollama server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no ':cloud' models.

Enforce offline mode (COPILOT_OFFLINE), the provider file (providers.json or COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG) and auto-update off by institutional means such as a locked environment or wrapper and read-only configuration: these are not CLI MDM/managed-settings keys. MDM or managed-settings.json supports only a fixed key list (for example a sandbox floor, permission deny rules, MCP allow/deny lists, telemetry, remote control and model), and user settings can override most keys; built-in first-party MCP servers are exempt from managed allowlists. Verify the effective configuration before each session, and keep no GitHub tokens or cloud-provider API keys in that environment. Block egress to GitHub and all other external hosts at the network level and confirm with egress monitoring before processing special-category data.

Disable CLI auto-update (COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false or --no-auto-update; the autoUpdate setting defaults to true and downloads CLI and first-party plugin updates at session start). Install and update a pinned CLI version through an institution-controlled channel.

Enable local sandboxing (off by default) with network access denied or limited to the local model endpoint. Use no remote MCP servers (they are never sandboxed), disable built-in MCP servers (--disable-builtin-mcps), restrict local MCP servers, and deny the web_fetch tool.

Do not use /delegate, Copilot in the cloud, remote control (remoteSessions), session sync (set remoteExport false or --sync-session=off), Copilot Memory, GitHub.com, the Copilot app or IDE extensions for special-category data.
residual_risks: The CLI is proprietary and closed-source (GitHub Copilot CLI License). Its offline-mode network behaviour is documented by GitHub but cannot be audited independently, and this review did not test it.

COPILOT_OFFLINE is documented only in two how-to pages and the 7 Oct 2026 changelog. It is not listed in the environment-variable table of the CLI command reference, and the offline-mode pages do not mention auto-update or plugin-marketplace updates specifically.

Without COPILOT_OFFLINE=true, GitHub documents that telemetry is still sent even with a local BYOK model and no GitHub sign-in. Discovering, adding or installing a local model with /model, or letting Copilot Fusion route to one, does not turn on offline mode.

GitHub's own CLI and app 'add LLM models' pages say that running a model locally (MAI Code 1.1 Flash) lets users 'use Copilot offline', which conflicts with the 28 Oct 2026 Fusion changelog; researchers may wrongly treat a local model as offline without COPILOT_OFFLINE=true and an egress block.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a CLI pointed at local Ollama can still send data to Ollama's cloud unless local-only mode is enabled.

Local sandboxing is off by default and is lightweight OS-level isolation, not a VM or container. The CLI's built-in file tools run in-process outside the OS sandbox and follow the sandbox policy only on a best-effort basis. Unsandboxed agent commands can reach any network the machine can reach.
Copilot CLI keeps full session records under ~/.copilot/session-state and a local SQLite session store (session-store.db). Institutional access, retention and deletion controls are needed.
Locally hosted models may lack the safety filters GitHub applies to its hosted models (GitHub says this of MAI Code 1.1 Flash), which matters when tool actions are auto-approved.

Capability depends on the local model, which must support tool calling and streaming. Token limits must be set to the model's real capacity; for an unknown model the CLI can default to 128,000 prompt tokens.
The CLI ships very frequently (v1.0.106 on 6 Nov 2026), so a pinned version needs regular institutional review of documented behaviour.

final_records.name: Devin Desktop
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Cognition in-house SWE models (SWE-2 and SWE-2 Flash, SWE-1.x, SWE-1-mini, swe-grep, swe-check) plus third-party models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and open-weight families (DeepSeek, Moonshot Kimi, Z.ai GLM, NVIDIA Nemotron); Adaptive routing and Fusion pairings. Availability depends on plan; Teams and Enterprise admins can allowlist models. Where the open-weight models are hosted is not documented.
final_records.data_handling_note: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop. Cognition may train on Customer Data by default; opt-out is limited to paid plans (Pro, Max, Teams; on Teams only an admin), after which Cognition applies no-training and model-provider ZDR, except for abuse/safety flags and legal process. Teams and Enterprise admins can also unlock Anthropic and OpenAI models that require provider retention for up to 30 days (no training). Since v3.11.238 (30 Oct 2026), members an Enterprise admin has listed for Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program can switch the program on or off themselves; with it off, their Anthropic requests follow the team's usual retention settings, and the retention and terms that apply with it on are not documented. Enterprise terms bar training without written consent. Provider ZDR does not end product retention: Cognition keeps processed data for the customer relationship (DPA: term plus 30 days), keeps Feedback and User Interaction Data as long as it determines, and collects anonymized Usage Data. Client telemetry can be lowered or switched off with the TelemetryLevel MDM device policy. The privacy policy (updated 26 Oct 2026) states that identifiers, commercial information and internet activity data are disclosed to advertising partners (opt-out via Privacy Choices or Global Privacy Control); personal information an organisation submits under an enterprise agreement is governed by that agreement. Third-party ACP agents run outside Devin Desktop's privacy terms, and the data terms for GPT requests billed to a linked ChatGPT plan are not documented. Customer Dedicated Deployment is Cognition-hosted; the Devin brain stays in Cognition Cloud.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-held Teams or Enterprise plan: Pro and Max are individual plans, and the Cognition DPA binds the contracting customer as data controller. On Teams an admin must opt out of training; Enterprise terms bar training without written consent. The posted Cognition DPA applies by reference. Keep ChatGPT-plan linking, third-party ACP agents, the provider-retention model toggles and the Anthropic Cyber Verification Program route off, and use the Teams/Enterprise model allowlist to restrict to models whose providers are listed DPA subprocessors. Deploy the TelemetryLevel device policy (MDM) set to off or error; it limits client telemetry and is not documented to stop server-side Usage Data, Feedback or User Interaction Data collection. Platform and Enterprise terms bar medical/health information and sensitive personal data (e.g., birth dates, ID numbers); remove these fields, because pseudonymization does not make medical data permissible. Customer Dedicated Deployment is still Cognition-hosted. Devin EU (app.devin.eu, EU-hosted; see rca-devin) is documented for the Devin web app; whether Devin Desktop can run under it is not documented.
suitability_notes.special: Inference for Devin Desktop's own agents stays in Cognition Cloud on every route offered to commercial customers, including Customer Dedicated Deployment and Devin Cloud Outposts. Cognition's federal-deployment docs also describe a beta air-gapped build of Devin Desktop and CLI that sends inference to customer-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints, obtained through an on-prem entitlement set up by the account team; availability to research institutions outside federal deployments is not documented. The legacy Windsurf self-hosted deployment has been in maintenance mode since May 2025 and takes no new customers. The platform terms also bar medical and sensitive personal data. Not suitable for special-category data under the controlled-infrastructure rule.

compliance: Cognition states SOC 2 Type II (security docs and DPA Appendix B); the trust centre is now publicly readable and lists SOC 2 Type 2 and a bridge letter, with reports released only after an NDA. The posted DPA (updated 21 Oct 2026) applies by reference; exact service/model scope requires confirmation.

US federal deployments only: Cognition lists FedRAMP High, IL4 and ITAR for Devin Desktop, with ZDR for all Desktop features; IL5 status differs between first-party sources (federal docs: in process; public-sector trust centre: met). Scoped to federal deployments, not commercial plans.
final_records.pricing: Free $0; Pro $20/month (includes Devin Cloud access); Max $200/month. Teams (up to 200 users): the pricing page lists $80/month plus $40/month per full seat, while the billing docs describe $80/month as a minimum met by $40 full seats and/or prepaid on-demand credits; Devin Desktop needs a full seat (flex seats exclude it). Usage beyond quota is billed at API pricing via on-demand credits. Enterprise: contractual ACU pricing.
final_records.academic: No current official student discount was confirmed.

The Devin cloud agent is catalogued separately as rca-devin. final_records.name: Google Antigravity
final_records.deployment: cloud inference for the Antigravity App (the Antigravity 2.0 desktop app), CLI, standalone IDE and IDE extensions (consumer Google account or Gemini Enterprise/Google Cloud); Remote Agents (rolling out from 3 Nov 2026 to Google AI Pro/Ultra personal accounts only) run sessions and tools in a Google-managed remote environment; local-capable Antigravity SDK with on-device or local OpenAI-compatible models
final_records.model_backend: Google-hosted Gemini models (Gemini 4 Argon on paid Pro, Ultra and Enterprise; Gemini 3.8 Flash on all plans; Gemini 3.7/3.6 Flash and 3.1 Pro on Enterprise only) plus third-party models offered through Google: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 on Google AI Pro (non-trial) and Ultra and, after administrator opt-in, on Gemini Enterprise; Claude Sonnet/Opus 4.6 (Free, Plus and Pro) and GPT-OSS-120b (Free, Plus, Pro and Ultra) until their announced 18 November 2026 removal. Lightweight first-party Gemini models still run in the background when Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5 is selected (documented as hybrid execution on the enterprise page), and Nano Banana 2 handles image generation. Only the SDK can use local models (Gemma 4 via LiteRT, or Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM endpoints).
final_records.data_handling_note: Consumer accounts: Google records and stores Interactions (user data, usage data, metadata, feedback) and uses them to evaluate, develop and improve Google and Alphabet products and machine-learning technologies; employees and contractors may review them, and the terms ask users not to submit confidential information. Turning off Enable Telemetry (Account settings in the Antigravity App) stops interaction collection for improvement, but the terms, revised after 10 Oct 2026, state that Google still uses data to provide the service, process feedback and keep Antigravity safe. The CLI's Enable Telemetry setting collects usage data to improve Antigravity, is saved with the account and is always off for business accounts. Deletion is by email request, and no retention period is stated. Remote Agents (consumer Pro/Ultra) keep conversations and uploaded files in Google-managed remote projects, with no stated retention period. Gemini Enterprise/Google Cloud: administrator-accepted Google Cloud terms apply, the Service Specific Terms bar training on Customer Data without permission, and client telemetry and model interactions are logged to the customer's selected Google Cloud project. After 10 Oct 2026 the Antigravity Additional Terms dropped the statement that they do not apply to enterprise users, so whether their Interactions clause (recording, storing and using Interactions to improve Google products and models) also binds Gemini Enterprise users is not stated. The Antigravity terms state that enterprise or other signed terms do not apply to use of the Antigravity Marketplace, from which the Antigravity Science plugin is installed. Enterprise inference stays in Google Cloud (global, us or eu; third-party models have no in-country regions; sign-in always reaches global endpoints). SDK with a Gemini API key: Gemini API terms apply (unpaid quota is used for product improvement with human review; paid quota is not, but prompts are logged for a limited period for abuse detection). No SDK-specific terms are published. The SDK local-model route is documented to run without an API key or internet connection.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Gemini Enterprise or a Google Cloud project under the institution's Google Cloud agreement, through the Antigravity App, the CLI or the IDE extensions (the standalone Antigravity IDE is not supported for enterprise). Keep telemetry in an institution project, choose the eu location where residency matters, and leave third-party models disabled unless assessed. Do not use Antigravity Marketplace plugins, including the Science plugin, with personal data: the Antigravity terms state that enterprise terms do not apply to Marketplace use. Since its 12 Oct 2026 version (current: 30 Oct 2026) the Google Cloud Services Summary no longer lists Antigravity separately; Gemini Enterprise is listed, and Agentic AI Services are stated to include any agentic feature of a Service, so confirm with Google that Antigravity use is covered by the institution's agreement and the Cloud Data Processing Addendum. Google Cloud lists no ISO 27001 or SOC 2 scope for Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise. Consumer accounts, Remote Agents and the free science access programme (individual terms) are not suitable for personal data; the SDK local-model route is an alternative.
suitability_notes.special: Only the Antigravity SDK local-model route qualifies: LiteRTAgentConfig with an on-device Gemma checkpoint, or LocalOpenAIAgentConfig against a localhost server, on researcher-controlled hardware with outbound network blocked and verified. Do not use LocalAgentConfig: despite its name it calls Google's cloud. The Antigravity App, the CLI, the standalone IDE, the IDE extensions and Remote Agents use cloud inference or Google-managed execution and are not acceptable, Gemini Enterprise and VPC Service Controls notwithstanding.

compliance: Enterprise route runs under the Google Cloud terms accepted by the administrator. The Google Cloud Service Specific Terms (last modified 30 Oct 2026) state that Google will not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune AI/ML models without permission (Section 18) and name 'Antigravity for Enterprise' as a service for Third-Party Enterprise Models (Section 9).

The Google Cloud Platform Services Summary lists Gemini Enterprise under Agentic AI Services but, since its 12 Oct 2026 version (current version last modified 30 Oct 2026), no longer lists Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise by name as the 30 Sep 2026 version did; the section states that Agentic AI Services include any agentic feature or functionality of a Service.

Google Cloud's AI developer tools overview (last updated 2026-11-06) states that Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise does not support Access Transparency, FedRAMP, IL4/IL5, ISO 27001/42001, ITAR or SOC 1/2/3.

Consumer use, including the free science access programme, is governed by the Google Terms of Service, the Antigravity Additional Terms and the Google Privacy Policy; no data processing addendum is listed for consumer use. The Antigravity terms state that enterprise or other signed terms do not apply to Antigravity Marketplace use.
final_records.pricing: Individual: USD 0 plan with weekly-refreshed quota (Google AI Plus has the same model access as the free plan); Google AI Pro and Ultra add higher rate limits, five-hourly quota refresh, Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5 (Pro non-trial only) and AI-credit overages charged at Gemini Enterprise consumption pricing (consumer plan prices are not listed on the Antigravity pricing page). Business plan via Google Cloud: API access with consumption-based pricing; for eligible Gemini Enterprise customers, Standard/Plus from USD 30 per seat per month (first-party Gemini models draw on pooled seat credits of USD 10 per month for Standard and USD 15 for Plus) or Pay-as-you-go with no seat fee. Enterprise third-party models require administrator opt-in and are billed by token consumption. Billing: Google Cloud's AI developer tools overview (2026-11-06) requires an active non-trial subscription and a project linked to Cloud Billing, self-serve with prepaid credits or invoiced; the Antigravity pricing and enterprise pages still refer to an invoiced Cloud Billing account.
final_records.academic: No academic tier is listed on the Antigravity pricing or plans pages. Since 13 Oct 2026 Google has run an application-based programme giving up to 10,000 selected scientists (non-commercial research; active affiliation with a university, degree-granting institution, non-profit research institute or national laboratory) six months of free access to the highest individual usage tier and Gemini 4 Argon. Access is to the individual Antigravity service under the individual terms, not an institutional Gemini Enterprise subscription, so it is not an institutional data-protection route. Google reported over 25,000 applications and 1,000 grants by 27 Oct 2026.

final_records.notes: Proprietary agentic development platform from Google, distinct from the open-source Gemini CLI. Surfaces: the Antigravity App desktop command center (formerly called Antigravity 2.0; v2.29.0, 3 Nov 2026), Antigravity CLI (agy, v1.5.1, 5 Nov 2026), IDE extensions (VS Code and Visual Studio; JetBrains, Zed, Xcode and Eclipse in preview), the standalone Antigravity IDE (v2.6.0, 26 Oct 2026; not supported for enterprise), Remote Agents (consumer Pro/Ultra, rolling out) and the Antigravity SDK. The SDK's Python layer is Apache-2.0 but depends on a closed compiled runtime binary shipped in the PyPI wheels; official local-model support arrived in SDK v0.1.18 (21 Sep 2026), the latest release is v0.1.23 (26 Oct 2026), and the package is still marked Alpha. The Plugin Marketplace added partner plugins in App v2.28.2 (29 Oct 2026). A separate managed Antigravity agent on the Gemini API (preview, Google-hosted sandbox) is cloud-only. The organization offer is the Business plan via Google Cloud and is included in eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions.
final_records.tier_gate: Gemini Enterprise or Google Cloud project under Google Cloud terms (no Marketplace plugins) for personal data; SDK local-model route (on-device LiteRT checkpoint or localhost model server) on researcher-controlled hardware with egress blocked for special-category data

required_controls: Use only the Antigravity SDK with LiteRTAgentConfig (on-device .litertlm checkpoint) or LocalOpenAIAgentConfig whose base_url is a server on the same host (localhost/loopback). Do not use LocalAgentConfig: despite its name it calls the Gemini API or Gemini Enterprise. Leave GEMINI_API_KEY, vertex=True and Google Cloud credentials unset.

Download and checksum the model checkpoint before isolating the host (litert-lm import pulls about 16.8 GB from Hugging Face). Then block outbound network egress during runs and verify that it stays blocked; the docs state the local route works without an internet connection.

Do not use web or search tools, remote MCP servers, cloud-backed skills (including the Antigravity Science skills), cloud-model subagents, or the documented hybrid pattern that pairs a cloud Gemini planner with local agents.
Leave OpenTelemetry export unset, or point it at an institution-controlled collector. Govern local session state, logs and workspaces.
residual_risks: The SDK depends on a closed compiled runtime binary (localharness). Its network behaviour in local mode is documented only as working without an API key or internet connection, and this was not independently tested.

No SDK-specific terms are published. The Antigravity Additional Terms reserve recording and storing Interactions while the Service runs, and they may apply to SDK use. Egress blocking is the technical control and DPO review is the contractual one.
The SDK changelog (v0.1.8) documents client OS and version information in telemetry headers. Whether the runtime emits any telemetry in local mode is not documented.

The SDK is pre-1.0 and marked Alpha on PyPI. The local route recommends at least 24 GB of VRAM or unified memory and works best with the Gemma 4 26B A4B LiteRT checkpoint, so capability is well below the cloud route.
The Antigravity App, the CLI, the standalone IDE, the IDE extensions and Remote Agents remain cloud-only.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: JetBrains Junie
final_records.deployment: cloud (JetBrains AI models, JetBrains-hosted Junie Lite, BYOK providers) / local-capable (Junie CLI only: Ollama, LM Studio, LiteLLM/custom endpoints, Junie Local engine)
final_records.model_backend: JetBrains AI subscription models (Junie subcontractors listed: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and "SpaceXAI" for Grok-family); JetBrains-hosted Qwen 3.6 27B as the free Junie Lite tier; BYOK in Junie CLI (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot) and, for Junie in AI Assistant's AI Chat, OpenAI or Anthropic API keys (not in the Junie plugin); local/custom endpoints documented in Junie CLI only (Ollama, LM Studio, LiteLLM, JSON custom profiles, Junie Local engine running Qwen3.6-27B-4bit or the Qwen3.8-3.6-27B blend)
final_records.data_handling_note: Local route: Junie CLI with Ollama (cloud features disabled), LM Studio or Junie Local keeps inference on the researcher's hardware; JetBrains states that after the Junie Local model download no prompts, code or diffs are transmitted. Cloud routes (JetBrains AI models, Junie Lite on JetBrains infrastructure, BYOK providers): the JetBrains AI Terms bar training generative models on inputs/outputs without express consent and bind subcontractors to the same, but inputs may be stored for a limited period for abuse monitoring; BYOK traffic follows the provider's own terms. Eco mode (interactive Junie CLI and ACP clients such as JetBrains Air, from 21 Oct 2026; not headless/CI runs) starts On for models that support it and hands implementation to a cheaper model, chosen by Junie, on the same provider route, possibly from a different model vendor. In JetBrains IDEs, detailed code-related data collection (full LLM prompts and responses, used to train JetBrains models, kept 1 year) is off by default for commercial individual and organizational licenses and needs explicit consent on free student/classroom/open-source licenses, but is ON by default (opt-out) for non-commercial licenses; whether it also covers Junie CLI is not documented. EAP and nightly builds fall under the Junie EAP Terms, which let JetBrains store and analyse inputs and outputs for product improvement and prohibit personal data as input.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a release (not EAP/nightly) build under an organizational or commercial license with detailed data collection off and the JetBrains DPA in place, or a release build with a fully local endpoint. Non-commercial licenses must opt out of detailed data collection first; the Junie EAP Terms (which cover nightly builds) prohibit personal data as input. Turn Eco mode off if processing must stay with one named model vendor.
suitability_notes.special: Only release-channel Junie CLI with a local runtime (Junie Local installed with the standard installer, Ollama with cloud features disabled, or LM Studio) on hardware the researcher or institution controls. The Junie IDE plugin (no local-model support), JetBrains Air (listed as EAP), Junie Lite, JetBrains AI models, BYOK, Eco mode on a cloud route, Remote mode, GitHub/GitLab runs and any nightly/EAP build are not acceptable.

compliance: JetBrains Data Processing Addendum (v1.3, last updated 27 Apr 2022, with GDPR standard contractual clauses) is published; coverage depends on the selected product and provider route.
JetBrains AI subcontractors are listed publicly (last update 29 Sep 2026); the AI Terms promise 30 days' notice before a new one is engaged.
The Junie site states that JetBrains tools hold SOC 2 certification; the report itself was not inspected.
final_records.pricing: AI Free (3 AI Credits/30 days); AI Pro $10/month individual or $20 organization; AI Ultimate $30 individual or $60 organization; AI Enterprise $60 (organizations only). Junie Lite (JetBrains-hosted model) is free with a JetBrains account (the docs list free, AI Pro and AI Ultimate accounts; AI Enterprise is not mentioned); the launch post footnote says the offer is valid until 31 Dec 2026. Junie Local and own local runtimes carry no JetBrains charge. BYOK is billed by the provider; a Junie API key gives usage-based billing.
final_records.academic: AI Free is available with educational, classroom and open-source IDE licenses, but AI Pro is not included in complimentary student, teacher or classroom All Products Pack licenses. Junie Lite is available with a free JetBrains account. Detailed data collection needs explicit consent on free student/classroom/open-source licenses but is on by default for non-commercial licenses.
use_cases: coding
agentic debugging
