CI/CD automation
final_records.notes: Agentic coding agent from JetBrains: Junie CLI (terminal, headless, GitHub/GitLab CI) and Junie inside JetBrains IDEs via AI Chat, the Junie plugin or JetBrains Air. Only Junie CLI is documented with local runtimes, so the qualifying controlled-infrastructure route is CLI plus a local runtime. Junie Lite (Oct 2026) is free but runs on JetBrains infrastructure, so it is a vendor cloud route; Junie Local (from Aug 2026) is an on-device engine for Apple Silicon Macs and, as of 16 Oct 2026 (stable; experimental since September), Windows PCs with 24 GB+ NVIDIA RTX GPUs. Eco mode (Oct 2026) splits planning and implementation across models. Do not generalize cloud no-training terms to local execution or vice versa.
final_records.tier_gate: Release-channel Junie CLI with a fully local runtime for special-category data (the IDE plugin has no local-model support; nightly/EAP builds bar personal data as input); for organizational cloud use, an organizational license (detailed data collection disallowed unless an admin or contract enables it) or AI Enterprise; non-commercial licenses must opt out of detailed data collection.

required_controls: Use a release-channel Junie CLI build: nightly and other EAP builds fall under the Junie EAP Terms, which prohibit personal data as input. The Junie IDE plugin does not support Ollama or local model selection.

Configure only local runtimes on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware: Junie Local installed with the standard (non-EAP) installer, Ollama in local-only mode, or LM Studio; add no BYOK keys, JetBrains account models, Junie Lite, or LiteLLM/Ingrazzio proxies that reach cloud providers.

Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in ~/.ollama/server.json of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models; Junie auto-discovers every model the server lists.

Check project-scope files in cloned repositories as well as $JUNIE_HOME: Junie loads model profiles from $JUNIE_HOME/models and .junie/models/*.json, and <project>/.junie/config.json by default, which can carry byok keys and proxies entries; any of these may point to a remote endpoint. Prefer --model-default-locations false and --config-default-locations false with explicit, reviewed locations.
Keep Eco mode off (or confirm the local model offers no Eco option): Eco behaviour on custom or local model routes is not documented, and Junie chooses the implementation model.
Do not use /remote (Remote mode tunnels the session to the Junie web app), JetBrains Air cloud runs, or the GitHub/GitLab integrations.
Set --share-anonymous-statistics false (or JUNIE_SHARE_ANONYMOUS_STATISTICS=false) and disable update checks (auto-update false or --skip-update-check); enforce and test network egress blocking.

Keep brave mode off. Sandbox mode is an EAP-only feature (EAP Terms bar personal data) and leaves network access unrestricted by default, so on the release build enforce egress blocking at OS or network level; review MCP servers, hooks, skills and shell commands, which can reach the network.
Protect local session stores (events.jsonl, transcript.md, cross-session prompt history) and Junie configuration under ~/.junie with institutional access and retention controls.
residual_risks: Junie CLI is a proprietary closed binary; JetBrains' statement that nothing leaves the machine with Junie Local is vendor-asserted and was not independently tested.
The default for Junie CLI anonymous usage statistics is not documented, nor is the network behaviour of auxiliary tools (web search, URL extraction) when only local models are configured.

Junie Local hardware requirements differ between first-party pages: the docs (05 Nov 2026) list macOS 26+, Apple Silicon M4 or newer and 48 GB RAM, while the landing page still lists M5 and 64 GB; Windows 11 with an NVIDIA RTX GPU (Ampere or newer, 24 GB+ VRAM) is stable since 16 Oct 2026. The installer downloads the inference engine and 4-bit quantized weights (download host not documented); the engine is updated separately via /local.
Ollama can serve cloud models through the same local endpoint when signed in with cloud features on, and Junie auto-discovers every model the server lists.
Local open-weight models are weaker than frontier models; small or heavily quantized models may fail Junie's tool calls and multi-step tasks.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Cline
final_records.deployment: local-capable / cloud provider dependent; Desktop can also run sessions on a user-chosen remote host over SSH; optional Cline-hosted Cloud agents (Cline cloud sandbox), started from the browser, the VS Code extension or Desktop
final_records.model_backend: Direct BYOK cloud providers or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; Cline-managed routes (Cline usage-billing, ClinePass, rotating free models); subscription or CLI-login providers such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and OpenCode, which fall under those vendors' own terms; documented local Ollama/LM Studio/Atomic Chat endpoints. Cloud agents offer only Cline-managed model routes.
final_records.data_handling_note: Route-dependent. With your own API keys, prompts go directly to the chosen provider, and Cline's ToS and privacy notice say Cline does not receive them; Ollama/LM Studio/Atomic Chat keep inference on the machine. On the Cline (usage-billing), ClinePass and free-model routes, Cline receives prompts to route them. Its enterprise page says code is never used to train models on Cline-managed inference, but its ToS (s. 3.5, Cline-provided keys) says upstream model providers may train unless opted out. Free-model usage may be used to improve models, and telemetry for Cline/ClinePass requests can include prompts and responses. Usage telemetry is on by default in the extensions, Desktop and CLI, also with own keys, and can be turned off. Sign-in and feature-flag calls continue, and Desktop and the CLI ignore the organization's telemetry setting. No public retention period is stated. On-premises and air-gapped enterprise deployments are advertised but not publicly documented.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local model, or a direct provider key covered by an institutional DPA/no-training terms, and turn telemetry off. Cline, ClinePass, free-model routes and Cloud agents need separate assessment: Cline sees those requests, free-model usage may improve models, and telemetry can include prompts. Cloud sessions can now be started from the VS Code extension (opt-in) and Desktop (on wherever available; they need a Cline account and a connected GitHub repo), so check which mode a task runs in. Subscription or CLI-login routes fall under those vendors' own terms, and Desktop web search is on by default for new sessions with providers that have built-in search.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a fully local Ollama/LM Studio/Atomic Chat model on institution-controlled hardware, used from the Apache-2.0 client (VS Code extension, CLI or Desktop), with Ollama cloud features disabled, telemetry off, no Cline account or Cline-managed provider, and outbound traffic restricted; a remote host used through Desktop's SSH mode must also be institution-controlled. Cloud agents and enterprise VPC wording do not establish this boundary.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Open-source client is free; inference is pay-as-you-go via Cline credits or BYOK. ClinePass is an optional $9.99/month subscription for selected open-weight models (its product page adds that an additional processing fee may apply), while the general pricing page still says no subscriptions are needed for the open-source version. Rotating free-model promotions have a usage quota; Cloud agents can use free or paid Cline models. Enterprise is custom/contractual.
final_records.academic: free (open-source tier)

final_records.notes: Apache-2.0 client: VS Code-family extension, CLI (also usable as the agent in Zed, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim and Emacs via ACP) and a beta Desktop app (announced 14 Sep 2026; v0.0.49 on 26 Oct 2026 added a Local Models page that installs, starts and manages Ollama or LM Studio models), with direct-provider and local-model routes; releases shipped on seven days in October 2026 (latest batch 26 Oct, none since) with commits every weekday. The JetBrains Marketplace plugin is free but is licensed under Cline's ToS with no public source. Cline Cloud agents (docs added 7 Oct 2026) run tasks in Cline's cloud sandbox with Cline-managed models only, and since 16 Oct 2026 can also be started from the VS Code extension and Desktop. Scope privacy claims to the selected route; enterprise governance runs through Cline's hosted admin console, and enterprise does not by itself mean self-hosted inference. Openness is recorded as open-core for the whole record: the clients in cline/cline are Apache-2.0, while the JetBrains Marketplace plugin, Cloud agents and the hosted enterprise console are not open source.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local Ollama/LM Studio/Atomic Chat model, no Cline account or Cloud sessions, telemetry off, egress blocked for special-category data; direct provider key under an institutional DPA/no-training terms with telemetry off for personal data

required_controls: Configure only a local runtime (Ollama, LM Studio or Atomic Chat) on the same machine or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network, reached directly with no gateway that forwards to external providers; no Cline, ClinePass, free-model, subscription/CLI-login or cloud BYOK provider.
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Use the Apache-2.0 client (VS Code extension, CLI or Desktop) without a Cline account; Cline's ToS states no User Content is collected with telemetry when calls stay on your infrastructure and no account exists.
Turn telemetry off (extension: Allow error and usage reporting; Desktop: Settings > General; CLI: telemetryOptOut), also turn off editor telemetry, and restart Desktop/the Cline hub.
Restrict outbound network traffic: with telemetry off, Cline still contacts its servers for sign-in and feature flags.

Do not use Cloud agents or Cloud sessions (browser, VS Code extension Local | Cloud toggle, Desktop, CLI CLINE_CLOUD_SESSIONS opt-in), web search, the Cline API, CLI messaging connectors (cline connect: Slack, Telegram, etc.), Composio connectors, remote MCP servers or marketplace add-ons that send data off the host; keep auto-approve/YOLO off for sensitive workspaces.

If Desktop's SSH remote mode is used, the remote host must also be institution-controlled and egress-restricted: Desktop uploads a Cline helper and hub to it and forwards the active provider key for the session.
residual_risks: Telemetry is on by default, including with own keys and local models. The Desktop v0.0.26 release note (11 Sep 2026) says prompt tracing was then limited to Cline/ClinePass requests, implying earlier Desktop builds traced own-key turns; keep installs current.

A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so prompts can leave the machine unless Ollama's cloud features are disabled and the log check is repeated after updates.
Desktop and the CLI ignore the organization's telemetry and provider settings, so these controls must be enforced on each machine.

Task and session histories are stored locally (~/.cline/data/tasks; hub sessions in ~/.cline/data). Enterprise Prompt Storage can sync them to S3/R2. Institutional access, retention and backup controls are required.

Offline or air-gapped operation of the open-source client is not publicly documented; enterprise VPC/on-prem/air-gapped deployment is advertised only, and enterprise governance uses Cline's hosted admin console.
Agent terminal, browser and MCP tools can move data off the host if egress is not blocked.

Since 16 Oct 2026 Cloud sessions are offered inside the VS Code extension (opt-in) and Desktop (on wherever available), so a signed-in client can send a task to Cline's cloud sandbox; Cloud requires a Cline account and GitHub connection, so staying signed out should keep this route closed (not tested on a signed-out install).
Desktop SSH remote sessions run a Cline hub on the remote host; the SSH docs do not say whether the local telemetry opt-out applies there.

final_records.name: Tabnine
final_records.deployment: Enterprise only: Tabnine-hosted SaaS, or private installation in the customer's own VPC (AWS/GCP/Azure) or on-premises, optionally fully air-gapped
final_records.model_backend: Tabnine Universal model for code completions. Chat/agent use admin-enabled models: on SaaS, Tabnine-served GPT, Claude and Gemini families plus open-weight models. Private installations use self-hosted open-weight models, admin-configured private endpoints (Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible) or, optionally, Tabnine-hosted inference over Private Service Connect. Model lists change frequently.
final_records.data_handling_note: Docs state a no-train/no-retain policy: inference context is processed ephemerally and deleted after the answer, including in private installations (privacy page last updated 2025-07-30). Exceptions: the global RAG (repository connection) index, an admin-enabled feature marked private preview, is retained on the Tabnine server, which on SaaS is Tabnine-operated. On Enterprise SaaS, Tabnine trains on customer code only if a private custom model is chosen. The privacy page says the policy applies regardless of the model used, but the AI Models page warns that third-party chat/agent models (GPT, Claude, Gemini families on SaaS) may have different privacy terms, and no provider-level retention terms are published. For self-hosted, non-air-gapped clusters, the privacy page says operational metrics and logs (kept one week) and one-way-hashed client telemetry (user email, hostname, IP) go to Tabnine, never code. A v4.6.0 release note says telemetry to Tabnine is optional and off by default. Air-gapped installs can send metrics and logs to the customer's own Prometheus and log aggregator.

suitability_notes.personal: Enterprise SaaS main datacenters are in the US (AWS North Virginia, GCP Council Bluffs Iowa, Heroku Virginia). Chat/agent can use third-party model families, and the global RAG index is retained server-side. Use only under a DPA covering subprocessors and transfers (DPA and subprocessor list are not public), with admin-restricted models and no repository connection; prefer a private installation.
suitability_notes.special: Only a private installation on institution-controlled infrastructure (on-premises or the institution's own cloud account; air-gapped preferred) serving self-hosted open-weight models. Tabnine SaaS, Tabnine-hosted inference and third-party cloud model endpoints do not qualify.

compliance: Trust Center lists SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001:2015 and GDPR, with reports gated; docs state SOC 2 and GDPR compliance. No report type or dates are public; verify the current report and that its scope covers the contracted deployment.
final_records.pricing: No public price list: on 2026-11-06 tabnine.com/pricing 301-redirects to a Tricentis contact page that does not mention Tabnine, and the tabnine.com homepage redirects to the Tricentis products page. Enterprise SaaS accounts are set up with the Tabnine team; private installation is an Enterprise option. Obtain a quote.
final_records.academic: None found: no academic or student offer in current first-party docs; there is no public pricing page (tabnine.com/pricing redirects to a Tricentis contact page, checked 2026-11-06)

final_records.notes: Enterprise-only commercial coding assistant (IDE plugins and agent, OpenCode-based CLI) with documented on-premises and air-gapped installation. Tricentis acquired Tabnine (announced 2026-07-30); the tabnine.com homepage and pricing page now redirect to Tricentis pages that do not mention Tabnine, while docs and private-installation releases continue (v6.7.0, 2026-10-21, made a new Tabnine Agent available to all teams with Agent access; v6.7.1 is listed without a date). The public IDE plugins no longer onboard new users; the legacy Tabnine CLI gets only critical fixes until 2026-12-31.
final_records.tier_gate: Tabnine Enterprise private installation on institution-controlled infrastructure (on-premises or own cloud account, air-gapped preferred) with self-hosted open-weight models; Tabnine SaaS, Tabnine-hosted inference and third-party cloud model endpoints do not qualify

required_controls: Tabnine Enterprise private installation on institution-controlled infrastructure (on-premises or the institution's own AWS/GCP/Azure account); fully air-gapped mode preferred.

Serve chat, agent and Context Engine models from self-hosted open-weight models on institution GPUs; leave third-party endpoints (Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure, OpenAI) and Tabnine-hosted inference or proxy options disabled.

Keep cluster metrics, logs and client telemetry inside the institution (air-gapped Prometheus/log aggregator, or confirmed-disabled telemetry to Tabnine) and block egress to Tabnine and third parties.

Keep the Jira connection disabled (it is off by default and team admins toggle it in the Admin UI) or connect only an institution-hosted Jira Data Center; confirm with Tabnine that this setting also governs the new Agent's built-in Jira access and the OpenCode-based CLI's Jira integration. Restrict MCP servers, native tools and repository connections through admin governance; connect only institution-hosted repositories.

For the OpenCode-based CLI: do not use session sharing (--share), which Tabnine docs do not list as an admin-governed control; check that users' existing OpenCode configs and MCP servers are not carried into Tabnine sessions; keep sign-in and updates pointed at the institution's Tabnine console.
residual_risks: Docs conflict on self-hosted telemetry: the privacy page says non-air-gapped clusters send metrics, logs and hashed user identifiers to Tabnine, while a v4.6.0 release note says this telemetry is optional and off by default.
Ownership changed (Tricentis, July 2026); contract terms, roadmap and long-term support for standalone private installations are not publicly documented.
Self-hosted open-weight models need multi-GPU H100/H200/B200-class servers and may be less capable than the frontier models offered on SaaS.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

The OpenCode-based CLI installs from and auto-updates against the organisation's Tabnine host (every 10 minutes while running; the Install page documents settings to turn auto-update off or redirect it), but docs do not state air-gapped support for it, and it reads users' existing OpenCode settings and MCP servers.

Jira: the integration page says establishing the Jira connection needs an internet connection and a browser, which conflicts with air-gapped use; docs do not say whether the admin Jira toggle governs the new Agent's and the CLI's built-in Jira access.

final_records.name: Tabby
final_records.deployment: self-hostable / cloud
final_records.model_backend: Tabby server: local models through its bundled llama.cpp (model registry), or HTTP connectors to self-hosted endpoints (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp) or remote provider APIs (docs name Claude and OpenAI). Pochi: BYOK OpenAI-compatible providers, including local Ollama or LM Studio, or Pochi-hosted models after account sign-in.
final_records.data_handling_note: Self-hosted Tabby with a local model, or Pochi in BYOK mode with a local model, keeps code and prompts on controlled infrastructure. Pochi BYOK needs no account and stores task history locally by default. Telemetry is on by default: the Tabby server and IDE extensions send non-code usage statistics (server and hardware info, completion counts and latency) under a random ID to app.tabbyml.com, and each can be disabled. The Tabby docs say this data is used only to improve Tabby, but the tabbyml.com Terms of Service (last modified 2024-11-05), which cover the self-hosted Software, state that TabbyML solely owns Usage Data and may use it for any legal purpose, including marketing (the clause adds that Usage Data is aggregated or masked before it is shared or publicly disclosed); the same terms say TabbyML has no access to information stored on a self-hosted instance. Pochi's extension source sends PostHog analytics only after a Pochi account sign-in (the signed-in user's email and name are attached). Remote model connectors fall under the chosen provider's own terms; Pochi-hosted models and Pochi cloud task storage leave this boundary and have no readable first-party retention or training terms. The tabbyml.com privacy policy (last modified 2024-11-11) covers only website visits and orders.

suitability_notes.personal: Use self-hosted Tabby or Pochi BYOK with a self-hosted model, and disable both server and extension usage collection. Assess any remote model API or Pochi cloud account separately.
suitability_notes.special: Only with self-hosted Tabby, or Pochi BYOK, using a local model on institution-controlled infrastructure (Ollama, if used, in local-only mode), with all telemetry disabled and no Pochi account, remote model API, web search or web fetch. Tabby's free Community plan covers up to 5 users; more users need Team or Enterprise. Tabby server has had no commits since 2026-06-30, so institutional security review must account for patching.

compliance: No compliance certification asserted in the first-party sources reviewed; self-hosted deployment
SSO, authentication domain and enforcement of IDE/extension telemetry policy are listed for Enterprise only (pricing comparison)
final_records.pricing: Community: free, open source, local deployment, up to 5 users. Team: $19/seat/month, up to 50 users, 'flexible deployment'. Enterprise: custom pricing, unlimited users. Tabby Cloud (Pochi): usage-based on LLM token cost, with $20 in free monthly credits. The pricing page still calls Pochi tab completion free, but Pochi docs say tab completion is switched off in current releases. A yearly-billing toggle shows annual plans that do not map to these tiers; they are not relied on here.
final_records.academic: Community self-hosted use is available; no separate academic entitlement is asserted.

final_records.notes: Two TabbyML products. Tabby is a self-hosted completion and chat server with no development activity since mid-2026: its latest stable release is v0.32.0 (2026-01-25), main has had no commits since 2026-06-30, and community PRs, including two opened in late October 2026, got no maintainer replies; no first-party announcement deprecates it. On main (not in v0.32.0), PR #4425 (2026-01-23) hard-disabled chat, Answer Engine search and Pages in the bundled web UI; the server-side code was not removed. Pochi, an Apache-2.0 VS Code agent and CLI, is under active development: VS Code extension releases run through 2026-11-04 (latest stable vscode@0.80.0, 2026-10-28), while the CLI's latest release is cli@0.6.21 (2026-08-10). Its tab completion has been switched off since July 2026. Keep Pochi BYOK/local-model use apart from the Pochi cloud account route. Licensing: Tabby is Apache-2.0 outside its ee/ directory; ee/ (including tabby-webserver and tabby-ui) is under the separate Tabby Enterprise licence, which ties production use to 'Tabby Subscription Terms of Service' at tabby.tabbyml.com/terms, a page that shows only the Apache-2.0 FOSS terms. A separate tabbyml.com Terms of Service (last modified 2024-11-05) governs the self-hosted Software, including Usage Data ownership and a restriction on using any release more than two versions older than the current one. Pochi is Apache-2.0. Third-party components keep their own licences.
final_records.tier_gate: self-hosted Tabby (Community up to 5 users; Team or Enterprise beyond) or Pochi BYOK, with a local model and telemetry off, for regulated data; a Pochi cloud account does not qualify

required_controls: Run the Tabby server on institution-controlled hardware with a local model (bundled llama.cpp, or a local Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp endpoint), or use Pochi in BYOK mode with a local Ollama or LM Studio model.

Point every Tabby model role (completion, chat and any embedding model) and every Pochi model setting at that local endpoint, keep no cloud provider API keys in server or client configuration or environment, and verify the effective server and client configuration after deployment and after each update.
Set TABBY_DISABLE_USAGE_COLLECTION=1 on the server and anonymousUsageTracking disable = true in every IDE extension config; both send usage data to app.tabbyml.com by default.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models. Keep Ollama bound to localhost or behind an allow list; Pochi's Ollama setup guide sets OLLAMA_ORIGINS='*' and itself warns about public exposure.
Do not configure remote model APIs, sign in to a Pochi account, use Pochi sharing or cloud task storage, or enable Answer Engine web search; do not use Pochi's webFetch tool or remote MCP servers.
Manage Tabby server and IDE-extension updates centrally instead of through unmanaged auto-update.
Block outbound network egress from servers and clients at host or network level, and test that the block holds.
residual_risks: Tabby server shows no development since 2026-06-30 (last stable release 2026-01-25). A request for private security reporting (issue #4528) was closed as not planned, private vulnerability reporting is disabled and the repository has no SECURITY.md, so patching and security review fall to the institution.
On Tabby's main branch, chat, Answer Engine search and Pages are hard-disabled in the bundled web UI (PR #4425, not in v0.32.0); future releases may drop these features.
Central enforcement of the IDE/extension telemetry policy is listed only for Enterprise; on Community and Team each client must be configured.
The Pochi agent runs commands, edits files, can fetch web URLs (webFetch tool) and can call local or remote MCP servers, any of which can move data outside the boundary.

Pochi source routes some auxiliary calls to the Pochi server regardless of the chat model: worktree branch-name generation sends the task prompt and attachments to the Pochi vendor with the user's Pochi credentials. On a signed-in client this leaves the boundary even when chat uses a local model; behaviour without sign-in was not tested.
Tabby usage data, if collection is left on, is owned by TabbyML under its Terms of Service and may be used for any legal purpose, including marketing.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a Tabby or Pochi setting that points at local Ollama does not by itself show that inference stays local.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Devin
final_records.deployment: Cloud. Devin Cloud runs the agent brain and Devbox in Cognition's multi-tenant cloud. Enterprise Customer Dedicated Deployment is a Cognition-hosted single-tenant VPC reached by AWS PrivateLink or IPSec; Enterprise Assured adds customer-managed AWS KMS keys. Devin Outposts (Pro, Max, Teams; off by default on dedicated tenants) executes commands on machines the customer operates or on partner platforms (e.g. Modal, Daytona, E2B, Cloudflare), while inference and planning stay in Devin's cloud. A separate Devin EU service (app.devin.eu, own accounts, including EU enterprise sites) is hosted in the EU, and Cognition says its AI model providers process content only in the EEA and Switzerland; some data (support, performance monitoring, billing/sales reporting) is stored or accessed outside the EEA, including by Cognition AI, Inc. and Datadog in the US under SCCs. It is documented only in Cognition's EU Privacy Notice (26 Oct 2026); which self-serve plans it offers and its contract terms are not published.
final_records.model_backend: Compound system operated by Cognition: Cognition SWE models (SWE-2 announced 10 Sep 2026 and in research preview in the agent selector since 21 Sep 2026) plus third-party models. The DPA (updated 21 Oct 2026) lists OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft/Azure and Google/Vertex as US model subprocessors; Databricks, xAI, Snowflake and Muse are listed only if enabled in Devin Desktop. Release notes (8 Apr 2026) also offer Cerebras as an optional enterprise inference provider, which the DPA list does not name. No customer LLM API keys; Pro, Max and Teams users can link a personal ChatGPT plan to pay for GPT usage. SWE-2 Flash (4 Nov 2026) is offered in Devin Desktop and CLI; Cognition says it is building a programme to share its weights with partners and researchers, which is not yet available.
final_records.data_handling_note: Platform terms (updated 30 Jun 2026) allow training on Customer Data by default, and only paid tiers can opt out (Teams: admin only). After opt-out, data is not used for training and ZDR is enabled with model providers; ZDR does not cover data flagged by abuse classifiers, safety/security/AUP review, or legal process. Enterprise terms: no training without prior written consent. Product-level retention remains: data processed through Devin is kept for the customer relationship, and the DPA retention period runs to 30 days after termination. Enterprise terms add a security exhibit with deletion within 90 days of a request or termination and audit logs kept at least one year; the self-serve platform terms only say Cognition may delete Customer Data at its option on termination. Feedback and interaction data are kept as Cognition decides. Memory (release notes, 9 Oct 2026) keeps per-user memory across sessions, refined nightly from recent sessions; it is personal and not shared with the organization; users and org admins can turn it off (enterprise admins can force it off), and nightly dreaming can be turned off separately (19 Oct 2026). Its retention period and training-opt-out coverage are not documented. Anonymised, aggregated Usage Data is collected; the DPA (21 Oct 2026) adds Tinybird (US) for analytics, and the US privacy policy (26 Oct 2026) discloses sharing identifiers, commercial information and network-activity information with advertising partners from Cognition's websites (opt-out via Privacy Choices or Global Privacy Control). Optional ChatGPT-plan linking sends GPT calls through the user's ChatGPT subscription; the docs do not say whether provider ZDR covers that route. Dedicated deployments and Outposts keep inference in Cognition Cloud.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-held Teams or Enterprise plan: Pro and Max are individual plans, and the Cognition DPA treats the contracting customer as data controller. On Teams an admin must opt out of training; Enterprise terms bar training without written consent. Keep ChatGPT-plan linking off, consider turning Memory off at org level, and rely on the Cognition DPA with an appropriate legal basis. Platform terms bar medical information and sensitive personal data such as birth dates; Enterprise terms bar protected health information and such data unless a separate written agreement permits it; the Acceptable Use Policy also bars special-category, biometric and government-ID data without a separate written agreement. DPA-listed subprocessors are in the US (one support subprocessor in India); EEA transfers rely on SCCs. EU institutions can ask about Devin EU (EU hosting, EEA/Swiss model processing, Cognition AI Labs Ireland as controller for account and usage data unless the organisation's agreement says otherwise; some support, monitoring and billing data still reaches US entities under SCCs), but its self-serve plans and contract terms are not published.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate: Cognition documents that inference and planning always run in its cloud, including Customer Dedicated Deployment and Outposts, and its Acceptable Use Policy prohibits uploading special-category data without a separate written agreement.

compliance: Cognition's Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2 and CCPA for the Cognition product (reports NDA-gated); ISO/IEC 27001:2022 appears only under the separate Cognition Public Sector product. The DPA states SOC 2 Type II.

DPA (updated 21 Oct 2026) incorporates EU SCCs (Modules 2 and 3) and the UK Addendum; listed subprocessors are US-based, plus one support subprocessor in India; new subprocessors are notified 15 days in advance.
Signed DPA and exact service/model scope require confirmation.
final_records.pricing: Free plan (Devin Cloud access unclear: the pricing page lists cloud agents from Pro upward, while billing docs say Free includes limited Devin usage); Pro $20/month; Max $200/month; Teams for up to 200 users with $40/month full seats and free flex seats that draw on shared on-demand credits. Teams wording conflicts: the pricing page reads “$80/month for team plan + $40/mo per full dev seat”, while billing docs describe $80/month as a minimum met by full seats and/or prepaid credits (two full seats = $80); confirm at checkout. Usage beyond quota is bought as on-demand credits at API pricing. Enterprise: contractual ACU pricing.
final_records.academic: No academic or student discount program documented.

Customer Dedicated Deployment is vendor-hosted, not customer-controlled on-prem. Outposts (introduced July 2026) lets sessions execute on a lab or institutional machine, but inference stays in Cognition's cloud, so it does not change the special-category classification; nor does the EU-hosted Devin EU service. The air-gapped build with customer-hosted model endpoints (federal docs, beta) covers Devin Desktop and the CLI only, not Devin Cloud. The local Devin Desktop IDE has its own catalog entry.

residual_risks: Inference and planning always run in Cognition's cloud, including Customer Dedicated Deployment and Outposts; Outposts moves only command execution to customer-operated or partner machines.

Cognition's Acceptable Use Policy prohibits uploading special-category data and regulated health information without a separate written agreement; the DPA records that the customer does not intend to submit such data, and Cognition assumes no additional obligations for it beyond the DPA security measures.

final_records.name: Replit Agent
final_records.deployment: cloud (Replit platform hosted primarily on Google Cloud in the US, with an opt-in India hosting region; Agent inference via third-party AI model providers; Enterprise can restrict published-app deployment geography). No Enterprise option is documented as customer-controlled for inference: sales-assisted single-tenant and private networking options are vendor-managed; Bring Your Own Cloud (announced October 16, 2026): Full BYOC (private preview) runs the Replit cell, including the Agent harness, in the customer's cloud tenant under Replit management while the control plane stays outside and model inference remains in Replit's managed Agent offering; BYOC for Published Apps (early access, Replit-operated in the customer tenant) and Image Exports (early access, deployed and operated by the customer's own team) cover published apps only, with development and Agent remaining on Replit-managed infrastructure. The Replit Desktop App (Windows, Mac, Linux) mirrors the web experience; local builds on Windows are a private preview, and no local model inference is documented.
final_records.model_backend: Replit-managed multi-provider stack with intelligent model routing across Free, Power and Max modes. The Agent's own model cannot be swapped (BYOK applies only to models an app calls, not to Agent). Agent uses third-party models: the subprocessor list names Anthropic, OpenAI and Google for AI models, and its AI-infrastructure entries include Baseten, Fireworks AI and Parallel Web Systems. Enterprise model settings also list DeepSeek, Kimi and Z.ai; open-source model providers are off by default. The model catalog changes frequently.
final_records.data_handling_note: Plan-specific. Starter/Core (Terms of Service): Replit's model-improvement page says prompts, instructions, context and generated responses are used to develop and improve its models and AI features, and the Privacy Policy (last updated October 21, 2026) names improving its machine-learning technologies such as code generation as a legitimate interest; no opt-out is documented for these plans. Pro (Pro Agreement C.2.c): Customer Content may be used to train models and AI features by default; the opt-out in Settings > Personalization covers new content only, deletes nothing, and leaves Replit's licence to use Customer Content to improve the Platform in place. Enterprise (Enterprise Agreement, last updated September 9, 2026, B.2.g): Replit will not use Customer Content to improve products or train machine-learning models except as expressly permitted in that agreement; the B.2.c licence still covers troubleshooting, improving and securing the Platform. No fixed product retention period is published; Enterprise prompt text is retained and retrievable through the Compliance API, and Enterprise audit logs are kept 30 days by default; the DPA allows a return or deletion request up to 90 days after termination, except where law requires retention. De-identified Usage Data may be used and shared with third parties; the Privacy Policy also allows disclosure to advertising partners (a possible 'sale or sharing', with an opt-out link). No zero-data-retention commitment covers Agent itself: the ZDR-only rule documented for Enterprise applies to OpenRouter models that apps call through Replit AI Integrations. All Agent inference is cloud-based: Replit's managed stack calls third-party model providers (the subprocessor list names Anthropic, OpenAI and Google for AI models and Fireworks AI and Baseten as AI infrastructure, all US).

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Starter/Core content feeds model improvement with no documented opt-out. For unpublished code or data, use Pro with the model-improvement opt-out set, or Enterprise.
suitability_notes.personal: Only through Enterprise (self-serve or sales-assisted) under the Enterprise Agreement and DPA, with admin controls set (approved model providers, private deployments, deployment geography) and review of retention and connected third-party services. Enterprise model controls are enabled through Replit sales, and at least one model from each of OpenAI, Anthropic and Google must remain enabled, so these three providers cannot be switched off. Pro's opt-out is an account setting, not the Enterprise contractual no-training term.
suitability_notes.special: Agent inference runs in vendor cloud (Replit's platform plus third-party AI model providers); Replit states the Agent model cannot be swapped, and its BYOC documentation says model inference stays in Replit's managed Agent offering even when the Agent harness runs in the customer's tenant. No local, self-hosted or customer-controlled inference route is documented, so it does not qualify under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: Replit states SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliance and says it is working toward ISO 27001; audit reports sit in the Trust Center and were not reviewed.
Enterprise Agreement (no-training term) and DPA (referenced by the Pro and Enterprise agreements; SCCs for international transfers) must be confirmed for the exact Replit plan.
No HIPAA/BAA offering found in the reviewed first-party sources.
final_records.pricing: Starter: free, with daily Agent credits up to a monthly cap, Lite build only (Full build, Plan Mode and connectors need Core) and one published app that goes down after 30 days. Core: $20/month, or $18/month billed annually. Pro: displayed at $100/month, or $90/month billed annually (base tier; larger credit tiers exist). Core and Pro include a Free Mode allowance and monthly credits; Power/Max modes, publishing and cloud resources draw on credits with effort-based pricing. Enterprise: self-serve (pay-as-you-go or annual credit commitment) or custom via sales. Prices exclude tax; confirm at checkout.
final_records.academic: Replit for Education (replit.com/edu) advertises free access for verified educators at approved schools and 50% off Core for students with a .edu email; eligibility depends on an approved school-domain list, to which institutions can request addition. Terms and data handling for education accounts are not documented, and education access does not give the Enterprise no-training term.

final_records.notes: Agent 4 launched in March 2026. Since August 2026, Agent work runs in Free, Power or Max mode with intelligent model routing, inside a wider Replit platform (Chat, Design, Routines, and inline data charts from Atta, whose acquisition was announced September 25, 2026). New OpenAI and Anthropic models were added from late September through October 2026, so model identities should not be frozen. October 2026 additions: Bring Your Own Cloud options for Enterprise (October 16), a Windows local-build preview of Replit Desktop (October 9), a Monitoring Agent that can triage production alerts (October 23), and Enterprise Cloud Agents that open GitHub or GitLab pull requests (October 30); Replit now markets its enterprise offer as 'Replit for Business'. Enterprise admins can restrict providers and models, require private deployments, set deployment geography and stream audit logs (30-day default audit-log retention). Scope note: kept for research coding use, although Replit now positions itself as a platform to create, launch and grow apps, sites, tools and businesses.
final_records.tier_gate: Enterprise (self-serve or sales-assisted) with Enterprise Agreement + DPA; Pro opt-out is not equivalent; Starter/Core not for personal data

residual_risks: The Agent model cannot be swapped and is served through Replit's managed stack and third-party AI subprocessors (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, AI-infrastructure providers); no local, self-hosted or customer-controlled inference endpoint is documented.

Full BYOC (private preview) places the Replit cell and Agent harness in the customer's cloud tenant, but Replit operates it, the control plane stays outside the tenant and model inference remains Replit-managed; Replit states it is not an air-gapped or entirely self-hosted installation.
Sales-assisted single-tenant and private networking options are vendor-managed and not documented as customer-controlled infrastructure.

final_records.name: OpenHands
final_records.deployment: local (Agent Canvas via npm/npx or Docker; desktop app preview build for macOS, Windows and Linux) / self-hosted (VM, Docker, Kubernetes Helm) / OpenHands Cloud SaaS / third-party cloud backends: DigitalOcean Managed Agents (Providers tab in the desktop app, v1.27.0+, or web build with MARS_WEB=1) and a documented self-deployed Agent Server on Modal / OpenHands Enterprise (self-hosted on-premises, private cloud or VPC via Replicated VM or Helm install; Docker Compose stack for evaluation; docs also mention managed deployment options)
final_records.model_backend: BYO key for LiteLLM-supported providers or a custom base URL (OpenAI-compatible endpoints); documented local model servers (LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang); OpenHands LLM provider via a Cloud account at provider rates. Agent Canvas can also run third-party ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode), which use their own providers and terms.
final_records.data_handling_note: Self-hosted Agent Canvas/Agent Server with a local model keeps code, prompts and conversation history on your machines. Outbound traffic then comes from optional integrations, MCP servers, ACP agents, cloud backends and product telemetry. Agent Canvas asks for analytics consent but sends one anonymous install event before consent unless telemetry is disabled (AGENT_CANVAS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or --disable-telemetry, since v1.17.0). The launcher and Docker image also pre-configure consent-gated PostHog telemetry for the automation and agent-server services unless VITE_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 / DO_NOT_TRACK=1 is set. OpenHands Cloud: the privacy policy (effective 3 Sep 2025, unchanged on 6 Nov 2026) allows All Hands AI to use content and feedback to train and tune its models, shares content with third-party AI providers, keeps data as long as reasonably necessary, and documents no training opt-out. Using the OpenHands LLM provider routes prompts through All Hands AI's LLM proxy. OpenHands Enterprise (self-hosted): the docs say code and conversations stay on customer infrastructure, but the same docs list periodic usage metrics for licence compliance, a Replicated licence-verification component and required outbound access to vendor endpoints; the Docker Compose evaluation stack sends PostHog analytics (first admin's work email, company and organisation names, automation names) unless ENABLE_POSTHOG_ANALYTICS=false and an empty POSTHOG_CLIENT_KEY are set. The chosen LLM provider's and any cloud backend's terms also apply.

suitability_notes.personal: Do not use OpenHands Cloud for personal data: its privacy policy allows training on content and documents no opt-out. Self-host with a local model, or use self-hosted Enterprise with an LLM provider covered by an appropriate contract/DPA; check every ACP agent, cloud backend (DigitalOcean Managed Agents, an Agent Server deployed on Modal), MCP server and integration you enable.
suitability_notes.special: Only self-hosted open-source Agent Canvas/Agent Server on institution-controlled infrastructure with a local model server (Ollama only in local-only mode), all product telemetry disabled and no cloud LLM, no OpenHands Cloud or DigitalOcean Managed Agents backend, no Agent Server deployed on Modal, and no third-party ACP agent. Self-hosted OpenHands Enterprise needs extra checks: its documented installs have licence verification, periodic usage metrics to the vendor, required outbound vendor endpoints and (Docker Compose stack) default PostHog analytics, and no air-gapped install is documented. Confirm in the contract what leaves the environment before any special-category use. Cloud OpenHands and cloud LLM routes are not acceptable.

compliance: Customer-operated deployment is distinct from OpenHands Cloud and Enterprise licensing.

Enterprise docs state that self-hosted code and conversations stay on customer infrastructure ('Nothing leaves your environment'), but the same docs list periodic usage metrics for licence compliance, required outbound vendor endpoints and, for the Docker Compose stack, default PostHog analytics; none of these covers the selected LLM provider.
No certification confirmed from first-party sources; the linked Vanta trust centre is not machine-readable (checked 2026-11-06).
final_records.pricing: Agent Canvas (open source, self-hosted): free. Teams (self-hosted): $500/month for up to 10 users (+$50/month per extra seat), 30-day trial, capped at 5,000 sessions per month. Enterprise: custom pricing, unlimited seats. OpenHands Cloud (hosted) is still documented as an Agent Canvas backend but has no published plan or price on the pricing page (checked 2026-11-06); OpenHands LLM provider credits are billed at provider rates with no markup, and two OpenHands-provided models are free only when run through OpenHands Cloud. Enterprise self-hosting without a commercial licence is limited to 30 days per calendar year (PolyForm Free Trial).
final_records.academic: No academic discount on the pricing or Enterprise pages (checked 2026-11-06); the self-hosted open-source Agent Canvas is free.

software engineering automation
agentic task execution
scheduled and event-driven automations
CI/CD integration
data analysis
final_records.notes: The OpenHands/OpenHands repository is Agent Canvas (MIT), a self-hosted control centre that runs the OpenHands agent from the MIT Software Agent SDK and can also drive third-party ACP agents; the README 'beta' badge was removed in v1.33.0, while the desktop app remains a preview build (macOS app not yet signed or notarised). The docs now state that the OpenHands CLI is no longer actively maintained and that the legacy local GUI is deprecated; the OpenHands/legacy snapshot is archived. Enterprise code (OpenHands/enterprise) is under the PolyForm Free Trial License 1.0.0, i.e. source-available, not open source. Active: 14 releases from v1.27.0 (12 Oct 2026) to v1.37.0 (6 Nov 2026). Check the licence of each repository you deploy.
final_records.tier_gate: personal data: self-hosted with a local model, or self-hosted Enterprise with a DPA-covered LLM provider (not OpenHands Cloud); special-category: self-hosted MIT Agent Canvas/Agent Server + local model + all telemetry off, no ACP agents, no OpenHands Cloud or DigitalOcean backend, no Modal-hosted Agent Server

required_controls: Self-host the open-source Agent Canvas/Agent Server (local, Docker, VM or Kubernetes) on infrastructure the institution controls; do not add an OpenHands Cloud, OpenHands Enterprise SaaS or DigitalOcean Managed Agents backend (the desktop app includes a DigitalOcean Providers tab), and do not deploy the Agent Server on Modal.

If OpenHands Enterprise is used instead: its documented installs include Replicated licence verification, periodic usage metrics and required outbound vendor endpoints; the Docker Compose stack sends PostHog analytics unless ENABLE_POSTHOG_ANALYTICS=false and POSTHOG_CLIENT_KEY is empty; no air-gapped install is documented. Obtain contractual confirmation of what is sent and restrict egress before special-category use.
Configure only a local model server (e.g. LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang) on that infrastructure; no cloud LLM provider and no OpenHands LLM provider.
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Use the built-in OpenHands agent only; do not enable third-party ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode), which run their vendors' CLIs with their own LLM, tools and terms and automatically reuse any provider login stored on the host.

Disable product telemetry: AGENT_CANVAS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or --disable-telemetry for the Canvas frontend; VITE_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 so the launcher/Docker image do not set the default automation PostHog key; DO_NOT_TRACK=1 for Agent Server; and decline analytics consent.
Keep listeners on loopback or behind a strong LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY plus network access control; prefer the Docker sandbox runtime.
Enable only integrations and MCP servers that stay inside the institutional boundary; enforce egress filtering.

Deny or disable built-in web browsing, search and fetch tools; disable or centrally manage auto-update and version checks; point every model role at the local model server and keep no cloud API keys in the environment or .env; verify the effective configuration; block egress at host or network level and verify it.
residual_risks: The agent executes shell commands with filesystem and network access; the no-sandbox install gives it full access to the host filesystem.
Conversation history, settings, secrets and optional completion logs (full prompts) persist on local disk and need institutional access and retention controls.
Telemetry is controlled separately for the Canvas frontend, the Agent Server and the automation service; verify actual egress after each upgrade.
Self-hosted Enterprise sends licence/usage metrics to the vendor; their content is not documented publicly.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost model URL alone does not guarantee local inference.

The OpenHands local-LLM guide's Ollama example binds the server to 0.0.0.0 and its LM Studio steps enable 'Serve on Local Network', exposing the model endpoint to the network unless host firewalling or a loopback bind is used.
Local models can have limited functionality compared with frontier cloud models, which may push users toward cloud routes.
Frequent releases (14 between 12 Oct and 6 Nov 2026) and the desktop app's preview status mean configuration must be re-checked after updates.

final_records.name: Jupyter AI
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: No agent ships by default. Built-in ACP personas (jupyter-ai-acp-client 0.3.x): Claude, Codex, Copilot, Goose, Kilo, Kiro, Mistral Vibe and OpenCode; each uses its own authentication, model configuration and data terms. The optional, experimental Jupyternaut persona and the optional %%ai magics call models through LiteLLM; the docs describe a local Ollama route (default 127.0.0.1:11434) and, for Jupyternaut, a self-hosted vLLM route. Customer-controlled inference needs that route or a separately reviewed local-capable ACP agent.
final_records.data_handling_note: Jupyter AI routes notebook context, attachments and tool calls to the selected persona; the ACP agent or Jupyternaut's model provider then applies its own retention and training terms. A local Jupyter server does not keep data local if the persona uses a cloud model. Chats are saved as .chat files in the workspace; Jupyternaut's persistent memory (local SQLite) is opt-in. The ACP client emits operational events to Jupyter Server's EventLogger, which records them only where an operator registers handlers; the code describes them as free of customer content and PII, though failure events carry error messages. Project Jupyter's policy says telemetry is opt-in and does not cover third-party hosted Jupyter.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-controlled model route (Jupyternaut with local Ollama or self-hosted vLLM, or a reviewed ACP agent with such inference), or separately approve the complete agent/provider route. Local JupyterLab alone does not keep notebook context local.
suitability_notes.special: Requires JupyterLab on institution-controlled infrastructure with local inference (experimental Jupyternaut with local Ollama/vLLM, or a separately reviewed local-capable ACP agent), isolated notebook execution and approved MCP integrations; a local notebook UI with a cloud agent does not qualify.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free and open source (BSD-3-Clause); costs come only from any connected agent subscription or cloud model provider
final_records.academic: free
use_cases: data analysis
coding
notebook AI assistant
agentic workflows in notebooks
multi-agent collaboration
final_records.notes: Notebook chat host for separately installed ACP coding agents, plus an optional experimental Jupyternaut persona whose future is under maintainer review (jupyter-ai#1618). Where context goes is set by the connected agent or model provider, wherever the notebook runs. v3.2.0 (3 Sep 2026) made real-time collaboration optional and fixed frontend tool calls running in every connected browser.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local model (Jupyternaut via local Ollama with cloud disabled or self-hosted vLLM, or a reviewed local-capable ACP agent), no cloud ACP agents or providers installed, no off-site event handlers, egress blocked for special-category data; DPA-covered agent/model provider for personal data

required_controls: Run JupyterLab on institution-controlled infrastructure with local inference only: the optional Jupyternaut persona pointed at a local Ollama/vLLM server, or a separately reviewed ACP agent configured for local models. Do not install cloud-backed ACP agents or providers; restrict Jupyternaut with JupyternautExtension.allowed_providers/allowed_models (the docs still show the older AiExtension prefix).

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Set LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True for Jupyternaut and magics, so LiteLLM does not fetch its model cost map from GitHub at import.

Keep Jupyter AI at v3.2.0 or later (frontend tool calls limited to the requesting browser; MCP server Host/Origin protection on by default), review .jupyter/mcp_settings.json, require tool-permission prompts, and isolate notebook execution.
residual_risks: Jupyternaut is documented as experimental, its docs are flagged out of date, and its future is under discussion; the ACP route depends on each agent's own local-model support and policies.

An institution-hosted Ollama/vLLM endpoint reached via api_base needs a separate network and access review; other outbound behaviour of LiteLLM and its dependencies beyond the cost-map fetch was not reviewed, so air-gapped operation is unverified.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

Chat files, opt-in Jupyternaut memory, Jupyternaut API keys saved to a .env file, logs, tools and MCP integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls, especially on shared JupyterHub servers.

final_records.name: Julius AI
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Julius models (default): Lite on all plans, the standard and Max variants on paid plans, Ultra on the Max plan and above (Model Selector docs). Julius states that it does not build its own AI models (docs, security page), and the changelog says Claude Fable 5.1 powers the updated Julius Ultra model (2026-09-09). Third-party general models from OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Meta and Moonshot AI (docs: paid plans); the pricing comparison table instead lists one named OpenAI and one Anthropic model for Plus, Pro and Business and 'All models' only for Enterprise, and the pricing cards name an OpenAI model that the docs and changelog do not list. Image generation uses an OpenAI image model; video generation supports a Seedance model (changelog 2026-08-07); the text-to-speech provider is not named. The lineup changes often (replacements on 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-29 and an addition on 2026-10-01; no changelog entries after 2026-10-01). The public subprocessor list names Anthropic and OpenAI but not xAI, Meta, Moonshot AI or the video-model provider.
final_records.data_handling_note: Changed in October 2026: the privacy policy (updated 2026-10-21, s.4) lets Julius disclose information to 'AI technology providers' (developers of AI models and AI research organisations) for their own use in evaluating, improving and developing their products, and the ToS (updated 2026-10-20) licence over user content explicitly includes sharing it with third-party AI technology providers to develop and improve AI models. The docs and security page now say Julius does not build its own AI models and may share prompts, uploaded files and outputs with AI technology providers to improve their models; the earlier 'never used to train' statement and the claim that providers are contractually bound not to train are gone. Opt-out is by email to privacy@julius.ai (privacy policy, 'Opting Out of AI Data Sharing', placed under the California-residents section); there is no documented in-product setting, and whether the opt-out also limits the ToS licence is not stated. The privacy policy (s.3) still says personal information is not used to train Julius's own models. The ToS also lets Julius use inputs and outputs to maintain, improve, modify and develop its AI features, 'notwithstanding' any other agreement, and says the terms of an executed DPA apply to customer personal data processed on the customer's behalf (DPA text not public; the former public DPA URL returns 404; the privacy policy no longer mentions standard contractual clauses). Location: the security page says all data is stored and processed in the US; the privacy policy (s.10) allows personal information to be transferred to and stored in other countries by service providers. Listed subprocessors include AWS and Google Cloud (user storage), E2B (code sandbox; may process or store workspace content), Raindrop (customer prompts, AI responses, agent traces), and PostHog and Sentry; the AI technology providers that receive content for their own model development are not named. Retention: Free-plan files are deleted after 1 h of inactivity and paid-plan files after 7 days of inactivity (Files docs); the pricing table now shows 7-day file storage for Plus, Pro and Business and permanent file storage only for Enterprise; containers spin down after 1 h of inactivity. The privacy policy says Julius will delete information accessible to it within seven business days of an account-cancellation and deletion request (s.8) and allows longer retention for service, business, legal and compliance purposes (s.11); the docs state there is no published backup-deletion deadline. The privacy policy asks users not to submit health, biometric or genetic data. No public HIPAA BAA or product-level ZDR is documented.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: By default, prompts, uploaded files and outputs may be shared with AI technology providers for their own model development; send the email opt-out before uploading unpublished or confidential research data.
suitability_notes.personal: Use only after both (1) a written, confirmed opt-out from sharing content with AI technology providers (email privacy@julius.ai; confirm that it applies outside California, covers every account in the workspace and limits the ToS licence) and (2) an executed institutional DPA that excludes provider model development, overrides the ToS licence and AI-feature improvement clause, and covers processing locations and international transfers, the listed subprocessors (including Raindrop, which receives prompts, AI responses and agent traces), retention and deletion. DPA text and plan eligibility are not public; confirm with the vendor. Do not publish artifacts or share conversation replay links; anyone with such a link can view them. Without both controls, personal data is not appropriate.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only service: inference, code execution and storage run on vendor and third-party infrastructure (US per the security page; the privacy policy permits transfers to service providers in other countries); by default content may be shared with AI technology providers for their model development; no self-hosted, on-premises or customer-controlled deployment is documented, and the privacy policy asks users not to submit health, biometric or genetic data. Not appropriate under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: SOC 2 Type II stated on the security and pricing pages; trust centre shows SOC 2 Type 2 as compliant with the final report available on request (restricted); verify scope before procurement

TX-RAMP stated on the security page (level not stated there); the trust centre lists a public 'TX-RAMP Level 2 Certification' document (not opened); Texas state programme, not relevant to GDPR or health-data approval
final_records.pricing: Free (75 one-time welcome credits plus 25 daily credits). Monthly / annual-billed per-month prices on the pricing page: Plus $20/$16 (2,000 credits/month); Pro $45/$37 (5,000); Max $200/$166 (25,000); Ultra $500/$416 (70,000); Business $450/$375 (60,000, up to 50 members); Growth 1-4 $750/$625, $1,400/$1,166, $2,500/$2,083, $5,000/$4,166 (100,000-850,000 credits); Enterprise custom. Max and Ultra are credit levels under the Pro card and Growth levels under the Business card. Paid plans also get 100 daily credits; purchased credits do not roll over and top-ups are not offered.
final_records.academic: The help docs state that Julius does not offer new student or academic discounts (existing student discounts carry over on plan changes). The docs describe redeeming institutional codes supplied by an instructor or workplace; their terms are not public.

database querying (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Supabase)

final_records.notes: Cloud AI workspace (data analysis with Python/R plus presentations, reports, websites, images and video). Since 2026-10-20/21 the ToS and privacy policy let Julius share user content with AI technology providers for their own model development by default, with an email opt-out; the earlier no-training commitment is withdrawn. Other material boundaries: US processing and storage per the security page (the privacy policy permits transfers to service providers in other countries); the ToS allows inputs/outputs to be used to improve AI features; a listed observability subprocessor receives prompts, AI responses and agent traces; paid-plan files persist up to 7 days of inactivity (permanent storage on Enterprise); published artifacts and conversation replay links are viewable by anyone with the link. A DPA is referenced in the ToS, but no public DPA text or HIPAA BAA was found.
final_records.tier_gate: Personal data only after a confirmed email opt-out from AI-provider data sharing and an executed DPA (referenced in the ToS; text and plan eligibility not public, so confirm with the vendor). Enterprise (custom) adds SSO, audit logging and fine-grained RBAC (pricing FAQ; the comparison table shows audit logs and SSO only under Enterprise) and is the only tier listed with permanent file storage. Verify the opt-out scope, the ToS licence and improvement-use clause, and retention in the contract.

residual_risks: Cloud-only: inference, code execution and storage run on vendor and third-party infrastructure (US per the security page; the privacy policy permits transfers to other countries), outside customer-controlled infrastructure.
By default, user content may be shared with unnamed AI technology providers for their own model development (privacy policy s.4, ToS licence); opt-out is by email only.
Prompts and outputs pass to multiple third-party model providers and subprocessors, including an observability service that receives prompts, AI responses and agent traces.
The privacy policy asks users not to submit health, biometric or genetic data; no public HIPAA BAA or self-hosted option is documented.

final_records.name: Hex
final_records.deployment: cloud (Hex-operated on AWS: US multi-tenant; EU multi-tenant on Team by contract or on Enterprise; HIPAA and single-tenant stacks as Enterprise add-ons, still run by Hex)
final_records.model_backend: Hosted Anthropic and OpenAI models by default; models Hex hosts itself (e.g. Kimi 2.7, on US infrastructure; Hex names Baseten for hosting certain features) and Hex-run typeahead models; the subprocessor list (last modified 2026-08-04) names Anthropic, Baseten, Google, Modal, OpenAI and Parallel as AI services. Grok 4.6 was added to the model picker on 2026-09-23; its serving route is not documented and the subprocessor list has no xAI entry. Fable 5.1 is offered only on multi-tenant and non-EU, non-HIPAA single-tenant stacks. Enterprise BYOK: Anthropic or OpenAI direct, or Claude models via AWS Bedrock or Google GEAP, optionally through a wire-compatible gateway (BYOK model list dated 2026-10-14 covers Claude and GPT models only).
final_records.data_handling_note: Self-serve plans (Community, Professional, Team not under an Order Form; ToS last modified 2026-05-14): unless the customer opts out in Settings > AI & agents, Hex may use AI inputs and outputs to develop, improve and evaluate its services. Enterprise (Hex Service Agreement for Order Forms from 2026-06-24): neither Hex nor its AI providers use Customer Data to train, improve or develop AI models, except models kept for that customer only; the previous Enterprise version (Feb 2025 to Jun 2026) only excluded training models offered to other parties. Hex's FAQ adds that staff may review AI prompts and related project data when needed to fix bugs or improve AI features. LLM providers do not train and run under zero data retention by default; an Admin toggle enables models that require provider safety retention (Anthropic: 30 days for Fable 5; Fable 5.1, added 2026-09-23, also needs the toggle). Product-level storage is separate: prompts carry project code, cell outputs, schema and table/column names; cell outputs are stored indefinitely unless custom retention (7-90 days, select Enterprise plans) is enabled, and backups are kept 30 days even then; schema embeddings (OpenAI Ada) sit in a vector database on Hex infrastructure. The subprocessor list gives Anthropic's processing location as USA, not the deployment region. BYOK (Enterprise) reroutes third-party inference only: typeahead still runs on Hex-run models, and Hex-hosted models such as Kimi are unavailable while BYOK is on.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Team or Enterprise with the DPA (EU/UK/Swiss transfers rely on Hex's Data Privacy Framework certification, with SCCs as fallback) and the EU stack where residency matters (Team: by contract). The EU stack does not keep all AI processing in the EU: the subprocessor list gives Anthropic and Parallel processing as USA, and Kimi runs on US infrastructure. On self-serve plans switch off AI-session improvement use, which is on by default; Enterprise Order Forms from 2026-06-24 exclude it contractually (check which agreement version an older contract uses). Keep 'Allow data retention for specific models' off, mark connections holding personal data as Sensitive (this governs Slack, MCP, API and CLI access only; MCP/API/CLI access to them is off by default), and consider turning off 'Allow agent web search' (the subprocessor list also names Browserbase, USA, for browser automation). Governed mode only steers the agent's choice of sources and is not an access control; restrict personal data with connection and warehouse permissions. Confirm with Hex how Grok 4.6 and Kimi 2.7 are covered by the subprocessor list and DPA before personal data reaches them.
suitability_notes.special: Every documented route, including the HIPAA add-on, single-tenant and BYOK, keeps processing on Hex-operated cloud, with inference at third-party or Hex-hosted model providers (under BYOK, Claude can be served from the customer's Bedrock/GEAP account, but typeahead, storage and orchestration stay with Hex). The DPA lists no permitted sensitive-data categories unless agreed in writing, and the terms treat genetic data and health data outside a BAA as At-Risk Data at the customer's risk. A BAA does not create a customer-controlled boundary, so Hex does not qualify under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: SOC 2 Type II and annual HIPAA audit stated by Hex; Trust Center shows SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, PCI, GDPR, CCPA and EU-US/UK-US/Swiss-US Data Privacy Framework badges, and on 2026-10-21 announced SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA audit reports for 1 Oct 2025 - 30 Sep 2026 (reports access-gated)
HIPAA (US customers): PHI only after a BAA and, on Enterprise, a HIPAA environment on the order form; Hex states a BAA with its LLM providers
GDPR DPA (last modified 2026-06-01): EU/UK/Swiss transfers rely on Hex's Data Privacy Framework certification, with SCCs as fallback; current contract, deployment and add-on scope must be checked
final_records.pricing: Community (free) - Professional ($36/editor/month) - Team ($75/editor/month, 14-day free trial) - Enterprise (custom). AI use is metered in credits: monthly per-seat grants (Community 5, Professional 30, Team editor 40 / explorer 10; Enterprise per order form) plus purchasable add-on credits. Academic: Professional plan free for students and educators at universities and bootcamps (contact support@hex.tech); discounted program for qualified non-profits.
final_records.academic: Students and educators at universities and bootcamps can get the Professional plan free (contact support@hex.tech). Professional runs under the self-serve terms, so the AI-session improvement opt-out has to be set; verify eligibility and terms with Hex.
use_cases: collaborative data analysis
SQL/Python notebooks
AI-assisted code and query generation
data app publishing
warehouse-native analytics
final_records.notes: Collaborative cloud analytics platform, now titled 'The Analytics platform for humans and agents' (FAQ still says 'AI Analytics Platform'). Hex documents that its AI features were formerly called Hex Magic; the agent suite covers the Notebook Agent, Threads, Chat with App, the Modeling Agent and Generative apps (available on all plans). The Hex agent is on Professional and above, with a trial on Community; per-feature availability varies by plan. Since October: Hex 4.0 announced on 2026-10-27 together with a $100m fundraise (private beta; code-defined projects that the Hex agent and external agents such as Claude, Codex or Cursor edit via the Hex MCP server), Governed mode on 2026-10-30 (steers which tables, semantic models and projects the agent uses; Hex states it is not a security boundary), and Enterprise API/MCP/CLI access to agent usage and credit data (2026-10-22). Earlier: six models added on 2026-09-23 (including Grok 4.6 and Fable 5.1), a 'Skip approvals' agent mode (2026-09-15) and project create/edit via the Hex MCP server. Provider ZDR does not mean Hex deletes or never uses AI-session data; plan terms, opt-out and contract scope must be checked.
final_records.tier_gate: Team/Enterprise + DPA, AI-session improvement opt-out (self-serve plans) and appropriate data stack

residual_risks: The documented route uses vendor/cloud inference or control-plane processing outside customer-controlled infrastructure; it does not qualify under this catalog’s special-category rule.

Hex's terms (self-serve ToS s7.3b; Enterprise agreement s7.3.3) treat genetic data and health-related data not governed by a BAA as At-Risk Data at the customer's risk, and DPA Annex 1 lists no permitted sensitive-data categories unless provided in writing.
The subprocessor list (last modified 2026-08-04, rechecked 2026-11-06) gives USA as Anthropic's location of processing, so an EU-stack workspace still sends Anthropic-model inference to the USA.

final_records.name: Kiro
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Amazon Bedrock-hosted models chosen in Kiro: the Auto router, Anthropic Claude models, OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna (generally available since Oct 2026; Global inference scope) and open-weight models (e.g., Kimi K3, DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Qwen; DeepSeek 3.2, MiniMax M2.1 and Qwen3 Coder Next remain Experimental). Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available to Enterprise organizations only, served from us-east-1 only. Kimi K3 is US-geography only and a Kiro Excluded Model (AWS output indemnity does not apply). Fable 5.1 and Kimi K3 are unavailable until an administrator approves them. The list and credit multipliers change; AWS GovCloud (US) has a separate catalog. No local or customer-hosted model endpoint is documented.
final_records.data_handling_note: Free Tier and individual subscribers (paid accounts using GitHub/Google social login or AWS Builder ID): content may be used for service improvement, including model training, and client telemetry is collected unless opted out (IDE, CLI and Web each have their own opt-out); their content is stored in us-east-1, and Free Tier inputs may also be kept up to 60 days for abuse detection. Enterprise users (IAM Identity Center, Okta or Microsoft Entra ID): content is not used for service improvement and users are auto-opted out of telemetry/content collection (administrators control user-activity telemetry); content may be stored in the profile Region (commercial: us-east-1 or eu-central-1) to operate the service, and admin-enabled IDE/CLI prompt logs and activity reports go to a customer-selected S3 bucket. IDE client telemetry goes to an endpoint in the profile's Region (dropped if none exists there). Cloud sessions (Kiro Web/Mobile, kiro-cli --cloud) keep conversation history, repositories and sandbox files in the cloud, in us-east-1 only for Identity Center organizations; Kiro Web data-collection preferences are set by each user. All users: operational signals may be collected and Bedrock abuse detection applies; OpenAI GPT classifier-flagged traffic is kept up to 30 days; all Claude Fable 5.1 traffic (Enterprise only) is kept up to 30 days, and AWS may review classifier-flagged traffic by hand. Inference Region can differ from storage Region. Local IDE/CLI/Crew execution does not make inference local.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a Kiro Enterprise profile under institutional AWS terms; paid social-login, Builder ID and Students accounts are not the Enterprise route. New profiles are offered credit pooling only, which requires IAM Identity Center (an external IdP can be synced into it). For EU data, use a Frankfurt profile. Model governance is off by default: every model except Claude Fable 5.1 and Kimi K3 is allowed, including newly added ones. Turn it on and approve only Geography-scope models available in the EU (GPT-5.6 is Global; Fable 5.1 runs in us-east-1 only with all traffic retained up to 30 days; Kimi K3 is US-only and lacks output indemnity). If the approved list must bind, block Auto and set an approved default model (Auto can route to Active models outside the list). Whether automatic model fallback in local V3 sessions respects the approved list is not documented. Keep Cloud Sessions/Kiro Web off unless separately assessed: cloud sessions run in us-east-1 only for Identity Center organizations; model availability settings now apply to Kiro Web, but customer-managed keys, MCP settings and other governance (e.g., web tools) do not. Confirm prompt-logging and retention settings.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud inference only (Amazon Bedrock); local IDE, CLI or Crew clients and AWS PrivateLink endpoints (a private network path to Kiro's service) do not change this. HIPAA eligibility (AWS lists Kiro excluding Kiro Web) or contractual controls do not satisfy this index's controlled-infrastructure requirement.
