final_records.name: Zed
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: Separate request paths: Zed-hosted models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google; Pro, Student, Business), provider API keys, existing subscriptions, gateways (e.g. OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vercel), local or self-hosted models (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible servers), External Agents via ACP, and Terminal Threads running agent CLIs. Edit prediction has its own provider setting; the default is Zed-hosted Zeta.
final_records.data_handling_note: Zed does not retain prompts or code context by default; it stores AI data only when a user rates a response or opts into Edit Prediction training data (open-source projects only). Defaults are hosted: the default agent provider is Zed-hosted and the default edit-prediction provider is hosted Zeta (both need sign-in). Zed-hosted models: provider agreements prohibit training and require ZDR, except provider safety retention for designated Covered Models (Anthropic: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Fable 5, at least 30 days); Zed's default settings withhold hosted requests to non-ZDR Anthropic models until the user consents. Zed's subprocessor list (last updated 2026-03-02) states that hosted summarization or commit-message requests may reach Anthropic, Google or OpenAI even when another model is selected; it still lists xAI as well, although Zed retired its hosted xAI models on 2026-05-15. Hosted Zeta edit predictions run on Baseten (US). BYOK, subscriptions, gateways, External Agents, Terminal Threads and third-party edit prediction follow their own terms. Client telemetry (diagnostics, metrics) is on by default and can be disabled; server-side telemetry is collected whenever hosted AI or collaboration is used.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a fully local model, or a hosted/BYOK route the institution has approved. A DPA is available on request (Zed acts as processor for Zed Business). Hosted Zed models send prompts and code context to US-hosted providers under no-training/ZDR commitments, with provider safety retention for Covered Models.
suitability_notes.special: Only the fully local route qualifies: Zed Agent, all feature-specific models and edit prediction on Ollama (in local-only mode), llama.cpp, LM Studio or a self-hosted endpoint on institution-controlled infrastructure that forwards nothing to external providers, signed out of Zed, telemetry off. Hosted Zed/provider models are not acceptable; Zed's Terms also bar HIPAA PHI from Customer Data sent to its hosted Service.

compliance: GDPR rights and EEA/UK complaint route in Privacy Policy (last updated 2026-06-09); DPA available on request (processor role for Zed Business)
Services hosted in the US; EEA/UK transfers under Standard Contractual Clauses
SOC 2 Type 1 in progress, not certified
Terms (last updated 2026-03-02) prohibit HIPAA PHI in Customer Data submitted to the hosted Service
final_records.pricing: Personal $0: unlimited use with own API keys or External Agents; Zed-hosted models and hosted Zeta edit predictions require Pro (edit predictions from other providers or a local model remain usable). Pro $10/month with $5 monthly hosted-model token credit, overage at provider list price +10%; 14-day Pro trial with $5 of GPT-6 Luna usage (the only hosted model in the trial, balance shared with Delta) and unlimited edit predictions, no card required. Business $30/seat/month, no bundled AI credit, no free trial, org-wide AI and data-sharing controls, role-based access, order forms at 25+ seats; SSO/SAML/SCIM not yet available. Student plan separately documented.

Multiplayer real-time collaboration
final_records.notes: Desktop editor with hosted, BYOK, gateway and fully local model routes. Licence scope (README): primarily GPL-3.0-or-later, with Apache-2.0 components where marked; open-core reflects the open client plus Zed-hosted services. Defaults point to hosted services (Zed-hosted agent model, hosted Zeta edit prediction, client telemetry on), so the local route needs explicit configuration; special-category suitability applies only to that route. SOC 2 Type 1 is in progress, not achieved. Delta, Zed Industries' separate multiplayer agent environment (public beta since 2026-09-16), is not covered by this record.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local route (local models for agent, feature models and edit prediction; signed out of Zed) for special-category data; Business for org-enforced data-sharing controls, which cover Zed-hosted services only

required_controls: Point Zed Agent and every feature-specific model (inline assistant, commit message, thread summary, compaction, subagent) to a local or self-hosted endpoint on institution-controlled infrastructure that serves only institution-hosted models and forwards nothing to external providers.

Stay signed out of Zed (sign-in is needed only for collaboration and Zed-hosted LLM features), so no Zed-hosted model or hosted edit prediction is used; hosted summarization and commit-message requests can reach cloud providers even when another model is selected.
Set edit prediction to a local provider (Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server) or to none; the default provider is hosted Zeta.

If Ollama serves any model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Disable client telemetry (diagnostics and metrics), do not rate responses or opt into Edit Prediction training data, and leave collaboration unused.
Configure or avoid External Agents, Terminal Threads, MCP servers, gateways and extensions separately; Zed settings and Business controls do not govern them.
Keep Zed Agent sandboxing on (Linux needs bwrap; Windows needs WSL) and use tool permissions to restrict terminal and fetch network egress.
residual_risks: Defaults point to hosted services (Zed-hosted agent model, hosted Zeta edit prediction, client telemetry on); signing in or a missed setting can re-enable cloud egress.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so pointing Zed at local Ollama alone does not show that inference stays local.
External Agents, Terminal Threads, MCP servers, extensions and agent fetch/terminal tools run under their own configuration and can send data off-machine.
Sandboxing covers only the Zed Agent terminal and fetch tools and may be weaker on Windows.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Amp
final_records.deployment: cloud (Amp Server on Google Cloud, US, runs the agent loop, routes inference and stores threads; tool execution can move to the local CLI, the user's own runners, or self-hosted orbs on customer infrastructure, but tool outputs and threads still flow to Amp)
final_records.model_backend: Amp-managed routing per mode and subagent; the /modes page currently lists low = GLM-5.3-Flash, medium = Opus 5.5, high = GPT-6 Astra, ultra = Fable 5.1, Puck = GPT-5.6 Sol, with Gemini, GPT and other system models for media, image and voice tasks; routing changes over time. Per the security page, Amp-managed inference runs on Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, Meta, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Vertex), Amazon Bedrock, Baseten and Fireworks (US servers), and TypeSafe's Jev decision model handles fast classification decisions. Customer connections: provider API keys (BYOK; Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter can use workload identity federation); cloud platforms (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry); Amp authenticates to Bedrock with IAM web identity federation and to Google Cloud Agent Platform with workload identity; routers/gateways (e.g. OpenRouter, Vercel or Cloudflare AI Gateway, Ollama Cloud) and Custom URL endpoints; linked ChatGPT, Grok or GitHub Copilot subscriptions. Amp sends all model requests from its own servers, so endpoints must be reachable from Amp. A Claude Pro/Max plan is used only by the Claude Code mode, which runs the Claude Agent SDK on Amp's servers.
final_records.data_handling_note: Training: per Amp's security page and MDR doc, Amp and its subprocessors do not train on user data unless the user opts in; in a workspace, opting in needs admin approval, and Enterprise workspaces cannot enable it. Provider retention: Minimal Data Retention (MDR) is available to all users on Amp-managed provider connections paid with Amp credits. Under MDR, providers keep prompts/responses only to return a response, except safety/abuse data, longer model- or feature-specific retention (up to 30 days), short-lived cached artifacts and legal requirements; some models and features are not eligible (flagged in-product). Claude Fable: Amp's Allowed Models doc states Anthropic retains prompts and outputs sent to Claude Fable for 30 days; Fable currently serves the ultra mode. Only the Enterprise Terms define ZDR contractually: ZDR for models and features Amp's documentation lists as eligible, MDR otherwise; workspace-wide ZDR applies only if the customer enables a setting restricting selection to eligible models, where offered (the public docs describe Allowed Models, including a Claude Fable switch, but no ZDR-only setting). The pricing FAQ still says all users and workspaces are covered by the zero and minimal data retention policy. BYOK, cloud-platform, gateway and linked subscriptions (ChatGPT, Grok, GitHub Copilot; Claude Pro/Max in Claude Code mode) follow that provider account's retention and training terms. Product retention (not covered by MDR): Amp stores threads (messages, responses, code snippets, tool results, attachments), user information and telemetry in a multi-tenant Google Cloud project in the US; with self-hosted orbs, file contents read, command output, diffs and attachments are still sent to and stored with the thread. Explicitly deleted threads are removed within 30 days, and account deletion removes owned threads within 30 days; Enterprise workspace threads stay with the workspace until the contract ends; configurable thread retention is offered to Enterprise on request. Paused Amp-hosted orb filesystems and memory are stored until the thread is deleted; project snapshots are reused for up to 72 hours, and a replaced snapshot is deleted only after all orbs created from it are deleted. Telemetry and tracking: the privacy policy (last updated 3 Nov 2026) adds advertising pixels (Google, Meta, LinkedIn, X, Reddit) on the public website and server-side conversion events (e.g. signup, first use, purchase, with hashed email) outside the EEA/UK/Switzerland, with opt-out via 'Your Privacy Choices' or GPC; for EEA/UK/Swiss visitors and visitors whose location cannot be determined it states no analytics or advertising cookies and no conversion reporting. Submitted content is not shared with advertisers. No opt-out for product telemetry was found.

suitability_notes.personal: Only on an Enterprise contract with a signed DPA (no public DPA found; the Trust Center is gated) and after accepting US storage of thread data (SCC-based transfers per the privacy policy). Use Amp-managed or institution-held model connections, not personal linked subscriptions (ChatGPT, Grok, Claude plans); a GitHub Copilot connection is per person and follows GitHub's terms for that seat. MDR is not end-to-end deletion: Claude Fable (ultra mode) carries 30-day Anthropic retention, so an admin should switch off the Claude Fable group in Allowed Models (check which model ultra then uses) and agree thread deletion/retention terms. Self-hosted orbs keep the checkout on institutional infrastructure but not the thread content sent to Amp.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate. Amp's Terms say the Services are not designed to store GDPR Art. 9 special-category data or HIPAA PHI and users must not use them to store it; Amp is not a HIPAA Business Associate. There is no self-hosted Amp deployment. Local runners and the new self-hosted orbs move tool execution only: per Amp's docs, Amp still runs the agent loop and model inference on its own servers and stores file contents, command output and diffs with the thread in its US cloud (Claude Code mode also runs on Amp's servers under the linked Claude plan).

compliance: Security page states SOC 2 Type II certification and annual penetration testing; reports are available on request through a gated Trust Center (scope not reviewed).
Terms: the Services are not designed for Sensitive Data (GDPR Art. 9 special categories, HIPAA PHI, government IDs, financial account data, credentials) and Amp is not a HIPAA Business Associate.

No public DPA found; the privacy policy (updated 3 Nov 2026) names Amp as GDPR controller for its own processing and SCCs for EEA/UK/Swiss transfers. An enterprise DPA and audit-report scope must match the selected service.
final_records.pricing: Hobby: free; Amp-hosted orbs pay-as-you-go, own runners and self-hosted orbs free; BYOK and linked subscriptions carry no Amp token fee; Amp-served inference uses paid credits at provider API prices without markup. Individual: Megawatt $20/month ($20 agent usage; 750 hours of a1.small orbs) and Gigawatt $200/month ($200 agent usage; 1,000 hours of a1.xxlarge orbs per the docs). Teams: no extra workspace charge; members can be on Hobby, Megawatt or Gigawatt; SAML/OIDC SSO needs at least one paid member. Enterprise: custom pricing, pooled credits only; an Amp fee may apply to tokens served by customer connections; self-hosted orbs are free for every workspace until 13 Nov 2026, after which Enterprise pays the standard orb price for them (volume discounts). Purchased credits expire after 12 months.
final_records.academic: Education discount: students and teachers can get Megawatt for $10/month (half the $20 price, with $10 included agent usage) via ampcode.com/edu after signing in and filling in a form. The /edu page says it applies only to Megawatt, is intended for use with a ChatGPT or Grok subscription, and can be changed or discontinued. Eligibility criteria (e.g. whether research staff qualify) are not stated publicly.

Multi-platform agent management (start in CLI, web, macOS, iOS or Android; monitor and continue from another client)
Running agents on your own machines via runners, including shared workspace runners (e.g. GPU boxes)

Parallel subagent workloads

Long-running autonomous coding tasks with context compaction

The security page still states Amp does not offer self-hosted deployments. The Claude Code mode runs the Claude Agent SDK on Amp's servers. The former /manual URL redirects to /docs. final_records.name: Sourcegraph Cody
final_records.deployment: cloud / self-hostable / on-prem
final_records.model_backend: Sourcegraph Model Provider (Cody Gateway) gives Enterprise instances hosted Anthropic, OpenAI and Google models. It is configured by default on Sourcegraph Cloud; self-hosted customers confirm access with their account manager. Autocomplete and Smart Apply models include Fireworks-hosted models (US Iowa); Claude Haiku 4.5 (Anthropic, global hosting) is also listed for autocomplete. Self-hosted instances can instead configure BYOK providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock for Claude models only, Google Gemini/Vertex, Fireworks), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or Hugging Face TGI; the docs say BYOK with managed services is supported only on self-hosted instances. The model list changes often; check the current supported-models page and the instance's modelConfiguration.
final_records.data_handling_note: Enterprise only. The Cody FAQ states Sourcegraph will not train on Enterprise customers' data; the ToS (last modified 2026-07-22) allows fine-tuning only if enabled for the instance and says Partner LLMs reached through Sourcegraph keep zero retention (temporary abuse/harm retention excepted) and do not train. Product-level retention is separate: the DPA (last modified 2026-10-05) lists maintaining AI conversation history during the subscription term as a processing purpose; after expiry Sourcegraph returns or deletes data on the customer's instruction, and without an instruction within 60 days deletes all Customer Personal Data, including AI conversation data, within 90 days. The partner zero-retention commitment applies only to access through Sourcegraph's Partner LLMs, so with BYOK the customer's own provider agreement sets retention. The AI Terms (2026-06-12) apply only to agreements signed before 2024-02-15 or Order Forms that incorporate them; the Cody notice (2024-02-15) applies only to older Cody licences. Self-hosted instances send aggregated pings (no code, but including the installer/admin email, instance URL and IP) and license verification checks, and export telemetry events (numeric metadata, anonymized user IDs) to Sourcegraph by default. Since October 2026 the docs state that instances connect to the services gateway (services.sourcegraph.com) for pings and telemetry, license verification, and credit/quota checks with consumption reporting; model inference through Cody Gateway is a separate connection.

suitability_notes.personal: Requires an Enterprise Order Form and the DPA (last modified 2026-10-05; EEA/UK transfer terms). The subprocessor list names Anthropic, Fireworks AI and Google (all USA) for AI queries and code snippets. OpenAI is listed only for embeddings when the customer enables them. Amp (USA) is listed for error data that can include customer code. Confirm which AI terms the Order Form incorporates, the model routing (Cody Gateway vs BYOK), conversation-history retention and deletion on request. Context Filters can restrict which repositories Cody sends as context. BYOK to a cloud model is still an external processor. Agentic context fetching is on by default. Its docs still say the review step defaults to Gemini 2.5 Flash (fallback Claude Haiku or GPT 4.1 mini), but Sourcegraph 8.1.0 (2026-10-14) removed the Gemini 2.5 models, so the current review model is unconfirmed. A Claude-only chat setup may still send context to Google or OpenAI; include this step in the routing check. The subprocessor page says self-hosted personal data is processed only when shared for support, but self-hosted instances using Cody Gateway still send prompts and code snippets to the LLM providers.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate. The ToS, which also covers self-hosted Software, says the product is not designed to store GDPR Art. 9 special-category data or HIPAA PHI and must not be used to store it; the DPA marks special-category data as not processed. Default routing also sends code snippets to cloud LLMs, and no first-party source documents an end-to-end deployment with inference on customer-controlled infrastructure.

compliance: SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 listed on the Sourcegraph Security Portal; reports are access-gated and Cody/AI-feature scope is not confirmed
Standard DPA (last modified 2026-10-05) with EEA/UK restricted-transfer terms
ToS: Sourcegraph is not a HIPAA Business Associate; GDPR Art. 9 special-category data excluded
Applicable Order Form and AI terms require confirmation

AI chat, inline edit, and autocomplete in VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio (experimental)

final_records.notes: Active, Enterprise-only. Sourcegraph 8.1.0 (2026-10-14) made Claude Sonnet 5.5 the default Cody chat model, added Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Sol/Luna and Gemini 4 Argon, and removed Gemini 2.5 and older Gemini Flash models. The editor extensions shipped again after a four-month gap: VS Code/Open VSX 1.156.0 on 2026-10-15 and JetBrains 7.156.1 on 2026-10-27; the Visual Studio extension (experimental) is still at 0.22.0 from 2025-11-25. The Cody FAQ still says Sourcegraph is fully committed to Cody Enterprise, but its 2026-10-05 edit removed the longer sunset section, including the statement that Cody Enterprise will be actively supported, developed and maintained; Sourcegraph's recent product and blog emphasis is on Deep Search and Agentic Batch Changes. Since Sourcegraph 7.0 (2026-02-25), Deep Search replaces Cody in the browser for Deep Search customers; the editor extensions are unaffected. Current AI use is governed by the Sourcegraph ToS and DPA. The AI Terms apply only to pre-2024-02-15 agreements or Order Forms that incorporate them, and the Cody notice (last modified 2024-02-15) only to older Cody licences. The model-provider docs nonetheless say the AI Terms apply to all Model Provider use. The Ollama local-model page is scoped to the discontinued Free/Pro plans. Default Cody Gateway routing sends prompts and code snippets to cloud LLM providers. Defaults: Anthropic (Claude Sonnet 5.5) for chat, Fireworks AI (US Iowa) for autocomplete; the agentic-context review step (on by default) is documented as Google Gemini, although the named Gemini 2.5 Flash was removed in 8.1.0. OpenAI models are selectable.

An OpenAI-compatible or Hugging Face TGI endpoint can be configured, but no first-party source documents an end-to-end customer-controlled deployment; the FAQ says self-hosted instances need internet access for external LLM services, and the docs require outbound access to services.sourcegraph.com for telemetry, license verification (unless the license is exempt) and credit/quota checks.

final_records.name: OpenCode
final_records.deployment: local-capable / cloud
final_records.model_backend: BYOK cloud providers (75+ via Models.dev, plus GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT Plus/Pro and GitLab Duo sign-in) or local Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM and other OpenAI-compatible endpoints (V2 auto-discovers Ollama, LM Studio and vLLM); optional hosted OpenCode Models (pay-as-you-go, formerly OpenCode Zen) and OpenCode Go (subscription) gateways, and in V2 the hosted OpenCode Console gateway for a workspace's own provider keys.
final_records.data_handling_note: The client keeps sessions, logs and credentials on the local machine (~/.local/share/opencode). The vendor states that it does not store code or context data and that prompts go directly to the selected provider. With no OpenCode key set, V1 and V2 enable the hosted OpenCode free models by default and can select one as the default model (V1 1.19.5 source; V2 models docs and 2.2.1 release notes), so choose a provider explicitly and block the rest (V2: OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS=1 or a provider policy). The hosted routes are not uniformly zero-retention. On OpenCode Models (formerly Zen), OpenAI and Anthropic requests are retained for 30 days, Mistral data follow Mistral's retention policy, several free models may use data to improve the model or retain it for 30 days, and NVIDIA free endpoints log use. On Go, the Grok 4.7, GPT Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Beam Free routes retain for 30 days; the Muse Spark Contributor models train Meta models and are blocked unless an admin allows paid training endpoints; Iceman Contributor Free uses prompts to improve the model; the DeepSeek ZDR agreement is renewed monthly. The V2 Console gateway records each request and its cost; its content retention is not documented. Console-hosted web search is stated to be zero-retention. The Terms allow Content from unpaid accounts on the hosted Services to be used to improve them. Session sharing was discontinued in 1.19.1 (15 Oct 2026), and V2 has no sharing. Both lines can send web searches to third parties (V1 with the OpenCode or Go provider or the Exa/Parallel flags; V2 through five search providers or Console search), and webfetch, allowed by default, can reach any URL. Disable web search and webfetch for private work, and review every selected provider.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local provider, or a direct provider or OpenCode Models/Go model whose retention and DPA you have verified. Hosted routes are not uniformly ZDR: some free models use data for improvement, Go's Contributor models permit training, and several routes retain for 30 days. The built-in OpenCode free models are enabled by default when no key is set: block them, and disable web search and webfetch.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a fully local model on controlled infrastructure (a self-run Ollama in local-only mode, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM), all other providers blocked (including the built-in OpenCode free models), web search, webfetch and outside-project access disabled, and the settings enforced through managed configuration (system config directory or macOS MDM, documented for 1.x and V2). OpenCode Models, Go, the Console gateway and Console web search, Ollama Cloud or Ollama ':cloud' models and other cloud providers are not acceptable.

compliance: Anomaly's trust centre (trust.opencode.ai, Comp AI) lists SOC 2 Type 1 and Type 2 as compliant and offers an OpenCode DPA; both documents are NDA-gated and were not reviewed, and their service scope is not stated.
final_records.pricing: The client is free and open source (MIT). OpenCode Models (optional, formerly Zen) is pay-as-you-go from prepaid Console credits, priced per 1M tokens, with a processing fee of 4.6% + $0.31 per credit purchase; auto-recharge is an optional rule. Console has no seat fees. OpenCode Go (optional) is a subscription: Go $10/month and Go Plus $40/month for single-member workspaces, Go Teams $20/member/month, with per-model usage limits and optional Extra Usage from credits. Console-hosted web search costs $0.01 per successful search. Enterprise is per-seat and quote-based, with no token charge when your own LLM gateway is used.
final_records.academic: The open-source client is available without an academic subscription; no special academic entitlement is asserted.

final_records.notes: Open-source coding agent for the terminal, desktop, web and IDE, with local, direct-provider and hosted OpenCode Models, Go and Console routes. OpenCode 2 (@opencode/cli; 2.0.0 on npm 11 Sep 2026, 2.2.5 on 30 Oct) is now the default from the opencode.ai installer and Homebrew core; the 1.x line (opencode-ai, 1.19.5 on 28 Oct) is maintained, no longer installs updates automatically (1.19.0) and stays on 1.x. Session sharing was discontinued in 1.19.1. V2 runs a shared local background service by default (it can be disabled, or --standalone used), does not run language servers, allows access outside the project directory by default, offers web search through five third-party providers or Console search, and accepts policies from system config, macOS MDM and a connected Console workspace. The Models docs say models are hosted in the US and EU; Go workspaces allow Europe and US regions by default; workspaces without saved privacy settings also allow Global for requests from China. No new advisory since GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 (September 2026, fixed in 1.18.22). Keep the client patched and do not expose the local server.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local model, all other providers (including the built-in OpenCode free models) blocked, web search, webfetch and outside-project access disabled, settings enforced through managed config, for regulated data

required_controls: Run inference only through a local model runtime (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM) on controlled infrastructure; do not use the separate Ollama Cloud provider.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in ~/.ollama/server.json of the account that runs the server), confirm the log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Block all other providers, including the built-in "opencode" free tier: V1 enabled_providers/disabled_providers; V2 a top-level policies provider.use deny "*" followed by an allow for the local provider, plus OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS=1 on the server process. Check the log, because invalid policy statements are dropped with a warning.

On V2 2.2.3 or later, use managed policies to deny integration.connect for the Console and web-search integrations and to deny mcp.use, skill.use and plugin.use except reviewed items, so a Console workspace cannot deliver providers, MCP servers or web search.

Set every model role explicitly to the local provider (V1 model and small_model; V2 model and agents.title.model), and confirm sessions do not switch models (V2 falls back to the newest available supported model when the configured one is unavailable). Keep no cloud API keys in the environment or .env files, and remove stored hosted-provider credentials from ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json.

Disable web search: on V2 set "websearch": false in system or MDM managed config, because a connected Console workspace outranks user and project files and its workspace config selects Console web search by default, and websearch.use policies need 2.2.6, unreleased on 6 Nov 2026; on V1 avoid the OpenCode/Go providers and leave OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA/PARALLEL off. Deny webfetch (V1 permission webfetch deny; V2 policy tool.use "webfetch:*" deny). Review MCP servers, plugins and LSP downloads for egress.
On V2, add an external_directory ask or deny rule, because V2 allows reads and edits outside the project without a prompt by default.

Enforce the settings through managed configuration that users cannot override: the system config directory (/etc/opencode, /Library/Application Support/opencode, %ProgramData%\opencode) or macOS MDM managed preferences (ai.opencode.managed), now documented for both 1.x and V2. Express restrictions as V2 policies, because ordinary settings cannot stop users adding providers, MCP servers or plugins.

Check the effective configuration before sensitive sessions, because project config files, remote .well-known config and environment variables are also loaded and may set providers, tools or permissions.

Manage updates centrally (V1 1.19.0 or later no longer installs updates automatically; V1 autoupdate false or OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE; V2 update "disable"). On offline hosts also disable the remote model-catalog fetch and LSP downloads (documented V1 flags: OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH, OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD).
Restrict host network egress to the local model endpoint, because shell commands run with the user's network access, and confirm with egress monitoring before processing special-category data.

Keep clients at or above the patched versions (1.x at least 1.19.1, where sharing is discontinued); do not expose opencode serve/web or the V2 background service beyond localhost, and set a server password (V2 OPENCODE_PASSWORD).
residual_risks: Local sessions, logs, credentials (auth.json) and the session database under ~/.local/share/opencode need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

Out of the box, V1 and V2 enable the hosted OpenCode free models, and V2 falls back to the newest available model when the configured one is unavailable; a missing deny rule or a stopped local runtime can route prompts to hosted models, some of which permit data use for improvement or training.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

V2 policies do not sandbox plugin code; invalid statements are dropped with a warning, and policy semantics changed in 2.2.3 (a broad integration.use deny no longer blocks MCP servers, skills or plugins).
A connected Console workspace can deliver providers, MCP servers and web search and keeps its last policy statements while unreachable; only managed policies can withhold what it delivers.
The local HTTP server and web UI have had high or critical advisories (most recently GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4, September 2026); V2 runs a shared local background service by default.
OpenCode 2 is a new, fast-moving major line; a V2 equivalent of the V1 model-catalog fetch flag is not documented (V2 does not run language servers).
Third-party MCP servers, plugins and LSP servers can send data outside the controlled boundary.

final_records.name: Crush
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: Bring your own provider: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Cerebras, Hugging Face, Vercel AI Gateway, Z.ai, MiniMax, Moonshot, xAI and other Catwalk-listed providers via API keys (Vertex AI and Bedrock also via Google Cloud or AWS credentials), or any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint; account sign-in for Charm Hyper (official, optional; open-weight models such as DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen and GLM plus the Prism routing model), GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT and xAI Grok; local models via Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, oMLX or LiteLLM
final_records.data_handling_note: The CLI keeps sessions, logs (./.crush) and state on the machine; model requests go to the providers configured for the model slots and to any configured model a subagent is moved to (v0.100.0). Built-in tools can still reach the web from a local-model setup: the sourcegraph tool (enabled by default, no permission prompt) sends model-written search queries to sourcegraph.com; agentic_fetch asks once, then a sub-agent searches DuckDuckGo and fetches pages without further prompts; fetch and download ask per call. Pseudonymous usage metrics (PostHog via data.charm.land) are on by default; the README states that prompts and responses are never collected, but source code shows crash and panic error messages are sent. Disable metrics with CRUSH_DISABLE_METRICS=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or `option metrics false`. A Hyper login links the metrics device ID to the Hyper account (now also stated in the README). At startup Crush queries the GitHub releases API for new versions (no documented opt-out) and, unless provider auto-update or default providers are disabled, refreshes the Catwalk catalog and the Hyper provider definition from hyper.charm.land. Optional Hyper (terms and privacy policy last updated 2026-10-14) is the README's suggested quickest start, and its handling now depends on the credit source. Personal Shred subscriptions are not ZDR: prompts and outputs processed from 2026-10-14 may be retained as long as needed for Model Training and used to train Charm's own models after automated redaction, are not deleted on account closure, and users outside the US must give separate opt-in consent. Business plans, Pay As You Go prepaid credits and Enterprise are ZDR: no training, content not stored by default but kept up to 30 days when retained for debugging, abuse prevention or legal compliance. On a Shred account, subscription Hypercredits are spent before any prepaid credits, so buying prepaid credits does not make Shred use ZDR until the weekly subscription allowance is exhausted. Operational usage data 90 days, analytics usage data 24 months. Inference runs through model subprocessors listed in DPA Annex 2 (US and other countries), whose terms bar training on customer data; Annex 2 also lists Google Cloud (US compute), which keeps User Content as directed by Charm. ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot and Grok sign-ins follow those accounts' own terms.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local model with metrics disabled and governed tool and network access, or approve the chosen cloud route separately: Hyper only on a ZDR credit source (a Business plan, prepaid Pay As You Go credits on an account without a Shred subscription, or Enterprise) under its DPA, or an API provider or signed-in account (ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Grok) under that vendor's terms. Hyper Shred personal subscriptions may train on prompts and outputs and are not appropriate for personal data; Hyper's privacy policy says not to input sensitive, confidential or personal information on plans without ZDR.
suitability_notes.special: Only with fully local models for every model slot and any subagent model (Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, LM Studio, oMLX, or LiteLLM serving local models only), no cloud sign-ins or provider keys, metrics and provider auto-update disabled, built-in web tools denied (sourcegraph, agentic_fetch, fetch, download), no yolo or sysadmin mode, egress blocked and controlled execution. Hyper (any plan) and all cloud providers are not appropriate. FSL-1.1-MIT is source-available, not an OSI open-source licence, until each release converts to MIT on its second anniversary.

compliance: Hyper: a DPA is published online at hyper.charm.land/legal/dpa (undated) and states it forms part of the Terms of Service, although the Terms (s.9.8) and Privacy Policy (s.8) still say a DPA is available on request; Charm is processor for User Content and independent controller for account, usage and analytics data and for content used for Model Training on plans without ZDR (Shred).

Hyper: services operated from the US; EEA, UK and Swiss transfers under EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Modules 2 and 3) with the UK Addendum and Swiss amendments. DPA Annex 2 lists inference subprocessors (Alibaba Cloud, Baseten, Emissary Technologies, Fireworks AI, io.net, Parasail) and Google Cloud, located in the US and other countries.
Hyper DPA: security incident notice within 72 hours; 10 days' notice of subprocessor changes; special categories of data listed as 'None intended'.
Hyper: users outside the US can choose a plan without ZDR only by ticking a separate Model Training consent box, withdrawable on the account page.
No SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA/BAA statement found on the Hyper home page, FAQ, docs, terms, privacy policy or DPA; GDPR compliance is a vendor statement.
Hyper terms do not govern a fully local model route.
final_records.pricing: Crush CLI: no licence fee (FSL-1.1-MIT); local models carry no vendor inference fee. Optional Hyper (checked 2026-11-06; the monthly free allowance has been retired): personal Shred plans at $10, $20, $50, $100 or $200 per month with 180 to 1,200 Hypercredits per week (not ZDR; may train on prompts); Business plans at $30, $40, $70, $120 or $220 per user per month with the same weekly allowances (ZDR); Pay As You Go prepaid Hypercredits from $5, non-expiring and ZDR; Enterprise on request. Weekly credits reset Sunday 00:00 UTC, with a five-hour rolling limit and concurrency caps; 1 Hypercredit is 5 cents. API providers and ChatGPT, Copilot or Grok subscriptions bill separately.
final_records.academic: FSL-1.1-MIT expressly permits internal use, non-commercial education and non-commercial research at no cost; only a Competing Use is excluded. No academic pricing for Hyper found on its first-party pages; the cheaper Shred plans are priced on the basis that Charm may train on prompts, so research groups needing ZDR pay Business or prepaid rates. Inference costs depend on the provider.

Multi-file codebase exploration and refactoring

MCP-extensible tool workflows (stdio, http, sse)
Local/offline coding on privacy-sensitive code via Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or oMLX
Multi-model mid-session switching for cost/quality tradeoffs
Plan Mode for agreeing a plan before the agent edits files
Background subagents for parallel tasks, each assignable to a different configured model

Non-interactive scripted runs with crush run

Air-gapped or restricted-network deployments
final_records.notes: Local-capable terminal coding agent from Charm under FSL-1.1-MIT (source-available; each release converts to MIT after two years). Actively maintained, with several releases a month (latest v0.100.0 on 2026-11-05, adding background subagents, a sysadmin permission mode that auto-approves every command, and configurable command block lists; v0.99.0 moved to Catwalk v3 and added lifecycle hooks). From 2026-10-14 the optional Hyper provider may train on prompts and outputs under personal Shred plans; Business, prepaid and Enterprise use stay ZDR, and the free tier is gone. Sensitive-data use requires fully local models, no cloud sign-ins, metrics and provider updates disabled, built-in web tools denied, no yolo or sysadmin mode, and blocked egress.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local models with cloud sign-ins, metrics, auto-update and built-in web tools off and no yolo or sysadmin mode for special-category data; for personal data, Hyper only on a ZDR credit source (Business, prepaid Pay As You Go credits without a Shred subscription, or Enterprise) under its DPA, never a Shred plan, or an approved provider contract

required_controls: Configure only local inference providers (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, oMLX, or a LiteLLM gateway that serves local models only), so every model slot and any model a subagent is moved to is local; `option default-providers false` hides built-in cloud providers.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in ~/.ollama/server.json of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Do not sign in to Hyper, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT or Grok, and keep cloud provider API keys out of the environment.
Disable usage metrics with CRUSH_DISABLE_METRICS=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or `option metrics false`.

Disable provider catalog auto-update (CRUSH_DISABLE_PROVIDER_AUTO_UPDATE=1 or `option provider-auto-update false`) and block egress at the network level, including the startup version check to api.github.com, then verify the block.
Deny the built-in web tools with `permissions deny sourcegraph agentic_fetch fetch download`; sourcegraph sends queries to sourcegraph.com without a permission prompt.

Keep tool permission prompts on (no --yolo and no sysadmin mode, which auto-approves every command and disarms the block list), restrict MCP servers, hooks and shell access, and review any project crushrc or crush.json before launch.
Apply institutional access, retention and encryption controls to local sessions, logs (./.crush) and the data directory.
residual_risks: A cloud provider key in the environment or a misconfigured provider, model slot or subagent model override sends prompts off the machine; verify egress.

A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, and Crush auto-discovers models from local providers, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
Project-local crushrc and crush.json run as trusted code at load, so an untrusted repository can execute commands.
Built-in web tools (sourcegraph without a prompt; agentic_fetch, whose inner web search and fetch calls skip prompts and hooks), MCP servers, hooks and shell tools can move data off the machine.
Sysadmin mode, reachable from the command palette or the Shift+Tab mode cycle, lets the agent run any command without prompts; yolo mode skips prompts too.
In the opt-in client/server mode, --yolo is first-wins per workspace, and with CRUSH_PERMISSIONS_PIPED=1 the host application answers permission prompts, so a client may not see or control approvals.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
FSL-1.1-MIT is source-available, not an OSI open-source licence, until each release converts to MIT on its second anniversary.

final_records.name: Mistral Vibe
final_records.deployment: cloud / local-capable / self-hostable
final_records.model_backend: Mistral-hosted models via the Mistral API: the CLI ships one built-in model, Mistral Medium 3.5, and its configuration docs list Mistral Large 3, Mistral Small 4, Codestral, Ministral 3 and Z.ai GLM 5.2/5.3 as available through Mistral's API; or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including self-hosted Devstral Small 2 or Mistral Small 4 (no bundled local model since v2.26.1). Unset utility models (smart-approve classifier, session titles) use a small Mistral model whenever a Mistral provider serves one. Teleport/Vibe Code Web sessions run on Mistral Medium 3.5 in Mistral's cloud. Model licences are separate from the client licence.
final_records.data_handling_note: Best route is local: the Vibe CLI with a self-configured OpenAI-compatible model server, enable_telemetry=false and enable_update_checks=false (the older enable_auto_update key now has no effect), and no Mistral credentials on the machine (no API key, no browser sign-in; browser sign-in is on by default for Mistral-provider configs). Mistral's offline docs say the CLI then does not contact mistral.ai, but a Mistral API key triggers a startup fetch of admin-managed config from Mistral, unset utility models fall to a small Mistral model when a Mistral provider is available, and MCP servers, connectors (including built-in web search, enabled by default) and skills that reach external systems must be disabled separately. Defaults are cloud-facing: telemetry (anonymous usage and error data) and daily update checks are on by default. Cloud training (help article modified 2026-10-20; rules unchanged): Vibe inputs/outputs train Mistral models by default unless opted out; Enterprise is opted out by default under admin control; no separate Team exception is stated; Mistral Studio Free mode may train (opt-out available) and pay-as-you-go customers can opt out. Thumbs-up/down feedback authorizes use of the rated input/output on any plan. Retention (Privacy Policy effective 2026-09-03): API inputs/outputs kept 30 rolling days for abuse monitoring unless ZDR is active; Vibe conversations until deleted. ZDR is discretionary and available only to pay-as-you-go organizations for stateless API calls; Vibe CLI calls follow it only when such an organization has approved ZDR; it never covers Vibe Work, Chat or other stateful products. Teleport ('/teleport', '&' prompts) moves a session into a Mistral cloud sandbox whose activity is retained per plan.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer the local route. Cloud route: Enterprise (training opted out by default) or a verified training opt-out on other plans, under the DPA where it applies to the plan; Mistral may train as controller unless the customer opted out. Accept 30-day API abuse-monitoring retention (ZDR only for approved pay-as-you-go organizations); give no thumbs-up/down feedback; do not teleport to Vibe Code Web unless its plan retention is accepted.
suitability_notes.special: Only the Vibe CLI on a self-configured local model server, with telemetry and update checks off, no Mistral API key or browser sign-in on the machine, utility models pinned to the local model, connectors/MCP/web tools and Teleport disabled, outbound traffic blocked except to the model server, Ollama (if used) in local-only mode, and the active provider checked each session. Cloud plans, Enterprise no-training or ZDR are not sufficient.

compliance: Mistral commercial processing terms are service/plan scoped; no general certification or EU-only storage guarantee is asserted.
DPA (effective 2026-07-27) allows transfers outside the EEA under adequacy decisions, other adequate safeguards or SCCs, and lets Mistral train as controller unless the customer has opted out.
final_records.pricing: Free (limited coding sessions); Pro $14.99/month (plan card lists $25.5/month in API credits); Team $24.99/user/month (price calculator starts at 2 users); Enterprise custom (private, self-hosted or on-premises deployments). Prices exclude tax; usage beyond plan limits can continue on pay-as-you-go at API rates. As displayed 2026-11-06 (pricing page last modified 2026-10-07).
final_records.academic: Pro Education: $5.99/month (excl. tax) for verified students at accredited higher-education institutions, for at most 12 months and only if they have not used Vibe or Le Chat before; the student card lists $15/month in API credits. No staff or institutional academic discount is stated on the pricing page.

Automated test generation
Pull request review and creation
Legacy code migration
Agentic terminal coding (long-running autonomous tasks)
IDE-integrated coding assistance (VS Code, JetBrains, Zed)
Codebase-wide context and search
GitHub/GitLab/Jira/Linear integration
Local/air-gapped coding with self-hosted Devstral Small 2
Research software engineering and scripting
API documentation generation
final_records.notes: Apache-2.0 repository; since v3.0.0 (changelog 2026-10-15) the legacy Python TUI and VIBE_CLI are removed, 'vibe' always starts the Rust TUI, and that crate's Cargo.toml now declares Apache-2.0 (it declared Proprietary up to v2.26.1). Commercial Vibe plans, a VS Code extension, ACP integration for JetBrains and Zed, and Vibe Code Web cloud sandboxes; the former Mistral Code product URL now redirects to the general Vibe product page. Actively maintained: v3.0.0 to v3.1.0 in October-November 2026 (v3.1.0 on PyPI 2026-11-04; changelog heading 2026-11-03). Security: advisory MAI-2026-003 (2026-09-14) reported shell-permission bypasses fixed in v2.25.4; no newer Vibe advisory is listed. v2.26.1 removed the built-in local Devstral model. Browser sign-in has been the default for Mistral-provider configs since v2.11.1 (2026-05), and the update key has been enable_update_checks since before v2.20.0; enable_auto_update now has no effect.
final_records.tier_gate: Cloud personal data: Enterprise (training opted out by default) or a verified training opt-out (DPA coverage per plan to confirm); special-category data: self-configured local model, telemetry and update checks off (enable_update_checks; enable_auto_update no longer works), no Mistral API key or browser sign-in, utility models on the local model

required_controls: Define the local OpenAI-compatible provider and model explicitly in config.toml (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio or Ollama on hardware you control), make sure no model entry in the effective configuration points to a hosted provider, and check the active model, provider, API base and credential source (for example with /status) before each session.
Pin [utility_models] smart_approve and title to "active" or to the local model alias; left unset, these background tasks use a small Mistral model whenever a Mistral provider serves one.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in ~/.ollama/server.json of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no cloud models.

Keep no Mistral credentials on the machine or in the environment: no API key (MISTRAL_API_KEY, OS keyring, ~/.vibe/.env) and no browser sign-in (on by default for Mistral-provider configs and offered by --setup even for local models). With a key present the CLI fetches admin-managed config from Mistral at startup, and Teleport and the hosted-default fallback can reach Mistral's cloud.

Set enable_telemetry = false and enable_update_checks = false in a local config the institution controls (enable_auto_update no longer has any effect, so older configs must be updated); do not rely on Mistral admin-managed config, which Mistral describes as a distribution mechanism, not a security control, and which is fetched over HTTP from Mistral.

Set enable_connectors = false (connectors include the built-in web search and are on by default), disable or vet MCP servers, skills and web tools that reach external systems, keep experimental_enable_model_catalog and experimental_enable_mistral_mcp_connector off, do not use /teleport, '&' prompts or Vibe Code Web, and do not trust repository folders that ship their own .vibe/config.toml.
Keep enable_otel off (OpenTelemetry export requires enable_telemetry = true, so it cannot be combined with the telemetry-off route).

Run v2.25.4 or later (MAI-2026-003 shell-permission fixes) inside an isolated workspace with least-privilege credentials; with update checks off, track Mistral security advisories and the changelog and update manually.
Block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the local model server, and verify the block before sensitive sessions.
residual_risks: If the configured model is missing or invalid (for example a stale pin to the built-in local model removed in v2.26.1), Vibe falls back to its built-in hosted default (Mistral Medium 3.5) with only a warning; with Mistral credentials present, code and data can go to Mistral's cloud.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost API base alone does not guarantee local inference.

Telemetry and daily update checks are on by default, and configs that still use enable_auto_update = false no longer stop update checks; a missed setting sends usage/error data or update queries off-host.

Configuration precedence (admin config > agent settings > CLI flags > VIBE_* env vars > project .vibe/config.toml > user config.toml) means an organization admin config, an agent file or a trusted repository's config can silently change the active model or provider; admin-managed values show only inside /config, with no startup indicator.

The configuration docs mention Mistral-side experiments that can assign a different model; they do not say whether this needs Mistral credentials, so the no-credentials control and the per-session /status check are the mitigation.

Since v3.0.3 the app server fetches the connector catalog at startup; the docs do not say whether this happens without Mistral credentials, so only an egress block and enable_connectors = false close it.
Shell-permission bypasses disclosed in September 2026 show prompt-injected content can trigger commands; treat the agent as able to read anything the user account can.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Cloud no-training or ZDR is not a substitute: ZDR covers only pay-as-you-go stateless API endpoints, not Vibe Work, Chat or other stateful products; Vibe Code Web retains session activity per plan.

final_records.name: Kiro CLI
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Managed cloud catalog; Kiro states it is powered by Amazon Bedrock. Includes Anthropic Claude models (incl. Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5), OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, open-weight models (Kimi K3, DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Qwen) and an Auto router. Since late October most models are generally available (Active); DeepSeek 3.2, MiniMax M2.1 and Qwen3 Coder Next remain Experimental. Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available to Kiro Enterprise organisations only and Kimi K3 (US geography only, a 'Kiro Excluded Model' without output indemnity) both need admin approval through model governance. Per the models page (updated 24 Oct 2026), GPT-5.6 has Global inference scope and uses the US endpoint even for Frankfurt profiles; other models have Geography scope (the enterprise profile's US or EU geography; Free and individual users use the US endpoint); Fable 5.1 runs only in us-east-1. AWS GovCloud (US) has a separate catalog with inference kept in GovCloud. The docs index lists no local or bring-your-own model option. Models and credit multipliers change often.
final_records.data_handling_note: Free Tier and individual subscribers (paid plans accessed via GitHub, Google or AWS Builder ID) may have content used for service improvement, which Kiro says can include model training, unless they opt out (CLI: turn off Telemetry and 'Share Kiro content with AWS'); their content is stored in us-east-1, and Free Tier inputs may also be kept up to 60 days for abuse detection. Students-tier accounts use the same sign-in methods and the Students FAQ points them to the same training opt-out; Kiro does not state whether they count as individual subscribers. Enterprise users (IAM Identity Center or external IdP) are excluded from service improvement and automatically opted out of telemetry/content collection, but content may be stored in the profile Region (US East (N. Virginia), Europe (Frankfurt) or AWS GovCloud (US)) to run the service; prompt logs and daily activity reports, when enabled, go to a customer-chosen S3 bucket in the customer's AWS account. Kiro may also collect operational signals (error logs and metrics based on instructions, feedback and responses). Model-specific abuse retention applies to all users: OpenAI GPT classifier-flagged traffic up to 30 days; all Claude Fable 5.1 traffic up to 30 days, with possible human review of flagged traffic by AWS. GPT-5.6 uses Global cross-region inference (possibly outside the profile geography). Optional --cloud sessions keep conversation history, cloned repositories and sandbox files in a Kiro-managed cloud sandbox (us-east-1 only for Identity Center organisations; off for Enterprise until an admin enables it); Kiro Web has its own content opt-out toggle, and the docs do not say which toggle covers CLI-created cloud sessions. CLI Memory (V3) is stored locally per user account. Running the CLI locally does not make inference local.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a Kiro Enterprise profile under institutional AWS terms (Frankfurt profile for EU storage). With model access management off, every model except Fable 5.1 and Kimi K3 is available, including Global-scope GPT-5.6; turn it on and keep GPT-5.6 (Global inference), Fable 5.1 (us-east-1 only, all traffic retained up to 30 days) and Kimi K3 (US only) off the approved list unless assessed, and block Auto if the approved list must bind (Auto can route to any Active model on the profile). Keep Cloud Sessions/Kiro Web off unless separately assessed, and decide deliberately on prompt logging. Individual paid, student or social-login plans are insufficient by themselves.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud inference only (commercial or GovCloud AWS Regions); no local or customer-controlled model endpoint is documented, so not suitable under the controlled-infrastructure rule.

compliance: Kiro documents HIPAA eligibility for Kiro IDE and CLI; AWS's HIPAA Eligible Services Reference lists Kiro excluding Kiro Web. A BAA, account, Region and configuration scope still apply; coverage of CLI cloud sessions is not stated.

final_records.pricing: Individual: Free $0 (50 credits/month; open-weight models and Claude Sonnet 4.5, with limits); Pro $20/user/month (1,000 credits); Pro+ $40 (2,000); Pro Max $100 (5,000); Power $200 (10,000). A first upgrade from Free gives the rest of that month free plus 500 trial credits valid 12 months. Paid add-on credits $0.04 each (packs $5 to $100, valid 12 months). final_records.name: Warp
final_records.deployment: Desktop client (macOS, Linux, Windows) and Warp Agent CLI, with Warp-cloud agent harness, control plane and run-data storage. Enterprise can self-host cloud-agent execution workers (Docker, Kubernetes, Direct or Command backends) and map cloud-agent run transcripts, artifacts and prompt attachments to its own AWS S3 bucket (Azure Blob Storage on request). Private networking (listed under Enterprise features; set up with Warp's account team via Private Service Connect, AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link, on-premises interconnect or IPsec VPN) lets Warp's hosted backend reach a private team-managed LLM gateway or MCP server. Orchestration, run records and the Warp Agent harness still run in Warp's cloud.
final_records.model_backend: Warp-managed models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and open-weights models hosted by Fireworks AI (e.g. GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek, MiniMax), plus Auto and custom routers. Customer-supplied inference: personal BYOK (OpenAI, Anthropic or Google keys), ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscription and OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints (public URL only, e.g. OpenRouter, LiteLLM, z.ai), limited to individuals and organisations with 10 or fewer employees; team-managed keys and endpoints on Business and Enterprise; Enterprise BYOLLM via AWS Bedrock (Claude and OpenAI models) or Gemini Enterprise (Vertex AI; Gemini and Claude partner models). All Warp Agent routes are relayed through Warp's server-side harness; Claude consumer subscriptions are not supported.
final_records.data_handling_note: Tier-specific. Business and Enterprise: Warp's privacy docs (last updated 3 Nov 2026) say these plans are covered by its ZDR agreement and no AI interaction or console data is collected; data collection is off by default and admin-enforceable. Free: telemetry must stay on to use AI features, and Warp's agent FAQ reserves the right to use collected data to train models (the privacy notice, last modified 18 Aug 2026, also lists model training as a purpose). Other paid plans (docs: 'paid teams'): data collection is on by default; users can opt out and keep AI. Provider ZDR (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Fireworks AI) covers Warp-managed inference only and excludes Claude Fable 5/5.1, which Anthropic retains (off by default for Enterprise teams; Business default not stated). With customer-supplied inference (BYOK, custom endpoints, ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscriptions, team-managed keys, BYOLLM) provider retention and training follow the user's or team's own provider terms and Warp says it cannot enforce ZDR; its BYOK and endpoint pages say Warp does not train on that relayed content. Team-managed keys fall back to Warp-managed inference when a member has no key, if allowed. Product-level retention remains: cloud-synced conversations (per-user setting; Enterprise admins can disable it org-wide; cloud-agent conversations are always stored) and cloud-agent transcripts, artifacts and attachments sit in Warp-managed storage; only the cloud-agent run data can be mapped to an Enterprise-owned S3 or Azure bucket, which Warp's control plane still reads, writes and periodically accesses for maintenance. Codebase Context keeps embeddings; telemetry, when collected, is kept indefinitely; shared sessions expire after about one week. Warp disclosed a security incident involving a vendor in its infrastructure on 26 Oct 2026; Warp has not published the scope on its docs or legal pages. First-party pages conflict: the privacy page requires telemetry for AI on Free while the security pages and pricing FAQ say any user can opt out (the FAQ calls this 'full ZDR'), and www.warp.dev/legal/security says ZDR is available on the Enterprise plan while the model page says ZDR applies across all plans.

suitability_notes.personal: Business or Enterprise only, with a signed DPA (EU SCCs; subprocessors in the US and Canada). Keep data collection disabled, restrict non-ZDR models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) in the Admin Panel, decide on cloud conversation storage and session/link sharing, and confirm every connected model provider or endpoint; member-provided inference (BYOK, ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscriptions) falls outside Warp's ZDR and can be disabled by admins. Before use, obtain Warp's account of the October 2026 security incident (data categories, affected customers, remediation); Warp has not published it in its docs.
suitability_notes.special: Not suitable under this index's rule: for the Warp Agent, the harness and inference routing run on Warp's servers on every route (BYOK, custom endpoints, subscriptions, team-managed keys, BYOLLM, self-hosted workers). Private networking (an Enterprise-section feature set up with Warp's account team) can connect a private or on-premises LLM gateway, but Warp's hosted backend still assembles and sends the requests; local models can be used only through a public URL or such a Warp-connected gateway. Claude Code or Codex runs on self-hosted workers call their provider directly, but orchestration, transcripts and tool output still pass through Warp's control plane.

compliance: SOC 2 Type II per Warp's security docs and pricing FAQ; report available on request via the Trust Center (security overview: Enterprise customers).
DPA (last modified 22 Aug 2025) incorporating EU SCCs (Module 2); subprocessor list last modified 14 Oct 2026.
Provider ZDR is separate from Warp's own collection and storage; Claude Fable models are excluded from ZDR.

The subprocessor list (last modified 14 Oct 2026) also names Morph LLM (AI-enabled functionality), Cohere, Turbopuffer and Voyage AI (codebase search), Wispr AI (voice transcription) and Docker and Namespace Labs (customer compute hosting); Warp's docs do not state their retention terms. xAI is offered under ZDR but is not on the list.

Security incident: Warp's CEO posted on 26 Oct 2026 that Warp had become aware of an exploitation of a vendor in its infrastructure, detected it within hours and remediated and mitigated the impact. A Warp blog post of 4 Nov 2026 says Warp rotated its Linux GPG signing subkey as a precaution after the incident and has no evidence of misuse. Affected data categories are not stated on Warp's docs or legal pages.
final_records.pricing: As listed on 6 Nov 2026: Free $0 (no included agent usage; pay-as-you-go usage, or bring-your-own inference limited to individuals and organisations with 10 or fewer employees); Build $20/month ($18 billed annually) with $20 of agent usage at API rates; Max $200/month ($180 annually) with $200 of usage; Business $50/user/month ($45 annually; up to 25 seats; $20 usage per seat); Enterprise custom. Warp Factories has separate plans (Pay as you go $0 with usage at 20% above API rates; Build $20/month; Business $50/user/month; Enterprise custom) and usage-based execution. Cloud runs, and Business/Enterprise local runs with customer-supplied inference, incur platform and compute charges; confirm the live amount before purchase.
final_records.academic: No student, non-profit or open-source-team discount: Warp's pricing FAQ states it does not currently offer discounts or program credits for students or non-profits, and the pricing page FAQ extends this to open-source teams.
use_cases: Terminal-native agentic coding with the Warp Agent in the desktop app or the Warp Agent CLI
Cloud agents on the Automation Platform (formerly Oz) triggered by schedules, Slack/Linear/GitHub integrations, API or CLI
Codebase indexing and search across large codebases
Running third-party CLI agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) inside Warp with rich input, notifications and code review
Issue triage, spec writing, implementation and PR review through Warp Factories (Early Access) or cloud agents
Team-wide AI-assisted terminal workflows with centralized Admin Panel governance
Enterprise BYOLLM with self-hosted execution workers
final_records.notes: Cloud-orchestrated terminal and agent platform. The Warp Agent harness runs on Warp's backend, so prompts and context pass through Warp even with BYOK, custom endpoints, team-managed keys, private networking or BYOLLM; Enterprise self-hosting keeps execution, repository clones and runtime secrets (and optionally run data in S3 or Azure Blob Storage) on customer infrastructure. Separate provider ZDR from Warp's own collection, conversation storage and telemetry, and check the exact plan. Warp disclosed a vendor-related security incident in late October 2026; check its scope before handling personal data. The client codebase is open source at github.com/warpdotdev/warp (AGPL-3.0; UI framework crates MIT); the backend that runs the harness and control plane is a Warp-operated cloud service.
final_records.tier_gate: Business or Enterprise with DPA; data collection kept off, non-ZDR models disabled, and Warp's October 2026 incident scope confirmed with the vendor

residual_risks: Warp's control plane orchestrates every run, records run data and routes Warp Agent inference, including runs on self-hosted execution workers; Claude Code or Codex harness runs call their provider directly but still send transcripts and tool output to Warp.
The Warp Agent harness runs server-side, so BYOK and custom-endpoint requests (including tunnelled local models) relay prompts and context through Warp's backend.
Session transcripts, which can contain code context and command output, route through Warp even when execution is self-hosted.

final_records.vendor: Harness, Inc. (bought Augment Code's Cosmos, Auggie CLI and Context Engine assets, announced 2026-10-08); the terms and privacy policy on augmentcode.com still name Augment Computing, Inc. as the contracting party
final_records.deployment: cloud (vendor-hosted Context Engine and inference; Cosmos tool execution in Augment sandboxes or on customer-run daemons, which still send all LLM calls to Augment)
final_records.model_backend: Managed multi-provider selection plus Prism routing: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), Google (Gemini; one model listed as hosted on Vertex AI), xAI (Grok), DeepSeek (hosted on Fireworks and Baseten), Zhipu AI GLM (hosted on Fireworks) and Moonshot AI Kimi (hosted on Fireworks and Baseten). Enterprise BYOK for customers with their own Enterprise Agreement with Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS or GCP. No local or customer-hosted model endpoint documented; the CLI product page's 'bring your own' model line is not backed by any documentation beyond Enterprise BYOK. See current model documentation for versions.
final_records.data_handling_note: Paid plans (Standard, Business, Enterprise) exclude training: pricing FAQ ('Commercial Terms of Service'); Professional and Enterprise Terms v1.9 §1.4 ('Company will not train its Models'); third-party model providers are bound by terms 'at least as protective'. Public pages do not say which terms document governs Standard/Business. The Community Terms v1.9 (2026-01-14) instead grant Augment and its model providers training rights on code, output and usage data; the pricing page lists no free plan, so confirm which terms govern a trial. Product retention: the Context Engine stores indexed code (every workspace file not excluded by .gitignore/.augmentignore); Cosmos session snapshots are kept 14 days; Cosmos Files (Expert outputs and memory) persist on Augment with version history (at least one weekly version kept beyond 30 days; deletions recorded as tombstones); the privacy policy (v1.2, 2025-08-28) gives no fixed periods ('as long as necessary'). No public product-level ZDR. Model use is gated by provider data retention: the models page says only eligible OpenAI GPT models and the Prism options can be used without approving provider data retention in the organisation's model settings, and Enterprise admins can allow-list models by retention policy. Default storage and processing in the US; EU tenants can enforce EU-inference-only; data residency and CMEK are Enterprise-only on the pricing page, and BYOK is documented in the Enterprise admin guide. DPA and subprocessor list on request (privacy policy). Harness's public subprocessor list now tags Google (US and EU data centres) and AWS as subprocessors for 'Augment Code' but names no model provider, so it is incomplete for this product. Telemetry goes to an Augment analytics endpoint; the terms exclude customer code from usage data; no telemetry opt-out was found.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a paid plan (no training under the commercial terms) and request a DPA, asking which entity (Augment Computing, Inc. or Harness, Inc.) signs it. Use .augmentignore to keep personal-data files out of the stored index; it is documented as an indexing exclusion only, and the IntelliJ and VS Code changelogs (Sep 14) show the agent can still read such files after user approval, so keep personal data out of the workspace and do not store it in Cosmos Files. Prefer Enterprise for an EU tenant with EU-inference-only and model allow-listing by retention policy; on other plans, leave provider data retention unapproved so only the models that do not need it are offered.
suitability_notes.special: Inference and the Context Engine run in Augment's cloud. This holds with self-hosted Cosmos daemons too (the docs say all LLM calls go to Augment), and BYOK only moves inference to another cloud account. The HIPAA/BAA claim on the security page does not meet this catalog's special-category rule.

ISO/IEC 42001 certification and CMEK listed for Enterprise
Security page self-declares GDPR, CCPA and HIPAA compliance and BAA availability; contractual scope not verified

final_records.notes: Augment's agentic coding platform: Auggie CLI (terminal, CI, ACP clients), the Cosmos event-driven agent platform and IDE extensions, all backed by the vendor-hosted Context Engine. On 2026-10-08 Augment and Harness announced Harness's acquisition of Cosmos, the Auggie CLI, the Context Engine and related technology; Harness says Cosmos will become the Harness Cosmos Software Factory Agent and that Harness Cosmos is now available. On 2026-11-06 the augmentcode.com footer reads '© 2026 Harness, Inc.', Harness's Cosmos product page sends sign-ups to cosmos.augmentcode.com (the same service), and the terms (v1.9) and privacy policy (v1.2) still name Augment Computing, Inc. and are unchanged since Aug 2025 / Jan 2026. final_records.tier_gate: Paid Standard/Business/Enterprise plan under Augment's commercial terms (not the Community Terms) + DPA on request; EU residency/EU-inference, CMEK and BYOK are Enterprise-only; no customer-controlled inference route; Harness Cosmos sign-up leads to the same cosmos.augmentcode.com service; confirm the contracting entity (Augment Computing, Inc. vs Harness, Inc.) before signing

residual_risks: Inference and Context Engine indexing run on Augment-operated cloud services; self-hosted Cosmos daemons execute tools locally but still send all LLM calls to Augment.
