Product assets were acquired by Harness (announced 2026-10-08); the site is now '© Harness, Inc.' and Harness's subprocessor list covers 'Augment Code', while the terms still name Augment Computing, Inc., so the processor and DPA counterparty are unclear.

Early-access, feature-flagged self-hosted Kubernetes sandboxes for Cosmos are another execution layer that needs outbound access to Augment's Cosmos gateway; the guide does not say where inference runs, so treat them like daemons.

final_records.name: mini-SWE-agent
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: LiteLLM by default (most providers), plus OpenRouter, Portkey and Requesty model classes; local models through LiteLLM-compatible endpoints such as Ollama or vLLM
final_records.data_handling_note: The agent runs locally and no telemetry is documented for mini itself (a source search found none). With a local model (e.g. vLLM, or Ollama in local-only mode) and Docker or Singularity/Apptainer execution on controlled hardware, code and prompts stay on that infrastructure, provided network egress from the execution environment is restricted: mini's default container settings add no network restriction. Cloud model providers, hosted routers (OpenRouter, Portkey, Requesty) and the cloud execution backends swerex_modal (Modal) and contree (ConTree) each create separate external processing boundaries. The default local environment runs commands directly on the host with no isolation. mini saves the full history of the last run to the global config directory, and API keys can be stored there in a .env file. The documented experimental bubblewrap environment (Linux-only, unprivileged sandboxing) was not assessed for the special-category route.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a fully local model and isolated execution, or independently approve each selected cloud model provider, router or cloud execution service (e.g. Modal, ConTree) under a DPA.
suitability_notes.special: Requires a fully local model (Ollama only in local-only mode) plus Docker or Singularity/Apptainer execution on controlled hardware with network egress restricted. Cloud models, hosted routers, cloud execution backends (swerex_modal, contree) and unisolated host execution are not acceptable.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free and open source (MIT); any selected cloud model provider, router or cloud execution service (e.g. Modal, ConTree) is billed separately
final_records.academic: Free academic open-source project
use_cases: autonomous issue resolution
software-engineering agent research
SWE-bench-style evaluation
trajectory generation in isolated environments
final_records.notes: Lightweight coding agent from the Princeton and Stanford team behind SWE-bench and SWE-agent, with local-model support. Default host execution is not isolated; use Docker or Singularity/Apptainer on controlled hardware. Latest release v2.4.6 (2026-07-23; also the latest on PyPI on 2026-11-06). No maintainer activity found since 2026-10-05: last commit to main 2026-09-03, no maintainer comment, review or merge since then, and 91 open PRs on 2026-11-06 (38 opened since 2026-10-10). The repository is not archived and community issues and PRs keep arriving. If there is still no maintainer activity at the next refresh, review retention.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local model + isolated execution for regulated data

required_controls: Local inference endpoint on the same host or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network (e.g. Ollama or vLLM), reached directly with no gateway that forwards to external providers, and configured through LiteLLM model_kwargs (custom_llm_provider, api_base).

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Docker or Singularity/Apptainer environment class on controlled hardware instead of the default local (host) environment.

Restrict network egress from the execution environment (through the Docker run_args setting or host/cluster firewall rules) and block outbound traffic from the host running mini except to the model endpoint, then verify the block; mini's container defaults set no network restriction.

No cloud model providers or hosted routers (OpenRouter, Portkey, Requesty) and no cloud execution backends (swerex_modal, contree); keep no cloud provider or router API keys in the environment or in mini's global .env file.
Check the effective model and environment configuration before each sensitive run, including the agent config file and global settings set through environment variables or the global .env file.
On firewalled or air-gapped hosts set LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True, because LiteLLM otherwise pulls its hosted model cost map.
residual_risks: The default local environment runs agent commands directly on the host with no isolation; one misconfigured run exposes the host and its files.

Agent-generated shell commands run with whatever network access the execution environment has; mini's default Docker and Singularity settings do not restrict it, so data can leave the boundary unless egress is blocked.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost api_base alone does not show that inference stays local.
Full run trajectories (saved by default to the global config directory), .env API keys and container images persist locally and require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
LiteLLM is a third-party dependency; since 2026-03-24 the project has excluded litellm 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 as compromised. Pin and vet dependency versions.
LiteLLM's outbound behaviour beyond the documented cost-map fetch (telemetry, callbacks) was not established, so air-gapped operation is unverified; rely on the egress block.
The README claim of >74% on SWE-bench verified names no model in the fetched text; small local models may perform far below published scores.

final_records.name: gptme
final_records.vendor: Superuser Labs Lund AB (Erik Bjäreholt) / gptme open-source community
final_records.deployment: Local CLI/TUI and desktop app; self-hostable gptme-server + web UI (Docker Compose documented); optional gptme.ai managed cloud service (beta)
final_records.model_backend: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Moonshot, NVIDIA, Azure OpenAI, Requesty, OpenCode Go, OpenRouter (100+ models; API key or browser sign-in); ChatGPT Plus/Pro and SuperGrok subscription sign-in; gptme.ai managed gateway; local/self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama-cpp-python); third-party provider plugins
final_records.data_handling_note: Local route: the MIT client runs tools with the user's permissions and saves every conversation, including tool calls, in local logs (~/.local/share/gptme/logs). With a local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama in local-only mode, LM Studio, vLLM), inference stays on the machine. Optional OpenTelemetry tracing is off by default (GPTME_TELEMETRY_ENABLED default false). Offline use needs a pre-cached tiktoken tokenizer, because gptme may otherwise fetch it. Cloud routes send prompts and any file content the agent reads to the chosen provider. OpenRouter requests default to data_collection='deny', which restricts routing to endpoints OpenRouter classifies as non-training but does not prove deletion: require OpenRouter ZDR when retention matters. ChatGPT Plus/Pro and SuperGrok subscription routes, and the OpenCode Go plan, fall under those services' own terms (not reviewed here). gptme.ai managed service (beta) has a provisional privacy policy (v0.1.4, updated 2026-10-02) naming Superuser Labs Lund AB as data controller. It states no training on instance content; instance data is kept while the instance exists and deleted 30 days after deletion; LLM request metadata (no prompt or completion content) is kept 1–90 days (default 90) and server logs 90 days. Conversation content is sent to third-party model providers: the policy lists OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter, and the ToS (v0.2.1, updated 2026-10-10) adds OpenRouter sub-providers and Google; the gptme/ gateway's default model is now routed via OpenRouter. Hosting uses Google Cloud GKE and Supabase in the EU, but the policy says some infrastructure and processors operate outside the EU (SCCs or comparable safeguards). Product analytics and error reporting via PostHog (EU) and cookieless Cloudflare web analytics; LLM gateway usage telemetry (metadata only) is opt-in. No DPA was located.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a fully local model and controlled execution. gptme.ai has provisional privacy terms, which name Superuser Labs Lund AB as data controller, and no DPA/processor agreement was found; do not use it, or ChatGPT/SuperGrok consumer-subscription routes, for personal data.
suitability_notes.special: Only the MIT client talking directly to a local model server (Ollama in local-only mode, LM Studio or vLLM) on the same host or on institution-owned hardware inside the network, run in a container/VM or restricted account with OS-level egress blocking (profile 'no network' rules are prompt-level only). Cloud providers, subscription routes and gptme.ai (managed instances or the gptme/ gateway provider) are not acceptable.

final_records.pricing: MIT client free; model providers billed separately (or via an existing ChatGPT Plus/Pro or SuperGrok subscription). gptme.ai (beta): free managed accounts admitted in cohorts (1 instance, no monthly credits); Pro $10.00/month incl. 10,000 credits, up to 2 managed instances and 1 GB storage; extra 10,000 credits $10.00; Enterprise custom (checked 2026-11-06).

Web research with the read-only 'researcher' profile

final_records.notes: Local-capable MIT terminal agent (also TUI, desktop app, self-hostable server) from Superuser Labs. Actively maintained: v0.35.0/v0.35.1 on 2026-10-15, v0.36.0 on 2026-11-02, dev pre-releases to 2026-11-05, and commits through 2026-11-04 from the maintainer, outside contributors and the project's autonomous agent 'Bob'. The OpenRouter data_collection='deny' default restricts routing to endpoints OpenRouter classifies as non-training but does not guarantee deletion.

required_controls: Configure only a local/ or [[providers]] endpoint served by Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM on the same host or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network, reached directly with no gateway or proxy that forwards to external providers; point every model the configuration uses at that endpoint.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Keep no cloud API keys in the environment, gptme configuration or ~/.config/gptme/credentials.toml, and no subscription or provider sign-ins (openai-subscription, grok-subscription, OpenRouter browser sign-in) or gptme.ai login (including the gptme/ gateway provider) on the host; remove any grok CLI login (~/.grok/auth.json), which gptme reuses automatically.
Run in a container/VM or restricted user account with OS/network-level egress blocking, and test that the block holds; agent-profile 'no network' rules are not enforced at tool level.
Leave GPTME_TELEMETRY_ENABLED unset/false and pre-cache the tiktoken cl100k_base tokenizer for offline operation.
Apply institutional access, encryption and retention controls to local conversation logs (~/.local/share/gptme/logs), which include tool calls and outputs.

Restrict tools (--tools allowlist or agent profile) and leave out the browser tool and other web tools in sensitive sessions; keep confirmations on for sensitive work, and consider GPTME_GUARDRAILS=enforce.

Check the effective configuration before sensitive sessions: environment variables (provider keys, OPENAI_BASE_URL), gptme.toml, hooks, plugins and MCP servers; keep gptme-server on localhost or behind authenticated TLS.
Use the CLI/TUI on controlled hosts; if the desktop app is used, block its self-update or manage updates centrally and roll out reviewed releases.
residual_risks: Shell, Python, file and browser tools act with the user's permissions; the OS-level sandbox (GPTME_SANDBOX) is documented as not yet widely used.
Agent-profile read_only/no_network behaviour rules are soft (system-prompt only).
GPTME_GUARDRAILS only logs by default; blocking requires enforce mode.
Small local models misuse tools more often; models under ~7B rarely follow the tool protocol reliably.
MCP servers, plugins and the browser tool can move data off-host wherever network access is available.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost endpoint setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
The desktop app checks GitHub releases and self-updates, so a reviewed configuration can change with an update.
Local logs persist; no automatic retention limit was found in the reviewed docs.

final_records.name: Open Interpreter
final_records.deployment: local-capable / optional hosted inference
final_records.model_backend: Rust terminal agent forked from OpenAI's Codex. Built-in providers are OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock and local Ollama/LM Studio; a generated catalogue adds hosted providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, Z.ai, Qwen, Groq), and custom Responses, Chat Completions or Anthropic Messages endpoints can be added. Model-specific harnesses shape requests. Open Interpreter-hosted models are a separate route.
final_records.data_handling_note: Route-dependent. Local Ollama/LM Studio providers keep model traffic on the machine (for Ollama only in local-only mode, because a signed-in Ollama server can also serve ':cloud' models through localhost); own API keys send content directly to that provider under its terms; Open Interpreter-hosted models pass through its servers, which log full prompts, responses, attachments and metadata for up to 30 days (privacy policy updated 14 July 2026; no training by Open Interpreter; US hosting possible). Sessions, logs and file-stored credentials are kept locally under ~/.openinterpreter; history.persistence="none" stops only the global prompt-history file (history.jsonl), and session records are still written (exec --ephemeral skips them for non-interactive runs). Source code (not the docs) shows analytics on by default: OTEL usage metrics to a Codex-inherited Statsig endpoint and, when signed in (all events with ChatGPT sign-in, plugin events only with API-key auth), events to an Open Interpreter endpoint; [analytics] enabled=false turns both off. User-initiated /feedback reports, which can attach session files, go by default to a Codex-inherited Sentry endpoint ([feedback] enabled=false disables the flow). Web search, MCP, memories and tools are separate data paths.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local model, or a direct provider under an institutional agreement. Open Interpreter-hosted models log full requests for up to 30 days and no public DPA was found, so do not use them for personal data.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a fully local model on controlled infrastructure (Ollama in local-only mode, no :cloud models), analytics/metrics export, web search and ChatGPT sign-in disabled, and network egress restricted. Hosted and direct cloud-provider routes are not acceptable.

final_records.pricing: The terminal agent is free Apache-2.0 software; chosen inference providers bill separately. The separate Interpreter Desktop app lists Free ($0/mo), Pro ($20/mo, adds Open Interpreter-hosted models) and Business ($60/mo) plans; the site does not say whether these plans extend hosted models to the CLI.
final_records.academic: No academic discount is listed; the open-source terminal agent has no software fee.
use_cases: local coding and shell automation
shell and file automation in a repository
code generation and execution
agentic workflows with local or direct-provider models
final_records.notes: Current product is a Rust fork of OpenAI's Codex with frequent releases (0.0.59 on 4 November 2026), now positioned as a coding agent for open, low-cost models. The original Python project continues as a community fork (endolith/open-interpreter). Interpreter Desktop is a separate app with its own plans. Controlled-data use requires a fully local model with analytics/metrics export, web search, ChatGPT sign-in and memories disabled, and institutional controls on locally stored sessions.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local model for special-category data; local model or institutionally contracted direct provider for personal data

required_controls: Run inference only through a local provider (Ollama or LM Studio via --oss) on infrastructure the institution controls, with every model role the configuration exposes pinned to it; no Open Interpreter-hosted, ChatGPT sign-in or direct cloud-provider route, and no cloud-provider API keys in the environment, .env files or ~/.openinterpreter credential storage.

Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1, or "disable_ollama_cloud": true in ~/.ollama/server.json of the account that runs the server), restart it, confirm the log shows 'Ollama cloud disabled: true', and serve no :cloud models.

Set [analytics] enabled = false (optionally also [otel] metrics_exporter = "none") so usage metrics and analytics events are not exported, and set [feedback] enabled = false so /feedback reports (which can attach session files) cannot be sent.
Set web_search = "disabled", keep memories off, and connect only vetted local MCP servers.
Keep sandbox_mode read-only or workspace-write with network off, set check_for_update_on_startup = false, and enforce host-level egress controls and test them on the deployed version.

Apply institutional retention and access controls to ~/.openinterpreter (sessions, logs, file-stored credentials); [history] persistence = "none" only stops the prompt-history file, and session records are still written unless non-interactive runs use exec --ephemeral.
Before use, check the effective configuration with /debug-config, because managed, user, trusted-project, profile and CLI layers can override these settings.
residual_risks: Telemetry and feedback defaults were established from source code and the generated config schema, not the user docs; runtime network behaviour was not observed and may change across frequent releases (feedback delivery changed in 0.0.58).
Layered configuration (managed, user, trusted project, profile, CLI overrides) can re-enable network access or features; check the effective config with /debug-config.

A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a session pointed at local Ollama can still send prompts to Ollama's cloud unless local-only mode is enabled.
Local model tool use can fail silently when the server context is too small; the docs warn this is not evidence the requested action happened.
The docs describe history.persistence = "none" as disabling saved transcript history, but the source limits it to history.jsonl; full session records persist locally.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Kilo Code
final_records.vendor: Anaconda, Inc. (Kilo Code, Inc., acquired July 2026)
final_records.deployment: Local client (VS Code, JetBrains, CLI; Kilo Desktop beta). Default inference goes through the hosted Kilo Gateway, and Cloud Agents, Code Reviewer, cloud sessions, Slack and mobile run on Kilo cloud services. A fully local route can be configured.
final_records.model_backend: Configurable: local Ollama, LM Studio, Atomic Chat or Anaconda Desktop model servers (Kilo Desktop also has its own local model server, which needs Kilo sign-in); self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints; BYOK cloud providers; Kilo Gateway (500+ models, 60+ providers; Auto Model Frontier/Efficient/Free tiers); ChatGPT Plus/Pro usage via Sign in with ChatGPT, routed through Kilo's model gateway. Ollama Cloud is a hosted route, not local inference.
final_records.data_handling_note: A fully local route is documented: Ollama/LM Studio/Atomic Chat inference, Ollama embeddings with LanceDB indexing, and local sessions in a local SQLite database. It requires explicit configuration: if small_model is left unset while signed in, background tasks fall back to Kilo Gateway's kilo-auto/small, autocomplete defaults to the Kilo provider, and voice transcription, when used, goes through Kilo Gateway by default. Product telemetry (usage events) is on by default, with a documented opt-out. On hosted routes, Kilo's Enterprise FAQ says Kilo does not train on code or prompts, and the security page says paid plans support no retention of AI prompts and outputs. However, the Terms (Anaconda, Inc., last updated 2 Nov 2026; this clause is unchanged from the 30 Sep 2026 version) grant a perpetual, irrevocable licence to use Customer Data to provide and improve the Services and Kilo's other products. Under the same Terms, declining to let an AI model train on your data may limit which models you can use. The Kilo subprocessor list (entries of 21 Sep 2026) names Sentry, Axiom, Supabase and Vercel as processing prompts, and Exa and Zilliz as processing queries and prompt-derived embeddings; 14 further entries added on 20 Oct 2026 have blank purpose and data fields (by name, AI model and inference companies, among them Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud, BytePlus, MiniMax, StepFun, Xiaomi, NVIDIA and Mistral AI). The privacy policy (29 May 2026) says Sentry receives no prompt content. Auto Free may route to providers that log prompts and use them to improve their services. Training and retention otherwise depend on the selected model provider. The Terms bar HIPAA-type regulated data.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer the fully local route. Hosted routes need an institutional agreement with a DPA (Enterprise), provider and model allowlists (Enterprise) that exclude prompt-training or prompt-retaining providers, no Auto Free, and review of Kilo's subprocessors. EU data residency is only an Enterprise, contract-scoped option.
suitability_notes.special: Only the fully local route on controlled hardware: local inference (Ollama in local-only mode with no :cloud models, LM Studio or Atomic Chat), small_model set to the same local provider, autocomplete and voice transcription disabled, logged out of Kilo Gateway, webfetch and websearch denied, local embeddings with LanceDB or self-hosted Qdrant, telemetry off, local sessions only, no Kilo Desktop and no cloud features. All Kilo cloud routes are excluded. The Terms prohibit providing regulated sensitive data to Kilo; obtain written confirmation from Kilo/Anaconda that this does not restrict fully local use, or written permission.

compliance: Trust Center (trust.kilo.ai now redirects to Anaconda's Trust Center) lists a SOC 2 Type 1 item for the Kilo Code product; report access-gated, scope and date not reviewed
Anaconda's SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 listings are scoped to the Anaconda (default) product and are not shown as covering Kilo services
DPA, MSA and a Kilo-specific subprocessor list offered for enterprise review (entries created 21 Sep 2026, plus 14 entries added 20 Oct 2026 with blank purpose and data fields)
EU data residency available only as an Enterprise, contract-scoped configuration
final_records.pricing: VS Code, JetBrains and CLI clients free and open source (MIT); Kilo Desktop (beta) licence unconfirmed. The Free plan card now also lists commercial use of 40K+ Anaconda Core packages; under Terms §5(E) (2 Nov 2026) that right covers only packages 'Used with Kilo'. Inference is billed separately: free, local or BYOK models at $0; Kilo Gateway pay-as-you-go at provider rates plus a 5% processing fee on credit purchases; optional Kilo Pass at $19/$49/$199 per month with up to 50% bonus credits. Teams $15/user/month; Enterprise custom; the 14-day trial is an Enterprise trial. Cloud compute (Cloud Agents, Code Review) is billed per second on top of inference.

final_records.notes: Anaconda, Inc. acquired Kilo Code (announced 15 July 2026). The Terms of Service contract with Anaconda, Inc. and were last updated on 2 Nov 2026; existing users are bound from the earliest of accepting them, first using Kilo Desktop or obtaining an Anaconda artifact, or 30 days after the update (2 Dec 2026). Compared with the 30 Sep 2026 version, the 2 Nov update limits the Anaconda Package Artifact licence to 'Use with Kilo'; the Customer Data licence and the regulated-data prohibition are unchanged. The privacy policy (last updated 29 May 2026) still names Kilo Code Inc. as controller. Kilo Desktop (beta) is covered by this record, not a separate one; it adds notebooks, conda environments and a local model server, all of which require Kilo sign-in, and since version 0.1.12 (15 Oct 2026) it requires acceptance of the Terms before use. Openness is open-core at record level: the VS Code, JetBrains and CLI clients are MIT-licensed (Kilo-Org/kilocode), while Kilo Gateway, Cloud Agents and Code Reviewer are vendor-hosted services and no public source or licence was found for Kilo Desktop. The special-category recommendation applies only to the fully local route, and the paid-plan no-retention wording is not a guarantee for every route.
final_records.tier_gate: Special-category: fully local inference and indexing (Ollama in local-only mode), small_model on the local provider, autocomplete and voice transcription disabled, logged out of Kilo Gateway, telemetry and cloud features off, no Kilo Desktop, and written confirmation from Kilo/Anaconda that the Terms' regulated-data prohibition does not cover fully local use. Hosted personal data: Enterprise (DPA, provider/model allowlists, audit logs, EU residency scoping); Teams lists organization 'data privacy controls' (contents not documented on the pricing page).

required_controls: Use only local inference (Ollama via ollama serve, LM Studio, Atomic Chat, or Anaconda Desktop after institutional review of its own sign-in, telemetry and data handling) on the same controlled machine; exclude Kilo Gateway (including Auto models and Auto Free), Ollama Cloud, Sign in with ChatGPT and cloud BYOK providers

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models

Set small_model explicitly to the same local provider, leave subagent_model unset, disable autocomplete, and log out of Kilo Gateway in the IDE extension or TUI so nothing falls back to kilo-auto/small
Keep codebase indexing local: Ollama or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible embeddings with LanceDB or a self-hosted Qdrant

If small_model is left unset while signed in, background tasks (session titles, commit messages, prompt enhancement) silently use Kilo Gateway's kilo-auto/small; autocomplete defaults to the Kilo provider

A misconfiguration (Ollama Cloud, a Gateway model, or no configured model, where Kilo's model precedence ends at Auto Free) moves prompts and code to hosted providers

Ownership moved to Anaconda and the Terms were updated again on 2 Nov 2026 (binding existing users by 2 Dec 2026 at the latest); the Terms do not say whether they govern fully local use of the MIT client. Re-check terms and defaults on each upgrade
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls

final_records.name: Google Colab (Data Science Agent)
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Google-hosted Gemini models. The BigQuery Data Science Agent guide (last updated 2026-10-27) lets users choose a model and names the default as "Gemini 3.0 Flash"; the Colab Enterprise guide and the consumer Colab FAQ name no model. Treat the model as Google-managed and subject to change.
final_records.data_handling_note: Colab Enterprise: Google states that Gemini does not use prompts or responses to train its models, and handles prompts under the Google Cloud terms and Cloud Data Processing Addendum; the Cloud Service Specific Terms also bar training on Customer Data without the customer's permission. Data Science Agent session data, such as conversation history, is stored at rest; the Colab Enterprise CMEK page says it is encrypted with the default runtime template's CMEK key, but the BigQuery Data Science Agent guide says CMEK is not supported. No retention period and no agent-specific zero-data-retention option are documented. Google does not guarantee that Data Science Agent requests are processed in the notebook's region. Consumer Colab (free or paid): Google collects prompts, related code, outputs, feature usage and feedback to improve products and machine-learning technologies; human reviewers may read them; data is stored so it cannot be linked to the user, deletion requests can then no longer be fulfilled, and it is kept up to 18 months; Google asks users not to include sensitive or personal information.

suitability_notes.personal: Use only Colab Enterprise in a Google Cloud project under an accepted Cloud DPA, with institutional review of region, VPC Service Controls and CMEK. Gemini processing may happen outside the notebook region, so check transfer terms. Consumer Colab AI is not suitable, including paid Colab or Google AI plans and Workspace accounts, where Colab is administered as an additional Google service.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. Do not use for special-category data under this index's controlled-infrastructure rule.

compliance: Google Cloud controls only where the exact Colab Enterprise service, region, and contract are in scope
Colab Enterprise documents VPC Service Controls and CMEK support for the Data Science Agent; the BigQuery Data Science Agent guide lists CMEK as unsupported, so confirm for the access path used
final_records.pricing: Colab Enterprise: Google's BigQuery product page lists Data Science Agent usage at USD 3 per million input tokens and USD 20 per million output tokens (the same rates as the Data Engineering and Conversational Analytics agents; list prices checked 2026-11-06). Runtime compute is billed separately: the Colab pricing page now lists only runtime prices (machines, accelerators, disks). Other Gemini in Colab Enterprise assistance is "currently available to try at no additional cost". Consumer Colab: free tier plus Colab Pro, Pro+ and Pay As You Go at country-specific prices on the sign-up page; eligible paid Google AI plans also add Colab compute benefits.
final_records.academic: No academic privacy tier was confirmed. Colab Pro for Education (free one-year Pro for US university students and faculty) is closed to new sign-ups; educational use does not change data-handling terms.
use_cases: Automated EDA (exploratory data analysis) from natural language prompts
Agent-planned Python notebook code for data cleaning, visualisation and predictive modelling
Statistical analysis and feature engineering
BigQuery-scale data processing with BigQuery DataFrames and BigQuery ML (Colab Enterprise)
Distributed processing with PySpark via Managed Service for Apache Spark (Apache Spark 4.0 code only)

Model training and evaluation within notebook environment

Google now documents Colab Enterprise as part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI). Consumer and Enterprise data terms differ substantially. Google's own docs disagree on CMEK for the agent (Colab Enterprise guide and CMEK page: supported; BigQuery guide: not supported). Avoid fixed model identities and broad GCP certifications without product, region and contract scope.

residual_risks: Cloud-only. Do not use for special-category data under this index's controlled-infrastructure rule.
