Agent session data such as conversation history is stored at rest by Google; no retention period is documented.
CMEK support for the agent is contested between Google's Colab Enterprise and BigQuery guides; VPC Service Controls and CMEK are Google Cloud controls, not a customer-controlled inference boundary.

final_records.name: Deepnote
final_records.deployment: Multi-tenant cloud (US, us-east-1) / Enterprise single-tenant (Deepnote-managed, or in the customer's own AWS, GCP or Azure account) or on-premise; no air-gapped option. Open-source VS Code extension, CLI and toolkit run notebooks locally.
final_records.model_backend: Native OpenAI and Anthropic models (chosen in Settings & members → AI, or Automatic). Enterprise adds OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints for Agent, block edits and prompt suggestions, plus EU-hosted OpenAI via Azure Sweden Central. Code completions use a separate Deepnote completions provider. The open-source CLI agent block supports OpenAI, Anthropic and a separate openai-compatible provider (OpenRouter, Ollama and LiteLLM documented, via DEEPNOTE_AGENT_BASE_URL); with no provider or model set it defaults to OpenAI.
final_records.data_handling_note: Deepnote states AI-processed content is not used for model training, that its provider agreements prohibit training, and that it does not host or fine-tune models. The AI privacy page and the security overview (rewritten since October) both say AI context can be retained by providers for safety (OpenAI up to 30 days) and cite zero-retention only for real-time code suggestions from certain providers; the security overview no longer states ZDR for Anthropic. The AI privacy page says context can be processed in the US and worldwide; the security page lists OpenAI and Anthropic as US subprocessors. Product-level retention of prompts, agent history and AI-action logs is not published. Other compute providers may store an encrypted temporary copy of workspace data, with AWS used for long-term storage. Sharing block outputs (which can include row-level data) with the LLM is a separate switch, and admins can disable Deepnote AI. The terms let Deepnote use usage statistics (not Customer Data) to improve the product. Enterprise custom endpoints cover Agent, edits and suggestions but not code completions.

suitability_notes.personal: The default multi-tenant cloud runs in the US (us-east-1, per the June 2025 deployment whitepaper), and Deepnote states AI context can be processed in the US and worldwide, with provider safety retention. Use an Enterprise agreement/DPA with single-tenant EU residency (EU-hosted OpenAI covers only OpenAI-model inference), or a customer-operated deployment with a controlled endpoint. Configure code completions and block-output sharing separately.
suitability_notes.special: Only a customer-managed Enterprise deployment (own cloud account or on-premise) with a customer-controlled model endpoint that serves only institution-hosted models can qualify. Disable code completions and block-output sharing, block native AI providers at egress, restrict external MCP access and the Agent's MCP integrations, configure any CLI agent block explicitly, review every integration and obtain institutional approval. Deepnote Cloud and Deepnote-hosted single-tenant deployments do not qualify.

compliance: Deepnote states SOC 2 Type II; pricing lists HIPAA compliance on Enterprise, and the acceptable use policy permits PHI only under a signed BAA. Exact deployment and signed DPA/BAA scope must be confirmed.
final_records.pricing: Free (3 editors, 5 projects, limited AI: 5 Agent calls and 10 code completions per month), Team and Enterprise (custom) are listed. Team is displayed at $39/editor/month billed yearly and includes $39 of AI credits plus CPU and GPU compute credits per month; the billing docs say AI use beyond a plan's quota is billed pay-as-you-go, with an admin-set monthly overage limit, while the Enterprise card lists Unlimited AI. Additional machines are pay-as-you-go on Team and Enterprise; Enterprise pricing and deployment terms are by quote.
final_records.academic: Free Education plan for students, teachers and researchers verified by school email (an Education workspace can invite educators and students). The education overview and FAQ exclude Deepnote AI, scheduling and advanced machines and limit the plan to learning and teaching; the verification page's 'all Deepnote features' wording conflicts. No institution-wide academic entitlement found.
use_cases: Collaborative data science notebooks (Python, R, SQL)
AI-assisted data analysis and code generation (Deepnote Agent, which absorbed Auto AI in October 2026)
Data team workflows with real-time multiplayer editing
Database querying and exploration (100+ native integrations)
Scheduled notebook execution and background jobs
Deploying data apps and running notebooks programmatically via the Deepnote API
Version-controlled notebooks with YAML format (.deepnote) for git workflows
Local notebook development with the VS Code extension (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity)
Connecting external coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to a workspace via Deepnote MCP or the open-source CLI
final_records.notes: Cloud collaborative notebook with Enterprise customer-managed or on-premise deployment; Deepnote states no air-gapped option. The open-source CLI (0.11.0, under active development) can run an agent block locally against a self-hosted endpoint through its openai-compatible provider, but it defaults to OpenAI unless configured, is headless and is not a complete local AI product; a local 'Singleplayer' app is still announced as coming soon. Agents connected through Deepnote MCP/API can write files and delete projects, notebooks and blocks; delete_file (added 30 Oct 2026) is permanent. Licence scope: Apache-2.0 covers the open-source .deepnote format, CLI, MCP and toolkit packages; the VS Code extension is MIT-licensed; Deepnote Cloud and the Enterprise platform are proprietary.
final_records.tier_gate: Enterprise for custom AI endpoints, single-tenant/customer-cloud/on-premise deployment and HIPAA/BAA; special data only with a customer-managed deployment plus a customer-controlled model endpoint

required_controls: Enterprise deployment in the institution's own cloud account or on-premise (not Deepnote-hosted single-tenant)

Customer-controlled OpenAI-compatible endpoint set as workspace default for Agent, edits and suggestions; the endpoint serves only models hosted on institution-controlled hardware and forwards nothing to external providers (verify with egress monitoring)
Code completions disabled
Native OpenAI/Anthropic providers blocked at network egress and the block tested; per-user model selection confirmed with Deepnote
Block-output sharing disabled
External MCP client access disabled or limited to approved clients; the Agent's connected MCP integrations and any other external tools limited to approved services inside the institutional boundary

If the open-source CLI agent block is used, set the provider explicitly to openai-compatible with an institution-controlled DEEPNOTE_AGENT_BASE_URL and model (an omitted or 'auto' model selects OpenAI), and keep no OpenAI or Anthropic API keys or *_BASE_URL overrides pointing outside the institution in the environment or .env files
Deepnote's automated updates and any maintenance access managed under institutional change control, with the effective configuration re-verified after each update
All integrations, telemetry settings and subprocessors reviewed
DPO or data-steward approval before use
residual_risks: Deepnote Cloud and Deepnote-hosted single-tenant deployments do not qualify.

No documented admin switch removes native providers from the Agent model selector, and the custom-models doc says the workspace can switch back to OpenAI or Anthropic from the dropdown at any time; misconfiguration can send notebook content to OpenAI or Anthropic.
Deepnote states it does not support air-gapped deployments; updates, collaboration and remote support need network connectivity, and maintenance access may be requested.

Customer-cloud ownership, automated updates and maintenance access are described in a deployment whitepaper created in June 2025 that the current enterprise page still links; confirm current terms with Deepnote.

The open-source CLI agent block defaults to OpenAI, supports Anthropic as a native provider since CLI 0.10.0 (October 2026), and its provider/endpoint settings have changed between minor versions, so its configuration must be re-checked at each CLI update.
Deepnote does not guarantee Agent quality on custom models; local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Agents connected through Deepnote MCP or the API can delete projects, notebooks and blocks and permanently delete project files (delete_file); restrict API keys and OAuth grants to least privilege.

final_records.name: Databricks Genie Code
final_records.deployment: cloud (Databricks workspace); the Genie Code CLI (Beta) runs in a local terminal, but its model inference goes through Databricks Unity Gateway
final_records.model_backend: Databricks-selected models. With the partner-powered AI features setting on (default for non-CSP workspaces), Genie Code's agentic capabilities use Azure OpenAI Service, OpenAI on Databricks and Anthropic on Databricks (Databricks states the Anthropic endpoints are hosted by Databricks within its security perimeter), and non-agentic chat uses Azure OpenAI Service and OpenAI on Databricks. With it off (default for CSP workspaces), Genie Code runs on a Databricks-hosted open-source model without agentic capabilities; in CSP workspaces this fallback exists only under the HIPAA, FedRAMP Moderate (US), PCI-DSS or HITRUST (US/ANZ) standards. Autocomplete always uses a Databricks-hosted model. Since 2026-09-08 the setting can no longer be switched off in the settings UI (it can still be switched on), and the Settings API can still change it in either direction. Databricks now says the setting will be removed 'at a later date' (the earlier 2026-11-01 date is no longer stated); existing values persist, and after removal changes go through the Databricks account team. The CLI (Beta) uses a Databricks-selected model via Unity Gateway (the specific model can change during Beta).
final_records.data_handling_note: Databricks states it does not use prompts, responses or submitted data to train generative foundation models it makes available to third parties; partner-powered features use partner zero-data-retention endpoints. Product-level retention remains: Genie Code chat history is stored with notebook content (small notebook results default to the Databricks control plane), admins can view a user's chat with a direct link, Genie Code saves automatic cross-session memory, and its agentic capabilities send data samples and cell outputs to the model. Provider ZDR is therefore not end-to-end deletion. These commitments are stated for the workspace AI assistive features; the Genie Code CLI (Beta) sends prompts and local file content as Unity Gateway model usage, and the trust page does not separately document how that traffic is handled.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institutional Databricks agreement on a full (non-Free-Edition) account in a suitable Geo (EU workspaces use a Europe-based model for AI assistive features; keep cross-Geo processing off unless approved), narrow Unity Catalog permissions, the 'Ask first' approval mode, no scheduled tasks or Genie Code job tasks on personal data (both always auto-approve), and defined retention for notebooks, chats and memory. Not on Free Edition, which has no compliance enforcement, SSO or security customisation. Model-provider ZDR is not notebook/chat deletion.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. ZDR / HIPAA-BAA is a contractual assurance, but data still leaves your environment — not appropriate for identifiable or controlled-access (DUA) health/genetic data. Use a tool that runs on infrastructure you control, and confirm with your DPO / IRB.

compliance: Contract-, cloud-, region-, and compliance-profile dependent; verify exact Databricks service scope

HIPAA requires the compliance security profile and an active BAA with Databricks; Genie Code, Genie Code Agent Mode, Genie Code Scheduled Tasks and Genie Code Job Task are listed in the HIPAA regional feature-support table (AWS)
Designated Service under Databricks Geos: content is processed in the workspace Geo unless cross-Geo processing is enabled
final_records.pricing: Pay-as-you-go since 2026-07-08. Each user (service principals excluded) gets 150 DBUs of free Genie LLM usage per month, shared across Genie One, Genie Agents and Genie Code; Genie compute (e.g. SQL Serverless) is billed separately. Usage above the allowance is billed in DBUs under the Serverless Real-Time Inference SKU; the pricing page lists $0.070/DBU (Premium, AWS, US East view; 150 DBUs = $10.50 there; varies by plan, cloud and region). Genie Code has a 25% promotional discount on that price until 2027-01-31; the separate free-usage promotion for Genie One and Genie Agents does not cover Genie Code. Spend controls are Unity Gateway budgets. Genie Code CLI (Beta) is billed as Unity Gateway model usage, not under Genie pricing.
final_records.academic: No research discount or trial-credit amount is asserted. Databricks Free Edition (no cost, quota-limited, non-commercial) includes Genie Code but lacks compliance enforcement, SSO and security customisation, so it suits learning with non-sensitive data only. Institutional programmes require current vendor confirmation.
use_cases: Autonomous multi-step data pipeline engineering (Lakeflow)
Exploratory data analysis and model training in notebooks
AI/BI dashboard generation and analysis
SQL query building and optimization in SQL Editor
Agentic debugging of pipeline failures and errors
Scheduled and job-embedded autonomous data operations (scheduled tasks, Genie Code tasks in Lakeflow Jobs)
GenAI application debugging and evaluation in MLflow
Document processing pipelines (parse, classify, extract) from unstructured files
SQL migration from other warehouse dialects to Databricks SQL (Genie Migrate)
final_records.notes: Cloud data-platform agent in the Databricks workspace (notebooks, SQL editor, Lakeflow, jobs, dashboards, MLflow). Chat history and notebook/control-plane content are kept separately from partner-model retention; automatic cross-session memory is also kept by Databricks (storage location and retention period not documented; users can ask Genie Code to forget or delete memories). Its agentic capabilities read data samples and cell outputs and, on first use, default to classifier-based auto-approve, which Databricks says is not a security boundary; scheduled tasks and Genie Code tasks in Lakeflow Jobs (GA since 2026-10-21) always auto-approve and cannot be switched to manual approval. It can also reach MCP servers, Databricks-provided connectors (e.g. Google Drive, Microsoft 365, Slack, GitHub) and (Beta, admin-enabled) web search. For research data, set 'Ask first' and scope permissions narrowly. Genie Code CLI (Beta, Databricks License) adds a local terminal client with cloud inference.
final_records.tier_gate: Full (non-Free-Edition) Databricks account under an appropriate contract; agentic capabilities need partner-powered AI features and a supported Geo; regulated data needs the compliance security profile (plus an active BAA for PHI) and workspace governance

residual_risks: Cloud-only. ZDR / HIPAA-BAA is a contractual assurance, but data still leaves your environment — not appropriate for identifiable or controlled-access (DUA) health/genetic data. Use a tool that runs on infrastructure you control, and confirm with your DPO / IRB.
Genie Code CLI (Beta) runs locally, but prompts and any file content it reads are processed by Databricks-hosted inference via Unity Gateway; it is not a local-inference route.

final_records.name: Posit AI Pass / Posit Assistant
final_records.deployment: Hosted model service (Posit AI Pass) used from a local client in RStudio, Positron, the pa terminal or own R/Python code (ellmer, chatlas); local-capable with Ollama/LM Studio; self-managed Posit Workbench (Posit Assistant generally available from Workbench 2026.10.0; admin provider/settings controls Preview)
final_records.model_backend: Posit AI Pass: Anthropic Claude models (ZDR agreement) plus open-weights models (GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek) that Posit serves through Baseten; Next Edit Suggestions use Posit-hosted models. The lineup changes often (Claude 5.5 models and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash were listed by November 2026); the in-app model picker is authoritative. Own-provider routes include Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, Snowflake Cortex and others (Databricks, Google Vertex AI, GitHub Copilot, LiteLLM, Portkey and OpenCode are Preview); local Ollama and LM Studio; custom providers for self-hosted or gateway endpoints (OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic protocol; LiteLLM and Portkey custom types are Preview). The OpenRouter built-in provider in Positron needs Positron 2026.11+. Posit Assistant 1.11.0 adds a Posit Connect provider that routes Amazon Bedrock models through the Connect LLM Gateway on Workbench.
final_records.data_handling_note: Posit AI Pass: training on user Content is opt-in at sign-up (Help Improve Posit AI). Opt-in trace data may be used for up to 5 years to train models and improve the service. Opted-out accounts: Posit keeps basic operational data, excluding prompts and responses, for 30 days and does not use it for training or improvement (FAQ). The Service Terms (1 Oct 2026) state that Posit will use Content to provide, maintain, develop, train and improve Posit AI; their Opting Out clause limits training of Posit's models to accounts that opt in. First-party pages disagree on ZDR scope. The FAQ, models page, Responsible Use Policy and product page (updated October 2026) say the model providers are under ZDR (Anthropic for Claude; Baseten for the open-weights models). The Service Terms say some, not all, models. NES runs on Posit-hosted models. Provider ZDR does not remove Posit's own retention. With own-provider or local Ollama/LM Studio routes, Positron documentation states that Posit receives no AI traffic, and the chosen provider's terms apply.

suitability_notes.personal: AI Pass route: leave trace collection off and review the click-through Service Terms (no AI Pass DPA found). The FAQ and the Service Terms disagree on ZDR scope. Alternatively, use an institution-approved provider agreement or a local model.
suitability_notes.special: Only Posit Assistant with an Ollama (in local-only mode) or LM Studio model server on institution-controlled hardware qualifies; on Workbench, enforce it with ai-providers-enforced. Cloud providers do not qualify, including Workbench managed-credential routes (Amazon Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex, Microsoft Foundry) and the Posit Connect LLM Gateway route to Bedrock. Posit AI Pass, NES, web search, remote MCP servers and remote plugin marketplaces must be off. The AI Pass Service Terms prohibit health data; the product page directs such work to an approved provider or a local model, and in this catalog only the local-model option qualifies for special-category data.

compliance: Posit AI Pass Service Terms and Responsible Use Policy (both 1 Oct 2026) prohibit inputting health information, financial information, government ID numbers or other highly sensitive data.

ZDR scope conflict: the FAQ, models page, Responsible Use Policy and product page say the AI Pass model providers are under ZDR; the Service Terms (1 Oct 2026) say some, not all, models. NES runs on Posit-hosted models under Posit's own retention terms.

AI Pass uses individual click-through terms (Massachusetts law; separate EU consumer terms); no DPA for AI Pass was found on fetched first-party pages. Posit's GDPR page offers a DPA on request for Posit Cloud Services (posit.cloud, shinyapps.io); whether it covers AI Pass is unconfirmed.

On Workbench, Posit Assistant is generally available from 2026.10.0, but its admin provider/settings controls are Preview (Enhanced and Advanced licence tiers); Posit describes administrator-managed settings as best-effort policy, not a security boundary.
final_records.pricing: Posit AI Pass Pro: $20/month including $15 of monthly Posit Assistant credits (no rollover) and unlimited NES; credit usage is charged at a 10% premium over model-provider rates. The free trial ended in September 2026; eligible new subscribers pay $5 for the first month, and a payment card is required. Extra credits: one-time purchases of $20-$250, or opt-in auto-recharge with an optional monthly cap of $15-$500; purchased credits expire after 12 months and need an active subscription. Own-provider or local use: the provider is paid directly; no separate Posit Assistant fee is stated on fetched pages. Workbench licensing is separate.
final_records.academic: The FAQ states there is no education discount at this time; Posit says it is exploring options for the academic community. Check institutional Workbench terms separately.
use_cases: R and Python code writing and debugging in RStudio and Positron
Exploratory data analysis with live session context (data frames, variables, plots)
Shiny and Streamlit app scaffolding and Quarto reports (/report)
Next Edit Suggestions inline completions (Posit AI Pass only)
Multi-step agentic tasks with Plan Mode, permissions, skills and plugins
Codebase understanding and refactoring
Terminal and headless use via the pa client
Calling Posit AI Pass models from own R or Python code via ellmer or chatlas
Local-model analysis via Ollama or LM Studio when data must stay on controlled infrastructure
final_records.notes: Posit Assistant is Posit's proprietary data-science agent for RStudio (2026.04+), Positron and the pa terminal client. Since Positron 2026.07 it is the default, replacing Positron Assistant and Databot. Posit AI Pass (renamed from Posit AI in October 2026) is the paid hosted model subscription; it also unlocks NES. Workbench 2026.10.0 made Posit Assistant generally available in RStudio Pro and Positron Pro sessions; the admin provider/settings controls and the per-user Agent Activity page are Preview. Positron console auditing (human vs agent) is on the roadmap and not shipped.
final_records.tier_gate: Cloud use: Posit AI Pass Pro with trace collection not opted in; special-category data: Posit Assistant with local Ollama (local-only mode)/LM Studio only, with AI Pass, NES, cloud providers and remote plugin marketplaces disabled

required_controls: Configure Posit Assistant with Ollama or LM Studio running on institution-controlled hardware; do not sign in to Posit AI Pass and keep Next Edit Suggestions (Posit-hosted) off.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Disable every cloud provider: in providers.json set providers.default.enabled to false and enable only ollama or lmstudio; on Workbench put this in the ai-providers-enforced file (Preview).
Keep web search off, deny web fetch (including the pre-approved Posit documentation fetches) and allow only local MCP servers.

Do not register remote plugin marketplaces; set plugins.strictKnownMarketplaces to [] (or to local-path entries only) and restrict plugins with plugins.blockedMarketplaces and plugins.allowedComponents through POSIT_ASSISTANT_SETTINGS_ENFORCED (on Workbench via assistant-settings-enforced).

Block outbound network egress at host or network level. In Workbench RStudio Pro sessions, set assistant-installation-enabled = 0 to stop update checks to cdn.posit.co and install a vetted Posit Assistant version from a local file with --file and --sha256 (admin-managed versions are Preview). In Positron, set update.mode to none and turn off update.anonymousUsageReporting, update.primaryLanguageReporting and extensions.autoCheckUpdates.
Confirm with Posit what Posit Assistant telemetry collects and disable it.
residual_risks: Posit Assistant telemetry is undocumented: the published settings schema has no telemetry key and rejects unknown top-level keys, and the current Workbench admin pages no longer show the earlier assistant.telemetry example, so its default and content are unconfirmed.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so pointing Posit Assistant at local Ollama alone does not show that inference stays local.
Workbench admin provider/settings controls are Preview, and Posit describes administrator-managed settings as best-effort policy, not a security boundary.

Plugins can bundle skills, commands and MCP servers from GitHub or other git marketplaces; plugin MCP servers start only after consent, but a user-registered marketplace fetches remote content unless policy blocks it.
The explicit no-AI-traffic statement covers Positron; no equivalent statement was found for RStudio Desktop.

Posit Assistant makes documented outbound calls by default: release notes state Posit documentation fetches are pre-approved (1.0.0) and assistant.posit.co is trusted for JSON schema downloads (1.3.0); whether a web-fetch deny rule overrides the pre-approval is not documented. Operation with all outbound egress blocked is not documented, and RStudio Desktop's own update and crash-reporting calls on the local route were not reviewed.
Local sessions, conversation history, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: marimo
final_records.vendor: Marimo Inc. (part of CoreWeave, Inc.); open-source Apache-2.0 notebook
final_records.deployment: Local (CLI via pip/uv/conda, VS Code) / self-hosted edit or app servers (Docker, Kubernetes operator, JupyterHub extension, Slurm) / marimohub self-hostable team platform (Apache-2.0, launched 2026-10-02) / cloud: molab (free hosted service on CoreWeave infrastructure)
final_records.model_backend: No model or key is set in the default config. The open-source editor uses providers you configure: OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google AI/Vertex, Azure, GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, Weights & Biases, OpenCode Go, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI and others, local Ollama or LM Studio, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If no chat model is set, the server falls back to openai/gpt-4o and uses OPENAI_API_KEY from the server environment or .env files when present. Agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and others) paired via marimo pair use their own backends; the older in-editor ACP external-agents panel is deprecated in favour of marimo pair. molab supplies free hosted open-source models (Weights & Biases listed as AI subprocessor). marimohub managed AI is operator-configured (Amazon Bedrock or an OpenAI-compatible upstream) and off by default.
final_records.data_handling_note: Local/self-hosted: marimo's default config sets no model or key and copilot completion off, and marimohub managed AI is off by default. When AI is used, notebook code, @-referenced variable values and whatever the chat assistant reads at its Notebook access level (Read only, Suggest edits or Full access; Full access can run arbitrary Python) from the notebook or kernel go to the configured provider under that provider's terms; if no model is set, marimo falls back to openai/gpt-4o and uses OPENAI_API_KEY from the server environment or .env files when present. Paired agent CLIs send notebook context to their own backends. With marimohub managed AI on, a per-user project Chat is also on by default (MARIMOHUB_AI_CHAT=on); conversations are stored by the hub with redacted tool previews, but saved resumable tasks keep tool payloads with credential-like fields masked. marimohub problem reports are off by default and, per its docs, exclude notebook content. Core telemetry: no usage analytics found in a source search; OpenTelemetry tracing is opt-in (MARIMO_TRACING) and writes to a local file by default; the CLI checks marimo.io for a new release once a day unless --skip-update-check or MARIMO_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1 is set (per the source code, a plain request without notebook content). molab is a separate hosted service: notebooks are 'public but undiscoverable by default'; built-in AI uses free hosted models (Weights & Biases subprocessor); the subprocessor list for molab, Community Cloud and marimo's websites also names Sentry (error/performance tracing) and PostHog (product analytics). molab terms (last updated 2022-09-22) prohibit HIPAA PHI and GDPR Article 9(1) data and grant Marimo a licence to use submitted content to operate, improve and provide the services; after account cancellation (molab terms) or an honoured deletion request (marimo data-requests page), content is deleted from active systems within 30 days and from backups within 60 days. Marimo's privacy URL redirects to CoreWeave's privacy policy (updated 2026-02-24), which permits AI/ML processing to improve and develop services; no molab-specific statement on training with notebook content or AI prompts was found.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local or self-hosted marimo/marimohub with a local or institution-approved model endpoint and approved integrations; any cloud model provider or paired agent CLI receives notebook code and referenced variable values under its own terms. molab notebooks are public-but-unlisted by default and molab is covered by CoreWeave's privacy policy; it needs separate institutional review.
suitability_notes.special: Only local/self-hosted marimo, or marimohub on institution-controlled compute and storage, with customer-controlled model inference (Ollama only in local-only mode) and approved integrations. molab does not qualify: it is pure cloud and its terms prohibit HIPAA PHI and GDPR Article 9(1) data. No local configuration is itself institutional approval.

compliance: Local installation, self-hosted marimohub and molab are separate governance boundaries; verify hosted-service contractual scope
molab terms prohibit HIPAA-regulated PHI and GDPR Article 9(1) special-category data
molab privacy is governed by CoreWeave's privacy policy; no public DPA or security attestation for molab was found on the fetched first-party pages
final_records.pricing: marimo and marimohub are Apache-2.0 and free to self-host; you pay for your own infrastructure and any model provider. molab is free per its docs (default 4 CPUs and 32 GB RAM, optional NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell GPU, sessions up to 12 h, limited persistent storage, free hosted AI models). No public paid plan or price list was found; cached-file size and persistence limits may change at molab's discretion.
final_records.academic: No academic licence needed: the notebook and marimohub are Apache-2.0. marimo's 'For researchers' page invites researchers to contact the team for help; molab is free but bound by its own terms.
use_cases: Reactive Python notebook with auto-rerunning cells on dependency change
SQL querying of dataframes (Polars, Pandas, DuckDB, SQLite, Postgres, MySQL)
Interactive data exploration with UI elements (sliders, plots, tables) synchronized with Python
Deployment of notebooks as web apps or WebAssembly HTML files
Git-friendly reproducible research (stored as pure .py files)
AI-assisted coding with BYO model key (local or cloud)
Pairing agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI) with a running notebook via marimo pair
JupyterHub/JupyterLab integration via marimo-jupyter-extension
Kubernetes deployment via marimo-operator and Slurm on HPC clusters
Self-hosted team notebook platform (marimohub) with projects, version history, scheduled jobs and SSO
final_records.notes: Open-source reactive Python notebook (Apache-2.0) from Marimo Inc., part of CoreWeave: CoreWeave announced a definitive agreement to acquire Marimo on 2025-10-30, and marimo's subprocessors page states 'Marimo is part of CoreWeave'. Actively maintained (0.25.2 released 2026-10-19; commits through 2026-11-06). marimohub, an Apache-2.0 self-hostable team platform launched 2026-10-02, is also actively released (v0.6.1, 2026-11-04) and adds a customer-controlled team deployment option; its compute backends also include third-party clouds. Unreleased changes on main (early November 2026) deprecate the ACP agents panel and rename AI modes to notebook access levels.
final_records.tier_gate: local or self-hosted marimo/marimohub with a fully local model (Ollama in local-only mode or an institution-owned endpoint), cloud keys removed, marimohub managed AI and project Chat off or on that endpoint, molab and paired cloud agent CLIs off, update check skipped and egress blocked for special-category data; a DPA-covered provider for personal data

required_controls: Run marimo locally or self-host it (edit/app server, JupyterHub, Kubernetes, Slurm or marimohub) on institution-controlled compute and storage; for marimohub use only local, Docker, Podman or Kubernetes compute and filesystem or institutional S3-compatible storage.

Configure only a local model endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio or an OpenAI-compatible server inside the institutional network that serves only institution-hosted models and forwards nothing to external providers) and set it explicitly as the chat, edit and autocomplete model; remove cloud provider keys (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) from the server environment and .env files, because marimo falls back to openai/gpt-4o with OPENAI_API_KEY when no model is set; leave marimohub managed AI off or point it at that endpoint (if on, project Chat is on by default; set MARIMOHUB_AI_CHAT=off unless approved); set ai.allow_provider_config=false to lock provider setup in the settings UI. ai.enabled=false only hides AI panels; code-completion settings stay available, so also keep completion.copilot off.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Keep token authentication on (do not expose servers started with --no-token) and run a current release; 0.23.0 fixed a critical pre-auth remote code execution via the terminal websocket (GHSA-2679-6mx9-h9xc).

Disable or restrict molab, cloud AI providers, paired cloud agent CLIs, MCP servers, GitHub and remote-storage connections; start servers with --skip-update-check or MARIMO_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1 where egress to marimo.io is not allowed; keep marimohub problem reports off (MARIMOHUB_SUPPORT_REPORTS=off, the default) or deliver them only to institutional destinations; apply institutional access, retention and logging controls.

Before use, check the effective AI configuration on the server (marimo.toml, .env files and environment variables), then block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the model endpoint and verify the block.
residual_risks: molab, third-party marimohub backends (e.g. CoreWeave Sandboxes, W&B, Modal, AWS ECS Fargate, E2B, Cloudflare) and cloud model providers are outside the customer-controlled boundary and do not qualify for special-category data.
The provider lock applies to the settings UI; users with access to marimo.toml, .env files or environment variables can still point AI at external endpoints, so enforce network egress controls.
Paired agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini) read variable values and outputs and send them to their own model providers unless run against a local model.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

Local session files, caches, logs and marimohub version history, snapshots, audit events, project-chat conversations and saved chat tasks retain data and need institutional retention and backup rules.
No local configuration is itself institutional (DPO, ethics or security) approval.

final_records.name: Runcell
final_records.deployment: cloud: JupyterLab 4.4+ extension (pip, conda/uv, a curl install script or JupyterLab Extension Manager; Docker recipes documented). Notebook code runs in the user's Jupyter kernel; every AI request goes through Runcell's cloud orchestrator, and networks must allow outbound HTTPS to *.runcell.dev; offline/air-gapped AI use is not supported. Also: Runcell Desktop beta (v0.3.8, 2026-10-29, bundles extension 0.2.9; macOS builds on the download page, plus Windows x64 (unsigned) and Linux x64/arm64 builds on GitHub releases; data flow undocumented) and a preview headless Agent runtime that calls service.runcell.dev. Stricter isolation or self-deployment only on request ('contact us').
final_records.model_backend: Runcell-hosted model access through Runcell's cloud orchestrator. No BYO key is needed, and no BYO-key or custom/local endpoint option is documented. The token-credit table (still the 2026-09-05 snapshot on 2026-11-06) lists Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT and Google Gemini models plus models from xAI, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax, Xiaomi, Z.ai and a Dolphin-Mistral (Venice edition) model; releases 0.2.6-0.2.8 (October 2026) added further models, so the inventory changes with each release. Some models are served through OpenRouter, and which ones is not documented. Hobby has limited model access; paid plans unlock advanced models. Since 0.2.6 some models offer Fast mode at different credit rates.
final_records.data_handling_note: Paid plans: Privacy Mode is on by default and Runcell does not use prompts, context or outputs to train or fine-tune models. The policy names Pro and Team; the pricing page also lists Privacy Mode for Pro+ and Ultra. Free (Hobby) has no Privacy Mode, and Runcell may retain and use prompts, context and outputs for training. Prompts, selected notebook context and short interaction history are assembled on Runcell's cloud and sent to the chosen model provider, for some models via OpenRouter. Runcell instructs providers not to train only where their controls allow it, and providers may run abuse/quality checks. No ZDR commitment is stated. Optional chat cloud sync stores conversations server-side; neither its default state nor a retention period is stated. Turning sync off stops new uploads; per policy section 5, previously synced content can be deleted from the account, and no automatic removal is stated. Storage of long-running Agent job state and of cross-session Agent Memory is not documented. Product analytics (Microsoft Clarity) and payload-free telemetry exclude notebook and chat content; no opt-out is documented. No public DPA or subprocessor list was found.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Use a paid plan. Free (Hobby) has no Privacy Mode, and its inputs/outputs may be used for training.
suitability_notes.personal: No public DPA or subprocessor list was found. Treat personal-data use as blocked unless the institution obtains and approves a signed processor agreement.
suitability_notes.special: Inference always runs through Runcell's cloud and third-party model providers. Offline/air-gapped AI use is not supported, and self-deployment is offered only on request. Not suitable.

final_records.pricing: Pricing page (checked 2026-11-06; plan data read from the page's own script bundle): Hobby free (20 credits/month, limited model access; no Privacy Mode per the privacy policy); Pro $20/month (500 credits); Pro+ $60/month (2,000 credits); Ultra $200/month (10,000 credits); Teams $40/seat/month (500 credits per seat). Annual billing is offered (Pro $180, Pro+ $600, Ultra $2,000, Teams $400 per seat per year). Ask/Chat and Agent use token-based credits at 30 credits per USD of provider-equivalent model cost (changed from 100 on 2026-07-15); other AI features use fixed or model-rate-based feature credits. Fast/Ultrafast speed modes (release 0.2.6) have different credit rates. Privacy Mode is listed on Pro, Pro+ and Ultra; Teams includes 'Everything in Pro'.
final_records.academic: No academic or student entitlement was found on first-party pages.
use_cases: Autonomous multi-step data analysis in JupyterLab
Long-running ML training jobs (multi-hour, end-to-end)
Cross-session project memory for iterative research workflows
Output-aware reasoning (reads charts, plots, DataFrame previews)
Automated cell execution, debugging, and error recovery
Domain-driven research analyses and figures (e.g. genomics circos plots) and risk/quantitative-finance modelling
Interactive learning and algorithm explanation in notebooks
Exploratory analysis, data wrangling, visualisation and model building in notebooks
final_records.notes: Cloud-connected notebook agent: code runs in the local Jupyter kernel, but inference always goes through Runcell's cloud. Paid Privacy Mode gives a no-training commitment; no public DPA was found. No public Enterprise plan is listed; stricter isolation or self-deployment is available only on request ('contact us'). Other surfaces: Runcell Desktop beta (v0.3.1-0.3.8, Sep-Oct 2026; binary-only GitHub repo, no stated licence, data flow undocumented; its 0.3.8 release notes mention 'Code Agent providers' without describing them) and a preview headless Agent runtime that uses the Runcell cloud backend. A sign-in 'Cloud Agents' web app (runcell.dev/agents, listed in the public sitemap) also exists; it is undocumented and was not assessed. The extension can also use MCP connections (local tools and remote services, since 0.2.2) and, since 0.2.6, import Skills from local folders or Git repositories; each remote connection is a further data path the user controls. Runcell Science (runcell.dev/science) is a separate Apache-2.0 open-source local research workspace that runs on the user's Claude Code or Codex CLI; it is not covered by this record. Some first-party pages overstate locality or are out of date: the docs landing page says 'Your data stays local', the Jupyter AI agent page says AI processing happens 'locally or through secure encrypted connections', and the home-page FAQ says there is no separate desktop app. The privacy policy states that prompts and relevant snippets go to Runcell's cloud and the model provider.
final_records.tier_gate: Paid plan (Pro, Pro+, Ultra or Teams) for Privacy Mode; personal data blocked pending a signed DPA

residual_risks: AI requests always pass through Runcell's cloud orchestrator and third-party model providers (some via OpenRouter); offline/air-gapped AI use is not supported.
Self-deployment is offered only as 'contact us', with no documented customer-controlled boundary.

final_records.name: JetBrains Datalore
final_records.deployment: Datalore Cloud (JetBrains-hosted) or Datalore On-Premises: Docker Compose or Kubernetes/Helm on 64-bit Linux (linux/amd64; linux/arm64 images since 2026.4), on premises or in the customer's own cloud account. Air-gapped operation is documented (the procedure preloads JDBC drivers into a custom SQL runtime image; the DataFrame Visualize tab needs a public CDN). The On-Premises option is also offered as a JetBrains-managed dedicated instance, which is not customer-controlled.
final_records.model_backend: Cloud: JetBrains AI service (FAQ, 23 Oct 2026: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5 and JetBrains-trained models by default; can also use OpenAI and Google models); Datalore AI only on the paid Cloud plan, not Cloud Free. On-Premises: admin selects JetBrains AI (relayed through JetBrains; docs list Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5 as default plus Claude Opus 5.5, OpenAI and Google Gemini models) or Bring Your Own Key (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible API, including a self-hosted LLM); AI needs an active paid On-Premises licence.
final_records.data_handling_note: 'local' applies only to customer-operated On-Premises with BYOK pointed at a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible LLM; with BYOK the FAQ says data goes directly from the instance to the configured provider. AI is off by default in both editions (Cloud: until the user accepts AI terms; On-Premises: until an admin enables it instance-wide). Cloud: AI is relayed through JetBrains; Datalore states it does not use LLM providers that train on customer data and does not take part in Detailed Data Collection, but it records users' prompts as prompt history (retention period not stated), and under the Cloud terms JetBrains keeps a backup of deleted hosted data for one month unless the customer asks for the backup to be deleted too. On-Premises with JetBrains AI: context is relayed through JetBrains infrastructure (stated not stored, not used for training). On-Premises with a cloud BYOK provider (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or an OpenAI-compatible service such as OpenRouter) sends prompts, selected cells, optional outputs, runtime-variable fragments and a list of attached file names to that provider under its terms. The AI setup page lists auth.grazie.ai and api.jetbrains.ai for the JetBrains AI option only (for BYOK it asks to allow the provider or local LLM), but the server configuration keeps them as Datalore AI default endpoints; whether a BYOK-only instance contacts them is not documented. On-Premises usage telemetry to JetBrains is not documented in the pages reviewed.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer customer-operated On-Premises with a self-hosted model. Cloud is possible after institutional review: AI requires the paid Cloud plan, the Datalore Cloud terms incorporate the JetBrains DPA, AI is relayed through JetBrains and prompts are kept as history. On Cloud team plans the Owner and Admins can access members' Private workspaces, and Cloud plans including Cloud Free list the Notebook API, through which external agents can reach notebook content. Use 'Review prompt' and leave 'Include outputs' off for personal data.
suitability_notes.special: Only a customer-operated, paid On-Premises installation (not the JetBrains-managed dedicated instance) with BYOK pointed at a self-hosted LLM, JetBrains AI not selected, and external integrations and agent-skill/API tokens restricted. A locally installed server using JetBrains AI or a cloud BYOK provider does not qualify.

compliance: Deployment- and contract-dependent; verify exact Datalore product scope
Datalore Cloud Terms of Service (v4.0, effective 20 Aug 2024) incorporate the JetBrains Data Processing Addendum (v1.3, with Standard Contractual Clauses)
Datalore security docs point to the JetBrains Trust Center for a non-public SOC 2 report; Datalore-specific scope not confirmed
final_records.pricing: Plans: Cloud Free (no Datalore AI; 120 CPU S machine hours, 10 GB), 14-day Cloud trial (up to 3 users), paid Cloud plan (seat-based, monthly or 1-year; includes Datalore AI, 750 CPU L hours and 6 credits per member) and On-Premises (licensed per active editor seat, viewers free, infrastructure costs extra). The buy page renders country-localized prices client-side; no list price is asserted here. Obtain a current Cloud or On-Premises quote.
final_records.academic: No Datalore academic programme confirmed. The JetBrains student/teacher Toolbox subscription (v4.2) explicitly excludes Datalore. Cloud Free exists but has no Datalore AI. Ask JetBrains sales about education terms.
use_cases: Jupyter-compatible notebooks in Python, R, Scala and Kotlin, with SQL cells for database queries
Collaborative real-time notebook editing for teams
AI-assisted code generation and modification in notebooks (Ask AI, Autopilot; Python, R, SQL and Markdown cells)
No-code DataFrame exploration via Data Explorer cells (2026.1)
Interactive data reports and dashboards shareable without code exposure
Scheduled notebook runs and automation
External AI coding agents working in Datalore notebooks and workspaces via the official agent skill and API (Datalore Cloud and On-Premises 2026.2+; workspace scope since 2026.3)
On-premises deployment for regulated data environments with BYOK AI, including a self-hosted LLM
final_records.notes: Notebook data-science platform with Cloud and On-Premises editions; On-Premises 2026.4 server image published 23 Oct 2026 (fixes a Critical vulnerability; JetBrains strongly recommends all on-premises installations update) and 2026.4.1 on 29 Oct 2026. The FAQ defines On-Premises as installation in a customer-controlled environment, including the customer's own cloud. The qualifying route is customer-operated Datalore plus a self-hosted model, with JetBrains AI not selected and external integrations and agent API access restricted. The official agent skill (MIT-licensed, version-matched branches per On-Premises release) lets external AI agents read, edit and run notebook cells and query workspace databases; that content then goes to the agent's own model provider.
final_records.tier_gate: Customer-operated Datalore On-Premises (paid licence) + BYOK self-hosted LLM

required_controls: Use an active paid On-Premises licence on infrastructure the institution operates (own servers or own cloud account), not the JetBrains-managed dedicated instance; run 2026.4 or later, since 2026.4 fixes a Critical vulnerability and JetBrains strongly recommends updating.

In Admin panel > AI select Bring Your Own Key pointed at a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible LLM running on institution-operated infrastructure (the Datalore host or another institution-controlled server inside the network), reached directly with no gateway that forwards to external providers; do not select JetBrains AI or a cloud BYOK provider.
Block or monitor egress to auth.grazie.ai, api.jetbrains.ai and cloud LLM endpoints, and confirm AI still works with only the local endpoint reachable.

Restrict API tokens (scopes: Notebook API, full user access, admin access; expiry 30 minutes to one year) and the Datalore agent skill (use the skill branch matching the installed version) to agents whose model runs on institution-controlled infrastructure; no instance-wide admin switch for them is documented in the pages reviewed, so enforce this through token issuance policy and network controls. Keep cloud storage, Google Drive and other external integrations disabled unless approved.
residual_risks: A locally installed server using JetBrains AI or a cloud BYOK provider sends prompts, selected cells, optional outputs, runtime-variable fragments and attached file names off-premises.

The AI setup page lists auth.grazie.ai and api.jetbrains.ai under the JetBrains AI option, but the server configuration keeps them as Datalore AI default endpoints; docs do not state whether a BYOK-only instance contacts them. Verify with network monitoring.
The agent skill/API lets an external agent read cell outputs and query workspace databases; if that agent uses a cloud model, data leaves the boundary regardless of Datalore's AI setting.

Datalore stores SQL result slices (first and last 100 values) and rendered outputs in its own database and storage; optional user activity logging records cell content. These need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: ChatGPT Data Analysis
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Managed ChatGPT model selection, varying by plan and rollout; do not infer the exact Python data-analysis backend from the model picker.
final_records.data_handling_note: Business, Enterprise, Edu and ChatGPT for Academic Researchers workspaces are excluded from model training by default; on Business/Enterprise/Edu, thumbs feedback does not permit training unless the organization signs a separate agreement. Individual plans (Free/Go/Plus/Pro) may be used for training unless 'Improve the model for everyone' is off; thumbs feedback can still submit the whole conversation. On personal accounts, content on shared Space pages can be used for training through a collaborator's settings even if the owner opted out. Business data may be run through automated content classifiers and safety tools. Product-level retention applies regardless: saved chats persist until deleted or removed by a workspace retention policy (then scheduled for deletion within 30 days); temporary chats may be kept up to 30 days. Files saved to Library or Space (Space replaces Library for eligible Pro/Business/Enterprise accounts from 2026-09-29) persist until deleted separately; deleting a chat does not delete them; in Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare workspaces they follow the workspace retention policy, and backups may keep deleted files up to 30 more days. Eligible new Enterprise/Edu workspaces can keep in-scope content (including Code Interpreter & Data Analysis artifacts) at rest in-region, with optional GPU inference residency (help centre: EEA+CH, US, UAE; US only for Enterprise bought via AWS Marketplace); CPU processing (e.g. text extraction from uploaded PDFs), metadata and external integrations may be outside the region, and the residency article does not say where the Python data-analysis environment runs. ZDR is documented for eligible API endpoints; for ChatGPT, the Business overview lists ZDR only as a sales-led contracted option, the Rosalind Academic Plan states ZDR is not available, and no ZDR terms for ChatGPT chats or files were found.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institutional Business/Enterprise/Edu workspace with an executed DPA (Business/Enterprise) or the institution's Edu data-processing terms, accepted retention settings and, where required, EU data residency (Enterprise/Edu only; not offered on Business). Consumer opt-out alone is insufficient; Library/Space files need their own deletion. ChatGPT for Academic Researchers workspaces (new applications closed) have no-training defaults, but the public page names no DPA. Rosalind Academic Plan labs (U.S. only) get a Business workspace with standard retention and no ZDR. Confirm terms and institutional approval before using personal data.
suitability_notes.special: The documented route uses vendor/cloud inference or control-plane processing outside customer-controlled infrastructure; it does not qualify under this catalog’s special-category rule.

compliance: DPA offered for ChatGPT Business and Enterprise; ChatGPT Edu (and Teachers) data processed under OpenAI's Student Data Privacy Agreement per the Enterprise privacy page; confirm the institution's executed terms

OpenAI states that ChatGPT Business and ChatGPT Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare each completed a SOC 2 Type 2 audit (latest report period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30, gated on the Trust Portal); the Trust Portal's ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate notice covers the API, ChatGPT Enterprise and ChatGPT Edu (with 27017, 27018 and 27701 controls); ISO scope for Business not confirmed

Data residency at rest for eligible new Enterprise/Edu workspaces (includes Code Interpreter & Data Analysis artifacts; no extra cost); optional GPU inference residency (help centre: EEA+CH, US, UAE; the business-data page names only U.S. or Europe); not available on Business
BAA offered for ChatGPT for Healthcare (US HIPAA); this does not change the catalog's special-category rule
final_records.pricing: Pricing-page comparison: Data analysis limited on Free and included on Go, Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise; interactive tables and charts only on Plus and above. ChatGPT Edu includes data analysis (Edu help article). Pro has three monthly plans (Pro 100/200/500 at USD 100/200/500). Business: Standard or Premium seats, at least two paid seats, for teams of 2–200, monthly or annual billing; for most countries Standard is USD 25/user/month monthly or USD 20 annual and Premium USD 125 monthly or USD 100 annual, with local prices varying by country/currency. Enterprise and Edu are priced through sales. Use the current localized pricing and the institutional order.
final_records.academic: ChatGPT Edu is available through institutional agreements. ChatGPT for Academic Researchers (complimentary 12-month workspace, up to five seats from one institution, Pro-level rate limits, no SSO/SCIM, no API credits) is closed to new applications; new signups join an informational waitlist, and existing approved participants can still set up workspaces. The Rosalind Academic Plan (announced 2026-10-15) gives approved labs at U.S. universities only up to 30 ChatGPT Business Standard seats at no cost for 12 months (card required at setup) plus GPT-Rosalind after trusted-access review, which includes naming an institutional biosafety contact; it has standard Business data retention, no ZDR and no API access. Universities with an OpenAI Enterprise agreement use their institution's route. No general individual academic discount is asserted.
use_cases: Exploratory analysis of uploaded spreadsheets (CSV/XLS/XLSX), PDFs and text/data files (JSON, XML, YAML, TXT, MD)
Python code generation and execution in a stateful Jupyter environment without external network access
Statistical analysis (comparative tests, correlation and regression, time series), calculations and data transformations
Data cleaning (missing values, outliers, duplicates, data types) and merging datasets on shared identifiers
Charts as static images (downloadable as PNG); interactive bar, line, pie and scatter charts on Plus and higher plans
Interactive table review of pandas DataFrames; tables downloadable as CSV
Summaries of rows, columns, trends and outliers
Conversational iteration on analysis methods and results
Files from connected sources (Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint) where plugins/connected apps are enabled
final_records.notes: OpenAI's help article is titled 'Data analysis with ChatGPT' (formerly Advanced Data Analysis / Code Interpreter); the catalog name ChatGPT Data Analysis is kept. Cloud-only: Python runs in ChatGPT's stateful Jupyter environment, which cannot make external web requests or API calls. From 2026-09-29 Space replaces Library for eligible Pro/Business/Enterprise accounts. Organizational no-training, retention and residency controls do not make it acceptable for special-category data under this index's controlled-infrastructure rule.
final_records.tier_gate: Business/Enterprise/Edu workspace with an executed DPA or Edu data-processing terms and accepted retention controls

residual_risks: The documented route uses vendor/cloud inference or control-plane processing outside customer-controlled infrastructure; it does not qualify under this catalog’s special-category rule.

final_records.name: Ollama
final_records.deployment: local-capable / self-hostable / cloud
final_records.model_backend: Open-weight models run locally or on optional Ollama Cloud; model availability is dynamic
final_records.data_handling_note: Ollama's privacy policy (last updated March 2026) says Ollama does not receive prompts or data processed with local models; cloud-model prompts and responses are processed transiently and never used for training. The pricing FAQ says cloud models are hosted primarily in the United States, may be routed to Europe for extra capacity, and are served with NVIDIA Cloud Provider partners that Ollama requires to have no-logging, no-training and zero-retention policies. The policy says Ollama may collect limited device and usage metadata, without prompt or response content. These are vendor statements; no public DPA, trust centre or certification was found. Cloud inference and web search can be switched off (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud).

suitability_notes.personal: Run in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud) with local models on controlled hardware, and assess each agent or integration using the runtime. Optional cloud inference is a separate service, hosted primarily in the US with possible routing to Europe, under Ollama's terms; local availability is not institutional approval.
suitability_notes.special: Only local-only mode with locally provisioned models on institution-controlled hardware qualifies. Govern the calling agent, its web tools, local files, the unauthenticated local API and network egress separately.

compliance: Local mode avoids a vendor processor; no exhaustive public cloud certification claim is made
final_records.pricing: Local runtime is free with no Ollama inference fee. Pay as you go: $0, no subscription, cloud models billed per token. Pro $20/month ($200/year) includes $60 monthly cloud usage credits; Max $100/month includes $300; Team (early access) $500/month for unlimited users includes $1,000 shared credits. Enterprise custom. Included credits do not roll over; purchased credits can be added on every plan and expire one year after purchase; some cloud models have cheaper off-peak rates (outside 12:00-18:00 UTC on weekdays).
final_records.academic: The MIT local runtime is available without academic eligibility; hardware and separately licensed model costs remain.
use_cases: local-only model infrastructure for coding agents (cloud features can be disabled)
private model serving for research workflows
backend for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Droid, and other compatible clients
local model evaluation and agent pipelines
final_records.notes: Local model runtime used by coding agents and notebooks, with a separate optional cloud service (cloud models, web search). The qualifying special-category route requires local-only mode, locally provisioned models and governed agent integrations.
final_records.tier_gate: local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud), locally provisioned models, API on 127.0.0.1 or behind an authenticating proxy, calling agent and its web tools governed, egress blocked (no documented opt-out for usage metadata) for special-category data; local-only mode on controlled hardware for personal data too, since Ollama Cloud has no public DPA

required_controls: Enable local-only mode with OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or "disable_ollama_cloud": true in ~/.ollama/server.json of the account that runs the Ollama server (on a Linux systemd install, the ollama service user, not the researcher). This disables cloud inference and web search; confirm the server log shows "Ollama cloud disabled: true".
Provision only local models on institution-controlled hardware, pulled through an approved route or imported from local GGUF/Safetensors weights.
Keep the API bound to 127.0.0.1 or put it behind an authenticating proxy; the local API requires no authentication.
Govern the calling agent and its integrations (web search/fetch, desktop-app connectors) and enforce network egress, update and local-state retention controls.
residual_risks: Agents launched through Ollama can select cloud models or web tools unless cloud features are disabled; the agent's own data flows need separate review.
The privacy policy reserves collection of limited device and usage metadata (e.g. app version, request counts); no separate opt-out is documented, so rely on egress controls.
The privacy policy lists model download metadata among data collected automatically, so pulls from the ollama.com registry are visible to Ollama; use local GGUF/Safetensors import where this matters.
In the source defaults, the unauthenticated API accepts browser requests from localhost, file:// and editor-webview origins, so local web content and editor webviews on the host can reach it.
Local sessions, logs, model files and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Grok Build
final_records.deployment: Local CLI/TUI (macOS, Linux, Windows; also headless and ACP). Default inference runs in SpaceXSI cloud (cli-chat-proxy.grok.com, or api.x.ai with an API key). Custom endpoints, including a local Ollama or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible server, are set in config.toml. Fleet policy via managed_config.toml, signed requirements.toml or macOS MDM.
final_records.model_backend: SpaceXSI models by default (grok-build is the documented recommended default; SpaceXSI states Grok 4.7 now powers Grok Build). Custom [model.*] endpoints speak Chat Completions, Responses or Messages APIs and can point to local Ollama/OpenAI-compatible servers, Amazon Bedrock or other providers. Admins can pin the selectable model set in signed requirements.toml.
final_records.data_handling_note: Individual (non-ZDR) accounts: SpaceXSI states the CLI shows a screen asking to retain data to improve the product and model, and /privacy offers Opt in/Opt out for 'Coding data, retention, and training'. The pre-selected default is not documented, so the catalog treats it as opt-out. On team accounts only an admin can change the setting. /privacy does not change product telemetry or session-trace upload; trace upload follows the telemetry switch when unset, and the config reference states only that the enterprise telemetry default is off. Team-level ZDR: SpaceXSI states no Grok Build trace or code data is retained and that ZDR turns off product analytics, session-trace upload and coding-data sharing. Non-ZDR inference-layer retention for Grok Build is not stated (the 30-day audit retention is documented for API requests). Remote session sync and share links use code.grok.com; local history stays in ~/.grok/. The consumer Terms and Privacy Policy (both updated 2026-10-27) cover SpaceXSI services for individuals, list model training among uses of user content and offer a training choice, but do not name Grok Build; the Privacy Policy excludes business offerings such as the API.

suitability_notes.personal: Cloud use only via a team account with admin-enabled ZDR (enabling it accepts the Enterprise Terms) or a negotiated Enterprise agreement, with sign-in restricted to that team (force_login_team_uuid) and telemetry, trace upload and feedback pinned off in signed requirements.toml; or use an institution-controlled endpoint. Individual accounts are not recommended for personal data: Grok Build is not named in the consumer terms, non-ZDR retention is not documented, and the /privacy opt-out does not stop telemetry or trace upload. Institutional DPA review still applies.
suitability_notes.special: Only with inference on a local model server (e.g., Ollama at localhost) pinned as the only selectable model in signed requirements.toml, SpaceXSI telemetry, trace upload, feedback, remote fetch and workspace snapshots pinned off, and tested network egress blocking to SpaceXSI hosts. Default SpaceXSI-cloud operation is not acceptable, ZDR notwithstanding.

compliance: Team-level ZDR (admin-enabled, self-serve where available): SpaceXSI states no Grok Build trace or code data is retained; ZDR does not mute a customer-configured external OTEL stream.
ZDR coverage of remote session sync and share links (code.grok.com) is not documented.
Local session history, memory files and logs under ~/.grok/ are outside ZDR and need institutional controls.
Login can be pinned to named team UUIDs (force_login_team_uuid) and API-key login disabled (disable_api_key_auth) in requirements.toml, so personal logins outside the ZDR team are rejected.
final_records.pricing: Free tier available (Grok 4.7 Fast excluded). Paid SuperGrok plans use one shared weekly usage pool across Grok products including 'Build' (the FAQ does not separate the CLI from grok.com Build mode); Grok 4.7 Fast is billed through the plan. API-key use is metered at xAI API rates (global endpoint, <200k prompt tokens, per 1M tokens: grok-4.7 $2.00 input / $6.00 output; grok-build-0.1 $1.00 / $2.00; higher at >=200k). Subscription prices not verified.
final_records.academic: No academic or student program found in SpaceXSI documentation (checked 2026-11-06).
use_cases: terminal-native agentic coding on large codebases
headless/CI scripting and long-running tasks
Agent Client Protocol integration into third-party editors
BYO/self-hosted model endpoint workflows for controlled environments
final_records.notes: Apache-2.0 Rust client; the repository README and LICENSE still name SpaceXAI, while docs and legal pages now use SpaceXSI (SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC). Synced periodically from the vendor monorepo; external contributions are not accepted. No GitHub releases: binaries ship via the x.ai installer and npm @xai-official/grok (1.0.77 on 2026-11-05). The public repository was last synced on 2026-09-29; 33 npm versions published since then have no matching public source, so shipped binaries cannot currently be audited against source. Enterprise docs list auth.x.ai and cli-chat-proxy.grok.com as required for core functionality, so offline operation with a local model must be tested, not assumed.
final_records.tier_gate: Cloud: team account with admin-enabled ZDR (or a negotiated Enterprise agreement), sign-in pinned to that team, plus telemetry, trace upload and feedback pinned off; individual accounts have only the /privacy coding-data choice, which does not cover telemetry or trace upload. Special-category data: local model server plus signed requirements.toml pins and tested egress blocking.

required_controls: Configure only a local model server (e.g., Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server at localhost) as [model.*]; pin it as models.default and the only entry in models.allowed_models in signed /etc/grok/requirements.toml; an institution-hosted endpoint changes the route and needs its own review.

Point every auxiliary model role (models.web_search, models.image_description, models.session_summary, models.prompt_suggestion) at the local model or disable those features, because they can otherwise resolve to SpaceXSI-served models.

Pin features.telemetry = false, telemetry.trace_upload = false, features.feedback = false, features.remote_fetch = false, harness.disable_workspace_teleport = true and cli.auto_update = false in signed requirements.toml (pins override remote settings); keep external OTEL off or limited to an institutional collector with content gates off.
Opt out of coding-data sharing (/privacy) or use a ZDR team account; disable relay sync and memory unless reviewed; restrict web search/fetch and MCP servers.

Use an external auth provider (auth_provider_command, documented for air-gapped networks) instead of SpaceXSI OAuth; block egress to all SpaceXSI hosts (auth.x.ai, cli-chat-proxy.grok.com, api.x.ai, code.grok.com, assets.grok.com, x.ai) and storage.googleapis.com, and verify by testing that sessions run without them.
residual_risks: Enterprise docs list auth.x.ai and cli-chat-proxy.grok.com as required for core functionality; running with a local model and no SpaceXSI connectivity is not documented end to end.
The pre-selected default of the first-run data-retention screen is not documented, and the consumer terms do not name Grok Build.
Local sessions (~/.grok/sessions/), memory files and logs (~/.grok/logs/; TUI file logging defaults to DEBUG) need institutional access, retention and encryption controls.

Unpinned behaviour can be changed by SpaceXSI remote settings; only signed requirements.toml pins override them. A July 2026 third-party press report, not confirmed by SpaceXSI, described an earlier CLI version uploading whole repositories to cloud storage until a server-side flag stopped it.
The public source has not been synced since 2026-09-29, so current binaries cannot be audited against published code.
Local models may be less capable than the default SpaceXSI models.

final_records.name: Muse Code
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Meta-hosted Muse models. In Muse Code: Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3 (Standard) and their Contributor variants muse-spark-1.2/1.3-contributor, Muse Wonder (muse-wonder-1.0, in preview; Standard model) and, on Power and Maximum Usage subscriptions only, Muse Wonder Full; all 1,048,576-token context. Muse Spark 1.1 is not available in Muse Code. Muse Code docs name muse-spark-1.2 as the default model; the API docs recommend 1.3 for new work. The client is provider-aware: the configuration docs and changelog refer to other providers, a --provider flag for muse serve and a keyless custom endpoint, and Meta's MIT SDK quickstart sets an endpoint_transport base URL to a loopback test endpoint. Changelog entries (1.4.3-1.4.12) also mention 'offline sessions', 'local-model setup' and Claude and GPT models served through a Meta gateway; none of these is documented for public use. Meta's open-weight models (Muse Spark Open, 816B-parameter MoE under the Muse Model License, and Muse Glimmer) can be self-hosted, but no first-party page documents connecting Muse Code to them.
final_records.data_handling_note: The no-train label applies to the personal-data route in tier_gate (organisation API key on a pinned Standard model); a Muse Code subscription on default settings runs in Contributor (training) mode. Terms depend on account route and model tier (Meta Model API Terms of Service, last updated 2026-10-09, unchanged at this review; Model Designation and Geographic Use Policy, last updated 2026-10-12). Standard models (Muse Spark 1.1/1.2/1.3, Muse Wonder, Muse Wonder Full): Meta acts as processor under the Meta Global Processor Terms and does not train on Content. Contributor models (muse-spark-1.2/1.3-contributor) permit training, and the ToS forbids sending personal, sensitive or confidential data (including confidential code) to them. A Muse Code subscription counts as Contributor by default whatever model is selected (ToS 3.3); switching to Standard applies prospectively only. Contributor mode is now a Muse Code setting (/settings > Model > Contributor mode), saved per computer and switched on by the first interactive session on each new computer; --contributor-mode on|off or MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE overrides it per run, and a headless run with an existing settings file but no saved value can run in Contributor mode. In Contributor mode requests are routed to the -contributor model variant. Changelog 1.4.8 says turning the setting off 'now fully opts out, including background requests', so earlier builds did not fully opt out. The setting is hidden, and Contributor mode stays off, on pay-as-you-go, on ZDR accounts and where an organisation's managed configuration controls it. Pay-as-you-go API-key use of the default model (muse-spark-1.2) is Standard unless a -contributor model is chosen. The ToS also warns that the system may route requests to a Contributor model. On every tier Meta may retain and process Content for policy enforcement and to develop safety and security systems, and the Data Commitments page also lists improving and maintaining the Model API. Without ZDR, Content and Usage Data (tool-call sequences, logs, telemetry) are retained 'as needed' with no stated period, and Usage Data may be used to develop and improve Meta products. The Data Commitments page says Content can be viewed and deleted through the account. ZDR is available only to qualified organisations, enabled by Meta through sales; personal accounts are not covered, support may vary by model, ZDR turns off stateful and background requests, file uploads, web search and Contributor mode (including the Muse Code setting), and flagged content may still be kept up to 2 years; support feedback is retained. CLI: changelog 1.4.0 refers to a saved opt-out for 'feedback and diagnostic upload', so it appears to be on unless disabled; what it sends is undocumented. A local session event log is kept by default (--no-session-log disables it), and saved sessions are kept indefinitely unless session_retention_days is set (macOS and Linux only); voice input is on by default on macOS; four background observer agents make extra model calls by default. By default Muse Code also loads skills from ~/.claude/skills and $CODEX_HOME/skills (or ~/.codex/skills) and from repo-local .claude/.codex skill folders, so other agents' skill files can enter the context sent to Meta; a user preference can disable the personal foreign skill roots. Client guardrails are on by default: approvals (default Auto-review profile, where an automated judge clears eligible requests), OS sandbox, proxy-only network with per-destination approval, workspace-scoped writes.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: A subscription runs in Contributor (training) mode by default on each new computer, and any -contributor model trains; Meta may then train on prompts, code and outputs. Use only public or non-confidential code there, as the ToS itself requires, or turn Contributor mode off in /settings on every computer (Muse Code 1.4.8 or later) and pass --contributor-mode off in scripts and CI.
suitability_notes.personal: Configuration-required. Use a Business & Enterprise (managed account) organisation API key on a pinned Standard model (not a -contributor variant), with ZDR enabled by Meta and confirmed in writing to cover Muse Code traffic and the models used (ZDR support may vary by model, and Muse Wonder is in preview). Where possible, enforce settings through the organisation's managed configuration, which keeps Contributor mode off. Turn off feedback and diagnostic upload and voice input (on by default on macOS) in settings, and do not attach session logs to /feedback. The institution must review the Meta Global Processor Terms, Data Security Terms, subprocessors, the Usage Data clause and the 2-year flagged-content exception, and check served model IDs because the ToS says requests may be routed to a Contributor model. Never use a personal Meta Account, a subscription, Muse Wonder Full (subscription-only) or a Contributor model. No security certification for Model API or Muse Code was named in the fetched pages.
suitability_notes.special: Inference runs on Meta-hosted Muse models. No first-party page documents a supported self-hosted or customer-controlled inference endpoint for Muse Code. Meta now publishes the open-weight Muse Spark Open for self-hosting, but its docs do not mention Muse Code; Meta's MIT SDK quickstart points the CLI's endpoint_transport setting at a loopback test endpoint, which shows the base URL can be configured, but it is not a documented model-serving route, and ToS 10.1(xiv) bars modifying the harness to operate with any model or service not provided by Meta. Not acceptable under this index's controlled-infrastructure rule, even with ZDR or processor terms.

compliance: Meta Global Processor Terms apply to Standard Services only (ToS section 5.1); no Model API or Muse Code security certification was named in the fetched legal, help or product pages.
final_records.pricing: Muse Code subscriptions: Everyday Usage $5/month, High Usage $15/month (5x Everyday usage), Power Usage $50/month (20x, adds Muse Wonder Full), Maximum Usage $200/month (80x), as listed on the product page and Help Center on 2026-11-06; benefits and availability vary by region. Subscriptions run in Contributor (training) mode by default until the setting is turned off. Pay-as-you-go per 1M tokens: Muse Spark Standard $1.25 input / $4.25 output / $0.15 cached input; Contributor $0.10 / $0.20 / $0.002, in exchange for training permission; Muse Wonder (Standard only) $4.00 / $20.00 / $0.20; web search $2.50 per 1,000 queries.
final_records.academic: No academic or student program found.
use_cases: agentic coding on large codebases (1M-token context)
CI/headless automation
parallel sub-agents in isolated git worktrees
