final_records.notes: Terminal/CI coding agent for macOS, Linux and Windows using Meta-hosted Muse Spark and Muse Wonder models. Subscriptions default to Contributor (training) mode, now an in-app setting saved per computer; the subscription docs and ToS 3.3 agree on this. A personal-data route exists only through an organisation account with Meta-enabled ZDR on Standard models. The programmatic SDK (meta-models/muse-code-sdk) is MIT-licensed; the CLI itself is proprietary, licensed in object code form only.
final_records.tier_gate: personal data only via a Business & Enterprise managed-account organisation API key (pay-as-you-go) on a pinned Standard model under the Meta Global Processor Terms, with Meta-enabled ZDR; confirm in writing that the processor terms and ZDR cover Muse Code traffic and the models used; feedback/diagnostic upload and voice input off; never a subscription (Contributor mode on by default, ToS 3.3), a personal Meta Account, Muse Wonder Full or a Contributor model

residual_risks: All inference runs on Meta-hosted Muse models; no first-party page documents a supported customer-controlled or local inference endpoint for Muse Code (the endpoint_transport base URL in Meta's SDK test harness is not a documented serving route, the self-hostable Muse Spark Open is not documented for use with Muse Code, and ToS 10.1(xiv) bars modifying the harness to operate with any model or service not provided by Meta).
ZDR and processor terms do not change the vendor-cloud boundary, and flagged content may be retained for up to 2 years even under ZDR.

final_records.name: Ante
final_records.deployment: local-capable (single binary; fully offline once its managed llama.cpp engine and a GGUF model are installed) / BYO cloud APIs
final_records.model_backend: Managed local llama.cpp/GGUF inference, attached llama.cpp-compatible servers, or user-configured cloud/OpenAI-compatible providers (including Antigma's optional Antix gateway).
final_records.data_handling_note: The v0.3.3 changelog (2026-11-05) states that published builds send telemetry through the Ante telemetry gateway, so official binaries export by default; utility commands send no telemetry. The export covers metrics and application logs; log bodies are not scrubbed and may contain home paths or tool arguments. Exports carry no username or hostname, but do carry a random installation id stored in ~/.ante/installation-id. ANTE_TELEMETRY=off disables export. Since v0.3.0, Antix is first in provider auto-detection, and Ante starts on Antix when nothing is authenticated. Stored API keys and sign-ins sit under ~/.ante/auth/credentials/. Local logs, sessions (including copies kept on rewind), TUI prompt history and auto-memory persist under ~/.ante; session saving and auto-memory can be switched off. Background Bash job output stays under ~/.ante/run/jobs/ for 24 hours after the job ends. WebFetch spill files and staging downloads sit in the OS cache and temp directories, outside ~/.ante. Local GGUF inference keeps model traffic on the machine. With cloud presets, the provider's terms govern. The optional Antix proxy records request and response bodies on every call; Antigma states this traffic is not used to train its models, and the upstream model provider's policy still applies.

suitability_notes.personal: Pin local GGUF inference (--offline-model or --provider local) or an institution-approved endpoint, and set ANTE_TELEMETRY=off, because published builds export telemetry by default. Without an explicit provider, Ante auto-selects Antix first, and the Antix proxy stores request and response bodies. With cloud presets, the selected provider's retention and training terms govern.
suitability_notes.special: Use locally provisioned GGUF inference on the same host (Ante-managed or institution-built llama.cpp) with ANTE_TELEMETRY=off; published builds otherwise export logs that may contain paths or tool arguments. Exclude Antix and other stored cloud credentials, gateway mode, /term-driven cloud agents, any non-loopback endpoint, the default WebFetch tool and remote or off-host MCP servers, and block host egress. Govern local logs, sessions, TUI prompt history (~/.ante/user_input_history.jsonl), memory and the OS cache and temp files.

final_records.pricing: Prebuilt binary is free, including commercial use, during the alpha preview under the Binary Preview Terms. Repository source (SDK, protocol and support crates, ACP and gateway apps) is Apache-2.0. Cloud providers and the optional Antix gateway are metered separately (Antix prices not reviewed); local inference still requires hardware.
final_records.academic: No special academic entitlement is asserted; binary preview terms apply to all uses.
use_cases: fully offline/air-gapped coding assistance on sensitive or pre-publication code, once telemetry export is off (ANTE_TELEMETRY=off), the local provider is pinned (auto-detection starts on Antix) and session saving is disabled or governed; published builds export telemetry by default
single-binary install on locked-down or HPC-adjacent machines

final_records.notes: Preview-stage terminal coding agent with managed local-model support. The README labels it a beta preview; the Binary Preview Terms call it an alpha research preview. Releases follow semver since v0.2.0 (Sep 2026); v0.3.0 (2026-10-28) changed credential configuration and made Antix the first auto-detected provider, and v0.3.3 followed on 2026-11-05. The Apache-2.0 repository holds the SDK, protocol and support crates plus the ACP and Slack/Discord gateway apps. The core agent ships only as a prebuilt binary: the open-sourcing tracking issue (#21) still lists moving more core crates and shipping source with the binary as open, and on 2026-10-15 a maintainer named re-architecting the backend as the blocker for releasing the CLI source.
final_records.tier_gate: fully offline same-host GGUF model + ANTE_TELEMETRY=off for regulated data

required_controls: Fully offline configuration only. Run the managed llama.cpp engine (installed in advance with `ante offline install`) or an institution-built llama.cpp on the same host, with a locally provisioned GGUF model, and start sessions with the local provider pinned (`--offline-model` or `--provider local`). Attach no non-loopback endpoint. Cloud presets, Antix and remote or LAN-hosted endpoints are not acceptable.
Set ANTE_TELEMETRY=off for every Ante process. Published builds send telemetry through the Ante telemetry gateway by default (v0.3.3 changelog).
Do not use gateway mode (Slack/Discord), and do not drive cloud-backed agent CLIs (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) through /term or Ante's tmux terminal sessions in this route.

Remove the WebFetch tool, which is enabled by default (--exclude-tools WebFetch, a --tools allow-list or a permission deny rule). Configure no remote (`url`) MCP servers and no MCP servers that reach beyond the host.

Keep no cloud provider API keys or sign-ins (including Antix) in the environment, Ante settings or the credential store; `ante auth list` shows stored credentials. Check the effective provider, telemetry and tool settings (including named profiles and project settings) before each sensitive session.

Block outbound network traffic at host or network level and verify that the block holds; this also stops telemetry export and the background update checks, for which the docs describe no opt-out. Install reviewed releases through institutional software management.
residual_risks: Published builds export telemetry by default; if ANTE_TELEMETRY=off is missed for any process on a networked host, exported log bodies may carry paths or tool arguments.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

WebFetch spill and staging files sit in the OS cache and temp directories outside ~/.ante; staging files fall outside the 48-hour cleanup. Rewinds keep abandoned dialog copies inside session directories, and background Bash job output stays under ~/.ante/run/jobs/ for 24 hours after the job ends. Session saving is on by default in all launch modes, and auto-memory is on by default in the TUI (off in headless runs); `--no-session-save` and `--disable-auto-memory` (or the built-in `bare` profile) reduce what persists, while application logs under ~/.ante/logs and the TUI prompt history (~/.ante/user_input_history.jsonl) are still written.

Ante labels any attached llama.cpp server as the 'local' provider, including one on another LAN host; confirm the endpoint is loopback/same-host, since a non-loopback attach is outside this local-only route.

The core is a closed-source preview binary that cannot be audited from source, and distribution may change or stop without notice. On networked hosts, background update checks contact the release manifest up to hourly; the update docs describe no opt-out.

final_records.name: Nanocoder
final_records.vendor: Nano Collective (volunteer-led community collective; fiscally hosted by Open Source Collective, no separate legal entity)
final_records.deployment: local-capable
final_records.model_backend: BYO: local runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, LocalAI, MLX Server, llama-swap, Atomic Chat); OpenAI-compatible cloud APIs and routers (e.g., OpenRouter, Requesty, OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, Together AI, Atlas Cloud, FutureInfra); native-SDK providers (e.g., Anthropic, Google Gemini, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT/Codex)
final_records.data_handling_note: No vendor cloud: model requests go to the provider endpoint(s) the user configures; configured MCP servers and network tools (fetch_url; web_search via Brave when a key is set; the browser tool released in v1.32.0) can carry prompt-derived content to other hosts. v1.32.0 docs state no telemetry and name two self-initiated calls, neither carrying code or prompts: an npm-registry version check (NANOCODER_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 turns it off; automatic checks at most once per 24 h per release notes) and a models.dev metadata download. Opt-in features add egress: voice mode's OpenAI cloud speech backends (local Whisper/Piper by default) and first-use downloads of audio tools and Chromium. Sessions are saved locally (autosave on, 30-day default retention); daily log files are written by default with pattern-based redaction (NANOCODER_LOG_DISABLE_FILE turns them off). Optional prompt scrubbing (default off) masks detected secrets and identifiers but leaves paths and URLs. A cloud endpoint subjects prompts to that provider's terms. No DPA or certification; these are project statements, not an independent network audit.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local endpoint, or a cloud API covered by an institutional processing agreement. Restrict network tools (fetch_url, web_search, browser, MCP), keep voice mode on its local backends, and account for local session and log files. Prompt scrubbing is pattern-based and off by default; it is not anonymisation.
suitability_notes.special: Only a local model runtime (Ollama in local-only mode if used) on institution-controlled hardware qualifies, with egress blocked except approved hosts, network tools (fetch_url, web_search, browser, MCP) disabled, the effective configuration checked in each working directory, and sessions/logs on controlled storage. Set NANOCODER_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to stop the automatic npm version check; the models.dev metadata download still needs an egress decision.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free and MIT-licensed; the project states it has no paid tiers. Costs are the chosen API provider's usage fees; no API cost with local models.
final_records.academic: Free community open-source project.
use_cases: local-first coding assistance where code must stay on-machine
low-egress or offline work with local models (documented self-initiated calls: npm version check, which can be disabled, and models.dev metadata)
teaching agentic coding without vendor lock-in

final_records.notes: Community terminal agent (latest release v1.32.0, 2026-11-04; daily commits) with subagents, MCP, LSP tools, hooks, in-process plugins, checkpointing, plan/architect modes and VS Code/ACP integration. v1.32.0 released a headless browser tool, added voice mode (local by default), an opt-in CI/CD review and fix daemon that can post to GitHub, and a directory-trust fingerprint covering hooks, plugins, MCP, project .env, confirmation-relaxing settings and project provider baseUrls. GitHub's licence detector reports NOASSERTION, but LICENSE.md and package.json state MIT. Privacy statements are project documentation, not an independent audit.
final_records.tier_gate: fully local model runtime (e.g., Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, vLLM) for regulated data

required_controls: Local-only provider configuration (e.g., Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, vLLM) on institution-controlled hardware; no cloud provider entries, including per-mode (modeProviders) and session-title (titleProvider) providers, and no cloud API keys in the environment.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Check the effective configuration in every working directory (nanocoder config list/diff): a project-level agents.config.json and NANOCODER_PROVIDERS are merged over the global file and can add providers or override nanocoder.* settings and disabledTools; the v1.32.0 trust fingerprint covers project provider baseUrls and confirmation-relaxing settings but not disabledTools or modeProviders.

Block or allowlist network egress at host or network level and verify the block; set NANOCODER_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 in the shell environment to stop the automatic npm version check, account for the models.dev metadata download, and install a pinned version that is updated centrally.
Remove network-capable tools via disabledTools (fetch_url, web_search, browser) and approve each MCP server, including servers an ACP editor sends per session.
Keep voice mode off or on its local Whisper/Piper backends (no /voice stt|tts cloud); leave ciWatch and daemon verify/auto-fix off unless their GitHub egress is approved.
Enable nanocoder.sandbox for execute_bash (macOS sandbox-exec, Linux bubblewrap; not supported on Windows) or run inside an isolated VM/container.
Keep sessions (30-day default) and logs on controlled encrypted storage; set sessions.retentionDays and NANOCODER_LOG_DISABLE_FILE per institutional policy.
residual_risks: No-telemetry statements are project documentation, not an independent network audit.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

A project-level agents.config.json in the working directory (for example in a cloned repository) can change disabledTools, modeProviders and titleProvider without triggering the directory-trust prompt; v1.32.0's fingerprint re-asks only for hooks, plugins, MCP, formatters, LSP servers, the project .env, confirmation-relaxing settings (alwaysAllow, defaultMode, sandbox, verify.trustLevel) and project provider baseUrls.
The OS sandbox does not restrict file reads and does not cover custom tools or MCP; headless and daemon-triggered runs execute tools (including the browser tool) without confirmation.
ACP sessions start in auto-accept, where MCP servers sent by the editor run unprompted and are not run through the project-config security check.
The browser tool does not prevent DNS rebinding between Nanocoder's address check and Chromium's own lookup (per its docs).

Open security-labelled issues on the project tracker as of 2026-11-06 (e.g., #1942 fetch_url SSRF guard bypass via IPv6-embedded IPv4, #1981 setup wizard writes agents.config.json with API keys world-readable, #1661 /doctor prints URLs with embedded credentials).
Local sessions, logs, semantic-memory files, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Qwen Code
final_records.deployment: local CLI (also desktop app, VS Code/Zed/JetBrains extensions, an experimental local daemon/web UI via qwen serve, and an experimental self-run Managed Agent mode); inference via cloud providers or local/self-hosted endpoints
final_records.model_backend: Multi-provider: Qwen Account with Subscription (Qwen OAuth sign-in with a Plus or Pro subscription from chat.qwen.ai, added in v0.26.8 on 2026-11-05; separate from the free Qwen OAuth tier discontinued 2026-04-15); QwenCloud (Token Plan or pay-as-you-go API key; China and International platforms); Alibaba Model Studio (Coding Plan, Token Plan or standard API key; Beijing and international/Singapore endpoints); built-in third-party providers DeepSeek, Grok, MiniMax, Z.AI, Kimi, Idealab, ModelScope, OpenRouter, Requesty; any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or Vertex AI endpoint; local OpenAI-compatible servers (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio).
final_records.data_handling_note: Docs state Qwen Code itself does not use prompts, code or responses for model training; training and retention follow the configured backend. Own API key: that provider's terms. Alibaba Model Studio (international): Alibaba Cloud says it never uses customer data for training but stores call data (period not stated); Token Plan Personal Edition is offered only in Singapore in Global deployment mode, so inference may happen elsewhere (cross-border transfer; the Team Edition page does not state this); Team Edition states conversation data is not used for training. QwenCloud: no training or retention statement found on the fetched international data-security page. Qwen Account with Subscription (new in v0.26.8): the Qwen consumer Privacy Policy (effective 2026-09-07, operator NTH Power Global Tech Singapore) allows de-identified user content and feedback to be used for model training, with no training-specific opt-out stated (only general data-subject rights such as the right to object) and an unspecified retention period; the same policy says the service does not provide features that process sensitive personal data. Usage statistics are ON by default for every authentication method (privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=true) and go to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; docs say they exclude prompts, responses, file content and PII, but the source also sends a pseudonymous installation ID, session ID, OS type/version, CLI version, model name and, for OpenAI-compatible auth (which includes local Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio endpoints), the configured base URL. Disable with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false or QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED=false (the environment variable takes precedence; a trusted project's .qwen/settings.json can switch the setting back on unless a system settings file overrides it). OpenTelemetry export is off by default; if enabled, logPrompts defaults to true. Automatic update checks and installations on startup (general.enableAutoUpdate) and a daily models.dev catalog download are also on by default; since v0.26.7, turning usage statistics off also stops the catalog download.

suitability_notes.personal: Only with a local/institution-hosted inference endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, an institutional OpenAI-compatible server) or a provider under an institutional DPA. Alibaba Model Studio (international) states no training on customer data but stores call data with no stated retention period, and Token Plan Personal Edition inference runs in Global mode with cross-border transfer; no DPA, QwenCloud terms or Beijing-region terms were reviewed here. Do not use Qwen Account with Subscription: it runs under consumer Qwen terms that allow training on de-identified content. Disable usage statistics (on by default).
suitability_notes.special: Only in a fully researcher/institution-controlled configuration: local CLI plus a local or institution-hosted inference endpoint (Ollama only in local-only mode) with every model role pinned to it, usage statistics disabled, automatic updates off, OpenTelemetry off or exported only to an institutional collector, the web_fetch tool blocked by a deny rule, and Qwen Account sign-in, Browser Use, Computer Use, Channels, Mem0, web search, Managed Agent mode and remote MCP servers not used. Any commercial cloud backend is not acceptable.

final_records.pricing: Tool free and open source (Apache-2.0); free with local models. Inference is billed by the chosen backend. Alibaba Cloud international docs (checked 2026-11-06): Token Plan Personal Edition Lite $6, Essential $10, Standard $18, Pro $68 per month (temporary new-user prices on Lite and Essential); Token Plan Team Edition Standard $20, Advanced $75, Premium $180 per seat per month, plus a $700 shared usage pack; QwenCloud lists the same Personal Edition prices. Coding Plan (now labelled legacy) Pro $50/month with limited, daily-restocked slots. Pay-as-you-go API also available. Coding Plan and Token Plan (Personal and Team) keys are for interactive use only, not automated scripts or backends. Qwen Plus/Pro subscription prices for Qwen Account sign-in were not visible without signing in. Beijing-region (CNY) prices not checked.
final_records.academic: No academic or student program found on fetched Qwen Code or Alibaba Cloud Model Studio pages.
