final_records.notes: Originally based on Gemini CLI v0.8.2 but independently developed since v0.1 with a multi-protocol provider layer, desktop app, agent plugins and its own release cadence - accepted as an independent open-source CLI agent, not a thin fork. Actively maintained: stable v0.26.8 on 2026-11-05 (twelve stable releases from v0.25.1 on 2026-10-11 to v0.26.8 on 2026-11-05), nightly builds and daily commits. Since October: QwenCloud added as the first /auth entry (v0.25.3); docs now state that usage statistics apply to every authentication method (resolving the earlier ToS conflict); Qwen Account with Subscription sign-in added (v0.26.8); Computer Use (desktop-app control via an opt-in MCP server, can capture window screenshots; documented for the upcoming CUA 0.27.0 release, whose packages the docs say are not yet published) and an experimental local Managed Agent mode (downloads a Java server JAR from an Aliyun OSS mirror on first launch) documented. Browser Use, Mem0 and Channels remain opt-in. Offline installation from a release archive with SHA256SUMS is documented.
final_records.tier_gate: local or institution-hosted endpoint + usage statistics off (default on) + web_fetch denied + no Qwen Account sign-in or cloud integrations, for regulated data

required_controls: Point Qwen Code only at an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio) on the workstation or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network, configured via modelProviders; no commercial cloud provider, QwenCloud or Alibaba Model Studio entry or key in the configuration, and no Qwen Account with Subscription sign-in.

Pin every model role to that endpoint: set model.name to a local model, leave fastModel, advisorModel, visionModel and compactionModel empty (fast, advisor and compaction then use the main model; an empty visionModel auto-picks a same-provider vision model) or set them only to local models, leave imageModel empty, keep agents.builtin.exploreModel at inherit, and do not configure subagents to use any other model. The settings docs state that advisorModel and visionModel send conversation content to the named model even when it uses another provider.
Keep cloud provider API keys out of the shell environment, .env files (Qwen Code auto-loads the first .env file it finds) and the env field of settings.json.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the server config of the account that runs it), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Disable usage statistics in two places: privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false in the system settings file and QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED=false in the system-wide environment (default is enabled for every authentication method; events go to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; the environment variable takes precedence, and a trusted project's .qwen/settings.json can otherwise switch it back on).
Keep OpenTelemetry off (default) or export only to an institution-controlled collector with logPrompts=false.

Block the built-in web_fetch tool with a permissions.deny rule or tools.disabled; keep web search off; do not enable Browser Use, Computer Use (node-repl MCP server), Channels, Mem0 or remote MCP servers for these sessions.
Keep artifact publishing at its default local mode (artifact.publisher=local); the source code also offers 'host' (user upload command) and 'oss' (Alibaba Cloud OSS upload) modes.

Set general.enableAutoUpdate=false (default true: update checks and installations on startup) and manage upgrades centrally; set model.catalogRefresh=false in the system settings file or QWEN_CODE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH=off in the shell environment to stop the daily models.dev download. Do not use the experimental Managed Agent mode (qwen serve --managed), which downloads a server JAR on first launch. On air-gapped hosts, install from a verified release archive (--archive with SHA256SUMS).

Enforce these settings in the system settings file (Linux /etc/qwen-code/settings.json, Windows C:\ProgramData\qwen-code\settings.json, macOS /Library/Application Support/QwenCode/settings.json), which overrides user and project settings. Before sensitive sessions, check the effective configuration: a project .qwen/settings.json overrides user settings, environment variables (including those loaded from .env files) override all settings files, and QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH can redirect the system file.

Block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the model endpoint and verify the block before processing special-category data; on Linux, tools.executionSandbox with network "closed" can additionally confine tool commands.
residual_risks: Prompts and file contents go to whichever endpoint is configured; adding a cloud provider, signing in with a Qwen account, switching models with /model or pointing a side-model setting (fastModel, advisorModel, visionModel, compactionModel) at another provider sends data off-host.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost baseUrl alone does not show that inference stays local.
Usage statistics default to on and include the configured base URL; a missed setting discloses endpoint metadata to Alibaba Cloud.
web_fetch is available by default and auto-approval modes can approve it without a prompt, so a missing deny rule lets the model fetch external URLs.
Browser Use operates in the signed-in Chrome profile and can capture page text, screenshots and cookies; Computer Use can capture desktop window screenshots and accessibility text.
Local sessions, logs, memory and tool outputs under ~/.qwen require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Fast release cadence (twelve stable releases between 2026-10-11 and 2026-11-05): defaults and integrations change often, so settings need re-checking after each upgrade.

final_records.name: Factory (Droids)
final_records.vendor: Factory (factory.com; website moved from factory.ai, product and API hosts remain *.factory.ai)
final_records.deployment: Factory Managed: Factory-hosted control plane (US, or a Factory-operated EU deployment on Enterprise); Droid runs on local machines, CI/CD, machines connected through Remote Control, or Factory-hosted Droid Computers / Factory Private (private preview): Factory-hosted control plane by default, with Droid sandboxes in the customer's VPC or data centre through the self-hosted OpenCompute orchestrator (private preview); a customer-hosted control plane only by arrangement / Custom Deployment: all of Factory inside the customer network with the sales-gated airgap build
final_records.model_backend: Factory-managed models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI plus a Droid Core open-weight pool, with an optional automatic Factory Router. BYOK custom models cover provider keys, cloud AI platforms (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure OpenAI), OpenAI-compatible gateways and local servers such as Ollama or LM Studio. Airgap builds use only customer-configured models. Model availability and multipliers change.
final_records.data_handling_note: Factory states customer code is not used as training data. Organisation SaaS Product Terms (27 Oct 2026) bar using Customer Data to develop or train AI models without prior consent; the DPA (2 Nov 2026) bars processing for model training or product improvement and requires return or deletion within 60 days after termination, apart from encrypted backup archives. The same SaaS terms let Factory use Usage Data (configurations and interactions, excluding Customer Data) for any lawful business purpose, including product improvement. Individual terms (14 Jul 2026) let Factory use Customer Data internally to provide the service and to generate aggregated de-identified data, which it may use and retain for business purposes including product improvement. Product-level retention: CLI sessions are mirrored to Factory cloud by default (cloudSessionSync true; users can switch it off, org admins can pin it); AutoWiki content (wikiCloudSync, on by default) also syncs. Orgs can set deletion of synced sessions after 14-365 days (sessionRetentionDays); no default period is published. Factory-hosted operational logs follow Trust Center terms, which are not publicly readable. The privacy policy (updated 26 Oct 2026) no longer states a storage region or a maximum retention period: data is processed primarily in the US, kept as long as necessary, and enterprise workspace data falls under the customer's DPA. ZDR is listed for Business and above; its scope relative to session sync is a contract question. Mythos-class Anthropic models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) carry 30-day trust-and-safety retention where org admins opt in. Telemetry: in connected deployments OTEL metrics (with user, session and repo attributes unless aggregate granularity is pinned) also go to Factory's collector; message-content spans are off by default and go only to a customer collector. Airgap builds send no runtime data to Factory.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a Business/Enterprise contract with the DPA (EU SCCs; EU deployment for residency on Enterprise). The DPA annex (2 Nov 2026) now covers individuals whose personal data sits in code, files and prompts, but excludes special-category data unless agreed in writing. Switch off cloud session sync and AutoWiki cloud sync, or set a short sessionRetentionDays; restrict models to ZDR-covered endpoints and avoid opt-in Mythos-class retention; keep message-content telemetry off or on an institutional collector. Inference-layer ZDR alone is insufficient.
suitability_notes.special: The documented qualifying route is a sales-gated Custom Deployment with the airgap build, in-network model endpoints and an in-network OTEL collector. Factory states Airgap Mode is cooperative, so isolation must come from institutional network controls. Factory Private does not qualify by default: Factory hosts the control plane, only sandboxes run in the customer VPC, and connected deployments send metrics to Factory's collector; it may qualify only once a contract places the control plane, inference, session storage and collectors inside institution-controlled infrastructure. Factory Managed (including EU), Factory-hosted Droid Computers and the public DPA (special-category data not anticipated unless agreed in writing) do not qualify.

compliance: Vendor-stated SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 (docs); reports are gated in the Trust Center and were not reviewed.

Public DPA (last updated 2 Nov 2026) with EU SCCs (Irish DPC as supervisory authority); its annex covers individuals whose data is contained in Customer Data and states that special-category data is not anticipated unless agreed in writing.

The public BAA template page has been removed (HTTP 404); the privacy policy and SaaS Product Terms require a separate BAA under an enterprise agreement before PHI is processed. A BAA does not make cloud routes suitable for special-category data in this catalog.
Enterprise EU deployment keeps session content and inference in the EEA; organization records, user profiles and billing data remain in the US deployment.
final_records.pricing: Pro $20/month, Plus $100, Max $200 (rolling 5-hour, 7-day and 30-day rate limits; prepaid Extra Usage from $10; Droid Core open-weight pool after Standard Usage; BYOK free up to an allowance). Teams $60/month per team plus $40/seat, up to 10 seats. Business and Enterprise custom: Business lists ZDR, SSO/SCIM and audit logs; Enterprise adds dedicated compute with partitioned inference, on-premise options and data residency. Factory Private, OpenCompute (both private preview) and airgap Custom Deployments are sales-gated. Confirm contract, model exceptions and session retention.
final_records.academic: Factory for Science offers free Droid access by application: personal licences for graduate students, postdocs and independent researchers (institutional email or evidence of active research) and team licences with admin controls for labs and institutions. The plan tier, usage limits and which privacy controls (ZDR, session sync/retention settings) apply are not published. A separate free-access application exists for open-source contributors.
use_cases: hosted or local asynchronous coding agents opening PRs from chat- or tracker-assigned tasks
air-gapped/on-prem autonomous coding for security-sensitive institutional codebases
enterprise-governed multi-agent software maintenance (code review, QA, incident response)
final_records.notes: Droid agents across the Factory App (desktop), Droid CLI, SDKs, headless exec and Slack/Linear/Jira/Teams delegations; Factory-hosted Droid Computers and Environments (generally available 12 Oct 2026) provide remote sandboxes, and OpenCompute (private preview, 14 Oct 2026) runs those sandboxes in customer infrastructure under Factory's control plane. The agent loop runs where Droid is installed, while model calls, session sync and metrics leave the machine in connected deployments. Website moved to factory.com; service hosts remain *.factory.ai. Factory announced acquisitions of Typedef (30 Oct 2026) and HumanLayer (4 Nov 2026); no product change from these acquisitions is documented yet. Releases are near-daily (CLI v1.0.0 on 29 Oct 2026; v1.5.0 on 6 Nov 2026).
final_records.tier_gate: special-category data: enterprise Custom Deployment with the airgap build, in-network models and collector (Factory Private only if a contract moves the control plane, inference, session storage and collectors in-boundary; private preview); personal data: Business/Enterprise contract (ZDR, DPA) with session sync off or short retention

required_controls: Use an enterprise Custom Deployment with the airgap build, with model endpoints, the OTEL collector and any managed-settings endpoint inside institution-controlled infrastructure. Use Factory Private only after a contract places the control plane, inference, session storage and collectors in-boundary; its default keeps the control plane at Factory.

Restrict models to in-network custom endpoints (airgap builds offer only customModels; connected builds use modelPolicy allowedBaseUrls/allowCustomModels), and confirm a localhost Ollama endpoint is not serving Ollama Cloud models. Factory-managed models, the Factory Router, session sync and Factory telemetry are unavailable in Airgap Mode; do not use Factory-hosted Droid Computers or Factory-managed Environments.
Pin telemetry.endpoint to an in-network collector and keep message-content export off unless that collector is approved for the data.
Enforce network isolation and sandbox egress rules, because Factory describes Airgap Mode as cooperative rather than an enforcement mechanism.
Limit MCP servers, plugins, hooks, Git remotes and external integrations to in-boundary destinations.
residual_risks: Airgap builds, Custom Deployments, Factory Private and OpenCompute are sales-gated; Factory Private and OpenCompute are in private preview.

Connected deployments (Factory Managed and default Factory Private) keep a Factory-hosted control plane and always send OTEL metrics to Factory's collector (session, model, tool and repo attributes; user identity unless aggregate). A CLI release note mentions a telemetry opt-out, but the enterprise docs do not document a setting that stops this.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls; opt-in message-content spans are exported raw without redaction.
The agent can run arbitrary commands, so the boundary depends on the institution's network and sandbox policy.
Factory's BYOK docs state that Ollama Cloud models work through the same localhost Ollama endpoint, so a localhost base URL alone does not prove local inference.

final_records.name: Roomote
final_records.deployment: Self-hosted (the only publicly offered route since 2026-10-28): one-command Docker Compose install on an own Linux server or VM (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or Debian 12+; public HTTPS by default, or a private network with internal TLS per the operator reference), with local Docker task sandboxes by default. Railway/Render/Fly.io templates and hosted sandbox backends (Modal, E2B, Daytona, Blaxel, Box, Azure Container Apps, Vercel Sandbox) move hosting or execution to provider infrastructure; Coolify runs the published images on a Coolify-managed server (self-hosted PaaS). Roomote Cloud (managed single-tenant deployment per workspace on Railway with Modal sandboxes, US-hosted) was removed from the public website, README and docs on 2026-10-28; existing hosted deployments are kept and its Cloud privacy policy and DPA remain online.
final_records.model_backend: BYOK direct APIs (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Amazon Bedrock, Azure, DeepSeek, xAI), gateways (OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Vercel AI Gateway, Requesty, OpenCode Zen) and linked subscriptions (e.g. ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Kimi for Coding); self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, vLLM, generic /v1) are documented with setup pages, and every model role can inherit the coding model. Coding tasks use an embedded OpenCode harness and need tool-calling models. Managed 'Roomote inference' (spend-capped credit) appears only where a hosting deployment provisions it. Optional judgment model: TypeSafe/OpenRouter/Vercel routes, or the Roomote judgment model at R_JUDGMENT_UPSTREAM_URL (docs: served on Roomote-operated infrastructure; self-hosted stacks can run it as a local CPU sidecar).
final_records.data_handling_note: Self-hosted (main route): Roomote says it does not receive deployment content; code, prompts, tasks and model traffic stay on the operator's infrastructure and the providers it connects. Content-free anonymous telemetry (usage events, daily aggregate instance report; forwarded to PostHog, US) is on by default and admin-disableable; a daily version check (instance ID and version) is documented as not optional. Licensed (>10-user) deployments report licence/user-count data to Roomote even with analytics off (docs: activation with Roomote's licensing service, lease up to 72 h, not sent to the Ping service; operator reference: keys verified offline, licence ID and user count sent to the Ping service; the sources still conflict). Memory is optional and admin-enabled. Embeddings come through an OpenRouter or OpenAI key unless a self-run embeddings upstream is configured. The docs say synthesis runs through the deployment's helper model, but the local-embeddings section says synthesis still goes to the configured memory provider (the docs are inconsistent). Vulnerability watch (new 2026-10-22, off by default) sends dependency names and versions to OSV. Roomote Cloud (no longer listed on the public website or docs; existing managed deployments; Cloud Privacy Policy and DPA last updated 2026-07-23): Customer Content processed under a DPA with SCCs; 'We never use Customer Content to train AI models'; BYOK inference goes straight to the customer's provider (model providers are not subprocessors); workspace deletion destroys deployment and backups; unconverted trials deleted 7 days after expiry; account metadata up to 30 days; billing records up to 7 years; usage telemetry and anonymous analytics cannot be disabled; subprocessors Railway, Modal, Vercel, Resend, Stripe, Google, PostHog, Intercom (all US); no SOC 2 or similar certification. The managed 'Roomote inference' credit and the Roomote-operated judgment model are not described in the Cloud legal pages, so their provider and retention are UNVERIFIED.

suitability_notes.personal: Self-hosted: disable anonymous telemetry, leave Vulnerability watch off or accept OSV lookups, and use an institution-approved inference provider or local endpoint; local Docker execution alone does not keep model traffic in the institution. If Memory is enabled, the OpenRouter/OpenAI contract must cover it. Existing Roomote Cloud deployments: DPA with SCCs, US hosting, single-tenant; BYOK inference under your own provider contract; no SOC 2/ISO 27001; avoid managed Roomote inference and the Roomote-operated judgment model, which the Cloud legal pages do not describe. Roomote Cloud is no longer listed on the public website or docs, so new users should plan on self-hosting.
suitability_notes.special: Self-hosted route only: institution-controlled Linux host reached over a private network only (internal TLS; no Cloudflare or other third-party tunnel), local Docker sandboxes with egress=none, every model role pointed at an institution-run Ollama (local-only mode), vLLM or OpenAI-compatible endpoint that forwards nothing to external providers, Memory off, Vulnerability watch off. Roomote Cloud, Railway/Render/Fly.io templates, hosted sandbox backends and cloud inference providers do not qualify. Documented configuration only; not tested hands-on.

final_records.pricing: Self-hosted: free up to 10 registered users with no licence key; $249/mo for 11-50 users; $499/mo for 51-100 users; 100+ by contact. Licences are requested from help@roomote.dev (self-serve purchase through Roomote Cloud was removed on 2026-10-28). Hosting, sandbox and inference costs are paid directly to those providers (BYOK or a supported subscription). Roomote Cloud pricing is no longer published.
final_records.academic: No academic or student programme found on first-party pages. FCL-1.0-ALv2 permits any non-competing use and explicitly names internal use, non-commercial education and non-commercial research; self-hosting is free up to 10 registered users.
use_cases: chat-assigned background coding tasks returned as reviewable PRs
self-hosted institutional coding agent where repositories (on self-managed GitLab or Gitea), task sandboxes and (via Ollama or vLLM) model inference stay on university infrastructure
team-shared agent fleet with cost analytics across BYOK inference providers
final_records.notes: Asynchronous, single-tenant coding-agent platform, now positioned as self-hosted only: on 2026-10-28 Roomote removed Roomote Cloud from its website, README and docs (PR #3611, 'preserving existing hosted deployments'). Very active development (v1.20.1 on 2026-11-05, several releases per week), so re-check settings after upgrades. FCL-1.0-ALv2 is source-available: no competing commercial service and no bypassing the 10-user licence key; each release converts to Apache-2.0 on its second anniversary. A self-hosted sandbox alone does not make inference local: the special-category route depends on pointing every model role at an institution-run endpoint.
final_records.tier_gate: Special-category data: self-hosted deployment reached over a private network only (no third-party tunnel), with an institution-run inference endpoint that forwards nothing to external providers for all model roles (Ollama in local-only mode), telemetry off, sandbox egress=none, Memory and Vulnerability watch off. A licensed (>10-user) deployment reports licence/user-count data to Roomote; the docs say paid seats need a current activation lease with Roomote's licensing service (up to 72 h), while the operator reference says keys are verified offline. Personal data: self-hosted with an appropriate model-provider contract, or an existing Roomote Cloud deployment under its DPA (not managed Roomote inference). Roomote Cloud is no longer listed on the public website or docs (existing hosted deployments are kept); whether it accepts new sign-ups is not documented.

required_controls: Self-host on an institution-controlled Linux server or VM (one-command installer); do not use Roomote Cloud or the Railway/Render/Fly.io templates
Reach the deployment over the private network only (--tls-mode internal, clients trust Caddy's local CA); do not front it with Cloudflare Tunnel or another third-party tunnel
Keep the default local Docker sandbox provider; do not configure hosted sandbox backends (Modal, E2B, Daytona, Blaxel, Box, Azure, Vercel Sandbox)
Set DOCKER_WORKER_EGRESS_POLICY=none

Connect only an institution-run Ollama, vLLM or OpenAI-compatible endpoint on a private network; remove every other inference provider (including any managed Roomote inference) and set every model role (coding, orchestration, helper, vision, audio/video, review, explore, advisor) and any fallback to it

The endpoint must serve only models hosted on institution-controlled hardware and must not forward requests to external providers (a LiteLLM-style gateway qualifies only if it meets this); verify with egress monitoring

If the endpoint is Ollama, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models
Set the judgment model to off or the local CPU sidecar (COMPOSE_PROFILES=judgment); leave TypeSafe/OpenRouter/Vercel judgment routes and Jev-based experiments disabled

Leave Memory disabled; the docs say local embeddings (COMPOSE_PROFILES=brain,local-inference) keep embeddings on your hardware while synthesis still goes to the configured memory provider, so enable it only after confirming every Memory call reaches the institution endpoint; do not configure OpenRouter/OpenAI R_BRAIN_* keys
Keep no cloud provider API keys (e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, TypeSafe or R_BRAIN_* keys) in the deployment environment or .env
Turn off anonymous telemetry in Settings > Deployment
Leave Vulnerability watch disabled (the default): when enabled it downloads the CVE feed from GitHub and sends dependency names and versions to OSV
Use self-managed Git (GitLab with GITLAB_BASE_URL, or Gitea) and email/password sign-in; leave Slack/Teams/Telegram/Discord/email, web search (Exa), voice and third-party integrations unconfigured

Enforce egress at host or network level (allow only the institution inference endpoint, self-managed Git and any Roomote metadata endpoints the DPO accepts; open image pulls only in a controlled install/upgrade window) and verify it with egress monitoring

Decide with the DPO whether the metadata-only daily version check (and, on licensed >10-user deployments, licence/user-count reporting) may leave the network; the effect of blocking or redirecting it via R_PING_BASE_URL is undocumented, and the licence forbids circumventing licence-key functionality
Run upgrades as deliberate operator actions and re-verify the effective configuration (Settings and environment) after setup and after every upgrade
Obtain institutional DPO/IRB approval before processing special-category data
residual_risks: A daily version check to Roomote's ping service (instance ID and version) is documented as not optional; R_PING_BASE_URL is configurable, but behaviour when the check is blocked or redirected is not documented; first-party sources also conflict on whether it can be turned off: the Website Privacy Policy lists version-check data among the anonymous analytics sent by deployments 'that have not opted out', while the docs Privacy page says the check is not optional (treat it as not optional)

First-party sources conflict on licensing: the docs Users page says paid keys are activated with Roomote's licensing service (lease up to 72 hours, otherwise the free 10-user limit applies) and that licence usage is not sent to the Ping service, while the operator reference says keys are verified offline and licensed deployments report licence ID and registered-user count to Roomote's Ping service even with analytics off

Roomote Cloud was removed from the public website, README and docs on 2026-10-28 and paid licences are now arranged by email; licensing-service continuity for self-hosted paid seats is not separately documented

The operator reference prerequisites still list a stable public HTTPS origin, a required GitHub App and Slack/Teams sign-in, and the docs source-control checklist assumes a public HTTPS URL, so a fully private deployment with self-managed GitLab/Gitea is assembled from several pages, not documented end to end
Whether task sandboxes can clone from a private-network GitLab under egress=none is not documented (Gitea clone traffic is documented as routed through a local proxy)
Memory documentation is internally inconsistent about where synthesis runs (helper model vs the configured memory provider) when embeddings are local
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same local endpoint, so pointing Roomote at Ollama does not by itself keep inference local
Installer and upgrades pull images from GitHub Container Registry and the judgment sidecar downloads its model from Hugging Face; no offline or mirrored installation is documented
Docker sandboxes share the host and the documentation says they are not a multi-tenant isolation boundary
Agent quality on local models depends on tool-calling support and hardware; Roomote's recommended model catalog targets cloud providers
Network behaviour of the embedded OpenCode harness, including any built-in web fetch tool, was not separately reviewed; sandbox egress=none and host-level egress blocking are the backstop
Rapid release cadence can change defaults; re-verify configuration after each upgrade

final_records.name: GitLab Duo Agent Platform
final_records.deployment: GitLab.com (SaaS); GitLab Dedicated (vendor-operated single-tenant SaaS); Self-Managed (customer-operated) with GitLab-managed, hybrid or fully self-hosted AI Gateway and models, including offline licences. GitLab Dedicated for Government (vendor-operated single-tenant SaaS on AWS GovCloud for US government agencies and regulated industries) runs GitLab Duo only on the Duo Self-Hosted architecture, because the GitLab-managed AI Gateway and models are not available there; Agentic Chat and foundational agents are authorized per capability, flows and external agents are not.
final_records.model_backend: GitLab-managed models via GitLab's AI Gateway (Anthropic Claude, with current defaults served through Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform; OpenAI GPT; Google Gemini; Fireworks-hosted Codestral for code completion; open-weight GLM, Kimi, MiniMax). Defaults can change without notice. On Self-Managed: a self-hosted AI Gateway with customer-served models (e.g. vLLM) or customer cloud endpoints (Bedrock, Azure OpenAI). Hybrid features and Duo Core use GitLab's gateway; offline licences cannot use GitLab-managed models.
final_records.data_handling_note: GitLab does not train generative AI models; AI model sub-processors are barred from training on input/output. Product retention: chat and workflow history (chats user-deletable), also kept on GitLab.com for anti-abuse; expanded logging keeps traces; opt-in usage-data collection logs full prompts, responses and tool calls (with a self-hosted gateway these logs stay on customer infrastructure); AI audit event storage (beta, off by default) stores agent-session audit records (metadata-only for some flows), but the setting does not stop real-time audit-event streaming, and before GitLab 19.6 it does not stop writes to audit_json.log. GitLab documents a ZDR policy only with Fireworks AI, and it does not hold when prompt caching is on, which is the default (vendor holds prompts temporarily in memory; cannot be turned off for OpenAI models). Certain Anthropic and OpenAI models have limited vendor-side retention. Prompt-injection scanning via HiddenLayer runs on GitLab's AI Gateway and defaults to Log only on GitLab.com; 'No checks' sends no prompt data to third parties. GitLab's sub-processor list (since October 2026) adds LangChain, Inc. for 'Logging for AI-Powered Product Features' (GitLab.com, Dedicated, Self-Managed); the Duo data-usage page does not say what it logs or how to turn it off. Telemetry: aggregated or de-identified Snowplow usage metrics. A self-hosted AI Gateway keeps code, prompts and responses in the customer network; online licences still send billing metadata to GitLab, offline licences do not connect.

suitability_notes.personal: Accept GitLab's DPA/SCCs; review chat/workflow history and GitLab.com anti-abuse retention; keep usage-data collection, expanded logging and AI audit event storage off unless approved; ask GitLab what the LangChain logging sub-processor receives; decide on HiddenLayer prompt scanning and prompt caching (on by default; cannot be turned off for OpenAI models); prefer models without vendor-side retention, or self-hosted models.
suitability_notes.special: Only Self-Managed Premium/Ultimate with a fully self-hosted AI Gateway and on-premises models (offline licence preferred); no hybrid GitLab-managed features, Duo Core or cloud LLM backends; flows on institution runners with an internally mirrored executor image that includes duo-cli, outbound traffic restricted at the network level to the institution's GitLab instance and AI Gateway, and the sandbox required where available (needs privileged runners); editor-extension telemetry off.

compliance: Trust Center lists SOC 2 (GitLab.com, Dedicated), ISO/IEC 27001/27017/27018, ISO/IEC 42001, CSA STAR and TISAX; documents gated, AI scope unverified
GitLab DPA with SCCs and public sub-processor list (AI: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, AWS, Fireworks AI, HiddenLayer; LangChain for AI logging)
final_records.pricing: Premium $29/user/month billed annually; Ultimate custom. Agent Platform consumes GitLab Credits ($1/credit on-demand list price; commitment pools with volume discounts; GitLab Flex annual commitments via sales). Premium/Ultimate include $12/$24 credits per user/month as a limited-time promotion; Free tier can buy credits. Flows run by service accounts bill the namespace, not included per-user credits. Offline self-hosted use requires the Agent Platform Self-Hosted add-on under a flat-fee ELA.
final_records.academic: GitLab for Education: free Ultimate (unlimited seats, SaaS or Self-Managed) for accredited non-profit institutions, for teaching and non-commercial research only. Community-program subscriptions get no included credits; Agent Platform needs purchased or evaluation credits.
use_cases: automating issue-to-merge-request development flows on institutional GitLab instances
code review and CI/CD pipeline repair agents on research software repositories
air-gapped agentic coding on Self-Managed GitLab with self-hosted open-weight models for sensitive codebases
final_records.notes: Agentic software-lifecycle platform inside GitLab (foundational, custom and external agents, flows run as CI/CD jobs, Agentic Chat in UI/IDE/CLI, MCP client and server), GA since GitLab 18.8 (2026-01-15); actively developed (19.5 released 2026-10-15). Code is under the source-visible GitLab EE licence. Only Self-Managed with a fully self-hosted gateway and on-premises models qualifies for special-category data.
final_records.tier_gate: Premium/Ultimate (Free with purchased credits); special-category data only on Self-Managed with self-hosted AI Gateway and on-premises models

required_controls: Self-Managed Premium/Ultimate with a fully self-hosted AI Gateway on institution infrastructure; every model endpoint it calls is served on institution-controlled hardware inside the network (same host or separate inference servers, e.g. vLLM); no hybrid GitLab-managed features, no Bedrock/Azure OpenAI or other external model endpoints.
Offline licence (cloud-licensing exemption, Agent Platform Self-Hosted add-on, ELA) where no GitLab connection is acceptable; online licences must reach GitLab billing endpoints.
Duo Core off (it needs GitLab's AI Gateway); GitLab.com, vendor-operated GitLab Dedicated and GitLab Dedicated for Government are not acceptable.

Flows only on institution runners using an executor image mirrored to an internal registry and pinned, v0.0.11+ (or custom) with duo-cli included, so jobs do not fetch duo-cli from gitlab.com or the image from registry.gitlab.com.

Runner hosts for flows restrict outbound traffic at the network level (firewall or Kubernetes NetworkPolicy) to the institution's GitLab instance and self-hosted AI Gateway; from GitLab 19.6, also require the execution-environment sandbox (needs privileged runner mode and a working SRT in the image) so flows fail instead of running unsandboxed.
Editor-extension telemetry turned off (VS Code telemetry level 'off') on researcher machines.
residual_risks: Online licences send billing metadata (instance ID, hashed user ID, call count, timestamp) to GitLab; GitLab states prompts, code and responses stay in the network.
Chat/workflow history, expanded-logging traces and AI Gateway logs persist on the instance and need institutional retention, access and deletion controls.
IDE/CLI agents lack network egress controls unless the experimental local sandbox (off by default) is on; MCP servers, external agents and Slack integration can move data out.

Flows run without the network/file-system sandbox when the job image lacks a working Anthropic Sandbox Runtime, unless the sandbox is required; projects with custom images or setup scripts control which srt runs.
GitLab editor extensions send usage and error telemetry to GitLab according to the editor's telemetry setting; whether Duo Snowplow telemetry is emitted from Self-Managed instances is not documented.

LangChain, Inc. is listed as an AI-logging sub-processor for Self-Managed as well as GitLab.com and Dedicated; what it receives from Self-Managed instances with an online licence is not documented (offline licences do not connect).

final_records.name: Clusy
final_records.deployment: cloud
final_records.model_backend: Plan-gated hosted models from DeepSeek (default Auto; mainland China), Moonshot, Alibaba (Qwen, Singapore), Cloudflare Workers AI (Kimi, GLM), AWS Bedrock (Claude) and Azure OpenAI (GPT). Per the docs, Plus adds GPT-6 Luna, while Claude and the other GPT models need Max; the pricing page and product FAQ now also list Haiku on Plus, which the docs model table does not show. BYOK for Anthropic/OpenAI keys on any plan; an optional local runner drives the user's own Claude Code/Codex CLI, with inference still at Anthropic/OpenAI. No local or self-hosted model route is documented.
final_records.data_handling_note: Clusy states it does not train, fine-tune or distil models on customer notebooks, prompts, chat or outputs. It does not send no-training/zero-retention instructions to every provider; provider-side training/retention on the default DeepSeek route is not established. Default Auto and inline completions (on by default; can be disabled in Settings > Models) use DeepSeek (mainland China). Per the Privacy Policy, a hosted-model turn whose provider fails is retried on DeepSeek whatever model was selected (local-runner docs say a dropped runner fails the turn instead; BYOK docs do not address fallback). Titles/tags and memory embeddings go to AWS Bedrock; agent web searches send queries/URLs to Exa and Firecrawl. Where a public IP is available, prompts carry it and an approximate location (opt-out by email). Hosted Fable 5.1 requests may be retained by AWS for up to 30 days for misuse review. BYOK applies the user's provider terms (key stored encrypted). Notebooks, files, chat and outputs persist until deletion; sub-agent logs 30 days; the performance-trace archive and security records have no set expiry. In-app PostHog analytics run by default (exclusion by email request). The local runner is a credential boundary, not a data boundary.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Suitable for public, anonymised or synthetic data. On Free the built-in model is locked to Auto (DeepSeek, mainland China); avoiding China routing there needs BYOK or the local runner. On every plan, inline completions (on by default) use DeepSeek unless disabled, and provider-failure fallback for hosted models can send a turn to DeepSeek; check institutional third-country or export rules even for non-sensitive work.
suitability_notes.personal: No personal-data recommendation: own-service no-training is documented, but provider controls are non-uniform, fallback can reach DeepSeek in mainland China without user choice, and content/trace retention remains material. A DPA is offered on request; institutional review would still be required.
suitability_notes.special: Terms prohibit GDPR special-category data and HIPAA PHI without a separate written agreement, and Clusy signs no BAAs. Execution and inference are cloud-only; the local runner does not keep data off Clusy's cloud. The dedicated in-account deployment offered for Clusy's separate Portal product covers Portal job checkpoints and records only, not the notebook agent, its sandboxes or model inference.

final_records.pricing: Free $0; Plus $12/month; Pro $30/month; Max $90/month (10x Plus usage) or $200/month (30x); Enterprise by call (higher limits, dedicated capacity, SSO, custom billing). Optional pay-as-you-go on paid plans, off by default, with a monthly cap you set. Models, GPUs, RAM and checkpoint storage vary by tier. The pricing page lists paused-sandbox retention (Free released after 3 days, paid 'indefinite'), but docs say there is no guaranteed retention period. Whether the default model and CPU are unmetered on paid plans is inconsistent: the docs say yes, and the Terms (29 Oct 2026) say both yes and no in different paragraphs.
final_records.academic: No academic or student program on pricing, product or documentation pages; Terms mention only discretionary promotional or sponsorship credits.
use_cases: exploratory ML experiments on public or non-sensitive datasets with agent-driven notebook execution
parallel branched model-architecture comparisons on rented GPUs
agentic analysis over non-sensitive Databricks/Snowflake tables
R or Python statistical analysis of public datasets in agent-driven notebooks
final_records.notes: Privacy Policy and Terms revised 29 Oct 2026 (effective 28 Nov 2026), mainly to add Portal; the notebook's data flows, retention and provider list are unchanged. Security page rewritten 29 Oct 2026: no SOC 2/ISO 27001 or other certification, no independent penetration-test report, no bug bounty. Clusy launched Portal (blog 2 Nov 2026; Terms call it invitation-only early access), a separate runtime that moves Python jobs between machines in the user's own cloud accounts; it is not a coding agent and does not change where notebook code or inference runs. Since September: native R notebooks and an in-sandbox terminal whose recent commands and output are summarised to the agent. Sandboxes reach the public internet: GPU sandboxes have no outbound restriction and Clusy does not inspect what a sandbox sends; connecting GitHub clones repositories, including private ones, to Clusy's servers. DPA on request; no HIPAA BAA. An October engineering blog says a local/remote execution bridge will 'soon' deploy; still not documented as a product feature. Retained cautiously for public/nonsensitive work; no personal or special-category route approved.
final_records.tier_gate: no qualifying route; personal data would at minimum need a signed DPA, a written commitment excluding mainland-China routing (Clusy says the product alone cannot guarantee this) and institutional review; Enterprise terms are not public. Special-category data is excluded by the Terms without a separate written agreement, and no route qualifies even with one because execution and inference run only in vendor-operated cloud.

residual_risks: Cloud control/provider processing remains outside customer-controlled infrastructure; paired-machine execution does not establish a local-only route.
Code runs only in third-party E2B (CPU) and Modal (GPU) sandboxes operated for Clusy; the documented local runner is a credential boundary, not a data boundary.
Terms exclude GDPR special-category data and HIPAA PHI without a separate written agreement; no BAAs are signed.

Per the Privacy Policy, provider-failure fallback for hosted models can send a turn to DeepSeek in mainland China regardless of the selected model; inline completions also go to DeepSeek unless disabled.

final_records.name: Ada (Automated Data Analyst)
final_records.vendor: Sainesh Nakra (independent open-source project; GitHub: saineshnakra)
final_records.deployment: Local Python package and command line that runs in the researcher's own process. The released version on PyPI (automated-data-analyst 0.7.0, 2026-10-31) provides the CLI, library, tool definitions and the Claude Code/Codex skill, and still bundles the Streamlit UI module and the optional OpenAI layer (extras [app] and [ai]). `ada chat` and the MCP server (`ada mcp`, stdio, or HTTP on 127.0.0.1 by default) were added on main on 2026-11-01 (changelog 0.8.0) and are not yet in a PyPI or GitHub release; on the same day the browser app, the OpenAI layer and the research/modelling workflow moved to the companion repository ADA Lab. The public demo (automated-data-analyst.streamlit.app) runs ADA Lab code, still deployed through a shim app.py in this repository.
final_records.model_backend: None for computation (pandas, SciPy, statsmodels, SymPy on main). Language models are optional callers. On main (unreleased 0.8.0) `ada chat` talks to any OpenAI-compatible chat server: Ollama at OLLAMA_HOST or localhost:11434 by default, or LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM or another server set with --base-url / ADA_BASE_URL (the model must support tool calling); tool definitions are documented for the Anthropic API, LangChain/LangGraph and MCP hosts (Claude Desktop, Cursor, LM Studio and others). Main contains no OpenAI or Anthropic client; the released PyPI 0.7.0 still ships the optional OpenAI layer (ada/ai_insights.py, [ai] extra), which on main has moved to ADA Lab.
final_records.data_handling_note: Package on main (changelog 0.8.0, unreleased as of 2026-11-06; docs/privacy.md, SECURITY.md): reading, cleaning, schema detection, Ask ADA answers, claim checks and folder scans run in-process; no database, no API key, no generated code executed, files written only when a command is told to (ada scan --template, ada skill). Two network paths: (1) `ada chat` sends ADA's instructions, tool definitions, data-file paths (with row counts and column names when there are few files), the user's questions and conversation, and ADA's tool results to the configured model server (--base-url / ADA_BASE_URL, else OLLAMA_HOST, else localhost:11434); the file itself is not sent, but results can name data values such as group labels; a server on localhost is reached directly, bypassing proxies, and ADA_API_KEY goes only to that server. (2) `ada mcp --http` listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and refuses requests from web pages on other hosts unless --allow-origin names them; with --host 0.0.0.0 anyone who reaches the port can read tables under the root. Tools read only files under their root folder. A search of the package source found no telemetry or other HTTP client. When ADA runs as a tool inside Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor or another MCP host, that host passes ADA's results to its own model under the host's terms. PyPI 0.7.0, the current pip install, has no ada chat or ada mcp and still includes the optional OpenAI layer and Streamlit UI (extras [ai], [app]); without those extras and without an OpenAI key it makes no network call. ADA Lab (separate MIT repository, same maintainer), which now holds the browser app and the public demo: uploads to the demo go to a Streamlit server; parsed uploads sit in a process-wide in-memory cache (at most 8 files, up to 1 hour); the optional OpenAI layer sends the planner the typed question plus column names, types and roles, and on a button press sends typed context, schema and computed evidence, which can name segment labels; requests set store=False and a hashed safety_identifier; OpenAI API terms apply (no training by default; abuse-monitoring logs up to 30 days, unless longer retention is required by law or OpenAI approves ZDR). ADA Lab pins Streamlit 1.59.2, whose browser.gatherUsageStats default is true and is not overridden in its config; with headless = true and no server.address, Streamlit looks up the host's external IP at checkip.amazonaws.com on startup; the app stylesheet imports Google Fonts.

suitability_notes.personal: Use the ADA package locally: the CLI or library with no model, or `ada chat` with a model on the same machine or an institution-run server. Do not upload identifiable data to the public demo. ADA's results can name data values, so connecting ADA to a cloud assistant or MCP host (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor) or to a hosted model API sends those values to that provider under its terms. If the ADA Lab app is self-hosted, keep its OpenAI layer off and set browser.gatherUsageStats = false. `ada chat` and `ada mcp` currently need an install from the repository (main after 2026-11-01); with PyPI 0.7.0 do not install the [ai] or [app] extras and set no OpenAI key.
suitability_notes.special: Only the ADA package on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware: the CLI or library with no model, or `ada chat` against a model server on the same host (ADA_BASE_URL, --base-url and OLLAMA_HOST unset or pointing at localhost); no cloud assistant, MCP host or remote model server receives ADA's results; `ada mcp` on stdio or on HTTP bound to 127.0.0.1 without --allow-origin, with --root limited to the project data; host egress blocked. ada-lab not installed in that environment (the ada command hands init/build/demo/research/model/auto/app to ADA Lab when it is installed), unless all ADA Lab controls apply (no OpenAI key and egress to OpenAI blocked, gatherUsageStats off, server.address bound, Google Fonts requests blocked or accepted, upload cache governed).

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free (MIT-licensed open source). Model costs, if any, are those of the model server or assistant the user connects; the optional OpenAI layer (ADA Lab; also PyPI 0.7.0's [ai] extra) is billed to whichever OpenAI key is configured.
final_records.academic: No academic programme; the software is free under the MIT licence.
use_cases: computing numbers from CSV/Excel research tables locally, each with its calculation and the rows used, or a refusal with the reason
giving a local open-weight model (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM) a deterministic statistics tool so the data stay on the machine
checking numbers stated in a draft or an assistant's answer against the data (`ada claim`)
teaching example of a privacy-first LLM-optional analysis architecture
final_records.notes: Single-maintainer personal project with a few outside contributors (six non-maintainer authors in the git history; two since 2026-10-10); very active (about 580 commits between 2026-10-10 and 2026-11-06), GitHub releases v0.3.0 to v0.7.0 (PyPI uploads 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-31), PyPI at 0.7.0; the changelog lists 0.8.0 (2026-11-01), which is not yet a GitHub release or on PyPI. `ada chat` and `ada mcp` exist only on main (0.8.0), not in PyPI 0.7.0. Repositioned in late October from a Streamlit dashboard for business-style tables to a computation and claim-checking tool for language models: CLI, Python library, MCP server, tool definitions and a Claude Code/Codex skill. Numbers are computed deterministically; a model only picks the tool and reads the result, and generated code is never executed. On 2026-11-01 the browser app, the optional OpenAI layer, the paper-table workflow and the modelling mode moved to ADA Lab (github.com/saineshnakra/ada-lab, MIT; not on PyPI as of 2026-11-06), which also serves the public demo. The qualifying route uses the package with no model or a model on the same host and keeps ADA's results away from cloud assistants.
final_records.tier_gate: ADA package run locally (CLI/library, or ada chat with a model on the same host), with no cloud assistant, MCP host or remote model receiving its results and host egress blocked, for regulated data

required_controls: Install and run the automated-data-analyst package on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware; use the CLI or library with no model, or `ada chat` with a model server on the same host (default Ollama at localhost:11434), leaving ADA_BASE_URL, OLLAMA_HOST and --base-url unset or pointed at localhost.

Do not connect ADA to a cloud assistant or MCP host (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor) or to a hosted model API for regulated data: ADA's results, which can name data values, go to that host's model.
Run `ada mcp` over stdio, or over HTTP bound to 127.0.0.1 without --allow-origin; never use --host 0.0.0.0; set --root to the project data folder only.
Block all egress from the host at host or network level and verify that the block works.

Install a pinned, reviewed commit of main (2026-11-01 or later) if `ada chat` or `ada mcp` is needed, since PyPI 0.7.0 lacks both; if PyPI 0.7.0 is used, install it without the [ai] and [app] extras and set no OPENAI_API_KEY.

Do not install ada-lab in the same environment (the ada command hands init/build/demo/research/model/auto/app to ADA Lab when it is installed) unless all its controls apply: no OPENAI_API_KEY and egress to the OpenAI API blocked (the sidebar key field is open to any user), browser.gatherUsageStats = false, server.address bound to 127.0.0.1 (also stops Streamlit's external-IP lookup), Google Fonts requests blocked or accepted, and the process-wide upload cache governed.
Govern local logs, terminal history, `ada scan` answers files and host retention.
residual_risks: Single-maintainer personal project with no stated support commitment; security fixes land only on the latest commit of main (SECURITY.md), and scope and code change daily.
PyPI (0.7.0) lags the repository (changelog 0.8.0); ADA Lab is not on PyPI and its app installs from git main.

Documented install routes (pip install automated-data-analyst, uvx automated-data-analyst mcp) resolve to PyPI 0.7.0, which lacks the MCP and chat commands the docs describe; uvx fetches from PyPI at launch.
ADA Lab pins Streamlit 1.59.2 while upstream is at 1.67.0 (2026-11-05).
In `ada chat` the final answer is model text: a small local model can misreport ADA's numbers, so the printed tool calls and results are the record to check.
Local sessions, logs, the host and its network need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Microsoft Copilot Analyst
final_records.deployment: cloud (Microsoft 365 tenant service boundary)
final_records.model_backend: Reasoning model with Python execution; the current Analyst model and its operator are not documented. Microsoft Copilot draws on Microsoft-hosted models (e.g. Azure OpenAI) and AI subprocessors whose use admins can switch per tenant (OpenAI-operated models, on by default for eligible commercial tenants; Anthropic models, on by default outside EU/EFTA/UK). Microsoft says OpenAI-operated models serve the same GPT-based Copilot experiences. The 2025 launch and GA posts named OpenAI o3-mini; treat that as historical.
final_records.data_handling_note: Microsoft states Analyst runs entirely inside the Microsoft 365 commercial data processing boundary and inherits Microsoft 365 privacy, security and compliance commitments. Prompts, responses and Microsoft Graph data are not used to train foundation LLMs; interactions are stored encrypted as Copilot activity history in the tenant, governed by Purview retention policies and user deletion. Optional user feedback may be used to improve Copilot (not foundation-model training) and is admin-controllable. Copilot opted out of Azure OpenAI abuse-monitoring human review; Anthropic models carry Anthropic-operated safeguards to detect illegal content. Models are Microsoft-hosted (e.g. Azure OpenAI; 'data does not leave Microsoft') or come from AI subprocessors under Microsoft's DPA: OpenAI-operated models (on by default for eligible commercial tenants since 24 Jul 2026; the admin setting does not affect Microsoft-operated Azure OpenAI models; in the EU Data Boundary with documented exceptions; outside in-country processing commitments; in certain Copilot experiences OpenAI's Responses API is used with ZDR subject to OpenAI's limits) and Anthropic models (on by default for most commercial tenants outside EU/EFTA/UK, off by default inside them; excluded from the EU Data Boundary and in-country processing commitments). Admins can also opt in to 'Anthropic models with Data Retention' (e.g. some Fable-class models), processed by Anthropic as an independent processor outside Microsoft's DPA: most inputs and outputs are kept up to 30 days, and content flagged by Anthropic's trust-and-safety classifiers up to two years (classification scores up to seven years); for certain organisations Microsoft states Fable 5.1 runs under the DPA with no Anthropic retention. Separate opt-in AI independent processors (Mistral in Copilot Studio; SpaceXAI in Copilot Studio and Cowork) also sit outside Microsoft's DPA. The fetched Microsoft docs do not say which model Analyst uses or whether Analyst can use any of these opt-in routes. LLM calls can route to other regions under high load; EU traffic stays within the EU Data Boundary (Anthropic models excepted). Python-sandbox data handling is not separately documented (unverified).

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institutional tenant with a Copilot licence, the Microsoft DPA and Purview retention. Keep AI independent-processor routes disabled ('Anthropic models with Data Retention', Mistral, SpaceXAI; all processed outside Microsoft's DPA), and review the tenant's AI-subprocessor settings: Anthropic models sit outside the EU Data Boundary and in-country processing commitments, and OpenAI-operated models sit outside in-country processing commitments.
suitability_notes.special: Microsoft-operated cloud is not researcher/institution-controlled infrastructure; HIPAA/GDPR/ISO claims and the tenant service boundary do not change that under this catalog's rules. No local or self-hosted option exists.

compliance: Microsoft organizational data protection and compliance scope depend on tenant, region, model and contract.

Microsoft's Copilot privacy page lists GDPR, ISO 27001, HIPAA and ISO 42001 offerings for Microsoft Copilot; certifications for OpenAI-operated subprocessor models are maintained by OpenAI, and 'Anthropic models with Data Retention' fall under Anthropic's own terms and DPA.
final_records.pricing: Analyst is included in the Microsoft Copilot user subscription license (USL), which requires a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan and carries fair-use usage limits. In posts dated 23 and 25 Sep 2026 Microsoft describes pairing the USL with usage-based billing (UBB) in Copilot Credits for Cowork, Code, Autopilot, new advanced experiences in apps and frontier models (no effective date stated); the business pricing FAQ (checked 2026-11-06) lists Copilot Cowork, Code, Autopilot and the Work IQ APIs as usage-based today. For enterprise customers UBB stays off until an admin creates a spending policy. US list prices on 2026-11-06: Microsoft 365 Copilot (enterprise add-on) USD 30.00/user/month paid yearly (USD 31.50 paid monthly, annual commitment); Microsoft 365 Copilot Business add-on (existing customers with an eligible Business plan) USD 21.00/user/month paid yearly, promotional USD 18.00 for the first year (offer 1 Jul-31 Dec 2026). Regional prices vary; confirm the institutional licence.
final_records.academic: Microsoft's education page lists Microsoft 365 Copilot as an academic offering at USD 18 per user/month (footnote: US prices accurate as of October 2025; regional prices vary). That page does not name Analyst; Microsoft states Analyst comes with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and is reached with a work or school account. Confirm EDU SKU contents and local price with the institution's licensing partner.
use_cases: statistical analysis of institutional spreadsheets and uploaded datasets inside the university M365 tenant
chain-of-thought data exploration with inspectable Python code
report/insight generation grounded in tenant documents under existing M365 governance
final_records.notes: Organizational cloud data analyst with inspectable Python execution, included in the per-user Copilot licence (USL) under Microsoft's September 2026 pricing model. Product family now branded Microsoft Copilot. Check the tenant's AI-subprocessor settings before personal-data use; organizational no-training does not make vendor-cloud processing a controlled-infrastructure route.
final_records.tier_gate: Copilot USL licence on a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan; for personal data: institutional tenant + Microsoft DPA + Purview retention, with AI independent-processor routes (incl. 'Anthropic models with Data Retention', Mistral, SpaceXAI) left off

residual_risks: Microsoft-operated cloud is not researcher/institution-controlled infrastructure; HIPAA/GDPR/ISO claims and the tenant service boundary do not change that under this catalog's rules. No local or self-hosted option exists.

final_records.name: Zerve
final_records.deployment: Zerve cloud (SaaS; the security page also describes managed cloud as 'an isolated tenancy we operate') / Bring your own cloud (BYOC): the Zerve app stays in Zerve's cloud at app.zerve.ai while code, results, environments and deployments run in the customer's AWS account (guided CloudFormation stack), existing GKE cluster or existing AKS cluster; set up by an org admin, plan not stated in the docs, and the pricing page lists self-hosted cloud under Enterprise / Enterprise Self-Managed: the whole platform, including the app, via private Helm chart on customer Kubernetes, on-premises or own cloud, with a documented air-gapped pattern
final_records.model_backend: Agents use Anthropic (default provider), OpenAI, Google Gemini, Amazon Bedrock (Claude models through the organization's own AWS credentials; only when compute runs in the customer's AWS account) or OpenRouter; admins approve providers and enable models (supported-models list dated 2 Oct 2026). New organizations start with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Claude Haiku 4.5. BYOK: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini and OpenRouter keys at organization level. Self-Managed also supports any customer-operated OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway. The security and pricing pages claim open-source, privately hosted and fully local model support, but the technical docs name no validated self-hosted model.
final_records.data_handling_note: The security page (Nov 2026) states that customer data 'never trains any model, ours or anyone's'. This is a web-page statement, not a contractual term. It sits in the section on own keys, gateways and local models, and the same sentence says Zerve never stores keys, while the docs say BYOK keys are kept in the organization's vault (the page also marks BYOK as unavailable on cloud and self-hosted VPC, contrary to the docs). The Terms of Service (effective 9 Jan 2026) let Zerve use Customer Data only to provide, operate and maintain the product; product improvement may use derived statistical data but not Customer Data itself. No training, prompt-retention or ZDR statement appears in the Terms, the privacy policy or the user docs. Zerve publishes no terms for the model-provider accounts it uses on the managed route (Anthropic is the default provider), and the docs say some newer Bedrock models require provider data sharing to be enabled in the customer's AWS account. Data handling therefore stays unknown. The privacy policy (effective 22 Jan 2024, unchanged) says the Services are hosted in the US, keeps personal data while the account is open, names Amplitude, Segment and Sentry, and lists OpenAI and Exafunction (Codeium) but not Anthropic as AI subprocessors. The Terms reserve residual backup copies after deletion. The EULA lets Zerve monitor use, including with third-party monitoring software, partly 'to help guide our future development'. BYOC keeps execution and storage in the customer cloud but the app and control plane stay Zerve-hosted; current docs no longer state the control-plane region. Self-Managed runs the whole platform in the customer environment and can route all agent traffic through a customer-operated OpenAI-compatible gateway.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Zerve cloud or BYOC only under an institutional agreement/DPA with Zerve that fixes model-provider routing, no-training terms, content retention/deletion, subprocessors and hosting location; the no-training statement is on a marketing page, not in the Terms. The public privacy policy (January 2024) lists OpenAI but not Anthropic, the default provider, and says the Services are hosted in the US. BYOC alone is insufficient because the app and control plane stay Zerve-hosted. Organization BYOK keys under the institution's own provider agreements cover only the model-provider leg; Zerve's own processing, retention and hosting still need the agreement. Self-Managed with a controlled gateway is the stronger route. Keep superagent channels (Slack, Telegram, X) and external MCP servers off unless approved.
suitability_notes.special: Only Enterprise Zerve Self-Managed can qualify. The whole platform must run on institution-controlled Kubernetes (on-premises or institutional cloud; the Self-Managed docs include an air-gapped pattern). All agent traffic must go through an institution-operated OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway that serves only institution-hosted models and forwards nothing to external providers; verify by egress testing that AI blocks also use the gateway. Zerve's gateway docs describe a gateway that holds provider credentials and makes the outbound calls itself, and they name no self-hosted model, so the in-boundary upstream is the institution's responsibility. Zerve cloud (including the managed isolated tenancy), BYOC and direct provider keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, OpenRouter) do not qualify.

final_records.pricing: The public pricing page (Nov 2026) shows only Enterprise (custom, per firm; on-premises, self-hosted cloud or managed cloud), a free Enterprise trial and a free self-serve start with a work email; it no longer lists Pro or Team prices. The docs list Free (50 credits a month; the largest Claude and newest GPT models excluded), Pro ($25 per user/month with 250 credits a month; add-on packs of 250 for $25) and Team (500 credits a month per seat; add-on packs of 500 for $50; seat price not stated), with Enterprise custom. Model usage is billed at the provider's price plus 20%, at about $0.10 per credit, and compute is billed per second in credits. With the organization's own API keys the provider is paid directly and Zerve still charges orchestration credits at a reduced rate, plus compute. AWS Marketplace purchase is no longer confirmed: the pricing FAQ answer to that question does not mention it.
final_records.academic: No academic discount or academic plan on the pricing page or in the plans docs. A University Partnerships page (US universities listed) offers curriculum integration with sandbox access, hackathons and guest lectures on request. The Terms of Service allow free Education Accounts for academic/non-profit noncommercial use at Zerve's discretion; eligibility and limits are not published.
use_cases: AI-assisted notebook analysis (Python, R, SQL) with persistent learnings and memory for research data teams
long-running multi-agent 'superagent' missions with inspectable notebook code, schedules and parallel batches
self-managed or BYOC data-science workspace inside the institution's own infrastructure
interactive reports, apps, APIs and scheduled jobs deployed from notebooks
final_records.notes: Agentic data and research platform with two products sharing one organization: Workspace (notebooks, threads, Evolve Mode agent) and Superagents (long-running multi-agent missions). Since October both the website and the user docs target quant, investment and data teams at hedge funds, banks and asset managers; the docs still call Zerve an 'AI platform for data and research work'. Deployment options are Zerve cloud, BYOC and Enterprise Self-Managed; the separate Self-Managed documentation (LLM Providers page last updated 14 Sep 2026) covers an air-gapped install and a customer-operated OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, which makes a configured special-category route possible when the gateway is backed by institution-hosted models. No self-hosted model is named or validated in the technical docs. The user docs now say the Self-Managed documentation is available on request, although the Self-Managed site is still publicly reachable. The security page states 'ISO 27001 certified', but Zerve publishes no certificate, scope, certification body or trust centre (security documentation is on request), so compliance stays empty. The 'SOC 2 compliant' wording seen in October is no longer found (the platform page now returns 404).
final_records.tier_gate: Enterprise Zerve Self-Managed with an institution-operated LLM gateway to institution-hosted models for special-category data; institutional contract/DPA with Zerve covering training, retention, hosting and subprocessors, plus either verified Zerve-managed model routing terms or organization BYOK under the institution's own provider agreements, for personal data on Zerve cloud/BYOC

required_controls: Enterprise Zerve Self-Managed install on institution-controlled Kubernetes (on-premises or institutional cloud); Zerve cloud, the managed isolated tenancy and BYOC do not qualify

All agent traffic routed through an institution-operated OpenAI-compatible gateway (LLMGW_API_BASE) whose upstreams are institution-hosted models; the gateway serves only models on institution-controlled hardware and forwards nothing to external providers; no install-level or organization-level provider keys; verify by egress testing that AI blocks on the compute backend also use the gateway
Egress blocked except to the gateway, with build images, base images and package indexes mirrored internally (documented air-gapped pattern)
Agent internet search, superagent channels (Slack, Telegram, X), external MCP servers and other external integrations disabled or blocked
Institutional OIDC identity provider with an access claim rule; institution-operated Postgres, Redis, Vault and object storage
Contract confirming that no telemetry, usage metering, monitoring or licence check sends data outside the boundary; DPO or data-steward approval before use
residual_risks: Zerve's gateway documentation assumes the gateway holds provider credentials and calls cloud providers; in-boundary inference exists only if the institution backs it with self-hosted models. The security and pricing pages now claim privately hosted and fully local model support, but the technical docs do not describe or validate it.

Technical docs name no self-hosted model. The gateway must serve OpenAI-format streaming and tool calls and map provider/model names to local models; Zerve filters out some open-weight models for agent reliability, and agent quality with open-weight models is unverified.
The docs say the gateway carries all agent traffic; gateway coverage of AI blocks is implied by the egress section but not stated.

The Enterprise page claims air-gapped installs run with zero external traffic, while the docs bill orchestration credits even with own keys and the EULA allows usage monitoring with third-party software; how Self-Managed installs meter credits, check licences or send telemetry is not publicly documented.

The Helm chart and images come from Zerve's private registry under an enterprise contract, so the install cannot be inspected before purchase; the user docs now describe the Self-Managed documentation as available on request.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: LM Studio Bionic
final_records.deployment: Desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux x64/ARM64) that runs inference on-device with local models; optional vendor Secure Cloud models (US-hosted) and web search; LM Link (preview) for inference on the user's own remote devices. Enterprise page advertises deployment on own infrastructure or edge devices via sales; no public deployment documentation.
final_records.model_backend: Local open-weight models via the LM Studio runtime (llama.cpp; MLX and, since Bionic 1.1.10, the oMLX engine on Apple Silicon; experimental Splash Metal backend for specific Qwen models on M3-or-newer Macs since Bionic 1.1.5); since Bionic 1.1.8, when LM Studio 0.4.26+ is running, Bionic uses LM Studio for local inference; remote local models via LM Link; optional US-hosted open models in LM Studio Secure Cloud (model names change and differ between vendor pages). Local voice transcription uses Voxtral; read-aloud of responses is on-device (Bionic 1.1.9+). Vision subagents can be set to a local or cloud model.
final_records.data_handling_note: Local route: local models run inference on-device and, with local or LM Link models, no LM Studio account is needed. The LM Studio Desktop App Privacy Policy (effective June 2026) states that local use transmits no messages, chat histories or documents, that the application has no telemetry or user-specific tracking, and that network contact is limited to update checks (app/OS version, IP) and model search/download (anonymized queries). Voice input is transcribed locally. LM Link, if used, uploads the device list to LM Studio servers for discovery. Cloud route (Secure Cloud models, web search): the pricing page states that cloud inference is US-hosted and the policy states transfer to the United States; per the policy, requests are processed transiently, not retained and not used for training, all processing parties, including third-party search providers, operate under 'Zero Data Retention or substantially equivalent terms', and Element Labs acts as processor; the policy also places data from connected Google Workspace connectors under the ZDR commitment. The policy does not name Bionic, which the docs describe as a separate app from LM Studio.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local models with Secure Cloud, web search and other network tools disabled, and governed project folders. Secure Cloud (US-hosted inference) and web search are vendor-side processing under ZDR claims, with transfer to the United States stated in the privacy policy, and need institutional review (GDPR transfer, processor terms) before use with personal data.
suitability_notes.special: Only local models on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware, with Secure Cloud, web search, LM Link, MCP servers, connectors, URL skill installs, browser access and shell Auto Review unused; if LM Studio 0.4.26+ runs alongside Bionic (it then serves Bionic's local inference), the same restrictions apply there. Secure Cloud is vendor cloud and remains unsuitable for special-category data despite ZDR.

final_records.pricing: Pricing page (checked 2026-11-06): Free USD 0 (Bionic agent, local models, offline voice transcription, LM Link up to 5 devices, limited web search); Bionic+ USD 20/month (US-hosted cloud open models, discounted bulk tokens, web search and page extraction); Pro USD 100/month (5x Bionic+ usage limits, early access). Credits cover cloud usage beyond the plan allowance. Teams: centralized credit billing via organizations; team subscription plans listed as coming soon. Enterprise via sales.
final_records.academic: No academic or education discount listed on the pricing page (checked 2026-11-06).
