final_records.name: Juggler
final_records.deployment: Local desktop app plus headless server (official binaries for macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, Windows x64 and Linux x64/arm64; Homebrew cask; or a source build). The server can run on a workstation, dev box or lab server (repo includes Docker packaging, whose image starts with LAN access on) with desktop or browser clients. Accepts loopback connections only by default; LAN access is opt-in, unauthenticated and can be saved to start on every launch; since v0.7.7 a same-machine reverse proxy (e.g. tailscale serve) is admitted only for host names named with --allow-host. Official binaries add WAN modes (Direct P2P via a rendezvous service, Cloudflare Tunnel) that source builds lack. The develop branch (unreleased as of 2026-11-06) moves to one server per machine, so LAN access there exposes every session on the machine.
final_records.model_backend: BYO: Anthropic API and Claude Code CLI, OpenAI API and Codex (ChatGPT plan), GitHub Copilot, Gemini, Mistral, Moonshot Kimi, Z.AI, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints and external ACP agents (e.g. Gemini CLI); local: Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, LocalAI. Optional hosted decision model for Auto-approve: Jev (TypeSafe, decision-only, API key).
final_records.data_handling_note: Per the README, no Juggler service sits in the model path: prompts, code and keys go straight to the chosen provider, and Juggler keeps copies only on local disk. Project state (conversations, session, bash output, per-project env files) is written to <project>/.juggler/, API keys to ~/.juggler/credentials.json (0600), and logs to the platform log directory (10 MB x 5 rotation, 14-day sweep, configurable). Default-on outbound traffic besides the model provider: with Updates on Automatic (the default) the server polls juggler.studio at start and every 6 h, sending version, OS, architecture, any package manager that installed it, and a first-of-day/month mark used to count installs, source builds included (Settings > Updates discloses all but the install mark; Updates can be set to Off, but a manual 'Check for updates' still contacts juggler.studio; official macOS and Windows builds also download found updates in the background); and the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch tools run without approval in the Default and Read-only strategies unless disabled. Up to v0.7.8 the web UI also loaded a diff script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com; v0.7.9 (28 Oct 2026) removed it. All of Juggler's own connections follow one outbound-proxy setting (System, Direct or Manual); loopback always goes direct. No privacy policy or telemetry statement was found. Hosted backends, background 'cheap model' and decision-model jobs (Jev is hosted), ACP agents, MCP servers, extensions and the official binaries' WAN modes each add separate boundaries.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local models or a provider approved under institutional terms for every model role (chat, cheap model, decision model), keep loopback-only access, set Updates to Off where install pings to juggler.studio are not acceptable, and disable the built-in Web Search and Web Fetch tools when prompts may carry personal data (they run without approval). Conversations, bash output and logs persist on disk; there is no privacy policy or DPA.
suitability_notes.special: Only on a single-user, researcher- or institution-controlled machine (or dedicated VM/container) with local inference (Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI) for every model role, background cheap-model and decision-model jobs on the same local model or unset, no hosted-provider keys stored or in the environment, Updates set to Off or juggler.studio egress blocked, the built-in Web Search and Web Fetch tools disabled, v0.7.9 or later (earlier versions load a script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com), loopback-only access with LAN/WAN-on-launch off and no --allow-host proxy, the Default or Read-only strategy (also for `juggler run`, which defaults to YOLO), and no ACP agents, WAN mode, Exa extension or remote MCP server. Young single-maintainer project without a privacy policy; prefer a reviewed source build for air-gapped or clinical environments.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free download, open source (AGPL-3.0-or-later application; Apache-2.0 SDK, bundled extensions and examples). No Juggler account and no resold tokens: model costs go to the chosen provider. LICENSING.md says official binaries may bundle proprietary paid ('pro tier') components; the website lists Direct P2P, Cloudflare Tunnel and in-app updates as what official binaries add, and no paid plan or price was published as of 2026-11-06. Commercial licensing for uses the AGPL does not permit is on contact.
final_records.academic: No academic or student program found; free open source.
use_cases: inspectable agentic coding: in the Default strategy, writes and most shell commands from Juggler's own tools wait for approval (shell commands the built-in analyser judges read-only and within allowed paths, and commands matching saved patterns, run without a prompt; ACP-agent backends run their own tools outside this), and every recorded model transaction (prompt, tools, output, tokens) can be opened
coding agents on sensitive codebases with local models (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, LocalAI)
self-hosted headless server on lab hardware with desktop or browser clients
teaching how agent tool-calling works (branching threads, editable context trees, MCP tool inspection)
final_records.notes: GUI-first local agent workbench (Go server, desktop app, browser clients) with persistent on-disk sessions; very active single-maintainer project (eleven releases 14 Sep to 28 Oct 2026, latest v0.7.9; daily commits through 6 Nov, including an unreleased rewrite to one server per machine). Loopback-only by default; LAN mode is unauthenticated; extensions run unsandboxed with the app's privileges; the develop SECURITY.md warns that any process or account on the machine can drive the agent, and that an approved agent command can turn on LAN access or a tunnel. Default-on egress besides the model provider: the update check contacts juggler.studio and counts installs, and the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch tools run without approval; for offline or regulated use set Updates to Off and disable the web tools. Official binaries are built from a private repository and add proprietary WAN modes (Direct P2P, Cloudflare Tunnel).
final_records.tier_gate: local inference (Ollama in local-only mode, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI) for every model role + single-user host + default loopback-only access + Updates set to Off + built-in Web Search/Web Fetch disabled for regulated data

required_controls: Run a reviewed source build (v0.7.9 or later) on a single-user, researcher- or institution-controlled machine or a dedicated VM/container (an official binary only with Updates Off, accepting its unauditable private components), with inference only through local runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI) under the same control.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Point the background 'cheap model' (tab naming, reply suggestions, auto-approve reviewer, extension text generation) at the same local model, or switch it off; leave the decision model unset (it then falls back to the cheap model) or set it to the same local model, never Jev (TypeSafe, hosted).

Store no hosted-provider credentials (Settings, ~/.juggler/credentials.json) and keep cloud API keys out of the environment Juggler starts in (it reads provider keys such as TYPESAFE_API_KEY from it), so no model role can reach a hosted provider.

Keep the default loopback-only access: never enable LAN access (p or --public up to v0.7.9; Start LAN access, `juggler server lan on` or `juggler serve --lan` on the develop branch) on shared networks, leave 'Start whenever Juggler starts' (connectivity.lanOnLaunch) and connectivity.wanOnLaunch unset, add no --allow-host names or reverse proxies, and do not use the official binaries' WAN modes (Direct P2P, Cloudflare Tunnel; WebRTC peer links default to Google's public STUN server). The Docker image starts with LAN access on, so publish its port only to localhost or an isolated network.

Set Settings > Updates to Off (default Automatic polls juggler.studio at start and every 6 h with version, OS, architecture and an install-count mark; official macOS and Windows builds also download found updates in the background) or block that egress, and confirm with egress monitoring after each upgrade. With Updates Off, a manual 'Check for updates' still contacts juggler.studio (without the install mark), so do not use it where that egress is not accepted.

Disable the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch capabilities in Settings > Extensions for every project (stored as plugins.disabled in <project>/.juggler/config.json), or deny the WebSearch and WebFetch tools globally with a beforeTool hook in ~/.juggler/hooks; both run without approval in the Default and Read-only strategies.
Use v0.7.9 or later: up to v0.7.8 the web UI loads diff_match_patch from cdnjs.cloudflare.com on each page load (no integrity attribute); on an older version, block or explicitly accept that egress.

Use the Default or Read-only strategy so writes and most shell commands need manual approval (shell commands the built-in static analyser judges read-only and within allowed paths, and commands matching saved patterns, run without a prompt); do not switch to YOLO or Auto-approve when the approval card suggests it after repeated approvals, save no broad allow rules, and do not run `juggler run` without an explicit --strategy (it defaults to yolo); do not use ACP agents (they bypass Juggler's strategies and their permission requests are auto-allowed by default); keep the Exa extension (ships disabled) and remote MCP servers off; install only reviewed extensions.

Deny shell commands that read ~/.juggler/server.json or call the Juggler server's control API (for example with a beforeTool hook in ~/.juggler/hooks); per the develop-branch SECURITY.md (unreleased per-machine server; the v0.7.9 SECURITY.md does not describe this path), an approved agent command can use that control token to turn on LAN access or a tunnel.

Before each sensitive session, check the effective settings of the project in use (providers, cheap model, strategy, disabled tools); the web-tool disable list is stored per project, so a new project starts with the web tools enabled unless the global beforeTool hook denies them.

Block outbound network traffic at host or network level, allowing only the local model runtime and any host explicitly accepted under these controls, and verify that the block holds; shell commands and extensions run with the user's privileges, so in-app settings alone do not stop egress.

Apply institutional access, retention and backup controls to <project>/.juggler/ (including per-project env files), ~/.juggler/ (credentials.json, env.json, server.json) and the platform log directory, and keep .juggler/ out of shared repositories and sync folders.
residual_risks: No privacy policy (juggler.studio/privacy returns 404), telemetry statement or DPA; Settings > Updates discloses version, OS, architecture and package manager, but the install-count mark is described only in source-code comments, and how juggler.studio handles request logs is undocumented.

Young project (repository created June 2026) with one principal maintainer, rapid releases and no LTS; the network stack is being rewritten (one server per machine, unreleased as of 2026-11-06), so network behaviour can change between versions.
The server binds all interfaces and relies on an application-level LAN gate (403 for non-loopback requests); a host firewall is still advisable.

There is no login on loopback: the develop SECURITY.md states that any process on the machine, under any account, can load the sessions page and drive the agent, so a shared multi-user server is not a safe host.

On the develop branch (unreleased per-machine server, per its SECURITY.md), an agent turn steered by prompt injection can turn on LAN access or a tunnel (exposing every session) through the control token in ~/.juggler/server.json if the command is approved, or automatically under YOLO, Auto-approve or a broad saved rule.
Shell commands run with the user's full privileges; SECURITY.md states the shell filter is not a security control, and agent tools can read files in the home directory, including stored API keys.
Extensions are unsandboxed JavaScript; their declared permissions are disclosure, not containment.
Built-in web tools are enabled by default and disabled per project; a new project or a new version can re-expose them unless a global hook or network egress control is in place.

Versions up to v0.7.8 run a third-party script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com without an integrity check in a page that can approve tool calls; v0.7.9 removed it, but older installs keep that supply-chain exposure.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
Official binaries are built from a private repository and may include proprietary components that cannot be audited from the public source.

final_records.name: OpenSquilla
final_records.vendor: Beijing TokenRhythm Technologies Co., Ltd. (OpenSquilla open-source project)
final_records.deployment: local/self-hosted: desktop app (macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64) or CLI/TUI on Windows/macOS/Linux with a gateway server bound to 127.0.0.1 by default; Docker/Compose publishes the port on 127.0.0.1 with token auth; LAN/public binding is opt-in. Vendor describes fully offline on-prem use; default-on network reporting, update checks and model-recommendation refreshes must be disabled for that. Desktop downloads available updates in the background unless the observability switch is set (installation needs confirmation).
final_records.model_backend: BYOK cloud providers (20+, e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Qwen), the optional TokenRhythm Studio API (aggregates third-party hosted models; since v0.5.8 Desktop can sign in to a TokenRhythm account and make it the primary model connection), or local Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio/OVMS and custom OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoints. The SquillaRouter (BERT-60M INT8 intent classifier + LightGBM tier selection since v0.5.8) and default embeddings run on-device.
final_records.data_handling_note: Configuration, sessions, logs, memory, scheduler state and caches stay on the user's machine. Prompts, tool results and selected files go to the configured provider. Per the policy, web search, channels, browser automation and other integrations contact external services when enabled. Since v0.5.5 (2026-09-23), one default-on Network reporting switch with no consent prompt covers V1 install and daily turn/token counts plus V2 reliability diagnostics and product/growth analytics. V2 events carry a hashed OS-machine-ID device token; V1 events carry a hashed MAC/IP-derived install ID. The policy excludes prompts, file contents and paths from these uploads; servers can see the source IP. OPENSQUILLA_PRIVACY_DISABLE_NETWORK_OBSERVABILITY=true stops all statistics uploads and update checks but does not erase queued events. The retention period and controller of the telemetry server are not documented. Since v0.5.8, when OpenRouter or TokenRhythm is configured (as primary provider or in a saved model profile) or a recommended ensemble mode is enabled, model recommendations are fetched from an Alibaba Cloud OSS (Beijing) bucket at each Gateway start and every 24 hours unless the same switch is set. The install-ID provider header is retired, but the code still attaches session, turn, execution and call-kind correlation IDs to TokenRhythm Studio requests unless the environment variable is set. TokenRhythm Studio's user agreement (updated 2026-10-12) says platform-key calls are relayed to third-party models, inputs and outputs are recorded, and de-identified data may be used for model optimisation unless the user opts out by contacting the company; BYOK calls through Studio are not stored long-term or used for training. Its privacy policy (updated 2026-09-28) says personal information collected in China is in principle stored in China; no fixed retention period is stated.

suitability_notes.personal: Use self-hosted local models and set OPENSQUILLA_PRIVACY_DISABLE_NETWORK_OBSERVABILITY=true before first start (reporting is on by default); govern local state and verify egress. Hosted providers have their own terms. TokenRhythm Studio platform-key calls are recorded and may be used, de-identified, for model optimisation unless you opt out by contacting the company; do not send personal data there without an agreement, and do not sign in to TokenRhythm in Desktop if it should not become the primary model connection.
suitability_notes.special: Only with customer-controlled local models (Ollama only in local-only mode), network reporting disabled before first start, no TokenRhythm sign-in, hosted routes, Browser Use and community skill hubs avoided, and egress verified. Telemetry service retention and controller remain undocumented.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); no paid tiers for the software found. The optional TokenRhythm Studio API is pay-as-you-go with per-model prices published in CNY per 1M tokens (images and video priced per item/second), plus an 'experience officer' programme offering free token credits.
final_records.academic: No academic or student program found.
use_cases: self-hosted agent runtime on lab or institutional hardware (gateway bound to localhost by default)
local-model agentic coding and data tasks with sandboxed shell and file tools
token-cost-sensitive agent workflows (local routing to cheaper model tiers; optional ensembles)
on-premises offline use with on-device routing and embeddings (network reporting disabled)
final_records.notes: Young, actively maintained self-hostable desktop/CLI/gateway agent from Beijing TokenRhythm (v0.5.7 on 2026-10-23, v0.5.8 on 2026-11-06). v0.5.5 expanded default-on reporting to device-keyed reliability and growth analytics; one switch disables all reporting, update checks and model-recommendation refreshes; only its environment-variable form also suppresses TokenRhythm correlation headers. v0.5.8 adds an optional TokenRhythm account sign-in in Desktop that can make the vendor's hosted API the primary model connection. Telemetry retention and controller terms are not published. Controlled use requires disabling reporting before first start, not signing in to TokenRhythm, and enforcing network boundaries.
final_records.tier_gate: fully self-hosted + local models + network reporting disabled before first start + no TokenRhythm sign-in for regulated data

required_controls: Institution-controlled infrastructure only: fully self-hosted with local model backends (Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio/OVMS or an institution-run compatible endpoint that serves only institution-hosted models and forwards nothing to external providers); TokenRhythm Studio and hosted providers avoided, and no TokenRhythm account sign-in in Desktop (it can make TokenRhythm the primary model connection).

Set the environment variable OPENSQUILLA_PRIVACY_DISABLE_NETWORK_OBSERVABILITY=true before first start (preferred over the [privacy] disable_network_observability = true config key, which does not suppress TokenRhythm correlation headers); this also stops update checks, background Desktop update downloads and model-recommendation refreshes. The legacy OPENSQUILLA_UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED alone does not stop V2 statistics.

Keep the gateway on 127.0.0.1 or behind token auth and an institutional firewall; paste the gateway token instead of passing it as a URL query, which writes it to the gateway access log; do not enable Browser Use, web search, channels or community skill hubs for regulated data.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
residual_risks: Network reporting is on by default and keyed to a hashed OS machine ID; a first start before the opt-out is set can upload install and usage statistics. Telemetry server retention and controller are not documented.
Local sessions, logs, memory, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls; disabling reporting does not erase locally queued events.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.

final_records.name: Pi
final_records.vendor: Earendil Works / Mario Zechner and contributors
final_records.deployment: local CLI with local/self-hosted or cloud inference
final_records.model_backend: Cloud APIs/subscriptions (including Earendil's optional Radius gateway, early alpha, which routes inference through OpenRouter) or local inference through the built-in llama.cpp router integration, or Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, SGLang and other compatible endpoints configured in models.json.
final_records.data_handling_note: Local JSONL sessions persist under ~/.pi/agent/sessions by default; --no-session disables persistence. Install/update telemetry (a ping to pi.dev carrying version, OS, runtime and architecture in the User-Agent) and provider attribution headers for OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM and OpenCode are on by default; analytics defaults off. Set enableInstallTelemetry false or PI_TELEMETRY=0; this setting does not control the pi.dev version check or the detailed User-Agent sent to model endpoints. --offline or PI_OFFLINE=1 stops automatic network activity (version check, pi.dev model-catalog refresh, package update checks, telemetry, /bug upload), not model, tool or MCP traffic. /share uploads a session to an organization-visible Radius artifact when Radius sign-in is configured, otherwise to a secret GitHub gist that anyone with the link can view; the sessionShareDestination setting can force gist or radius. /bug can upload a report to radius.pi.dev without login. suitability_notes.personal: Use a governed local endpoint with telemetry off and /share, /bug upload and Radius unused, or a separately approved direct cloud-provider agreement (not Radius, whose alpha terms are not a DPA and tell users to avoid personal data); protect session files.
suitability_notes.special: Only local/customer-operated inference with offline mode, telemetry, sharing, Radius, and unreviewed MCP servers and extensions disabled qualifies. Radius terms (2 November 2026) prohibit submitting health, genetic, biometric or other special-category data.

compliance: MIT source is not a product compliance certification.

final_records.academic: Available without academic eligibility; model-provider offers are separate.

repository editing
terminal automation

final_records.notes: Actively maintained extensible terminal coding agent (interactive, print/JSON, RPC and TypeScript SDK); package @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent reached 1.0.0 on 1 October 2026 and 1.5.0 on 2 November 2026 (npm latest). Canonical repository earendil-works/pi (redirects from badlogic/pi-mono). Built-in MCP, llama.cpp, codemode and tool-search extensions load by default; --no-mcp disables MCP for one run, --no-extensions disables all built-ins, and a -builtin:<name> entry in the extensions setting disables one persistently. Radius is an optional Earendil-hosted, closed-source gateway and artifact service in early alpha. The experimental Pi Durable SDK package in the same repository is not covered by this record.
