final_records.tier_gate: Local endpoint; --offline with install telemetry/analytics off; no /share, /bug upload, Radius or unreviewed MCP; no cloud inference

required_controls: Configure an institution-controlled local endpoint (llama.cpp router via /login llama.cpp, or models.json). Set enableInstallTelemetry false or PI_TELEMETRY=0, keep enableAnalytics false, and run with --offline or PI_OFFLINE=1.

Prohibit /share, /bug uploads and Radius sign-in (which also adds the Radius MCP server); disable built-in MCP (--no-mcp, or "-builtin:mcp" in the extensions setting) or allowlist MCP servers, and review extensions and packages.
Restrict shell tools and network egress (container or VM per Pi's isolation guide); govern local JSONL history or use --no-session.
residual_risks: Only local/customer-operated inference with telemetry, sharing, Radius and external integrations disabled qualifies.
Pi runs tool calls without per-call approval and has no built-in sandbox; context files load regardless of project trust.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Zencoder
final_records.vendor: For Good AI Inc. (dba Zencoder Inc.)
final_records.deployment: Local IDE plugins (VS Code, JetBrains, Android Studio) and Zenflow desktop app using Zencoder-managed cloud models and services / Enterprise private deployment with customer-operated model endpoints; Zenflow can also run on a customer-operated Ubuntu VM over SSH (remote hosts, Zenflow 2.5.1+, still marked experimental)
final_records.model_backend: Managed models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI plus Zencoder Auto (routes across Zencoder-self-hosted and vendor models) and Auto+; third-party agent runtimes (Claude Code and Codex in IDE agents and Zenflow; Gemini CLI in Zenflow); BYOK; or custom settings.json endpoints (OpenAI-compatible, OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini APIs), including documented local Ollama/vLLM.
final_records.data_handling_note: Managed cloud: ToS (updated 15 Jun 2026) §4.1 permits training on Free-account content (including lapsed trials); Trial/Paid training needs 'further consent', which ToS §4.1 says may be given through account settings, product controls, an order form or other written or electronic authorization, while benchmarking and service improvement remain permitted. Zencoder docs and Enterprise pages say code is never used for training; the ToS is the binding text. Managed model providers may retain requests for limited periods; BYOK follows the user's provider terms. Docs list chat messages as retained per org settings and Enterprise retention as configurable, so there is no universal zero storage despite a docs 'zero-storage' claim. ToS §5.3(a) bars personal data in Your Content without exception; the AUP bars personal and regulated sensitive data unless the applicable Governing Terms (e.g. an Enterprise Agreement) or authorized product settings expressly permit it. ToS §4.3 (IDE/hosted services) and Zenflow terms §4.2 (with or without an account) allow usage telemetry, stated to exclude content. The private route (custom local/VPC models, useDefaultProviders:false) serves chat and agent runs from customer endpoints; sign-in, telemetry and integrations remain separate egress paths.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Free-account content (including lapsed trials) may be used for model training; Trial and paid accounts require further consent for training, which may be given through account settings or product controls (ToS §4.1), so check those settings; benchmarking and service improvement remain permitted.
suitability_notes.personal: Standard self-serve terms (Free, Pro, Pro Plus, Pro Max) bar personal data in submitted content (ToS §5.3(a); AUP). Use only under a written Enterprise agreement that expressly permits personal data, with a DPA, no training consent and acceptable product/provider retention, preferably on the private local-model route.
suitability_notes.special: Only private operation with local models (useDefaultProviders:false), all external traffic controlled, and a written agreement that expressly permits special-category data qualifies; standard terms prohibit personal data.

compliance: Vendor states SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 plus GDPR compliance; the Trust Center (trust.forgood.ai) offers certificates and SOC 2 Type II/SOC 3 reports on request. Audit scope not confirmed.

Trust Center subprocessors: Anthropic and OpenAI (AI/ML), Google Cloud (infrastructure, EU/US), Amplitude (analytics), Atlassian, FrontEgg, HubSpot, Slack. xAI is not listed although Grok models are in the managed catalog, and Google is listed for cloud infrastructure only although Gemini models are offered.
final_records.pricing: Free $0 (no bundled credits; BYOK); Pro $45/user/month ($40 billed annually; 30,000 credits), Pro Plus $95 ($85; 80,000), Pro Max $195 ($175; 180,000); Enterprise custom (prepaid usage, private deployment). 7-day trial with 5,000 credits; model credit multipliers; top-ups from $20.
final_records.academic: No current academic entitlement is asserted.
use_cases: coding
repository editing
terminal automation
research software development
final_records.notes: AI agent platform with IDE agents (VS Code, JetBrains, Android Studio) and the Zenflow desktop app; Zenflow Work is a business-task surface outside this catalog's scope. The documented private route uses customer-operated model endpoints and is listed as an Enterprise feature; the default managed service has different training, retention and contract terms. Docs state that further private-deployment controls are still being built.
final_records.tier_gate: Enterprise agreement with private deployment that expressly permits personal/special data; customer-operated local models with useDefaultProviders:false; sign-in, telemetry and integration egress controlled

required_controls: Enterprise agreement covering private deployment that expressly permits personal and special-category data (standard ToS §5.3(a) and the AUP prohibit personal data in submitted content), with a DPA and no training consent.

Declare only customer-operated local model endpoints in settings.json and set useDefaultProviders:false; disable third-party CLIs, cloud BYOK keys, cloud integrations/MCP connectors and cloud multi-repo indexing.
Control and verify egress: Zencoder sign-in, usage telemetry/analytics, auto-updates and any remaining calls to Zencoder services.
residual_risks: Docs document only the model-routing steps and state that additional private-deployment controls are still being built.
IDE plugins require Zencoder sign-in and Zenflow collects usage telemetry with or without an account; exclusion of content from telemetry rests on vendor statements.

IDE plugin agent logs (structured logs panel) and the MCP audit trail (added August 2026) record model responses and tool inputs/outputs; their storage location is not documented (the docs' IDE 'debug information' page returns 404), and traces can be passed to vendor support by Operation ID. Zenflow docs state its log files (agent.log: tool calls and model responses; integrations.log: MCP activity) are stored locally and never transmitted automatically, and Help > Export Logs packages a redacted 24-hour bundle for support; however, Zenflow terms §4.2 say usage telemetry, collected with or without an account, may include error logs (stated to exclude Your Local Content). Organisation Audit Logs (agent usage and tool invocations, exportable; Pro Plus, Pro Max and Enterprise) also have no documented storage location. Sessions, logs, tools and integrations need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Poolside Agent CLI
final_records.deployment: local CLI; inference via Poolside-hosted Platform (the documented recommended login option), OpenRouter (no active OpenRouter endpoints for any Poolside model on 6 Nov 2026), or a customer-operated OpenAI-compatible endpoint (local Ollama/vLLM, or self-managed Poolside inference in a VPC, on premises or air-gapped)
final_records.model_backend: Poolside Laguna models with public weights on Hugging Face (Laguna XS.2 and M.1 Apache-2.0; Laguna XS 2.1 and S 2.1 OpenMDW-1.1), served by Poolside Platform, any OpenAI-compatible server, or OpenRouter (listed, but no active endpoints on 6 Nov 2026); for local Ollama use, Laguna XS.2 is documented for 32 GB RAM or an 8 GB NVIDIA GPU and Laguna S 2.1 for 128 GB unified or system memory; an experimental, unvalidated Laguna XS 2.1 checkpoint is documented for vLLM Metal on Apple silicon Macs with 36 GB or more unified memory.
final_records.data_handling_note: The Poolside Terms (updated 21 Jul 2026) cover Poolside Platform, Chat, Console and the Agent CLI; installing pool binds the user to them. Content (prompts, code, output) may be used to train Poolside models unless the user selects the Training Opt-Out; even after opt-out, content tied to Feedback or flagged for safety review may still be used, and via OpenRouter the third-party platform's settings may govern. Poolside also collects content-free Product Metrics; what the CLI sends in local mode is not documented and no telemetry switch is documented. The CLI shows a startup dialog when a newer version is available (changelog v1.0.16), /share returns a web trajectory-viewer link for the session, and /feedback can attach logs that may contain prompt and response text. The privacy policy (updated 21 Jul 2026) gives need-based retention with no fixed period; a DPA (updated 27 Apr 2026) is incorporated by reference for personal data. With locally pulled Laguna weights on Ollama/vLLM, or self-managed Poolside inference, Poolside docs state code and model traffic stay on the local machine or inside the customer environment; Ollama ':cloud' model tags run in Ollama's cloud even through the localhost endpoint. Built-in web_fetch is on by default, and remote HTTP/SSE MCP servers are not subject to sandbox network rules.

suitability_notes.personal: Prefer a local or institution-operated endpoint. If Poolside-hosted inference is used, set the training opt-out (the DPA is incorporated in the Terms); feedback and safety-flagged content remain usable for training and hosted retention periods are not stated.
suitability_notes.special: Only with locally pulled open-weight Laguna on Ollama (cloud features disabled, no ':cloud' tags; Ollama's own pool integration page uses a ':cloud' model as its example) or vLLM, or self-managed Poolside inference on institution hardware, on premises or air-gapped; web tools, remote MCP servers, /share and /feedback log attachments off; sandbox network policy allow-list (the 'off' value sets no policy) plus host-level egress blocking to Poolside, verified. The standard Terms bar using any Product, including the locally run CLI, for protected health, biometric and other heightened-regulation data unless Poolside permits it in writing, so written permission or an enterprise agreement is a precondition.

compliance: Published DPA with SCCs and UK Addendum (updated 27 Apr 2026); the Trust Center returned HTTP 403, so no certification is asserted.
Standard Terms prohibit processing highly sensitive or regulated data (including PHI and biometric data) with any Product unless Poolside permits it in writing.
final_records.pricing: Poolside docs (log-in page) and the models page still describe free Poolside Platform API keys and hosted Laguna use 'free for a limited time' (limits and end date not stated), but on 6 Nov 2026 OpenRouter lists no active endpoints for any Poolside model (paid or ':free' variants), and user reports on the pool GitHub repository since 1 Nov 2026 say hosted models no longer work; Poolside has published no statement found on this, and its status page shows inference operational, so free hosted availability and current price are unconfirmed. Self-managed and on-premises deployments require contacting Poolside (no public price; poolside.ai/pricing returns 404). Model weights are downloadable under their own licences.
final_records.academic: No academic or student program found on fetched pages.
use_cases: local agentic coding with an open-weight Laguna model served by Ollama on a laptop or workstation
institution-operated coding agent against self-managed Poolside inference on premises or air-gapped
non-interactive pool exec runs in scripts and CI against a controlled endpoint
ACP integration of the same local agent in JetBrains or Zed
final_records.notes: Terminal coding agent from a foundation-model lab that publishes Laguna weights and documents both a local Ollama route and self-managed (including air-gapped) inference bundles. The CLI is proprietary under the Poolside Terms (repository LICENSE: all rights reserved); model licences are separate. The changelog starts at v1.0.0 (28 Apr 2026); GitHub releases run from v1.0.3 (27 May 2026) to v1.0.16 (14 Aug 2026), which is still the latest version on the download server on 6 Nov 2026; the last repository commit is 18 Aug 2026, no issue reply from the Poolside team has appeared since mid-August 2026, and user reports from early November that hosted models no longer work have no Poolside answer. Research-community adoption is not yet established.
final_records.tier_gate: training opt-out, or a local/institution-operated endpoint, for personal data; for special-category data, Poolside's written permission plus locally pulled or self-managed inference with Ollama cloud, web tools, remote MCP and sharing disabled and vendor egress blocked

required_controls: Obtain Poolside's written permission or an enterprise agreement first: Terms section 2.2 prohibits using any Product, including the CLI, for PHI, biometric and other heightened-regulation data.

Connect pool only to locally pulled Laguna weights on Ollama or vLLM, or to self-managed Poolside inference on institution hardware; do not use Poolside Platform or OpenRouter keys, and disable Ollama cloud features (no ':cloud' model tags).
Disable web_search and web_fetch, keep remote HTTP/SSE MCP servers off, and run the local sandbox with network policy allow-list limited to the local endpoint; 'off' configures no network policy.
Do not use /share or /feedback with log attachments; review logs.zip before any sharing.
Block and verify outbound traffic from the CLI host to Poolside services (startup version check, Product Metrics); no telemetry switch is documented.
residual_risks: CLI Product Metrics, update-check and trajectory-sharing behaviour in local mode are undocumented; only network-level verification can confirm no egress.
Without a sandbox, shell tools run on the host with the host's network access; approvals are documented as a convenience, not a security boundary.
Local logs, trajectories and session history stay on disk and can contain prompt and response text; they need institutional access and retention controls.

Proprietary CLI Terms and the separate open-weight model licences (Apache-2.0, OpenMDW-1.1) both apply and can change independently; no CLI release since v1.0.16 (14 Aug 2026) as of 6 Nov 2026, and maintainer activity on the public repository has stalled.

final_records.name: Snowflake CoCo
final_records.deployment: Snowflake cloud service. CoCo in Snowsight runs each session in a Snowflake-managed Cloud Agents container (commercial regions only). The CoCo CLI and Desktop run locally, act on local files and shell, and the CLI can also run tools in a Snowflake-managed container (--cloud). Scheduled CoCo automations (Preview) run unattended in a Snowflake-managed sandbox. All model inference is remote: per Snowflake, open-weight models run on Snowflake GPUs and frontier models on cloud-provider endpoints, reached through cross-region inference.
final_records.model_backend: Cortex models granted to the active role, chosen per session or as an account default (Auto, Auto Intelligent, Auto Efficient or a pinned model). By default all users inherit access to all models. The Service Consumption Table lists Claude, OpenAI GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi models for CoCo, many marked Preview. Snowflake states that frontier models run on cloud-provider infrastructure: Claude on AWS Bedrock, GPT on Azure OpenAI, Gemini on GCP. Some models carry Snowflake's Model and Service Pass-Through Terms.
final_records.data_handling_note: Snowflake states that AI inputs and outputs, including Usage Data, are not used to train models made available to other customers. CoCo inputs are classified as Usage Data and outputs as Customer Data; Snowflake describes Usage Data as accessible to its operations personnel. On all three surfaces, CoCo writes every prompt and response trace to SNOWFLAKE.LOCAL.AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS in the customer account; rows cannot be modified, only an AI_OBSERVABILITY_ADMIN role can delete them, and no automatic expiry is stated. CLI, Desktop and automation runs also keep conversations as Cortex threads in the account, with no stated retention. CLI and Desktop keep full conversations (file content, tool output, SQL) under ~/.snowflake/cortex/conversations/; Desktop memory is stored under ~/.snowflake/cortex/memory/. The CLI --private flag disables conversation persistence and server-side logging. Ratings and feedback comments go to Snowflake as product feedback; per Snowflake, it receives the request ID and comment, not the prompt or response. Desktop Artifacts and Cloud automations (both Preview, Desktop v1.24.0, Nov 2026) publish agent-written files to the account and can email run reports. CoCo requires cross-region inference: prompts and outputs go transiently to the processing region and are not persisted there. Routing is an account parameter (any region, one cloud, or a region group such as AWS_EU or AZURE_EU). The documented default differs between pages and by account age, so check the effective value. Retention at the cloud-provider model endpoints and for Snowsight chat history is not stated, and client-side telemetry from CLI and Desktop is not described. By default, Cloud Agents sandboxes have read-only HTTPS egress to package registries; admins can disable non-Snowflake egress.

suitability_notes.personal: Only under an institutional Snowflake agreement whose DPA and AI terms are confirmed to cover CoCo inputs, which are contractually Usage Data rather than Customer Data. Also required: cross-region routing pinned to an acceptable geography; an actively restricted model list (all models are granted by default); least-privilege roles or Restricted Session Scope; a retention schedule for AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS and Cortex threads; Cloud Agents non-Snowflake egress and web search disabled; and automations (EXECUTE AGENT TASK is granted to PUBLIC by default) and Desktop Artifacts restricted or disabled. Confirm Snowsight chat retention and the pass-through model terms.
suitability_notes.special: Cloud-only. Inference always runs on Snowflake-managed or cloud-provider model infrastructure, which the institution does not control. Not appropriate for identifiable health, genetic or clinical data under this catalog's rule, whatever the contract.

compliance: Scope depends on the Snowflake contract, edition, region and AI terms; no CoCo-specific certification is asserted here.
final_records.pricing: Billed by token consumption in AI Credits per million tokens, at per-model rates in the Service Consumption Table (Table 6(e), effective 4 Nov 2026). Table 2(b) lists On Demand AI Credit prices of $2.00 (Global) and $2.20 (Regional), with capacity pricing by contract value. Individual CLI/Desktop subscriptions start with a 30-day trial and include a fixed monthly usage allowance. Cloud Agents currently carries no additional charge. Automations (Preview) add standard task billing. Warehouse compute and storage are billed separately.
final_records.academic: No CoCo-specific academic or student offer found on fetched pages. Snowflake's general Academia Program for instructors at nonprofit, accredited institutions (blog, Apr 2025) does not mention CoCo.
use_cases: agentic SQL and Python notebook authoring over Snowflake tables
dbt projects and Streamlit apps from the local CLI or Desktop under Snowflake RBAC
machine learning and data engineering workflows with built-in Snowflake skills
sandboxed shell and Python execution in Snowsight Cloud Agents
final_records.notes: Snowflake's data-platform coding agent (also documented as Cortex Code) across Snowsight, Desktop and CLI. Snowsight sessions run in the Cloud Agents sandbox. The Cortex Agents Coding Agent API (GA 26 Aug 2026) gives developers the same runtime. Excel and Google Sheets add-ins, the CoCo Agent SDK, automations and Desktop Artifacts are in Preview. Relevant mainly where an institution already holds research data in Snowflake.
final_records.tier_gate: institutional Snowflake agreement covering CoCo inputs, with pinned cross-region routing, an admin model allow-list, event-table retention and egress controls; not for special-category data

residual_risks: Cloud-only: inference always runs on Snowflake GPUs or on cloud-provider model endpoints (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP), none of which the institution controls. Contractual no-training and no-persistence statements do not make it suitable for special-category data under this catalog's rule.

final_records.name: Notebook Intelligence
final_records.vendor: Plmbr GitHub organization (maintainer Mehmet Bektaş); community open-source project
final_records.deployment: local-capable / self-hosted JupyterLab or JupyterHub extension; cloud provider dependent
final_records.model_backend: Provider-dependent. Default mode supports four providers: GitHub Copilot; OpenAI- or LiteLLM-compatible endpoints, cloud or self-hosted (e.g. vLLM/TGI); and Ollama, local or on a host set through OLLAMA_HOST at server launch. Claude mode uses the Claude Code CLI for chat and the Anthropic API (or a configured Base URL) for inline chat and auto-complete. An experimental ACP mode, off by default, runs OpenAI Codex as its only agent type; since v6.3.0 it needs an administrator-preinstalled codex-acp adapter and no longer downloads one from npm at startup. Launcher tiles open the Claude Code, opencode, Pi, GitHub Copilot CLI or Codex CLIs in a terminal when they are installed.
final_records.data_handling_note: NBI runs inside the user's Jupyter Server and has no central server of its own. It documents no external telemetry: its in-process usage events go nowhere unless an administrator registers a listener. Prompts, surrounding cell source and attached files go to the configured provider. Saved cell outputs are sent when a notebook or cell is attached or read. Ollama keeps inference on the configured host. Claude mode is available to users by default (user-choice) and sends data to Anthropic through the Claude Code CLI outside NBI's provider list; ACP mode is off by default. Launcher tiles run agent CLIs directly in a terminal. API keys are stored in plaintext in ~/.jupyter/nbi/config.json. A remembered Copilot token is encrypted with a shared default password unless one is set. An open pull request (#533) states that chat messages currently load Markdown images without user action (v6.3.0); the fix was unmerged on 2026-11-06.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local Ollama or an institution-operated endpoint, or a cloud provider route covered by an approved DPA or no-training agreement. On shared hubs, pin the provider and set Claude mode by admin policy. Clear sensitive cell outputs before attaching notebooks, and protect the plaintext key file.
suitability_notes.special: Only with the admin-guide HIPAA/sensitive-data preset applied in full, plus extra controls. The preset disables the Copilot, OpenAI-compatible and LiteLLM-compatible providers with environment re-enabling blocked, forces Claude and ACP modes off, disables the command-execute and file-edit tools, and serves Ollama on hardware the institution controls. In addition, hide all coding-agent launcher tiles, remove agent CLIs from the image, block egress to external LLM hosts, GitHub and npm, and pin the NBI version. A self-hosted vLLM/TGI route keeps the OpenAI-compatible provider enabled, and its Base URL is not documented as admin-lockable, so network egress control must enforce it. A LiteLLM proxy that forwards to cloud models does not qualify. The developer calls the preset a starting point, not a HIPAA certification, and it is not institutional approval.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free and open source (GPL-3.0); provider charges, where applicable, are paid directly to the chosen provider.
final_records.academic: free
use_cases: AI chat, inline edit and autocomplete in JupyterLab notebooks
Agent mode that edits, runs and fixes notebook cells
Chatbook natural-language notebook cells
Claude Code sessions inside JupyterLab; experimental Codex via ACP
Administrator-pinned providers, models and feature policies on managed JupyterHub
Local-model notebook assistance with Ollama for sensitive datasets
final_records.notes: JupyterLab extension with its own agent mode, admin policy controls, optional Claude Code mode and experimental ACP (Codex) mode. The repository moved to the plmbr GitHub organization. v6.3.0 (2026-10-29) adds interface translations and an opt-in reply-in-JupyterLab-language setting, and requires a preinstalled ACP adapter. Agent modes and launcher tiles bypass the provider list unless they are separately disabled, so the sensitive-data preset must be applied as a whole and enforced with network egress controls.
final_records.tier_gate: Regulated data only with the documented local-only preset (cloud providers, Claude mode and ACP mode forced off), coding-agent launcher tiles and CLIs removed, egress blocked, and Ollama or an egress-enforced self-hosted endpoint on institution-controlled infrastructure

required_controls: Apply the admin-guide HIPAA/sensitive-data preset in full. Set disabled_providers to github-copilot, openai-compatible and litellm-compatible with allow_enabling_providers_with_env=False. Disable nbi-command-execute and nbi-file-edit with allow_enabling_tools_with_env=False. Set claude_mode_policy and acp_mode_policy to force-off.

Serve models from Ollama on institution-controlled hardware (OLLAMA_HOST set at server launch). If a vLLM/TGI endpoint is used through the OpenAI-compatible provider instead, enforce its Base URL with network egress control, since that field is not documented as admin-lockable. Do not use LiteLLM proxies that forward to cloud models.

Hide all coding-agent launcher tiles with disabled_coding_agent_launchers (claude-code, opencode, pi, github-copilot-cli, codex) and remove those CLIs from the image or PATH, because the tiles are independent of claude_mode_policy and the CLIs stay usable from a terminal.

Block egress to external LLM hosts, github.com, codeload.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com and registry.npmjs.org at the network layer. Pre-install MCP servers and host skills manifests internally. Pin the NBI version and review the changelog before upgrades. Protect the ~/.jupyter/nbi/ secrets.
residual_risks: Claude mode (user-choice by default) and ACP mode reach their own backends outside NBI's provider list. Agent-CLI launcher tiles and the Jupyter terminal are separate surfaces, so disabling providers alone does not make a deployment local-only.
NBI has no provider allowlist mode, so a new built-in provider added in a minor release would auto-enable unless the version is pinned. User config overrides base config for endpoint fields.

Saved cell outputs are sent when notebooks or cells are attached, and API keys are stored in plaintext. Local sessions, staged uploads, logs and tool actions need institutional access, retention and egress controls. The developer describes the preset as a starting point, not a HIPAA compliance certification.

Pull request #533 states that, as of v6.3.0, chat Markdown images in user, model and tool messages load automatically, a channel through which injected content can trigger outbound requests. The fix was not merged on 2026-11-06, so network egress blocking must cover it.

final_records.name: MLJAR Studio
final_records.deployment: local desktop app (Windows, macOS incl. Apple Silicon, Linux via Ubuntu .deb) with local Python execution; AI via hosted MLJAR AI by default, or with the perpetual licence via BYOK cloud providers or local/self-managed model servers
final_records.model_backend: Hosted MLJAR AI by default (underlying model providers not disclosed); with the perpetual licence: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud, or local/self-managed servers (Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, vLLM, llama.cpp, custom OpenAI-compatible)
final_records.data_handling_note: Notebook code and Python run locally. MLJAR AI, a hosted service, is the default LLM provider; its underlying model providers, prompt retention and processing location are not published. The AI policy points to the Privacy Policy for MLJAR AI details, but that policy covers the mljar.com website and accounts and has no MLJAR AI retention or provider terms. The AI policy also states that by default no data is transmitted externally, which conflicts with the hosted default in the provider docs and with the home-page claim that data stays on the computer. MLJAR states it does not train its own models on customer data unless agreed, and does not control how external providers train. With own keys, prompts go to that provider under its terms. A local model keeps prompts on the machine. DataFrame enrichment sends each unique cell value of the chosen column to the provider Studio selects. First launch needs sign-in or licence activation, and AI Provider Settings run a licence access check. The downloads-page FAQ states the app works offline once signed in or activated, and that data does not leave the machine; the second claim ignores the hosted default, and how the access check behaves offline is not documented. Desktop-app telemetry is not documented.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local or institution-operated model endpoint (perpetual licence required), or an own-key provider covered by an approved DPA/no-training agreement. The default hosted MLJAR AI route has no published retention, subprocessor or DPA terms.
suitability_notes.special: Only with the perpetual licence and a local or institution-operated model server on controlled hardware. Leave MLJAR AI, OpenAI, OpenRouter and Ollama Cloud unused, along with conversation publishing, MLJAR-hosted Mercury deployment and cloud database connections. Verify at the network layer that chat, AutoLab, Workflows and enrichment requests reach only that endpoint, and that sign-in, licence and update traffic carries no data.

final_records.pricing: Pricing page on 2026-11-06 (unchanged since 2026-10-10): Free $0 (50 prompts/month), Pro $20/month (500 prompts), Business $60/month (2,000 prompts); perpetual licence $199 one-time with one year of updates, required for Ollama/local servers and own provider keys. EULA: perpetual licence covers 1 user and 3 devices; newer releases after the update period need a renewal. The MLJAR AI docs describe extra hosted usage as an add-on that requires the perpetual licence, and the Terms still call the Studio licence subscription-based; both differ from the pricing page, so verify at purchase.
final_records.academic: No academic or student programme is stated on the pricing page.
use_cases: Natural-language exploratory analysis of CSV/Excel data with generated, inspectable Python code
AutoML and AI-run AutoLab experiments on tabular research data
AI-assisted notebooks with local Python execution and whole-notebook AI edits
Local-model data analysis via Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, vLLM or llama.cpp for private datasets
final_records.notes: Desktop AI data analyst built on local Python notebooks, from the vendor of the open-source mljar-supervised AutoML package; Studio itself is proprietary. The local-model route needs the perpetual licence. The default hosted MLJAR AI route has undisclosed model providers and retention, and the vendor's AI policy misstates the default. Desktop telemetry is undocumented.
final_records.tier_gate: perpetual licence + local or institution-operated model server for regulated data; hosted MLJAR AI not for personal data without a DPA

required_controls: Buy the perpetual licence and configure a local or institution-operated model server (Ollama in Local mode, LM Studio, Jan, vLLM, llama.cpp or custom OpenAI-compatible); confirm the endpoint executes on controlled hardware.

Switch away from the default MLJAR AI provider; do not use OpenAI, OpenRouter or Ollama Cloud; do not publish conversations, deploy Mercury apps to MLJAR hosting, or connect cloud databases (e.g. Databricks, Snowflake, Supabase).

Verify with institutional network controls that model requests from chat, AutoLab, Workflows and enrichment reach only the configured endpoint, and restrict sign-in, licence-check and extension-update traffic.
residual_risks: MLJAR AI is the default provider and its model providers, retention and processing location are undisclosed; the AI policy's statement that no data leaves the machine by default conflicts with this.

Licence activation and the AI Provider Settings access check contact MLJAR. The downloads-page FAQ claims offline use after sign-in or activation, but air-gapped operation, offline behaviour of the access check and desktop-app telemetry are not documented.
Local notebooks, sessions and app logs (documented app-data and log folders) require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: JASP
final_records.vendor: JASP Team (open-source project supported by the University of Amsterdam; institutional support via JASP Services B.V.)
final_records.deployment: Local desktop application; the optional AI assistant (off by default) sends requests to a user-configured OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint: a shipped cloud preset or a Custom Provider URL, which can be a local or institution-operated server
final_records.model_backend: Bring-your-own key/endpoint. Shipped presets in v0.99.0 (community build): OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Xiaomi, xAI (all cloud). An 'Azure OpenAI (Entra ID)' sign-in preset was added in v0.99.0 but is listed only in PRO builds (JASP Services client builds); community builds hide sign-in presets. Custom Provider accepts any OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint; release notes list local models as supported
final_records.data_handling_note: JASP runs no AI service of its own; data handling follows the configured endpoint. The AI is off until enabled; the enable dialog states that information from the data set, analyses, output and chat messages may be processed by the AI service and warns against sensitive, confidential or restricted data. Tool calls return dataset metadata (file path, column names and types, row counts) and analysis results. All shipped community presets are cloud providers; JASP's own blog (October 2026 update) recommends free API tiers, including Nvidia Build endpoints via Custom Provider, while noting that free use means paying with your data. JASP's privacy policy (2018, no AI mention) says the software collects no user data but states it does not apply to the software itself. Update checks are opt-in. Since v0.98.8 the full AI request body is logged only when an internal verbose flag is on (off by default; source comment says dropped in release builds); provider HTTP error bodies are still logged, and log files persist only if logging to file is enabled. Since v0.98.8 administrators can enforce settings via forced.json beside the app or Windows group policy (source code; not described in user docs).

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institution-approved paid provider under a DPA/no-training agreement, or a local/institution-operated endpoint via Custom Provider. Do not use free API tiers, which may use submitted data.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a Custom Provider pointing to a local or institution-operated OpenAI-compatible model server, no cloud preset key stored, and network egress verified. The local route rests on one release-note line and the Custom Provider endpoint field; there is no dedicated setup guide, the pull request lists only cloud providers as tested, and the Azure OpenAI sign-in preset (PRO builds) is a vendor cloud, not a customer-controlled boundary.

final_records.pricing: Free and open source (AGPL-3.0). The AI assistant needs a user-provided API key/model, so provider costs or free-tier data terms apply. JASP Services B.V. offers Economy, Standard and Premium service plans for organisations (no prices published).
final_records.academic: free
use_cases: Natural-language creation and execution of statistical analyses in a GUI
Plain-language annotation and interpretation of analysis output
AI-composed reports combining several analyses
Teaching statistics with configurable AI personas
External agent or MCP access to JASP analyses through an optional local JSON-RPC server
final_records.notes: Established open-source statistics package; optional agentic AI assistant added in 0.98.0 (2026-07-01; pull request titled 'JASP AI Beta'). Releases since: v0.98.8 (release notes 2026-10-11; AI input crash fix) and v0.99.0 (2026-10-21; Azure OpenAI/Entra ID sign-in preset for PRO builds in the provider list). Repository commits continue (2026-11-06). Data handling depends entirely on the configured endpoint; all shipped community presets are cloud providers.
final_records.tier_gate: Custom Provider with local or institution-operated endpoint for regulated data; approved paid provider (no free tier) for personal data

required_controls: Configure a Custom Provider pointing to a local or institution-operated OpenAI-compatible model server; store no keys for cloud presets or free tiers.
Keep the MCP/JSON-RPC server disabled (default), or loopback-only behind a host firewall, because it has no authentication.
Keep logging to file off, or treat JASP log files as regulated data; verify network egress from the workstation.
Where JASP is centrally deployed, consider enforcing AI and RPC settings through forced.json or group policy (v0.98.8+, source code only; test before relying on it).
residual_risks: AI requests carry dataset metadata, analysis output and chat text to the endpoint; a misconfigured or switched provider sends them off-boundary.
When enabled, the JSON-RPC server accepts unauthenticated calls that can load files and read results, and its bind address is configurable.

The AI feature was labelled beta at release and the local-model route has no dedicated documentation or listed testing; JASP's own blog says local models on typical laptops are far less capable than cloud models.
Local sessions, exported reports and logs require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: IBM Bob
final_records.deployment: IBM-hosted SaaS on IBM Cloud (US East, Frankfurt or Tokyo region) / Enterprise self-hosted backend on customer-managed Red Hat OpenShift, including disconnected (air-gapped) clusters
final_records.model_backend: SaaS: IBM selects the model automatically per task; users and organisations cannot choose or restrict models. The FAQ does not name providers but says output indemnity covers 'IBM-developed models and the third-party generative models IBM Bob uses'. Self-hosted: exactly one customer-provided core model through the Model Gateway, either a self-hosted open-weight model from IBM's supported list (at review: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super, Poolside Laguna S 2.1; Mistral Medium 3.5 only with the IBM Z package) or a frontier model via AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Azure OpenAI (listed: Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.7 Flash, OpenAI GPT5.6 Sol); openai/gpt-oss-20b is the documented guardrail model for air-gapped deployments. IBM's vLLM runtime page states that the models it lists (Nemotron 3 Ultra, Laguna S 2.1, Mistral Medium 3.5) accept text input only; no such statement was found for Nemotron 3.5 Super.
final_records.data_handling_note: SaaS (IBM Cloud): the FAQ says prompts, code and responses are held only in temporary memory for the interaction (generally minutes), are never written to persistent storage and are not used to train models; IBM calls this 'effectively zero-retention' and points to the IBM Bob Service Description (not reviewed) for contractual terms. SaaS connects over standard HTTPS only; private connectivity (PrivateLink, VPN) is not supported. The data-residency page says inference, processing and conversation data stay in the selected region (US East, Frankfurt or Tokyo) and expire at session end; account, admin, billing and user-management data are kept in US East regardless of region, and billing metadata is retained under IBM retention policies. Client telemetry (actions, features, errors; IBM says no code or prompts) is on by default and can be switched off; Enterprise Bobalytics needs it on. Bob IDE 2.3.0 (October 2026) adds admin policies for telemetry and external OpenTelemetry export; OTEL export can also be set through the user's local environment variables (policies take precedence when set), and external OTEL exports can include tool inputs and outputs. Task history is stored locally on the user's machine; by default Bob IDE deletes unpinned tasks not updated in 30 days (Settings > Chat > Task retention; 0 disables deletion; pinned tasks are kept), and Bob Shell has the same 30-day default (tasks.retentionDays). Self-hosted (Enterprise entitlement): the backend runs on the customer's OpenShift cluster; inference runs wherever the single configured core model is served, on premises for the supported open-weight models or at AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Azure OpenAI in hybrid configurations. IBM's install guide lists telemetry as disabled for air-gapped installs and on by default (can be disabled) for connected installs. Usage metering reports only the active-user count (automatic 24-hourly upload when connected, manual upload when air-gapped).

suitability_notes.personal: SaaS only under an accepted institutional agreement and the IBM DPA: no training and in-memory payload handling are documented, but account, admin and billing data stay in US East whatever region is chosen. The self-hosted route is preferable.
suitability_notes.special: Only the Enterprise self-hosted deployment on institution-operated OpenShift, installed by the air-gapped method (on-premises inference only, telemetry disabled per IBM's install guide) with a supported open-weight core model and the gpt-oss-20b guardrail served on premises. Hybrid/frontier-model configurations and SaaS do not qualify.

compliance: IBM's Bob FAQ states 'IBM is ISO 27001 certified' at company level; penetration-test summaries and ISO 27001 certificates for Bob are offered under NDA. Bob-specific certification scope and audit reports not reviewed
final_records.pricing: SaaS: 30-day free trial (50 Bobcoins, no payment); Pro $20/month (50 Bobcoins), Pro+ $60/month (180), Ultra $200/month (1000); yearly billing advertised at 20% off; 1 Bobcoin = $0.50; prices indicative, vary by country, exclude taxes; opt-in overage. Enterprise (team admin, Bobalytics, on-premises/air-gapped deployment) via sales; self-hosted needs a self-hosted entitlement and its price is not published. Premium Packages cost extra (DevSecOps $20/month, Java Modernization $20/month, IBM i $40/month; IBM Z Enterprise-only, annual).
final_records.academic: No academic or student programme listed on the pricing page.
use_cases: agentic coding in a standalone desktop IDE (macOS, Windows, Linux)
terminal and CI automation through Bob Shell
codebase understanding and modernization (Java, IBM i, IBM Z packages)
institution-hosted, air-gapped coding assistant on OpenShift with on-premises models
final_records.notes: IBM's agentic IDE and terminal assistant (Bob IDE, Bob Shell); Bob IDE 2.3.0 and Bob Shell 2.0.9 (both October 2026). The self-hosted option became generally available on 30 September 2026 and is Enterprise-only. The validated self-hosted 2.0.0 release pairs with Bob IDE 2.2.0 and Bob Shell 2.0.5; the backend runs on customer-managed OpenShift 4.20-4.22 (amd64); model serving is sized separately, and IBM's recommended vLLM settings (tensor-parallel size 8 for the models on IBM's vLLM runtime page: Nemotron 3 Ultra, Laguna S 2.1, Mistral Medium 3.5) come from H200 testing. This first self-hosted release has no in-place upgrades, no Admin UI activity logs and no Bobalytics. IBM's group-policies page says enterprise policies (including GatewayUrl to pin the backend endpoint) are supported by Bob IDE only; Bob Shell's changelog documents only the EnforcedHooks policy. IP output indemnity is offered for Enterprise only. Product focus is enterprise software delivery and modernization, so research use needs an institutional platform team. The public IBM/ibm-bob GitHub repository carries an Apache-2.0 licence but holds only a README, the issue tracker and the self-hosted install bundle (release v2.0.0); the product itself is proprietary and installation requires accepting IBM licence terms.
final_records.tier_gate: Enterprise self-hosted entitlement, air-gapped installation on institution-operated OpenShift with a supported open-weight model and guardrail served on premises; SaaS and hybrid/frontier-model configurations do not qualify for special-category data

required_controls: Deploy Bob self-hosted (Enterprise self-hosted entitlement) on an institution-operated OpenShift cluster using the air-gapped installation method (mirrored images; IBM documents on-premises inference only and telemetry disabled for this method).
Configure the single core model as a supported open-weight model served on premises (e.g. Red Hat OpenShift AI or vLLM) plus the gpt-oss-20b guardrail; configure no hybrid or frontier model endpoint.

Turn off client telemetry in Bob IDE and Bob Shell, use the offline usage-metering upload, pin clients to the self-hosted endpoint (GatewayUrl policy for the IDE; BOB_GATEWAY_URL for Bob Shell), manage client updates through the UpdateMode group policy, leave the experimental web_search tool off, configure no external OpenTelemetry export, block egress (including Bobalytics links, external MCP servers and browser tools), and set task-history retention to the approved period.

Keep clients on IBM's validated self-hosted pairing (Bob IDE 2.2.0, Bob Shell 2.0.5) or re-validate before upgrading (UpdateMode none/manual); if Bob IDE 2.3.0 or later is used, enforce telemetry off (EnableTelemetry) and no OtelConfiguration by policy, because users can otherwise set OTEL export through environment variables; configure no HTTPS hook handlers that send event payloads to external endpoints.
residual_risks: IBM documents telemetry as disabled for air-gapped installs, but does not state what the IDE and Shell clients send, or where, when connected to a self-hosted backend; confirm with network monitoring before use.

IBM's group-policies page says enterprise policies are supported by Bob IDE only; for Bob Shell only the EnforcedHooks policy is documented, so Shell endpoint, telemetry and update settings rely on per-user configuration.
If external OpenTelemetry export is configured, Bob 2.3.0 can export tool inputs and outputs as spans; the collector then holds code and data.

Bob IDE 2.1.0 added IBM documentation search tools (search_ibm_docs, list_ibm_doc_libraries) and 2.2.0 added HTTPS hook handlers; IBM does not document how they behave against an air-gapped backend, so treat them as possible egress paths and confirm with network monitoring.
On-premises model serving needs substantial GPU capacity and its own hardening; vLLM collects anonymous usage stats unless VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS or DO_NOT_TRACK is set.
First self-hosted GA release: no in-place upgrades and no Admin UI activity logs; security logging is the customer's responsibility at OpenShift level.
Task history and other local sessions, logs, tools and integrations are stored on user machines and require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Coder Agents
final_records.deployment: self-hosted only: agent loop in the customer's Coder control plane (servers, Kubernetes or Docker), workspaces on customer infrastructure; air-gapped installs documented; no SaaS component
final_records.model_backend: Administrator-configured providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (self-hosted models, internal gateways, LiteLLM); optional per-user BYOK.
final_records.data_handling_note: The agent loop, chat history (Coder PostgreSQL database) and tool execution stay inside the customer's Coder deployment; prompts, attachments and tool results go only to the configured LLM provider (except for experimental ACP subagents, below), whose own retention and training terms apply unless a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint is used. Retention defaults keep chats indefinitely: auto-archive is off by default, and only archived conversations are purged (default 30 days after archiving; turning retention off keeps them indefinitely). Project memories (early access since v2.39.0, but not behind an experiment flag, so available by default) are durable agent-written notes kept per project until the agent, an API call or project deletion removes them; the dashboard does not show them yet (experimental API only), and chat retention does not purge them. Chats can be shared read-only with users or groups, and viewers can download chat attachments, unless the administrator disables chat sharing; administrators can access all chats. Chat debug logging (full LLM requests and responses) is off by default; if enabled, debug data is kept 30 days by default. Experimental ACP subagents (off unless the administrator enables the chat-acp-subagents experiment) run external harnesses in the workspace with their own credentials and model provider, outside the configured Coder providers. Deployment telemetry to Coder is on by default and, per the source code, includes per-chat metadata (IDs, status, message and token counts, configured provider and model names) but not message content, plus the administrator email; CODER_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=false turns it off. Licences with usage publishing send hourly Agent Time totals (licence JWT and deployment ID, no chat data) to Coder's Tallyman server, shared with Metronome; air-gapped customers must arrange an alternative with Coder.

suitability_notes.personal: Self-hosted deployment with either a self-hosted model endpoint or a provider covered by an institutional agreement/DPA; disable BYOK where personal keys are not allowed, and set retention and telemetry.
suitability_notes.special: Only with control plane, PostgreSQL and workspaces on institution infrastructure, a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model as the only enabled provider, BYOK disabled, ACP subagents experiment left off, telemetry and update checks off, debug logging off, retention/auto-archive set, chat sharing restricted, and all egress (workspace templates, MCP servers, provider-native web search, STUN/DERP, usage reporting) controlled.

final_records.pricing: Pricing page: Community free (open source), Premium billed annually per user (price not shown), AI Premium custom. Pricing page and Agents licensing docs now agree: Community and Premium allow up to 5 concurrently active Coder Agents deployment-wide (extra agents queue; no Agent Hours limit); AI Premium removes the concurrency cap and draws from a purchased pool of Agent Time. Infrastructure and model costs are separate.
final_records.academic: No academic programme listed on the pricing page; the Community edition is free, and Coder's site links to free homelab licences (terms not checked).
use_cases: delegating coding tasks to an agent that provisions and works in self-hosted Coder workspaces
API-triggered background coding automation on institutional infrastructure
institution-wide self-hosted coding agent with centrally governed models, including on-premises models
final_records.notes: Standalone Go agent built into the Coder control plane; Coder states it is not a wrapper around Claude Code or Codex. Generally available in Coder v2.37.0 (1 September 2026; GA blog 9 September). Coder v2.39.0 (3 November 2026) added early-access chat Projects (shared instructions, skills and agent-written memory persisting across chats) and experimental ACP subagents that delegate work to external harnesses such as Claude Code or Codex inside the workspace. It needs a running Coder deployment with workspace templates, so it suits institutions with a platform or research-computing team rather than individual researchers. Coder's separate Agent Relay connects cloud-hosted agents such as Cursor to Coder workspaces and does not keep inference in-house. Licence: the repository core, including the coderd chat/agent code, is AGPL-3.0 (LICENSE; whether -only or -or-later was not established, so the SPDX id is left as AGPL-3.0); the enterprise/ directory is under Coder's licence-key-gated Enterprise licence (LICENSE.enterprise), shown as LicenseRef-Coder-Enterprise.
final_records.tier_gate: Self-hosted Coder deployment on institution infrastructure with a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model as the only provider; Community (free) and Premium run up to 5 concurrent agents; AI Premium unlimited concurrency against purchased Agent Time

required_controls: Run the Coder control plane, PostgreSQL and workspaces on institution-controlled infrastructure; configure only a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model endpoint and disable AI Gateway BYOK.

Set CODER_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=false and CODER_UPDATE_CHECK=false, disable public STUN and use Coder's built-in or institutional DERP relays, and agree an alternative to Tallyman usage reporting with Coder if a licence with usage publishing is used.

Do not enable the chat-acp-subagents experiment unless every configured harness uses an institution-controlled model endpoint; ACP harnesses use their own credentials and providers, and Coder auto-approves their tool permission requests.

Restrict workspace-template, MCP-server and web-search egress, keep chat debug logging off, set auto-archive and conversation/debug retention to the institution's policy, and restrict or disable chat sharing (CODER_DISABLE_CHAT_SHARING) as policy requires, and review or delete project memories through the experimental memories API, since the dashboard does not show them and chat retention does not purge them.
residual_risks: Chats are kept indefinitely by default (auto-archive off); chat history, attachments, project memories and any debug logs persist in the Coder database, whose access, backup and retention are the institution's responsibility.

Project memory is on by default (no experiment flag) and written by the agent without being asked; the agent is only told not to save personal details, memories are not shown in the dashboard and are not purged by chat retention, so special-category data can persist across chats.
Agent workspaces have full internet access unless templates restrict outbound network access.

Agent quality depends on the self-hosted model chosen; computer use needs an Anthropic or OpenAI provider or a Claude model on AWS Bedrock, and provider-native web search needs an Anthropic, OpenAI or Google provider.

GA only since Coder v2.37.0 (September 2026) with frequent releases, breaking changes and early-access/experimental features (Projects, ACP subagents); v2.39.0 is a mainline release, and Coder advises enterprise customers without a staging environment to install the latest stable release; pin versions and review release notes.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Kimi Code CLI
final_records.deployment: local CLI/TUI (single binary or npm) with a local web UI; Kimi-managed cloud inference by default; Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible and Google endpoints configurable
final_records.model_backend: Kimi Code managed service via /login OAuth (membership quota; managed API at api.kimi.com, or api.kimi.ai/coding/v1 after kimi login --region global) or a Kimi Platform API key from platform.kimi.com or platform.kimi.ai (default base_url api.moonshot.ai); Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible (base_url override, usable for institution-hosted servers), OpenAI Responses, Google GenAI and Vertex AI provider types configurable in config.toml.
final_records.data_handling_note: Default managed route. Users outside mainland China fall under the kimi.ai privacy policy (NOVASCENT PRIVATE LIMITED, last updated 2026-11-05): user content (prompts, files, generated content) is processed to provide and improve the services, including training and optimising AI models, on legitimate-interest or consent grounds 'depending on your jurisdiction'; the policy says consent is obtained where law requires it but describes no training-specific opt-out or objection mechanism, and data may be stored on servers outside the user's country. The kimi.com policy (Beijing Moonshot; new version updated 2026-11-05, effective 2026-11-12) states it applies only to users in mainland China; there, de-identified input/output is used to optimise models, training can be stopped by contacting customer service, and storage is in the PRC. API-key route: the Kimi Open Platform policy (Moonshot AI Pte. Ltd., Singapore, last update 2025-04-30) lists training among uses with no training-specific opt-out; the kimi.ai policy states its relevant provisions also apply to Open Platform products unless that policy provides otherwise; platform terms were not assessed. No DPA found. CLI: anonymous telemetry on by default, with or without sign-in (telemetry=false or KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to disable); per source code it sends device ID, model, session ID and crash/API-error events with paths, emails, URLs and tokens scrubbed, to a region-specific Kimi collector (telemetry-logs.kimi.com for mainland-cn, telemetry-logs.kimi.ai for global). The region follows the login, or before first login the install channel (the code.kimi.ai install script writes 'global'), and otherwise defaults to mainland-cn. The opt-out was ignored in print mode until 0.41.0 (2026-09-04). Auto-update on by default (KIMI_CODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 disables the update check, background install and prompt); signed-in users' web fetches use the managed Kimi fetch service unless an endpoint is set; /feedback can attach diagnostic logs and codebase context; Remote Control (paid membership, signed in) relays sessions through Kimi's relay. Sessions, logs and credentials are stored under ~/.kimi-code.

suitability_notes.personal: Only with an institution-controlled OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a third-party provider under an institutional agreement, with telemetry disabled and no Kimi OAuth sign-in. The managed Kimi routes have no verified DPA; the policy for users outside mainland China uses content for model training with no stated opt-out, and the mainland and Open Platform policies also permit training use.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a self-hosted/institution-controlled OpenAI-compatible endpoint, telemetry=false, no /login to the managed service, no Remote Control or /feedback, auto-update and plugin marketplace controlled, and network egress limited to that endpoint and verified at the network layer.

compliance: MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification; no Kimi Code DPA, certification or data-residency commitment was found.
final_records.pricing: CLI free (MIT). Managed Kimi Code use requires a Kimi membership: Plus and above on current plans (Andante and above on legacy plans); the Go tier has no coding quota. New-plan members have a rolling 5-hour window and a monthly total quota but no weekly limit. Subscribed members can opt in to pay-as-you-go Extra Usage (RMB balance, not available for Enterprise) after quota. Membership prices were not captured (UNVERIFIED). Kimi Platform API keys are billed by the Open Platform; third-party API and self-hosted inference costs are separate.
final_records.academic: No academic or student programme found on fetched pages.
use_cases: terminal agentic coding and repository editing
driving sessions from Zed or JetBrains over ACP
coding against an institution-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint for data-sensitive work
running file and shell tools on an SSH host or Docker container (e.g. a lab server) while model requests stay on the local machine
final_records.notes: TypeScript successor of the archived Python kimi-cli (archived, 'no longer maintained'); v2.0.0 released 2026-09-17, latest stable 2.5.2 on 2026-11-06 with near-daily releases. Includes ACP mode, a plugin marketplace, a local web UI and Remote Control (available without a flag since 0.42.0; started with kimi rc; requires a signed-in paid membership). 2.4.0 added import of local Claude Code and Codex sessions; 2.5.0 added remote environments (SSH, Docker or custom command), where file and shell tools run on the target while model requests and credentials stay on the local machine, and turned web cross-session full-text search off by default. In remote environments, hooks, stdio MCP servers not bound to the target and web search/fetch tools still run on the local machine, so local egress controls still apply. TUI built on pi-tui (MIT); the VS Code extension (Apache-2.0) and Kimi Code Desktop are separate surfaces. The docs document base_url override and vLLM-compatibility fixes but no dedicated local-model guide.
final_records.tier_gate: Institution-controlled OpenAI-compatible endpoint, telemetry=false, no Kimi OAuth sign-in and no Remote Control for regulated data

required_controls: Configure only an institution-controlled OpenAI-compatible provider (base_url to a self-hosted server); do not run /login to the Kimi Code managed service or use a Kimi Platform API key.

Set telemetry=false or KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1; set disable_feedback_survey=true and do not use /feedback; set [upgrade].auto_install=false or KIMI_CODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1; do not start Remote Control (kimi rc), which relays through Kimi's service.

Point KIMI_CODE_PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE_URL to a local file or block it; restrict MCP servers, web search/fetch and online /provider catalog import; limit network egress to the approved endpoint and verify it at the network layer.
Protect ~/.kimi-code session, log and credential files under institutional retention rules.

If remote environments are used, declare only institution-controlled SSH hosts or containers as targets; the target also runs an installed Kimi Code CLI, so install it from a controlled source and apply the same telemetry, auto-update and egress controls on the target.
residual_risks: No dedicated local-model guide; the endpoint override must be validated together with network egress before use.
Telemetry is on by default and posts to a Kimi collector; its opt-out was ignored in print mode until 0.41.0, so a regression could leak metadata unless egress is blocked.

Managed-route policies permit training use (the policy for users outside mainland China describes no opt-out mechanism) and differ by route and region; an accidental managed sign-in moves data to Moonshot under those terms.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Sessions imported from Claude Code or Codex become Kimi sessions; continuing them sends their content to whichever provider is configured.

final_records.name: Deep Agents Code
final_records.deployment: local Python CLI (dcode) that runs a local LangGraph dev server on localhost; tools run locally or in optional remote sandboxes; inference via the chosen provider, including local Ollama
final_records.model_backend: Any LangChain-compatible chat model. OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini integrations are included by default. Extras include Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Groq, Fireworks, Hugging Face, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter and LiteLLM, among others. Also local Ollama, OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoints (configurable base_url), and ChatGPT sign-in (openai_codex).
final_records.data_handling_note: BYOK: no dcode-hosted inference service is documented, so provider terms govern inference. Since 0.2.3 (2026-11-02) dcode requires an explicit or saved model and no longer picks one from OPENAI, ANTHROPIC or GOOGLE keys in the environment (PR #7365); the providers docs still describe the old fallback. The config-file docs also describe a managed-gateway setup: a gateway key exported with OPENAI_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL is used by default, with the LangChain-hosted LangSmith LLM Gateway as the example. LangSmith tracing is off unless a LangSmith key is stored via /auth or the shell already sets LANGSMITH_TRACING=true with a key. It sends agent operations and tool calls to LangSmith. --no-tracing or DEEPAGENTS_CODE_LANGSMITH_TRACING=false disables it. Before 0.2.2 (2026-10-26) the local server could also upload usage metadata to LangSmith when a LangSmith key was set; 0.2.2 stopped this (PR #7252). Default-on network calls: a PyPI update check and auto-install at session start, and an hourly pricing-catalog refresh. Also, on each launch, langgraph-cli sends a usage ping (OS, OS version, Python and CLI version, command name, anonymised flags) to a Supabase endpoint unless LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; dcode does not set this variable and its docs do not mention the ping. Since 0.2.3 the official LangChain plugin marketplace is preconfigured; per PR #7364 its catalog downloads when first browsed or when a plugin is installed, then refreshes via the background updater. Optional cloud services: Tavily web search, remote sandboxes, MCP servers, plugins. Sessions, history and credentials live under ~/.deepagents. Offloaded conversation archives are deleted after 30 days by default.

suitability_notes.personal: Use local Ollama, an institution-hosted endpoint, or a cloud provider under an institutional agreement. Pin allowed models (managed [models].allowed). Keep LangSmith tracing off unless LangSmith itself is approved. Its trace secret redaction does not redact general personal data. Set LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1. Use version 0.2.2 or later. Control remote sandboxes, Tavily web search, MCP servers and marketplace plugins.
suitability_notes.special: Only with local Ollama (or an institution-hosted endpoint inside the controlled network) enforced by a managed model allowlist. Also required: version 0.2.2 or later, tracing disabled, LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1, update checks and pricing refresh disabled, no remote sandboxes, no web-search key, no marketplace plugins, and egress limited to the local endpoint.

compliance: The MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification. LangSmith tracing, Tavily web search and remote sandboxes are separate services with their own terms.
The required local server runtime (langgraph-api, langgraph-runtime-inmem) is Elastic-2.0 licensed according to PyPI metadata (source-available, not OSI).

final_records.academic: No academic or student programme found on fetched pages.

repository editing and test running with approval controls
group-wide agent settings (model allowlist, approval mode, tracing, updates) enforced by administrators via managed_config.toml

Forked from deepagents-cli at v0.1.0 (2026-05-12, per changelog). deepagents-cli is marked deprecated deployment tooling on PyPI, which points to Managed Deep Agents (mda) instead. dcode launches a local LangGraph dev server, whose langgraph-cli wrapper sends an anonymous usage ping unless LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1. Administrators can enforce settings, including a model allowlist, with managed_config.toml.
final_records.tier_gate: Local Ollama or institution-controlled endpoint pinned by managed model allowlist; version 0.2.2 or later; tracing, LangGraph CLI analytics, update checks, remote sandboxes, web search and marketplace plugins off for regulated data

required_controls: Use local Ollama (or an institution-hosted endpoint inside the controlled network) only. Enforce it with managed_config.toml [models].allowed (e.g. ollama:*) so launch defaults, --model, /model, saved defaults, Auto classifiers, rubric graders and explicit local subagent models stay local.
Run deepagents-code 0.2.2 or later, where the local server no longer uploads usage metadata to LangSmith.

Disable LangSmith tracing (DEEPAGENTS_CODE_LANGSMITH_TRACING=false), LangGraph CLI analytics (LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1), update checks ([update] check=false), pricing-catalog refresh (prices_auto_update=false) and remote sandboxes. Store no Tavily web-search key.
Unset LANGSMITH_TRACING and LANGSMITH_API_KEY in the shell environment: disabling dcode tracing does not cover tracing emitted by agents run in shell commands.

Remove the default official marketplace per user (dcode plugin marketplace remove; no managed_config control is documented) and install no plugins; restrict MCP servers and shell egress to the local endpoint; govern ~/.deepagents session, history and credential files.
