The LangGraph CLI analytics ping is on by default and is not documented in the dcode docs; a missed environment variable re-enables it.
Removing the default marketplace is a per-user action; administrators cannot enforce it through managed_config.toml according to current docs.
Docs lag releases: the providers page still describes environment-key model auto-detection that 0.2.3 removed.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: Oh My Pi
final_records.vendor: Stencil Labs, Inc. / Can Bölük (fork of Pi by Mario Zechner)
final_records.deployment: local CLI/TUI with local or cloud inference; optional Stencil-hosted services (encrypted /share server, /collab relay, auto-QA collector, experimental Spotlight tool-output shaping at cloud.stencil.so, and with an invite-only stencil.so account omp stream/clip); self-run auth broker
final_records.model_backend: Cloud APIs, OAuth/coding-plan subscriptions and documented local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM) plus custom OpenAI-compatible providers; downloadable on-device models (local catalog) for auxiliary tiny and speech roles. Unset role chains fall back to built-in priority lists that can include cloud services.
final_records.data_handling_note: Provider terms govern cloud inference. Several network paths are on by default: a startup update check (compiled binaries query build.stencil.so), marketplace plugin-update notices, and a background model-catalog refresh from catalog.stencil.so. Auto-QA (dev.autoqa) is on by default; the first report opens a consent dialog, and on Yes the model-written reports plus model, version and install ID go to qa.omp.sh. Unset tiny-role title generation uses an online model. OTLP export starts only when an endpoint is configured. /share uploads an encrypted session to my.omp.sh/s by default (or a secret gist); /collab uses the wss://my.omp.sh relay (autoStart off); omp stream/clip send screen content to live.omp.sh. The experimental Spotlight setting (spotlight.experiment.enabled, default off) sends tool results to cloud.stencil.so for shaping and ranking, authenticated with the Stencil credential. Local tiny and speech models download their runtimes on first use and their weights on first use unless prefetched, so first use needs network access. Stencil's Privacy Policy (effective 2026-10-02) covers omp and its supporting services and allows training on Content unless the user opts out in account settings; Content submitted as Feedback or flagged for safety review may be used regardless of that opt-out. Stencil's Terms bar GDPR Art. 9 data from the hosted Services. Local use of the MIT software is governed by the licence alone.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local or institution-hosted endpoint, or a cloud provider under an institutional agreement; set dev.autoqa false, leave OTLP unset, keep the Spotlight experiment off, and do not use /share, /collab, stream or clip.
suitability_notes.special: Only with a local server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM) or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint on controlled infrastructure, explicit local tiny/memory/judge roles with empty fallback chains, auto-QA, update checks, sharing, collaboration, streaming, the Spotlight experiment, web_search, browser and cloud security scans off, and egress limited to the local endpoint. Stencil-hosted services are excluded by Stencil's own Terms for Art. 9 data.

compliance: MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification.
final_records.pricing: MIT software is free. Cloud provider APIs/subscriptions and local hardware costs are separate. Stencil's Terms reference Paid Services for its hosted offerings; no omp price was found.
final_records.academic: Available without academic eligibility; no academic programme found.
use_cases: terminal coding with local open-weight models
language-server and debugger-assisted repository editing
coding sessions with persistent project memory
final_records.notes: Fork of Pi (rca-pi) that has diverged substantially (README: about 80k lines of Rust core, LSP/DAP tools, agent memory, collaboration; over 13,000 commits by the lead maintainer); not a thin fork. v18.17.0 released 2026-11-06, about 30 releases since 2026-10-09; open backlog growing (about 2,700 open issues and 2,000 open pull requests on 2026-11-06). Session sharing, collaboration relay, streaming, Spotlight, auth broker and extensions require separate review.
final_records.tier_gate: Local endpoint and explicit local-only role chains; auto-QA, update checks, OTLP, sharing, collaboration, streaming, Spotlight and web search off; no cloud inference or Stencil-hosted services for regulated data

required_controls: Configure only a local provider (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint) on institution-controlled hardware; assign tiny, memory and judge roles to local models with explicit empty fallback chains so no role falls back to online defaults.

Set dev.autoqa: false (or PI_AUTO_QA=0) rather than relying on the consent dialog; set startup.checkUpdate false, keep update.auto false and marketplace.autoUpdate off; keep spotlight.experiment.enabled false and PI_SPOTLIGHT_EXPERIMENT unset; leave OTLP endpoints unset; prohibit /share, /collab, omp stream/clip and Stencil login.

Disable or egress-block web_search, browser, URL reads and cloud security scans; restrict extensions, project inputs (hooks, MCP), shell tools and network egress to the local endpoint; govern local session files.
residual_risks: Default-on update checks, catalog refresh from catalog.stencil.so, install-ID consumers, on-demand tool downloads and first-use installs of local model runtimes and weights create outbound traffic; exercise or prefetch the local models and their runtimes (omp tiny-models, omp setup speech, one test run of each local role) before isolating the host, and verify egress in the deployed configuration.

Stencil-hosted supporting services fall under a privacy policy that allows training on Content unless opted out and Terms that prohibit GDPR Art. 9 data; one accepted consent dialog or share command moves data there.
Very fast release cadence; settings and defaults can change between versions.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: DeepSeek Harness
final_records.deployment: local Node launcher (dsh, npm @deepseek-ai/dsh) with web, headless, ACP and SDK profiles; Python runtime wheel packages the same command; macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows (64-bit) desktop app; inference via DeepSeek official model services or user-configured providers
final_records.model_backend: DeepSeek official model services via a DeepSeek API key or a signed-in DeepSeek account route; built-in third-party providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM) and custom OpenAI Chat Completions/Responses or Anthropic Messages endpoints, including company gateways and self-hosted servers.
final_records.data_handling_note: The Harness privacy policy (last update 2026-09-20, unchanged on 2026-11-06) separates official model services from custom model services. On the official route DeepSeek collects session logs (inputs, uploaded files, model outputs, tool invocations, plugin configuration), uses personal data to train and improve its models, keeps input data for as long as the account exists, and stores data in the PRC; a training opt-out is listed only among rights that may be available depending on jurisdiction. With custom model services no login is needed and DeepSeek Harness does not store or process inputs/outputs server-side; the chosen provider's terms govern. Desktop product analytics are on by default (the `enabled` setting defaults to true) with no user-facing control; they carry available device and user IDs, app version and hardware/OS fields, and exclude prompts, responses and API keys; switching them off requires editing configuration. Ordinary Web clients collect no product events; session telemetry defaults to feedback-only. In the 0.2.2 pre-releases (npm latest 0.2.2-rc.1) the default web-search provider is the DeepSeek Search API: whenever a DeepSeek credential is available, each search sends the query and, unless `sendOriginalQuestion` is set to false, the latest prompt cut to 128 characters to DeepSeek, also when the chat model is a custom endpoint. Whether the Web UI's DeepSeek API-key route falls under this Harness policy or separate DeepSeek Open Platform terms was not checked; both send data to DeepSeek. The vendor labels the project an unaudited developer preview.

suitability_notes.personal: Not recommended during the developer preview: the vendor states the software is unaudited and not production-ready and advises against exposing sensitive data. The official DeepSeek route uses data for training, with PRC storage. This is stricter than comparable open-source CLIs with a local-endpoint route; reassess at the first stable release.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate during the developer preview even though custom self-hosted endpoints are documented: the vendor states the software is unaudited and not production-ready, and the Harness privacy policy says the Services are not designed or intended to process sensitive personal data. Reassess after a stable release with a verified institution-controlled endpoint and telemetry configuration.

compliance: MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification; the vendor states no security audit has been performed.
final_records.pricing: Software free (MIT licence). The documented DeepSeek route needs a DeepSeek API key from platform.deepseek.com; model charges not captured here. In the 0.2.2 pre-releases the default web search may incur DeepSeek Search API charges (amounts not captured). Third-party and custom endpoints are billed by their providers.
final_records.academic: No academic or student programme found on fetched pages.
use_cases: repository exploration and editing in a local workspace via the web profile
headless one-shot agent jobs from the shell
plugin-extended agent workflows on nonsensitive data
final_records.notes: GitHub repository created 2026-08-13; all 37 releases so far are pre-releases (latest dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1 on 2026-11-04; npm latest 0.2.2-rc.1). The vendor warns of compatibility-breaking changes. Frequent merges (last push 2026-11-04); GitHub issues are disabled and feedback goes through GitHub Discussions. The optional Exa and Perplexity web-search packages were removed in 0.2.2-alpha.2. Third-party plugins (dsh-plugin topic) can add code execution and network access; the vendor advises reviewing them and running in a disposable VM or container.
final_records.tier_gate: Nonsensitive/public work only during developer preview

residual_risks: Vendor designates the project an unaudited developer preview that must not be treated as secure or production-ready.
Official model services use data for training and store it in the PRC.
Desktop product analytics (device and user IDs, hardware/OS fields) are on by default with no user-facing control.

Default web search (0.2.2 pre-releases) sends queries and up to 128 characters of the latest prompt to the DeepSeek Search API whenever a DeepSeek credential is available, including alongside a self-hosted chat endpoint.
Third-party plugins can add code execution and network egress.

final_records.name: Data Formulator
final_records.deployment: Local-first Python web app (uvx/pip, Docker, or unsigned Windows/macOS preview desktop builds) bound to 127.0.0.1:5567 by default; can also be self-hosted as a multi-user server with OIDC/OAuth2/GitHub/Azure EasyAuth sign-in. A public online demo (data-formulator.ai) linked from the README is outside this record.
final_records.model_backend: Bring-your-own model through LiteLLM. The configuration template ships entries for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama (default base http://localhost:11434); other LiteLLM providers can be added by environment variable, and users can add custom endpoints in the UI unless DISABLE_CUSTOM_MODELS is set.
final_records.data_handling_note: Data Formulator runs no AI service of its own; prompts and data context go to the configured LiteLLM model endpoint. What reaches the model is not limited to small samples: besides schema, sample rows and conversation, the analyst agent runs Python via execute_python_script and receives its printed stdout (truncated at 8,000 characters per call), so any rows the generated code prints can be sent to the model. Workspaces (uploaded files, parquet tables, metadata) are stored by default under ~/.data_formulator on the machine running the server; Azure Blob and ephemeral backends are optional. AI-generated Python runs in a local warm subprocess with audit hooks or, optionally, a disposable Docker container. No telemetry is documented and no analytics dependency appears in the reviewed Python and frontend manifests, but the project publishes no privacy statement for the software and no full source audit was done. The public online demo has no privacy terms on its page and must not receive research data.

suitability_notes.personal: Run locally or on an institution-run server and use a local/institution-operated model endpoint, or a cloud provider covered by an approved DPA/no-training agreement. Do not use the public online demo. Set DISABLE_CUSTOM_MODELS=true or DF_ALLOWED_API_BASES on shared servers so users cannot point the app at unapproved endpoints.
suitability_notes.special: Only as a single-user local or institution-hosted instance with Ollama (or another OpenAI-compatible server) on institution-controlled hardware, cloud provider entries disabled in .env, custom UI endpoints blocked, external data connectors limited to approved internal sources or disabled, and network egress to external LLM hosts blocked. Generated-code output can carry raw rows to the model, so the model endpoint must sit inside the same boundary. The project calls itself a research prototype and the desktop builds are unsigned previews, so this is a configuration route, not an approved deployment.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free and open source (MIT). Model charges, where applicable, are paid directly to the chosen provider.
final_records.academic: free
use_cases: Natural-language exploration and visualisation of tabular research data (CSV, TSV, Excel, JSON, databases)
Agent-written Python and DuckDB/SQL transformations with inspectable code and branching Data Threads
Extracting tables from screenshots or text into analysable data
Composing exploration results into shareable reports
Data exploration with a local Ollama model for private datasets
final_records.notes: Microsoft Research project for AI-agent data exploration and visualisation; the package metadata describes it as a research prototype (Development Status 4 - Beta). Latest stable 0.7.0 (GitHub 2026-05-28; PyPI latest stable) and beta 0.8.0b1 (2026-08-15, PyPI pre-release); the dev branch is active, with commits through 2026-11-06. Desktop builds are automated, unsigned previews. Data stays with the server operator except what is sent to the configured model and to any connected external sources.
final_records.tier_gate: Regulated data only as a local or institution-hosted instance with an institution-controlled model endpoint, cloud provider entries disabled, custom endpoints blocked and egress controlled; never the public online demo

required_controls: Run Data Formulator on an institution-controlled workstation or server (Profile 1 single-user local on 127.0.0.1, or Profile 3 with SSO sign-in and ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=false); never use the public online demo.

Serve models from Ollama or another OpenAI-compatible server on institution-controlled hardware (OLLAMA_API_BASE); set OPENAI_ENABLED, AZURE_ENABLED and ANTHROPIC_ENABLED to false and store no cloud API keys.
Set DISABLE_CUSTOM_MODELS=true, or DF_ALLOWED_API_BASES to the internal endpoint only, so users cannot add other endpoints in the UI; env-configured global models bypass the allowlist.

Limit data connectors to approved internal sources (or DISABLE_DATA_CONNECTORS=true), keep WORKSPACE_BACKEND=local on institution storage, prefer the Docker sandbox when running on the host, and block egress to external LLM hosts at the network layer.
residual_risks: Schemas, sample rows, prompts and the printed output of agent-generated Python (up to 8,000 characters per call, repeatable) reach the model endpoint; a misconfigured provider entry sends them off-boundary.
Generated Python runs on the host in the default local sandbox (audit hooks, not a container); the agent can also load data from URLs and connected sources.

No privacy or telemetry statement exists for the software; absence of telemetry rests on reviewed manifests only (LiteLLM and connector libraries not audited). The project is a research prototype and desktop builds are unsigned previews.
The unreleased dev branch adds new model routes (including a ChatGPT-account transport) and MCP server support; re-check the boundary before upgrading past 0.8.0b1.
Workspaces under ~/.data_formulator and the credential vault for connectors need institutional access, retention and backup controls.

aliases: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio notebooks AI agent
final_records.name: Amazon SageMaker Data Agent
final_records.deployment: AWS-hosted agent inside Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio notebooks and Query Editor (IAM and IAM Identity Center domains); inference on Amazon Bedrock with geographic or global cross-region inference depending on the domain Region
final_records.model_backend: Amazon Bedrock; the reviewed pages do not name the models.
final_records.data_handling_note: Prompts and the agent's generated code and responses are stored in the domain's AWS Region; conversations are kept for 90 days. AWS may use prompts and responses for service improvement unless the organisation sets an AWS Organizations AI services opt-out policy for Amazon DataZone; AWS's general opt-out documentation says service improvement can include model training and storage outside the Region of use. Code the user writes, notebook context and metadata, and data from the Glue Data Catalog or other sources are listed as not stored and not used for improvement. With cross-region inference, prompts, code context and Glue Data Catalog metadata may be processed in other Regions of the same geography (Europe: Frankfurt, Ireland, Paris, Stockholm), and globally for domains in Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, São Paulo and Canada (Central). The agent also reads the data catalog, diagnoses failed cells and queries ("Diagnose with agent", "Fix with AI"), and can create notebook schedules and background runs; whether error messages, cell outputs or data samples reach the model is not stated.

suitability_notes.personal: Only in an institution-governed AWS account under an AWS agreement approved by the institution, with an AI services opt-out policy for Amazon DataZone in force before use, a domain in a geographic cross-region-inference Region (for EU data, a European Region), and the agent disabled in IdC domains (or the DataZone SendMessage/GenerateCode/StartConversation permissions withheld from project roles) where it is not approved.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate: inference runs on AWS-hosted Amazon Bedrock with cross-region routing; no customer-controlled inference route is documented.

final_records.pricing: Pay-as-you-go: $0.04 per Data Agent credit, metered to 0.01 credit (simple prompts use less than one credit, complex ones more). Notebook compute and other SageMaker Unified Studio services are priced separately.
final_records.academic: No academic offer identified on the reviewed pricing page.
use_cases: Natural-language generation of Python, PySpark and SQL in SageMaker Unified Studio notebooks
Error diagnosis and fixes for notebook and Query Editor code
Exploratory data analysis over Glue Data Catalog, S3, Athena and Redshift data
ML model development plans and code in AWS-hosted research data platforms
final_records.notes: AI agent in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio notebooks (announced 2025-11-21) and Query Editor. Service-improvement use of prompts and responses is on by default; the documented opt-out is an AWS Organizations AI services opt-out policy (Amazon DataZone, which AWS lists as covering SageMaker Data Agent). Organisational controls do not make AWS-hosted Bedrock inference a customer-controlled route.
final_records.tier_gate: Organisational AWS account with AI services opt-out policy for Amazon DataZone and a geographic cross-region-inference Region for personal data; not for special-category data

residual_risks: Prompts, code context and catalog metadata are processed on AWS-hosted Bedrock, possibly in other Regions; some domain Regions route globally.
Prompts and responses may be used for service improvement until an AI services opt-out policy is applied; conversations are retained for 90 days.
The models and whether data samples or cell outputs are sent to them are not documented on the reviewed pages.

final_records.name: Open WebUI
final_records.deployment: Self-hosted web application on researcher- or institution-controlled infrastructure (Docker image, pip package, official Helm chart for Kubernetes); offline and air-gapped operation is documented. Open Terminal, a separate MIT-licensed execution environment, runs in a Docker container (recommended) or on bare metal and gives the agent files, shell and code execution. Open WebUI Desktop 0.1.x runs it on one computer with optional llama.cpp local models. The multi-user Terminals orchestrator is alpha and needs an Enterprise License for production.
final_records.model_backend: BYO: Ollama (default endpoint http://localhost:11434) and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, both enabled by default; these can be institution-run servers or cloud providers. Models can delegate to other configured models as sub-agents. No vendor-hosted inference.
final_records.data_handling_note: No vendor cloud: the FAQ states Open WebUI does not send data to external services by default, and prompts go only to the model providers the administrator connects. Chats, files, knowledge bases and accounts are stored on the operator's server; admins can open other users' chats by default (ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS=True). The default OpenAI-compatible connection points at https://api.openai.com/v1 (used only once an API key is set), and account sign-up is enabled by default (ENABLE_SIGNUP=True). Default-on outbound features: version update check (ENABLE_VERSION_UPDATE_CHECK=True), automatic embedding/reranking model updates, and community-sharing UI (ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING=True). OFFLINE_MODE disables update checks and automatic model downloads, but the docs state that blocking external access needs separate network controls. The official Docker image sets SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS, DO_NOT_TRACK and ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false; equivalent settings for pip installs were not confirmed. The openwebui.com privacy policy covers the vendor website and community service, not self-hosted instances. These are project statements, not an independent network audit.

suitability_notes.personal: Self-host it on institutional infrastructure. Connect only institution-run model endpoints, or cloud APIs covered by an institutional processing agreement, and restrict external models by group. Turn off community sharing, keep direct user connections off (default), and set SSO/RBAC, TLS, admin chat-access and retention policy. Admin-installed Tools and Functions run arbitrary Python on the server.
suitability_notes.special: Only a deployment on institution-controlled hardware with institution-run inference (Ollama in local-only mode, vLLM or llama.cpp), OFFLINE_MODE on, community sharing and web search off, Open Terminal in Docker with egress filtering, and network-level egress blocking. Any cloud model connection removes this route.

compliance: self-hosted
final_records.pricing: Free under the Open WebUI License for standard use with the original branding intact. Branding changes for deployments above 50 end users in a rolling 30-day period, white-labelling and enterprise-only offerings (Terminals, Tether) need an Enterprise License, quoted by sales (no public price). Inference costs depend on the chosen backend.
final_records.academic: No academic or education programme found on the enterprise page (checked 2026-11-06); the page carries a testimonial from the JGU Mainz data centre describing a university-wide self-hosted deployment.
use_cases: institution-hosted chat and agent workspace over local or institution-run models
data analysis and scripting in an isolated Open Terminal container (files, shell, Python packages)
air-gapped or offline research environments with pre-provisioned models
shared departmental deployment with SSO, group-based model access and knowledge bases
final_records.notes: Widely self-hosted AI platform (since 2023) that now works as an agent harness over Open Terminal, a separate MIT-licensed execution environment (repository created February 2026; v0.17.2 on 2026-11-06). v0.13.0 (2026-11-03) added a tabbed workspace with multiple terminal sessions, a Git panel, Browser and Desktop tabs on a connected Open Terminal, and multi-model sub-agents (sub-agents previously used the parent model); v0.12.0 (2026-10-10) added two-factor sign-in, multi-file skills and separate switches for Tools, Functions and tool servers. The Pyodide and Jupyter code-interpreter engines are now legacy, with Pyodide the in-browser default. Core licence is the custom Open WebUI License (recorded as LicenseRef-Open-WebUI-License: BSD-3-Clause text plus a branding clause, CLA for contributions); Open Terminal is separately MIT-licensed; GitHub reports NOASSERTION, and it is not an OSI-approved licence. Scope note for the curator: Open WebUI is a general AI platform; it is proposed for its documented agentic code/data execution on institution-controlled infrastructure, unlike general chat apps such as Jan (not added in October).
final_records.tier_gate: any self-hosted deployment (free standard licence) with institution-run model endpoints for regulated data; the Terminals multi-user orchestrator needs an Enterprise License and is alpha

required_controls: Deploy Open WebUI and Open Terminal on institution-controlled hardware; connect only institution-run model endpoints (Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp) and remove or disable every cloud provider connection (ENABLE_OPENAI_API only for internal endpoints); keep ENABLE_DIRECT_CONNECTIONS off so users cannot add their own endpoints.
If Ollama serves the models, run it in local-only mode and serve no :cloud models; confirm that any institutional endpoint does not forward requests to external providers.
Set OFFLINE_MODE=true (disables update checks and automatic model downloads), pre-provision embedding, reranking and speech models, set ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING=false and keep web search off.
Block or allowlist outbound network traffic at firewall or container-network level and verify it; the docs state offline settings alone do not prevent external access.
Run Open Terminal in Docker (not bare metal) with an API key, resource limits, an internal Docker network and egress filtering; do not mount the Docker socket.

Keep Workspace Tools and Functions restricted to trusted administrators (USER_PERMISSIONS_WORKSPACE_TOOLS_ACCESS=false, the default) and review every Tool, Function, MCP or OpenAPI tool server before enabling it.

Enforce SSO/RBAC, HTTPS/TLS and database encryption; turn off open sign-up (ENABLE_SIGNUP defaults to True) or set new users to pending; decide on ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS; keep chats, uploads, knowledge bases, logs and backups on controlled storage with defined retention.
For pip installs, set the analytics opt-outs that the official Docker image sets (SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS, DO_NOT_TRACK, ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false).
Track the project's GitHub security advisories and upgrade promptly; set sub-agent limits (SUBAGENTS_MAX_* default to no limit since v0.13.0).
residual_risks: No-external-data statements are project documentation, not an independent network audit; no egress test was performed.
Several outbound features are on by default (version check, embedding model auto-update, community sharing) and must be switched off deliberately.
The offline-mode tutorial is labelled a community contribution not supported by the Open WebUI team.

Tools, Functions and Open Terminal execute arbitrary code; bare-metal Open Terminal runs with the user's permissions, and prompt injection through documents or web content can drive tool calls. The security docs advise bare metal only on a personal machine for personal projects.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve :cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so an Ollama connection alone does not show that inference stays local.
Central multi-user server: administrators can open other users' chats by default, and all chat data sits in one database.
Source-available licence with a branding clause, not OSI open source; frequent releases (v0.12.0 to v0.13.0 in under four weeks) can change defaults, so pin and review versions.

High volume of published security advisories (166 GHSA entries; 55 published since 2026-08-01, 16 rated high), including session-token theft and, before 0.11.4, users reaching disabled model-provider backends; an unpatched instance can undermine the endpoint restriction.
The project's threat model treats administrators as trusted actors with full system control, so the route depends on institutional governance of the admin role.

final_records.name: Codewhale
final_records.vendor: Shannon Labs, Inc. (Delaware; Codewhale product; GitHub: codewhale-hq; formerly the DeepSeek-TUI open-source project, not affiliated with DeepSeek)
final_records.deployment: local terminal TUI/CLI (single binary via install script, npm, Cargo, winget or Homebrew) with a local web UI, ACP mode and a local Runtime API; inference via the configured provider (DeepSeek's hosted API by default) or local Ollama, vLLM, SGLang or DS4; optional Codewhale account services (managed inference from a prepaid balance; cloud computer dispatch in preview)
final_records.model_backend: BYOK across 40+ built-in providers (default DeepSeek's hosted deepseek-flash; also Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral, Moonshot, OpenRouter, xAI and others) and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Local runtimes ollama (localhost:11434), vllm, sglang and DS4 are keyless by default. Experimental ChatGPT-plan sign-in. Account-backed routes: the 'codewhale' provider (Codewhale API at api.codewhale.net, a Codewhale account key over provider keys connected to the account) and Codewhale-managed inference paid from a prepaid AI balance, routed through Vercel AI Gateway to DeepInfra per the privacy policy. Separate hosted ollama-cloud provider.
final_records.data_handling_note: BYOK client: no account is needed and keys added with /provider stay on the machine, so the selected provider's terms govern inference. The default provider is DeepSeek's hosted API (its retention and training terms were not assessed here; do not assume ZDR or no-train). If no provider is configured and a local Ollama server is serving a chat model, Codewhale uses it automatically; a signed-in Ollama can also serve ':cloud' models (Ollama docs). Default-on network calls: usage telemetry (aggregate counts with a 90-day rotating install ID; no prompts, code or file names per TELEMETRY.md) to telemetry.codewhale.net, which the privacy policy says may be passed to PostHog as a processor; a startup GitHub release check whose default update mode downloads new release binaries in the background (release-binary installs only; the same page also says Codewhale only notifies, so the docs are inconsistent); a ~24-hour Models.dev catalog refresh; and keyless Firecrawl web search with DuckDuckGo/Bing fallback. Opt-outs: codewhale config set telemetry false (a floor over CLI/env switches; CODEWHALE_TELEMETRY=0 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 as kill switches), [update] check_for_updates = false or CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1, CODEWHALE_DISABLE_MODELS_DEV_FETCH=1, [features] web_search = false. Optional Shannon Labs services (account, Codewhale API, managed inference, cloud computers in preview) store account data, conversations, Work runs and usage records; account auth/session state is in Cloudflare's US jurisdiction with no residency commitment; managed-route retention and training follow the selected provider's terms. No DPA found.

suitability_notes.personal: Use a local runtime, an institution-hosted endpoint, or a cloud provider under an institutional agreement. Do not rely on the default DeepSeek route, the Codewhale API provider, Codewhale-managed inference or cloud dispatch without institutional review (no Shannon Labs DPA found). Turn telemetry off and review web search, MCP servers and plugins.
suitability_notes.special: Only with local-only inference (Ollama with cloud features disabled, vLLM, SGLang or DS4 on loopback, or an institution-operated endpoint inside the controlled network), no cloud provider keys in the environment, no Codewhale login, Codewhale API provider, managed inference or cloud dispatch, telemetry, update checks, Models.dev fetch and web search disabled, and network egress limited to the local endpoint and verified at the network layer. Windows machines have no OS sandbox.

compliance: The MIT source licence is not a product compliance certification. No DPA, certification or data-residency commitment was found for Shannon Labs' hosted services; the privacy policy states there is no residency selector.
final_records.pricing: CLI free (MIT). BYOK provider usage is billed by the provider; local inference has hardware cost only. Optional prepaid packs (USD, sold by Shannon Labs via Stripe): an AI balance for Codewhale-managed models, deducted at the provider's price without markup, plus a Platform fee on each AI-balance purchase; a separate computer balance when hosted computers are offered. No subscription or automatic top-up; balances expire after 12 months; unspent balance refundable within 30 days. Pack prices and fee amounts not captured (UNVERIFIED).
final_records.academic: No academic or student programme found on fetched pages. The docs include a classroom/lab install checklist for IT staff.
use_cases: terminal agentic coding and repository editing with local Ollama, vLLM, SGLang or DS4 models
scripted or CI runs via codewhale exec with the workspace-write sandbox
classroom or lab deployment on managed Windows machines
final_records.notes: Renamed from DeepSeek TUI at v0.8.41 (legacy ~/.deepseek state and DEEPSEEK_* variables still read; the old repository URL redirects); the README states it is not affiliated with DeepSeek. Active releases: v0.10.0 (2026-09-22), v0.10.1 (2026-10-08), v0.10.2 (2026-10-24); the changelog dates a 0.10.3 source candidate 2026-11-06. In the default Ask permission, file edits apply without asking and non-read-only shell commands ask first; exec --auto defaults to Full Access (no sandbox) unless --sandbox workspace-write is set. OS sandbox: Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux when installed, none on Windows. Managed config and requirements files (/etc/deepseek/) can restrict approval policies and sandbox modes. The README carries a sponsored OrcaRouter referral link from which the project earns a fee. Cloud computer dispatch is a preview that needs codewhale login and cannot transfer local-only inference. Development is concentrated in one maintainer (Hmbown: 7,271 contributions vs. 163 for the next account, GitHub API 2026-11-06). The classroom checklist targets Windows, where there is no OS sandbox, and notes the public installer is unsigned.
final_records.tier_gate: Local runtime (Ollama with cloud disabled, vLLM, SGLang or DS4) or institution-approved endpoint; telemetry, update checks, Models.dev fetch and web search off; no Codewhale login, Codewhale API provider, managed inference or cloud dispatch for regulated data

required_controls: Pin a local provider in user config (ollama with OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in ~/.ollama/server.json, vllm, sglang or ds4 on loopback, or an institution-operated endpoint inside the controlled network); keep DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, CODEWHALE_API_KEY, OLLAMA_API_KEY and other cloud provider keys out of the environment and config.
Do not run codewhale login, codewhale dispatch, codewhale auth chatgpt, the 'codewhale' (Codewhale API) or 'ollama-cloud' providers, or Codewhale-managed inference.

Set telemetry = false (codewhale config set telemetry false; it overrides CLI and environment switches), [update] check_for_updates = false (or CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1), CODEWHALE_DISABLE_MODELS_DEV_FETCH=1 and [features] web_search = false; keep signed cloud facts off (off by default).

Use the Ask permission or --sandbox workspace-write on macOS, or Linux with bubblewrap installed, and enforce allowed sandbox modes through /etc/deepseek/requirements.toml; restrict MCP servers, plugins and the Computer Use plugin; do not use exec --auto without --sandbox workspace-write.
Limit network egress to the local endpoint and verify it at the network layer; govern ~/.codewhale session, receipt and credential files under institutional retention rules.
residual_risks: Ollama auto-detection: with no provider configured, a running Ollama server is used automatically, and a signed-in Ollama can serve cloud models through the same localhost endpoint unless its cloud features are disabled.
Telemetry, update checks (with background binary download by default), the Models.dev refresh and keyless web search are on by default; a missed setting re-enables outbound calls.
No managed provider allowlist was found in the reviewed configuration docs; the requirements file shown covers approval policies and sandbox modes only.

Fast release cadence, one dominant maintainer and preview account services from a commercial vendor; defaults can change between versions. Windows has no OS sandbox, and exec --auto defaults to Full Access.
Local sessions, logs, tools and integrations require institutional access, retention and egress controls.

final_records.name: MATLAB Copilot
final_records.deployment: Add-on for the MATLAB desktop (Mac, Windows, Linux). From R2026b it must be installed; in R2025a to R2026a it is available after sign-in to the MATLAB desktop. Requires an internet connection and a MathWorks Account sign-in. Not available in China or in MATLAB Grader; the FAQ says it is only available in certain regions. Inference is always in the cloud: by default on MathWorks Copilot Services (the 'MathWorks Public Cloud' LLM), processed by an unnamed third-party cloud service provider under contract with MathWorks; from R2026b, Bring Your Own Key (via MATLAB Connector, set up per computer) routes queries to the organization's OpenAI or Microsoft Azure account.
final_records.model_backend: MathWorks does not name the LLMs or the provider behind its default MathWorks Public Cloud route. Chat responses are based on MathWorks documentation and code examples. From R2026b, Bring Your Own Key routes queries to the organization's OpenAI or Microsoft Azure account; on Azure the organization must deploy the base models MathWorks lists (set up in Microsoft Foundry). No local, self-hosted or other-provider route is documented.
final_records.data_handling_note: The FAQ says MathWorks does not use end-user data submitted to MATLAB Copilot to train AI models, and uses that data only to fulfil requests. Nearby code may be sent as extra context. The MathWorks privacy policy (updated 25 Mar 2026, section 10) says requests go to a third-party cloud service provider and are not stored by MathWorks or third-party services after the request is completed. Thumbs-up/down feedback is stored and used to improve MathWorks products. The fetched pages do not name the provider, the processing region or the model. MathWorks' general data-storage note says most MathWorks data is stored in the US. With Bring Your Own Key, queries go to the organization's OpenAI or Azure endpoint, and that provider's terms and retention apply. The BYOK page does not say whether any request content still passes through MathWorks. MATLAB sends user experience information to MathWorks unless the user opts out at installation or in preferences. The BYOK setting 'Help improve MATLAB Connector' also sends experience information. MathWorks provides a DPA, SOC 2 report and GDPR subprocessor list on request.

suitability_notes.personal: Use an institutional licence. Obtain MathWorks' DPA and GDPR subprocessor list (Trust Center, on request) to identify the LLM provider and processing region. Alternatively, from R2026b, use Bring Your Own Key with an OpenAI or Azure account that the institution owns and covers with its own DPA and region choice. Opt out of user experience information, do not rate responses that contain personal data, and keep identifiers out of code, variable names and comments that may be sent as context.
suitability_notes.special: Inference is cloud-only, on the MathWorks public cloud or on an organization's OpenAI or Azure account. No local, self-hosted or on-premises model route is documented, so the tool does not qualify under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: MathWorks Trust Center: SOC 2, HECVAT, Data Processing Agreement and GDPR subprocessor list available on request; SOC 3 report published; Copilot-specific scope not stated
Trust Center references EU Standard Contractual Clauses and the UK International Data Transfer Addendum
final_records.pricing: Prices for MATLAB Copilot are not visible in the static pricing content (the linked pricing page is headed 'MATLAB Pricing' and asks you to select licence details). The FAQ says individual licences are sold to commercial and academic customers and that Copilot is included in campus-wide access, the Institute-Wide License and the MATLAB startup suites. The requirements page says the default MathWorks Copilot Services route requires a MathWorks Software Maintenance Service subscription; Bring Your Own Key does not require MathWorks Copilot Services, but the organization pays its own OpenAI or Azure usage.
final_records.academic: The FAQ lists campus-wide access and the Institute-Wide License among offerings that include MATLAB Copilot. Academic individual licences are sold, but the Copilot price is not shown in the static page. The default cloud route also requires an active Software Maintenance Service subscription. Check whether your institution's MATLAB licence includes it.
use_cases: Chat about MATLAB functions and workflows grounded in MathWorks documentation
Code autocompletion in the MATLAB Editor
Generating or modifying MATLAB code from natural-language descriptions
Explaining code and error messages and adding comments
Generating unit tests with MATLAB Test
Insights for tables and timetables (R2026b)
final_records.notes: This is an in-editor assistant, not an autonomous agent: the fetched documentation describes chat, completion, code generation, explanations and test generation, but not file-system or multi-step agent actions. A user setting disables it (all features, or autocompletions alone). The release notes load client-side and could not be read, so the dates of the R2026b changes (installation requirement, Bring Your Own Key, table insights) come from the R2026b documentation, not from dated release notes. MathWorks does not name the provider behind its public-cloud models.
final_records.tier_gate: Default route: MATLAB Copilot licence (individual, or included in campus-wide / Institute-Wide licences) plus an active Software Maintenance Service subscription. Personal data: institutional licence with MathWorks' DPA and GDPR subprocessor list (on request), or Bring Your Own Key (R2026b+) to an OpenAI or Azure account the institution owns; user experience information turned off. Special-category data: not appropriate (cloud-only).

residual_risks: Inference is cloud-only (MathWorks public cloud via an unnamed third-party provider, or an organization's OpenAI or Azure account). No customer-controlled inference route is documented.

final_records.name: KNIME K-AI
final_records.deployment: AI assistant panel in KNIME Analytics Platform (desktop) and KNIME Hub, used with a KNIME Hub account (Community Hub, or a Business or Enterprise plan). Inference is in the cloud: KNIME-managed OpenAI models by default. On Business (add-on) and Enterprise plans, KNIME can configure K-AI on request to use the organization's own OpenAI or Azure OpenAI account. The 5.12 changelog says some newer K-AI features (data-fetch permissions in Build mode, workflow-building tools) work with Community Hub but not yet with Business Hub 1.18.x.
final_records.model_backend: OpenAI by default. KNIME's admin documentation lists an OpenAI chat model and text-embedding-3-small. With bring-your-own model, an organization-owned OpenAI or Azure OpenAI deployment is used. Admins cannot change the backend themselves: KNIME configures it on request. No local or self-hosted backend is documented for K-AI.
final_records.data_handling_note: KNIME's documentation says K-AI sends chat text plus column names and types (and, in script nodes, the current code and prompt) to the LLM provider. K-AI reads actual cell values only after the user grants the 'Inspect port object' permission for the current workflow; Auto approve still asks before data access. The KNIME privacy policy says K-AI query logs and Hub user IDs are retained until the contract ends (account closure). OpenAI is the data processor under a DPA with Controller-to-Processor SCCs. Chat and workflow information 'may be shared with OpenAI and KNIME in order to provide and improve the service'. No explicit statement on model training was found, so training is not established. With bring-your-own model, requests go to the organization's provider, whose terms then govern retention. When K-AI searches public workflows and components on the KNIME instance, their descriptions are shared with the LLM provider (on by default; can be turned off on request). KNIME still logs K-AI interactions; the admin chat-history audit record excludes message content. The documentation conflicts on routing: one page says K-AI is not hosted by KNIME and connects directly to the OpenAI API, another says requests route through KNIME-managed AI infrastructure, and the Python guide says data goes to the configured KNIME Hub and OpenAI.

suitability_notes.personal: Use only on a Business or Enterprise plan under KNIME's data processing agreement, preferably with bring-your-own Azure OpenAI in the institution's chosen region. Deny 'Inspect port object' and keep Auto approve off for workflows with personal data; check which K-AI version your Hub runs, since the 5.12 changelog says Build-mode data-fetch permissions are not yet available on Business Hub 1.18.x. Keep identifiers out of column names and prompts. Get written confirmation of how the 'improve the service' clause and query-log retention until account closure apply. Do not use a personal Community Hub account.
suitability_notes.special: K-AI inference runs on OpenAI or Azure OpenAI cloud services (KNIME-managed or organization-owned). No local, self-hosted or on-premises K-AI backend is documented, so the tool does not qualify under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: Privacy policy: OpenAI acts as KNIME's data processor for K-AI under a DPA with Controller-to-Processor Standard Contractual Clauses
Business/Enterprise Hub: K-AI interactions are logged for admin audit (content excluded from the chat-history audit record); admins can restrict K-AI features
final_records.pricing: On KNIME Hub plans, K-AI uses AI credits: one credit is 10,000 input or 1,667 output tokens plus a service fee, sold as annual capacity bands. Band prices are not public (the pricing page is a contact form). Bring-your-own model is an add-on for Business and included in Enterprise according to the plan page (the bring-your-own-model page calls it a paid add-on for both). It replaces the standard rate with a reduced 0.17-credit service fee plus the provider's token costs. K-AI can be used with Community Hub, but free-tier limits or prices are not documented in the fetched pages (UNVERIFIED).
final_records.academic: No academic K-AI terms were found in the fetched KNIME pages.
use_cases: Building and refactoring KNIME workflows from natural-language descriptions
Schema-aware code generation in Python, R and Java snippet and expression nodes
Explaining node errors with likely causes and fixes
Generating workflow annotations
Node suggestions for data preparation and analysis steps
final_records.notes: This record covers only the K-AI assistant, not KNIME Analytics Platform or its separate AI-extension nodes for workflows. KNIME's licence page distributes the Analytics Platform under GPL v3 with KNIME's additional permissions (Sec. 7); K-AI's backend is a hosted KNIME/OpenAI service, so no SPDX licence is recorded for this entry and the licence status stays unconfirmed. KNIME's documentation is being reorganized and its pages conflict on request routing; re-check before relying on any single page. Analytics Platform 5.12.0 (released 6 July 2026) added several K-AI features.
final_records.tier_gate: Personal data: Business or Enterprise Hub with an executed KNIME DPA and written confirmation that K-AI data is not used for model training, ideally with bring-your-own Azure OpenAI; 'Inspect port object' denied. Special-category data: not appropriate (cloud-only).

residual_risks: K-AI inference is on OpenAI or Azure OpenAI cloud services (KNIME-managed or organization-owned); no customer-controlled inference route is documented.
KNIME's Sovereign Execution moves workflow execution to customer infrastructure, but K-AI requests still go to the configured cloud LLM provider.

final_records.name: Claude for Excel
final_records.deployment: Microsoft Office add-in for Excel on the web, Excel on Windows with a Microsoft 365 subscription, and Excel on Mac. Anthropic serves the task pane from pivot.claude.ai. Users can sign in with a Claude account (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise). Without Claude accounts, admins can route it through the organization's Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI or Azure AI Foundry, or through an LLM gateway. Chat history, skills and credentials are kept in the Office webview's browser storage on each device.
final_records.model_backend: Claude models only: Anthropic first-party, or Claude on Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI or Azure AI Foundry, called directly or through an LLM gateway such as LiteLLM, Portkey or Kong. The gateway path is documented only for Claude models (Anthropic, Bedrock or Vertex API formats). No documented local-model route.
final_records.data_handling_note: With a Claude account, the add-in sends conversations, the workbook content Claude reads and attached files to Anthropic. Clearing chat history in the add-in does not delete what Anthropic keeps. Pro, Max and Ultra follow consumer terms: model training is opt-out, and even after opting out, feedback and content flagged for Usage Policy review can still be used. If model improvement is on, data may be kept de-identified for up to 5 years. Deleted chats leave back-end storage within 30 days. Team and Enterprise follow commercial terms, under which Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content. Anthropic's organization data-retention article says inputs and outputs are deleted on the backend within 30 days, with exceptions: flagged content is kept up to 2 years and classifier scores up to 7 years; feedback is kept 5 years; Covered Models have additional retention; data may be kept as required by law. Anthropic's zero-data-retention article does not list Claude for Microsoft 365 among the products ZDR applies to. Files attached with a Claude sign-in expire 28 days after upload (since 15 Sep 2026; earlier versions set no expiry). If Anthropic does not accept an expiry for the organization, the file is uploaded with no expiry. The add-in does not inherit the organization's custom retention settings. Enterprise audit logs exclude its activity, but the Enterprise Compliance API covers its sessions. On Bedrock and Vertex AI, Anthropic says it cannot access prompts or outputs and does not train on them; it can access metadata such as tool use and token counts. On Azure AI Foundry, Anthropic runs the models as an independent processor for Microsoft, and Anthropic's data-use terms apply. Azure-hosted Foundry deployments keep prompts and responses in Azure, apart from usage metadata and content flagged by Anthropic's safety systems. Anthropic-hosted Foundry deployments process prompts and responses on Anthropic's infrastructure. In every mode, the add-in loads from pivot.claude.ai and contacts claude.ai for feature flags and usage events; Anthropic says these exclude prompts and responses. With a Claude sign-in, error reports to Sentry can contain conversation and document content. Local chat history keeps the 50 most recent conversations per user, organization and Office app, has no age-based expiry, and stores credentials unencrypted in the Office webview profile.

suitability_notes.personal: Use Team or Enterprise (commercial terms), or a third-party deployment through Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure AI Foundry or a gateway under the institution's cloud agreement and region. For Foundry, confirm the Claude deployment is Azure-hosted, not Anthropic-hosted. Do not use personal Pro, Max or Ultra accounts. Turn off third-party analytics in the Claude organization settings and keep credentials out of the manifest URL query string. Manage the device-local chat history through the device profile lifecycle. Treat any custom OpenTelemetry collector as holding prompt and document content. Anthropic's own documentation advises against models containing highly sensitive or regulated data without proper controls, and against untrusted workbooks because of prompt injection.
suitability_notes.special: Inference uses Claude models only, served by Anthropic, AWS, Google or Microsoft cloud, and the add-in itself loads from Anthropic's server. No customer-controlled inference route exists, so it does not qualify under this catalog's special-category rule.

compliance: Enterprise Compliance API covers Claude for Excel sessions; Enterprise audit logs do not include add-in activity
Third-party platform deployments (Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure AI Foundry) fall under that platform's terms and region; on Azure AI Foundry Anthropic acts as an independent processor for Microsoft
Anthropic's zero-data-retention article lists eligible APIs, products using a commercial API key, and Claude Code for Enterprise; it does not list Claude for Microsoft 365
final_records.pricing: Included in paid Claude plans; not available on Free. On the Claude pricing page (checked 2026-11-06): Pro USD 17/month billed annually (USD 200 up front) or USD 20 monthly; Max USD 100/month; Team standard seat USD 20/seat/month billed annually or USD 25 monthly, premium seat USD 100 or USD 125; Team is for 2 to 150 seats; Enterprise is self-serve or sales-assisted, with no list price shown. The pricing page also marks Claude for Microsoft 365 as included in Ultra (USD 200/month), while the Excel documentation names Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. Third-party deployments are billed through the cloud provider or gateway.
final_records.academic: Anthropic's pricing page lists an institution-wide Education plan with discounted student and faculty access; it does not say whether that plan includes Claude for Microsoft 365. The Claude Team plan for scientists (promotional Supplemental Terms effective 27 Aug 2026) offers eligible PIs at accredited universities and nonprofit research institutes Standard seats at USD 0 and Premium seats at USD 15/month for 12 months, limited to an initial 10,000 verified scientists; the pricing page lists Microsoft 365 among Team plan features, but the promotion terms do not name the add-in.
use_cases: Asking questions about open workbooks with cell-level citations
Adjusting model assumptions while preserving formula relationships
Tracing and fixing spreadsheet errors
Building or populating spreadsheet models across multi-tab workbooks
final_records.notes: This record covers the Excel add-in of Claude for Microsoft 365. The PowerPoint, Word and Outlook add-ins share the same local store and data paths but are not data-analysis tools. Known issue: after the September and October 2026 Microsoft 365 updates on Windows, some users lost local chat history and skills. Until 23 Sep 2026, usage events, including the text of rating comments, went to Segment. Plan-level training and retention terms come from Anthropic's general privacy and terms pages; the add-in documentation does not repeat them.
final_records.tier_gate: Personal data: Team or Enterprise, or an institution's Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure-hosted AI Foundry or gateway deployment; not personal Pro, Max or Ultra accounts. Special-category data: not appropriate (cloud-only inference, Anthropic-served add-in).

residual_risks: Inference uses Claude models on Anthropic, AWS, Google or Microsoft cloud; the gateway path is documented only for Claude models.

The add-in UI is always served from Anthropic's pivot.claude.ai and contacts claude.ai for feature flags and usage events in every deployment mode, so the workflow boundary is never fully customer-controlled.

final_records.name: Freebuff
final_records.deployment: Local terminal CLI (npm package freebuff, a launcher that fetches a prebuilt binary) and desktop app; included-model inference runs on Freebuff's hosted, ad-supported service. A BYOK route to the user's own provider or a loopback endpoint exists in the CLI source but has no first-party user documentation of its data flows. The same vendor also offers Freebuff Web (app builder), Freebuff Cloud (agents on connected GitHub repositories) and Freebuff Chat; CLI threads are described as living in the cloud.
final_records.model_backend: Freebuff-hosted curated catalog of third-party models, with availability by plan, region and capacity. On 2026-11-06 the README picker listed DeepSeek, GLM, Xiaomi MiMo, Upstage Solar, Google Gemini, Meta Muse Spark and OpenAI GPT models; the plans page also lists Claude Haiku 5.5, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and Glyph Cluster. The public repository's CLI source includes a '/byok' command (OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; plain HTTP allowed only on loopback, i.e. a local server). This route is not described on freebuff.com, in llms.txt or in the npm README, and whether a BYOK session still sends prompts, traces or telemetry to Freebuff is not documented. Freebuff Desktop can also run locally installed Claude Code and Codex under the user's own provider accounts.
final_records.data_handling_note: Ad-funded service. The privacy policy (last updated 18 Oct 2026, effective 12 Nov 2026; the version in force before then was not reviewed) defines Prompt and Project Data as prompts, code, files, repository data and anything an agent reads or produces. Freebuff may use this data to personalise ads, derive a profile of the projects you work on, and train the models that select and measure ads. For any model or feature labelled 'May use data for AI training', Freebuff or the model provider may train on submissions and Freebuff may share, license or sell them, including agent traces, to third parties; such data may not be removable once de-identified, used in a model or passed on. Repositories connected to Freebuff Cloud may undergo 'Codebase Evaluation' of their technical or commercial value, including human review by evaluation partners. Retention is 'as long as reasonably necessary'; saved projects and conversation history stay with the account until a deletion request completes. Usage, device, installed-tool and crash data are collected, as is device fingerprinting (FingerprintJS) and phone/identity verification for free access. Processing is in the US and other countries. Freebuff states it does not give uploaded files, project files or connected repositories to advertising providers. No ad-free or no-training paid tier is documented, and the privacy policy does not exempt BYOK sessions.

suitability_notes.nonsensitive: Only for public or freely shareable code and data. Prompts and project content feed ad personalisation and ad-model training on every route, so unpublished results or code you do not want profiled should not go in. Avoid any model or feature labelled 'May use data for AI training', because its submissions may be sold to third parties, and do not connect private repositories to Freebuff Cloud.
suitability_notes.personal: Not appropriate: prompt and project data are used for advertising profiles and ad-model training, can be sold for some models, and are retained without a fixed period. No DPA or processor terms were found.
suitability_notes.special: Not appropriate: included-model inference runs only on Freebuff's hosted service. The CLI source has a BYOK route that accepts loopback endpoints, but no first-party documentation establishes that a BYOK session keeps prompts, traces and telemetry off Freebuff's service, so no customer-controlled workflow is documented.

compliance: No DPA, SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA/BAA statement found on the Freebuff pages checked.
Privacy policy names US processing with recognised transfer safeguards 'where required'; no EU data residency stated.
final_records.pricing: Free plan $0/month with 30 hours refilled daily; paid Starter $8, Plus $25 and Pro $60 per month with more daily hours and a monthly bonus (plans page, 2026-11-06; allowances shown are for full-access regions and the page says prices and allowances may change during beta); a yearly option is listed with a stated 22% saving. Usage is metered in hours at per-model multipliers (1 hour = 5 Freebucks); unused daily hours do not roll over. The plans page does not say that paid plans remove ads or change data use.
final_records.academic: No academic terms reviewed; no academic entitlement asserted.
use_cases: Free terminal coding agent for public or teaching code
Agentic edits and test runs on open-source repositories
Trying hosted frontier and open-weight models without an API key
final_records.notes: Warning record: listed so researchers can recognise the trade-off of a free, ad-funded agent. The GitHub repository CodebuffAI/freebuff (created 2024; the old CodebuffAI/codebuff path now resolves to it) has an Apache-2.0 root LICENSE and is updated through automated 'Sync public snapshot from freebuff-private' commits; its last GitHub releases date from October 2025. The freebuff/ subfolder README and the npm package (0.2.36, 2026-11-03) both state MIT, and the npm package is a launcher that downloads a prebuilt binary, so whether the shipped binary matches the repository source was not verified. Freebuff, Inc. operates both Freebuff and Codebuff; Codebuff is described as the open multi-agent framework Freebuff is built on. Regions outside full-access countries and VPN users get limited access to a smaller model set. The reviewed privacy policy takes effect 2026-11-12; the version in force before then was not reviewed.

prior_record.data_handling_note: Jules FAQ: no training on private-repository content; app setting text excepts private-repo content the user chooses to include with feedback. proposed_changes.old: Business, Enterprise, Edu and API data are not used for training by default (API sharing is opt-in). Free, Plus and Pro personal workspaces share data for training by default, with an opt-out under Data Controls. With ChatGPT sign-in, Codex follows the workspace's retention and residency settings; with an API key, the API organization's retention settings apply. API abuse-monitoring logs are kept for up to 30 days; ZDR or Modified Abuse Monitoring needs OpenAI approval, and OpenAI can make specific models ineligible after written notice. API ZDR does not define ChatGPT Work retention, and no Codex-cloud-specific deletion schedule was found; for Work cloud tasks, execution state follows a lifecycle separate from chats. Local clients send anonymous usage and health metrics to OpenAI by default (opt-out via [analytics]); OTel export is off by default. With the Amazon Bedrock provider, requests go to Amazon Bedrock with AWS authentication and OpenAI's hosted Responses API is not in the request path; AWS-side retention was not assessed.
proposed_changes.new: Business, Enterprise, Edu and API data are not used for training by default (API sharing is opt-in). Local clients send anonymous usage and health metrics to OpenAI by default (opt-out via [analytics]); OTel export is off by default, and explicit OTLP exporters run independently of the analytics setting. With the Amazon Bedrock provider, requests go to Amazon Bedrock with AWS authentication and OpenAI's hosted Responses API is not in the request path; the Vertex AI provider sends requests to the user's Google Cloud project. AWS- and Google-side retention was not assessed.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Classification is unchanged: Gemini CLI is an active Apache-2.0 client (stable v0.64 to v0.67, 13 Oct to 4 Nov) with cloud-only inference, so special-category data stays 'no'. Two backend retention defaults changed. Gemini API projects created on or after 26 Oct 2026 now log Generate Content calls in AI Studio by default for up to 55 days, so researchers on the API-key route must switch logging off. On Agent Platform, Google's abuse-monitoring page now exempts only Cloud Master Agreement customers from prompt logging and describes default durable (at-rest) caching, which replaces the record's 'request an exception' wording. The README now positions the CLI for Code Assist Standard/Enterprise, calls API/Vertex keys legacy and says it is not optimized for Gemini 4.

proposed_changes.old: The CLI is an Apache-2.0 client; data handling follows the backend route. The supported routes (paid Gemini API, Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise) do not use prompts or code for training by default. Retention differs by route. On the paid Gemini API, prompts and responses are logged for a limited period for abuse monitoring, and Google points users who need guaranteed ZDR to Vertex. Agent Platform allows ZDR if you request an abuse-monitoring exception; it also keeps a 24-hour in-memory cache, which can be disabled per project. Google describes Code Assist Standard/Enterprise as stateless services that do not store prompts and responses in Google Cloud. The CLI's built-in google_web_search tool uses Grounding with Google Search, whose logs cannot be disabled: 30 days on the Gemini API, up to 3 days on Agent Platform. Unpaid use is no longer a supported Gemini CLI route. If an API key without an active billing account still works, the unpaid terms let Google use content to improve products, except in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, where the paid-service data-use terms also cover unpaid quota. Anonymous usage statistics are on by default and do not include prompt content, per the docs; turn them off with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false. Free and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended on 2026-06-18.
proposed_changes.new: The CLI is an Apache-2.0 client; data handling follows the backend route. The supported routes (Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise, and the paid Gemini API and Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform keys) do not use prompts or code for training by default. Retention differs by route. Paid Gemini API: Google logs prompts and responses for a limited period for abuse monitoring and points users who need guaranteed ZDR to Vertex. Separately, AI Studio API logging (developer-owned logs, private to the project, kept up to 55 days by default) is on by default for Generate Content calls in projects created on or after 2026-10-26; the project owner can turn it off, and these logs are not used for product improvement unless shared as datasets. Agent Platform: under the online Google Cloud Platform Terms, Google may log prompts flagged by its abuse classifiers (stored up to 90 days in the selected region); customers with a Google Cloud Master Agreement are exempt by default. Implicit caching (in memory and, by default, durable at rest) is deleted within 24 hours and can be disabled per project. Google describes Code Assist Standard/Enterprise as stateless services that do not store prompts and responses in Google Cloud. The CLI's built-in google_web_search tool uses Grounding with Google Search, whose logs cannot be disabled: 30 days on the Gemini API, up to 3 days on Agent Platform. Unpaid use is no longer a supported Gemini CLI route. If an API key without an active billing account still works, the unpaid terms let Google use content to improve products, except in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, where the paid-service data-use terms also cover unpaid quota. Anonymous usage statistics are on by default and do not include prompt content, per the docs; turn them off with privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false. Free and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended on 2026-06-18.
proposed_changes.why: Adds default-on AI Studio logging for Generate Content calls in Gemini API projects created on or after 2026-10-26 (55-day default retention, owner can turn off). Replaces 'ZDR if you request an abuse-monitoring exception' with the current Agent Platform terms: classifier-triggered prompt logging up to 90 days for online-terms customers, Cloud Master Agreement customers exempt by default. Adds default durable at-rest caching alongside the 24 h in-memory cache.

proposed_changes.old: Use only a paid route covered by a Google data processing addendum: a Gemini API key in a billed Cloud project (Gemini API Paid Services terms), Vertex AI/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, or a Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licence (Google Cloud terms). For regional processing, use Agent Platform with GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION set to a regional location (not global) where the chosen model is offered; global endpoints give no data-residency guarantee. For ZDR on Agent Platform, request the abuse-monitoring exception. Code Assist processing is not guaranteed to stay in-region, and the paid Gemini API may cache data in any country. Restrict the built-in tools (tools.core) so that google_web_search stays off, because grounding logs cannot be disabled. Turn off usage statistics, and enforce the authentication type in system settings (security.auth.enforcedType). If you enable OpenTelemetry, set telemetry.logPrompts to false, because it defaults to true. On the Gemini API route, share no AI Studio log datasets with Google, because shared datasets are processed under the unpaid terms. Confirm with your DPO.

On a Gemini API project created on or after 2026-10-26, turn off AI Studio logging, and share no log datasets with Google, because shared datasets are processed under the unpaid terms. proposed_changes.old: Terms (3 Sep 2026) bar training on Content without explicit agreement; turning Privacy Mode off lets Cursor store and use code data to train its models, and some inference providers may temporarily store inputs and outputs. Privacy Mode is on by default for Teams and Enterprise and admin-enforceable; the individual-plan default is not stated (Cursor's MDM guidance warns personal accounts might not have it on). With Privacy Mode on, providers run under ZDR agreements, but abuse-flagged data may be stored for investigation, and the Privacy Policy (29 Sep 2026) allows analysis of security-flagged inputs. Standard Privacy Mode still lets Cursor store code for Cloud Agents and Grok Bot; Privacy Mode (Legacy) does not support Cloud Agents and blocks Grok Bot. Exceptions: BYOK is outside Cursor's ZDR and still transits Cursor's backend. Anthropic retains Claude Fable 5/5.1 inputs and outputs for harm review (deleted after 30 days unless under safety investigation or legal hold); these models stay off until an admin approves the retention policy on Enterprise (approved per organization, then controlled per team or group) or with Privacy Mode on, but are on by default for individual and Teams accounts with Privacy Mode off. Cursor temporarily caches encrypted file contents. Cloud Agents keep transcripts (prompts, responses, tool calls, diff context) indefinitely by default (deletable via API; Enterprise can cap retention) and encrypted VM snapshots including cloned code for up to 90 days of inactivity, not deletable on demand; other Cursor pages state shorter retention, so the longest documented figure is used. Grok Bot, included with paid individual plans and on by default for Teams, keeps files on persistent US cloud computers not covered by the US-only residency program by default, and ignores model allowlists; its security page says team Privacy Mode applies, while Cursor's privacy FAQ calls it a separate product surface with its own data flows. The DPA bars sensitive/special-category data and does not cover individual plans.

Cloud Agents keep transcripts (prompts, responses, tool calls, diff context) indefinitely by default (deletable via API; Enterprise can cap retention at 90 days) and encrypted VM snapshots including cloned code for up to 30 days of inactivity, not deletable on demand (one governance page still says repository copies are deleted when the agent completes). Grok Bot, included with paid individual plans (Premium and above on The X Subscription) and on by default for Teams, keeps files, browser sessions and credentials on persistent US cloud computers and ignores model allowlists; its security page says team Privacy Mode applies, while Cursor's privacy FAQ calls it a separate product surface with its own data flows. Google Cloud lists no ISO 27001 or SOC 2 scope for Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise. Consumer accounts are not suitable for personal data; the SDK local-model route is an alternative.
proposed_changes.new: Use Gemini Enterprise or a Google Cloud project under the institution's Google Cloud agreement, through the Antigravity App, the CLI or the IDE extensions (the standalone Antigravity IDE is not supported for enterprise). Keep telemetry in an institution project, choose the eu location where residency matters, and leave third-party models disabled unless assessed. Do not use Antigravity Marketplace plugins with personal data: the Antigravity terms state that enterprise terms do not apply to Marketplace use. The Google Cloud Services Summary of 30 Oct 2026 no longer lists Antigravity separately (Gemini Enterprise is listed), so confirm with Google that Antigravity use is covered by the institution's agreement and the Cloud Data Processing Addendum. Google Cloud lists no ISO 27001 or SOC 2 scope for Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise. Consumer accounts, Remote Agents and the free science access programme (individual terms) are not suitable for personal data; the SDK local-model route is an alternative.
proposed_changes.why: Marketplace exclusion in the revised Antigravity terms; Antigravity no longer named in the Services Summary; free science programme runs under individual terms.

proposed_changes.old: Only the Antigravity SDK local-model route qualifies: LiteRTAgentConfig with an on-device Gemma checkpoint, or LocalOpenAIAgentConfig against a localhost server, on researcher-controlled hardware with outbound network blocked and verified. Do not use LocalAgentConfig: despite its name it calls Google's cloud. Antigravity 2.0, the CLI, the IDE and IDE extensions use cloud inference and are not acceptable, Gemini Enterprise and VPC Service Controls notwithstanding.
proposed_changes.new: Only the Antigravity SDK local-model route qualifies: LiteRTAgentConfig with an on-device Gemma checkpoint, or LocalOpenAIAgentConfig against a localhost server, on researcher-controlled hardware with outbound network blocked and verified. Do not use LocalAgentConfig: despite its name it calls Google's cloud. The Antigravity App, the CLI, the standalone IDE, the IDE extensions and Remote Agents use cloud inference or Google-managed execution and are not acceptable, Gemini Enterprise and VPC Service Controls notwithstanding.
