proposed_changes.old: Individual: USD 0 plan with weekly-refreshed quota; Google AI Pro and Ultra add higher rate limits and AI-credit overages (consumer plan prices are not listed on the Antigravity pricing page). Business plan via Google Cloud: API access with consumption-based pricing; for eligible customers, Gemini Enterprise Standard/Plus from USD 30 per seat per month or Pay-as-you-go with no seat fee. Enterprise third-party models require administrator opt-in and are billed by token consumption. Google Cloud's AI developer tools overview states that the enterprise project must have Cloud Billing enabled on an invoiced billing account.
proposed_changes.new: Individual: USD 0 plan with weekly-refreshed quota (Google AI Plus has the same model access as the free plan); Google AI Pro and Ultra add higher rate limits, five-hourly quota refresh, third-party models and AI-credit overages charged at Gemini Enterprise consumption pricing (consumer plan prices are not listed on the Antigravity pricing page). Business plan via Google Cloud: API access with consumption-based pricing; for eligible Gemini Enterprise customers, Standard/Plus from USD 30 per seat per month (first-party Gemini models draw on pooled seat credits of USD 10 per month for Standard and USD 15 for Plus) or Pay-as-you-go with no seat fee. Enterprise third-party models require administrator opt-in and are billed by token consumption. Google Cloud's AI developer tools overview requires an active non-trial subscription and a project linked to Cloud Billing, either self-serve with prepaid credits or invoiced.
proposed_changes.why: Plans/models pages add Google AI Plus and credit pricing basis; enterprise page states pooled seat credits; Cloud overview (2026-11-06) now allows self-serve billing accounts with prepaid credits, where October required an invoiced account.

proposed_changes.old: No academic tier or education entitlement is listed on the Antigravity pricing or plans pages. Consumer Google AI plans are not an institutional data-protection route.
proposed_changes.new: No academic tier is listed on the Antigravity pricing or plans pages. Since 13 Oct 2026 Google has run an application-based programme giving up to 10,000 selected scientists (non-commercial research; active affiliation with a university, degree-granting institution, non-profit research institute or national laboratory) six months of free access to the highest individual usage tier and Gemini 4 Argon. Access is to the individual Antigravity service under the individual terms, not an institutional Gemini Enterprise subscription, so it is not an institutional data-protection route. Google reported over 25,000 applications and 1,000 grants by 27 Oct 2026.
proposed_changes.why: New programme announced on the science use-case page (absent from the 10 Oct 2026 Wayback snapshot); eligibility and governing terms stated on the linked Google interest form.

proposed_changes.old: Proprietary agentic development platform from Google, distinct from the open-source Gemini CLI. Surfaces: Antigravity 2.0 desktop agent command center (v2.22.0, 8 Oct 2026), Antigravity CLI (agy), IDE extensions (VS Code and Visual Studio; JetBrains, Zed and Xcode in preview), the standalone Antigravity IDE (last release 13 Aug 2026; not supported for enterprise) and the Antigravity SDK. The SDK's Python layer is Apache-2.0 but depends on a closed compiled runtime binary shipped in the PyPI wheels; official local-model support arrived in SDK v0.1.18 (21 Sep 2026), and the package is still marked Alpha. A separate managed Antigravity agent on the Gemini API (preview, Google-hosted sandbox) is cloud-only. The organization offer is the Business plan via Google Cloud and is included in eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions.
proposed_changes.new: Proprietary agentic development platform from Google, distinct from the open-source Gemini CLI. Surfaces: the Antigravity App desktop command center (formerly called Antigravity 2.0; v2.29.0, 3 Nov 2026), Antigravity CLI (agy, v1.5.1, 5 Nov 2026), IDE extensions (VS Code and Visual Studio; JetBrains, Zed, Xcode and Eclipse in preview), the standalone Antigravity IDE (v2.6.0, 26 Oct 2026; not supported for enterprise), Remote Agents (consumer Pro/Ultra, rolling out) and the Antigravity SDK. The SDK's Python layer is Apache-2.0 but depends on a closed compiled runtime binary shipped in the PyPI wheels; official local-model support arrived in SDK v0.1.18 (21 Sep 2026), the latest release is v0.1.23 (26 Oct 2026), and the package is still marked Alpha. A Plugin Marketplace with partner plugins launched in October 2026. A separate managed Antigravity agent on the Gemini API (preview, Google-hosted sandbox) is cloud-only. The organization offer is the Business plan via Google Cloud and is included in eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions.
proposed_changes.why: Current versions from the changelog; standalone IDE received v2.6.0 after a gap since 13 Aug; Eclipse extension v1.0.0 (27 Oct 2026); Remote Agents and Plugin Marketplace added.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Classifications are unchanged (local; ok/cfg/cfg; config-required, local-only). Since October, JetBrains documents Junie Local without a nightly restriction (docs dated 5 Nov 2026, standard installer with --local-model), and Windows NVIDIA RTX support became stable on 16 Oct 2026, so researchers can now use the bundled on-device engine on a release build on Macs or 24 GB RTX PCs. proposed_changes.old: Local route: Junie CLI with Ollama (cloud features disabled), LM Studio or Junie Local keeps inference on the researcher's hardware; JetBrains states that after the Junie Local model download no prompts, code or diffs are transmitted. Cloud routes (JetBrains AI models, Junie Lite on JetBrains infrastructure, BYOK providers): the JetBrains AI Terms bar training generative models on inputs/outputs without express consent and bind subcontractors to the same, but inputs may be stored for a limited period for abuse monitoring; BYOK traffic follows the provider's own terms. In JetBrains IDEs, detailed code-related data collection (full LLM prompts and responses, used to train JetBrains models, kept 1 year) is off by default for commercial individual and organizational licenses and needs explicit consent on free student/classroom/open-source licenses, but is ON by default (opt-out) for non-commercial licenses; whether it also covers Junie CLI is not documented. EAP and nightly builds fall under the Junie EAP Terms, which let JetBrains store and analyse inputs and outputs for product improvement and prohibit personal data as input.

required_controls: Configure only a local runtime (Ollama, LM Studio or Atomic Chat) on the same machine or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network, reached directly with no gateway that forwards to external providers; no Cline, ClinePass, free-model, subscription/CLI-login or cloud BYOK provider.
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Use the Apache-2.0 client (VS Code extension, CLI or Desktop) without a Cline account; Cline's ToS states no User Content is collected with telemetry when calls stay on your infrastructure and no account exists.
Turn telemetry off (extension: Allow error and usage reporting; Desktop: Settings > General; CLI: telemetryOptOut), also turn off editor telemetry, and restart Desktop/the Cline hub.
Restrict outbound network traffic: with telemetry off, Cline still contacts its servers for sign-in and feature flags.

Do not use Cloud agents, web search, the Cline API, CLI messaging connectors (cline connect: Slack, Telegram, etc.), remote MCP servers or marketplace add-ons that send data off the host; keep auto-approve/YOLO off for sensitive workspaces.
residual_risks: Telemetry is on by default, including with own keys and local models. The Desktop v0.0.26 release note (11 Sep 2026) says prompt tracing was then limited to Cline/ClinePass requests, implying earlier Desktop builds traced own-key turns; keep installs current.

A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so prompts can leave the machine unless Ollama's cloud features are disabled and the log check is repeated after updates.
Desktop and the CLI ignore the organization's telemetry and provider settings, so these controls must be enforced on each machine.

Task and session histories are stored locally (~/.cline/data/tasks; hub sessions in ~/.cline/data). Enterprise Prompt Storage can sync them to S3/R2. Institutional access, retention and backup controls are required.

Offline or air-gapped operation of the open-source client is not publicly documented; enterprise VPC/on-prem/air-gapped deployment is advertised only, and enterprise governance uses Cline's hosted admin console.
Agent terminal, browser and MCP tools can move data off the host if egress is not blocked.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Nothing material changed at TabbyML since 2026-10-10: Tabby server still shows no commits since 2026-06-30 and no release after v0.32.0, pricing, privacy policy, telemetry code and licences are unchanged, and Pochi keeps shipping (stable vscode@0.80.0 on 2026-10-28). Two facts the October record missed now matter for researchers. The tabbyml.com Terms of Service, which cover the self-hosted Software, give TabbyML ownership of default-on usage data for any legal purpose, including marketing, which is a stronger reason to switch telemetry off. Pochi's source also sends some auxiliary requests, such as worktree branch-name generation with the task prompt, to the Pochi server whatever chat model is chosen, so a signed-in Pochi client is not local-only. Suitability levels and the special-category route (config-required, customer-controlled, local-only) are unchanged.

proposed_changes.old: Self-hosted Tabby with a local model, or Pochi in BYOK mode with a local model, keeps code and prompts on controlled infrastructure. Pochi BYOK needs no account and stores task history locally by default. Telemetry is on by default: the Tabby server and IDE extensions send non-code usage statistics (server and hardware info, completion counts and latency) under a random ID to app.tabbyml.com, and each can be disabled. Pochi's extension source sends PostHog analytics only after a Pochi account sign-in (the signed-in user's email and name are attached). Remote model connectors fall under the chosen provider's own terms; Pochi-hosted models and Pochi cloud task storage leave this boundary and have no readable first-party retention or training terms. The tabbyml.com privacy policy (last modified 2024-11-11) covers only website visits and orders.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Training, opt-out, ZDR and retention terms are unchanged since October (platform, enterprise, AUP and security pages still dated 8-30 Jun 2026), and inference still always runs in Cognition's cloud, so special-category use stays 'no'. New since October: Cognition's 26 Oct 2026 privacy update discloses Devin EU (app.devin.eu), an EU-hosted service with EEA/Swiss model processing that EU institutions may want to evaluate for personal data, though its plans and contract terms are unpublished. A per-user cross-session Memory feature (9 Oct) adds a retention surface that admins can switch off. The DPA (21 Oct) adds Tinybird analytics. One correction: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 on the Trust Center belongs to the Public Sector product, not commercial Devin.

proposed_changes.old: Cloud. Devin Cloud runs the agent brain and Devbox in Cognition's multi-tenant cloud. Enterprise Customer Dedicated Deployment is a Cognition-hosted single-tenant VPC reached by AWS PrivateLink or IPSec; Enterprise Assured adds customer-managed AWS KMS keys. Devin Outposts (Pro, Max, Teams; off by default on dedicated tenants) executes commands on machines the customer operates or on partner platforms (e.g. Modal, Daytona, E2B, Cloudflare), while inference and planning stay in Devin's cloud.
proposed_changes.new: Cloud. Devin Cloud runs the agent brain and Devbox in Cognition's multi-tenant cloud. Enterprise Customer Dedicated Deployment is a Cognition-hosted single-tenant VPC reached by AWS PrivateLink or IPSec; Enterprise Assured adds customer-managed AWS KMS keys. Devin Outposts (Pro, Max, Teams; off by default on dedicated tenants) executes commands on machines the customer operates or on partner platforms (e.g. Modal, Daytona, E2B, Cloudflare), while inference and planning stay in Devin's cloud. A separate Devin EU service (app.devin.eu, with its own accounts) is hosted in the EU, with AI model providers processing content only in the EEA and Switzerland; it is documented only in Cognition's EU Privacy Notice (26 Oct 2026), and plan availability and contract terms are not published.

proposed_changes.old: Platform terms (updated 30 Jun 2026) allow training on Customer Data by default, and only paid tiers can opt out (Teams: admin only). After opt-out, data is not used for training and ZDR is enabled with model providers; ZDR does not cover data flagged by abuse classifiers, safety/security/AUP review, or legal process. Enterprise terms: no training without prior written consent. Product-level retention remains: data processed through Devin is kept for the customer relationship, and the DPA retention period runs to 30 days after termination. retained_reviews.appraisal: Status, licence, plan-level training terms and prices are unchanged; the Privacy Policy was reissued on October 21, 2026 without changing the training or retention position. The material change is Enterprise Bring Your Own Cloud (October 16): Full BYOC (private preview) can run the Replit platform and Agent harness in an institution's cloud tenant, but Replit operates it, the control plane stays outside, and Replit states model inference remains in its managed offering, so special-category use stays 'no'. The ZDR wording is narrowed: Enterprise ZDR applies only to OpenRouter models that apps call through Replit AI Integrations, not to Agent itself.

proposed_changes.old: Plan-specific. Starter/Core (Terms of Service): Replit's model-improvement page says prompts, instructions, context and generated responses are used to develop and improve its models and AI features, and the Privacy Policy names improving its machine-learning technologies such as code generation as a legitimate interest; no opt-out is documented for these plans. Pro (Pro Agreement C.2.c): Customer Content may be used to train models and AI features by default; the opt-out in Settings > Personalization covers new content only, deletes nothing, and leaves Replit's licence to use Customer Content to improve the Platform in place. Enterprise (Enterprise Agreement, last updated September 9, 2026, B.2.g): Replit will not use Customer Content to improve products or train machine-learning models except as expressly permitted in that agreement; the B.2.c licence still covers troubleshooting, improving and securing the Platform. No fixed product retention period is published; Enterprise prompt text is retained and retrievable through the Compliance API, and Enterprise audit logs are kept 30 days by default; the DPA allows a return or deletion request up to 90 days after termination, except where law requires retention. De-identified Usage Data may be used and shared with third parties. No zero-data-retention commitment was found. All Agent inference is cloud-based: Replit's managed stack calls third-party model providers (the subprocessor list names Anthropic, OpenAI and Google for AI models and Fireworks AI and Baseten as AI infrastructure, all US).

retained_reviews.appraisal: No rename, acquisition, licence or Cloud privacy-policy change since 10 Oct: Agent Canvas stays MIT, and the Cloud policy (effective 3 Sep 2025) still allows training on content with no opt-out. The pricing page was rebuilt: the free Cloud Individual plan is gone, replaced by free self-hosted Agent Canvas, a $500/month self-hosted Teams plan and custom Enterprise. For the special-category route, two new outbound paths need blocking: Agent Canvas can now send work to third-party cloud sandboxes (DigitalOcean Managed Agents, Modal), and the Enterprise Docker Compose stack sends PostHog analytics by default. The docs now also call the CLI unmaintained. Suitability ratings are unchanged.

proposed_changes.old: Self-hosted Agent Canvas/Agent Server with a local model keeps code, prompts and conversation history on your machines. Outbound traffic then comes from optional integrations, MCP servers, ACP agents and product telemetry. Agent Canvas asks for analytics consent but sends one anonymous install event before consent unless telemetry is disabled (AGENT_CANVAS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or --disable-telemetry, since v1.17.0). The launcher and Docker image also pre-configure consent-gated PostHog telemetry for the automation and agent-server services unless VITE_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 / DO_NOT_TRACK=1 is set. OpenHands Cloud: the privacy policy (effective 3 Sep 2025) allows All Hands AI to use content and feedback to train and tune its models, shares content with third-party AI providers, keeps data as long as reasonably necessary, and documents no training opt-out. Using the OpenHands LLM provider from the CLI may send usage metadata to All Hands AI. OpenHands Enterprise (self-hosted): the docs say code and conversations stay on customer infrastructure. The same docs also list periodic usage metrics for licence compliance, a Replicated licence-verification component, and required outbound access to vendor endpoints. The chosen LLM provider's terms also apply.
proposed_changes.new: Self-hosted Agent Canvas/Agent Server with a local model keeps code, prompts and conversation history on your machines. Outbound traffic then comes from optional integrations, MCP servers, ACP agents, cloud backends and product telemetry. Agent Canvas asks for analytics consent but sends one anonymous install event before consent unless telemetry is disabled (AGENT_CANVAS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or --disable-telemetry, since v1.17.0). The launcher and Docker image also pre-configure consent-gated PostHog telemetry for the automation and agent-server services unless VITE_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 / DO_NOT_TRACK=1 is set. OpenHands Cloud: the privacy policy (effective 3 Sep 2025, unchanged on 6 Nov 2026) allows All Hands AI to use content and feedback to train and tune its models, shares content with third-party AI providers, keeps data as long as reasonably necessary, and documents no training opt-out. Using the OpenHands LLM provider routes prompts through All Hands AI's LLM proxy. OpenHands Enterprise (self-hosted): the docs say code and conversations stay on customer infrastructure, but the same docs list periodic usage metrics for licence compliance, a Replicated licence-verification component and required outbound access to vendor endpoints; the Docker Compose evaluation stack sends PostHog analytics (first admin's work email, company and organisation names, automation names) unless ENABLE_POSTHOG_ANALYTICS=false and an empty POSTHOG_CLIENT_KEY are set. The chosen LLM provider's and any cloud backend's terms also apply.
proposed_changes.why: Added Enterprise Docker Compose telemetry (documented PostHog events incl. admin work email, company/org names) and cloud backends; Cloud privacy policy re-checked and unchanged. The CLI-metadata sentence was replaced because the CLI is no longer maintained; the LLM provider docs state the SDK connects to llm-proxy.app.all-hands.dev.

Confirm in the contract what leaves the environment before any special-category use. Cloud OpenHands and cloud LLM routes are not acceptable.

required_controls: Self-host the open-source Agent Canvas/Agent Server (local, Docker, VM or Kubernetes) on infrastructure the institution controls; do not add an OpenHands Cloud backend.

If OpenHands Enterprise is used instead: its documented install includes Replicated licence verification, periodic usage metrics and required outbound vendor endpoints, and no air-gapped install is documented. Obtain contractual confirmation of what is sent and restrict egress before special-category use.
Configure only a local model server (e.g. LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang) on that infrastructure; no cloud LLM provider and no OpenHands LLM provider.
Run Ollama in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Use the built-in OpenHands agent only; do not enable third-party ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode), which run their vendors' CLIs with their own LLM, tools and terms.

Disable product telemetry: AGENT_CANVAS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or --disable-telemetry for the Canvas frontend; VITE_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 so the launcher/Docker image do not set the default automation PostHog key; DO_NOT_TRACK=1 for Agent Server; and decline analytics consent.
Keep listeners on loopback or behind a strong LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY plus network access control; prefer the Docker sandbox runtime.
Enable only integrations and MCP servers that stay inside the institutional boundary; enforce egress filtering.

Deny or disable built-in web browsing, search and fetch tools; disable or centrally manage auto-update and version checks; point every model role at the local model server and keep no cloud API keys in the environment or .env; verify the effective configuration; block egress at host or network level and verify it.
residual_risks: The agent executes shell commands with filesystem and network access; the no-sandbox install gives it full access to the host filesystem.
Conversation history, settings, secrets and optional completion logs (full prompts) persist on local disk and need institutional access and retention controls.
Telemetry is controlled separately for the Canvas frontend, the Agent Server and the automation service; verify actual egress after each upgrade.
Self-hosted Enterprise sends licence/usage metrics to the vendor; their content is not documented publicly.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve cloud models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost model URL alone does not guarantee local inference.
Local models can have limited functionality compared with frontier cloud models, which may push users toward cloud routes.
Frequent releases (several per month) and Agent Canvas beta status mean configuration must be re-checked after updates.

The pricing page now shows Ultra and Growth 1-4 levels with prices, and the paid-plan file-retention conflict is resolved (7-day storage on Plus/Pro/Business, permanent on Enterprise). Julius also states it no longer builds its own models, and the help docs now say no new student or academic discounts are offered.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Hex's plans, prices, terms and privacy classification are unchanged since October: self-serve plans still allow AI-session improvement use unless the workspace opts out, Enterprise excludes it by contract, and every deployment stays on Hex-operated cloud. New since October are Hex 4.0 (private beta, announced 2026-10-27 with a $100m raise), Governed mode (2026-10-30), which Hex says is not a security control, and new SOC 1/SOC 2/HIPAA audit reports for the year to 2026-09-30. For researchers nothing changes in practice: personal data needs Team/Enterprise with the DPA, the opt-out and retention toggle set; special-category data remains unsuitable, and Grok 4.6's serving route is still undocumented.

Enterprise BYOK: Anthropic or OpenAI direct, or Claude models via AWS Bedrock or Google GEAP, optionally through a wire-compatible gateway.
proposed_changes.new: Hosted Anthropic and OpenAI models by default; models Hex hosts itself (e.g. Kimi 2.7, on US infrastructure; Hex names Baseten for hosting certain features) and Hex-run typeahead models; the subprocessor list (last modified 2026-08-04) names Anthropic, Baseten, Google, Modal, OpenAI and Parallel as AI services. Grok 4.6 was added to the model picker on 2026-09-23; its serving route is not documented and the subprocessor list has no xAI entry. Fable 5.1 is offered only on multi-tenant and non-EU, non-HIPAA single-tenant stacks. proposed_changes.old: Self-serve plans (Community, Professional, Team not under an Order Form; ToS last modified 2026-05-14): unless the customer opts out in Settings > AI & agents, Hex may use AI inputs and outputs to develop, improve and evaluate its services. Enterprise (Hex Service Agreement for Order Forms from 2026-06-24): neither Hex nor its AI providers use Customer Data to train, improve or develop AI models, except models kept for that customer only; the previous Enterprise version (Feb 2025 to Jun 2026) only excluded training models offered to other parties. Hex's FAQ adds that staff may review AI prompts and related project data when needed to fix bugs or improve AI features. LLM providers do not train and run under zero data retention by default; an Admin toggle enables models that require provider safety retention (Anthropic: 30 days for Fable 5; Fable 5.1, added 2026-09-23, also needs the toggle). Product-level storage is separate: prompts carry project code, cell outputs, schema and table/column names; cell outputs are stored indefinitely unless custom retention (7-90 days, select Enterprise plans) is enabled; schema embeddings (OpenAI Ada) sit in a vector database on Hex infrastructure. The subprocessor list gives Anthropic's processing location as USA, not the deployment region. BYOK (Enterprise) reroutes third-party inference only: typeahead still runs on Hex-run models, and Hex-hosted models such as Kimi are unavailable while BYOK is on.

Hex's FAQ adds that staff may review AI prompts and related project data when needed to fix bugs or improve AI features. LLM providers do not train and run under zero data retention by default; an Admin toggle enables models that require provider safety retention (Anthropic: 30 days for Fable 5; Fable 5.1, added 2026-09-23, also needs the toggle). The subprocessor list gives Anthropic's processing location as USA, not the deployment region. proposed_changes.old: Training: per Amp's security page, Amp and its subprocessors do not train on user data unless the user opts in; in a workspace, opting in needs admin approval, and Enterprise workspaces cannot enable it. Provider retention: Minimal Data Retention (MDR) is available to all users on Amp-managed provider connections paid with Amp credits. Under MDR, providers keep prompts/responses only to return a response, except safety/abuse data, longer model- or feature-specific retention (docs: up to 30 days), short-lived cached artifacts and legal requirements; some models and features are not eligible for MDR (flagged in-product). Amp's docs state Anthropic requires data retention for Claude Fable models, which the default high (Oracle) and ultra (agent) routing currently uses. Only the Enterprise Terms define ZDR contractually: ZDR for models and features Amp's documentation lists as eligible, MDR otherwise; workspace-wide ZDR applies only if the customer enables a workspace setting restricting selection to eligible models, where offered (the public docs do not describe that setting). The pricing FAQ and a 13 Sep 2026 post say the zero and minimal data retention policy covers all users and workspaces. BYOK, cloud-platform, gateway and linked subscriptions (ChatGPT, Grok; Claude Pro/Max in Claude Code mode) follow that provider account's retention and training terms. Product retention (not covered by MDR): Amp stores threads (messages, responses, code snippets, tool results, attachments), user information and telemetry in a multi-tenant Google Cloud project in the US. Explicitly deleted threads are removed within 30 days; Enterprise workspace threads stay with the workspace after a user leaves until the contract ends; configurable thread retention is offered to Enterprise on request. Paused orb filesystems and memory are stored until the thread is deleted; project snapshots are reused for up to 72 hours, and a replaced snapshot is deleted only after all orbs created from it are deleted. The privacy policy (last modified 10 Sep 2026) describes event analytics and a server ping; no telemetry opt-out was found.
proposed_changes.new: Training: per Amp's security page and MDR doc, Amp and its subprocessors do not train on user data unless the user opts in; in a workspace, opting in needs admin approval, and Enterprise workspaces cannot enable it. Provider retention: Minimal Data Retention (MDR) is available to all users on Amp-managed provider connections paid with Amp credits. Under MDR, providers keep prompts/responses only to return a response, except safety/abuse data, longer model- or feature-specific retention (up to 30 days), short-lived cached artifacts and legal requirements; some models and features are not eligible (flagged in-product). Claude Fable: Amp's Allowed Models doc states Anthropic retains prompts and outputs sent to Claude Fable for 30 days; Fable currently serves the ultra mode. Only the Enterprise Terms define ZDR contractually: ZDR for models and features Amp's documentation lists as eligible, MDR otherwise; workspace-wide ZDR applies only if the customer enables a setting restricting selection to eligible models, where offered (the public docs describe Allowed Models, including a Claude Fable switch, but no ZDR-only setting). The pricing FAQ still says all users and workspaces are covered by the zero and minimal data retention policy. BYOK, cloud-platform, gateway and linked subscriptions (ChatGPT, Grok, GitHub Copilot; Claude Pro/Max in Claude Code mode) follow that provider account's retention and training terms. Product retention (not covered by MDR): Amp stores threads (messages, responses, code snippets, tool results, attachments), user information and telemetry in a multi-tenant Google Cloud project in the US; with self-hosted orbs, file contents read, command output, diffs and attachments are still sent to and stored with the thread. Explicitly deleted threads are removed within 30 days, and account deletion removes owned threads within 30 days; Enterprise workspace threads stay with the workspace until the contract ends; configurable thread retention is offered to Enterprise on request. Paused Amp-hosted orb filesystems and memory are stored until the thread is deleted; project snapshots are reused for up to 72 hours. Telemetry and tracking: the privacy policy (last updated 3 Nov 2026) adds advertising pixels (Google, Meta, LinkedIn, X, Reddit) on the public website and server-side conversion events (e.g. signup, first use, purchase, with hashed email) outside the EEA/UK/Switzerland, with opt-out via 'Your Privacy Choices' or GPC; for EEA/UK/Swiss visitors it states no analytics or advertising cookies and no conversion reporting. Submitted content is not shared with advertisers. No opt-out for product telemetry was found.
proposed_changes.why: Privacy policy rewritten (last updated 3 Nov 2026): advertising pixels and server-side conversion reporting outside EEA/UK/CH, EEA/UK/CH exclusion, GPC opt-out; earlier 'event analytics and server ping' wording replaced. Allowed Models doc now states a 30-day Anthropic retention for Claude Fable (October listed this as unresolved); /modes shows Fable only in ultra. Self-hosted orbs doc states tool outputs are stored with the thread. Security page adds 30-day account deletion. MDR doc re-dated 2026-11-03 with the same substance.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Cody is still an active, Enterprise-only assistant: the IDE extensions shipped again in October (VS Code 1.156.0 on 2026-10-15, JetBrains 7.156.1 on 2026-10-27) after a four-month gap. Sourcegraph 8.1.0 made Claude Sonnet 5.5 the default chat model and removed the Gemini 2.5 models that the agentic-context docs still name as the review-step default, so that routing detail is now unconfirmed. ToS, DPA, AI Terms and subprocessor list are unchanged, and new docs state that self-hosted instances must reach services.sourcegraph.com for telemetry, licence and credit checks. Ratings are unchanged: personal data needs the DPA and a confirmed model routing, and Cody remains unsuitable for special-category data.

proposed_changes.old: Sourcegraph Model Provider (Cody Gateway) gives Enterprise instances hosted Anthropic, OpenAI and Google models. It is configured by default on Sourcegraph Cloud; self-hosted customers confirm access with their account manager. Autocomplete and Smart Apply models include Fireworks-hosted models (US Iowa). Self-hosted instances can instead configure BYOK providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini/Vertex, Fireworks), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or Hugging Face TGI; the docs say BYOK with managed services is supported only on self-hosted instances. The model list changes often; check the current supported-models page and the instance's modelConfiguration.

proposed_changes.old: Enterprise only. The Cody FAQ states Sourcegraph will not train on Enterprise customers' data; the ToS (last modified 2026-07-22) allows fine-tuning only if enabled for the instance and says Partner LLMs reached through Sourcegraph keep zero retention (temporary abuse/harm retention excepted) and do not train. Product-level retention is separate: the DPA (last modified 2026-10-05) lists maintaining AI conversation history during the subscription term as a processing purpose; after expiry Sourcegraph returns or deletes data on the customer's instruction, and without an instruction within 60 days deletes all Customer Personal Data, including AI conversation data, within 90 days. The partner zero-retention commitment applies only to access through Sourcegraph's Partner LLMs, so with BYOK the customer's own provider agreement sets retention. The AI Terms (2026-06-12) apply only to agreements signed before 2024-02-15 or Order Forms that incorporate them; the Cody notice (2024-02-15) applies only to older Cody licences. Self-hosted instances send aggregated pings (no code, but including the installer/admin email, instance URL and IP) and license verification checks, and export telemetry events (numeric metadata, anonymized user IDs) to Sourcegraph by default.

retained_reviews.appraisal: OpenCode is active, MIT-licensed and fast-moving (V2 2.2.5 and V1 1.19.5 in late October). Since October, session sharing was discontinued (1.19.1), OpenCode Zen was folded into the OpenCode Console as 'OpenCode Models', Go Teams was added, and Go now blocks paid training endpoints by default. For researchers the most useful change is that V2 now documents system and MDM managed configuration with top-level policies and an OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS switch, so the local-only route can be enforced on V2 as well; new caveats are that V2 allows outside-project file access by default and that the websearch.use policy needs an unreleased client, so web search must be disabled with websearch:false.

proposed_changes.new: BYOK cloud providers (75+ via Models.dev, plus GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT Plus/Pro and GitLab Duo sign-in) or local Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM and other OpenAI-compatible endpoints (V2 auto-discovers Ollama, LM Studio and vLLM); optional hosted OpenCode Models (pay-as-you-go, formerly OpenCode Zen) and OpenCode Go (subscription) gateways, and in V2 the hosted OpenCode Console gateway for a workspace's own provider keys.

proposed_changes.old: The client keeps sessions, logs and credentials on the local machine (~/.local/share/opencode). The vendor states that it does not store code or context data and that prompts go directly to the selected provider. With no OpenCode key set, V1 and V2 enable the hosted OpenCode free models by default (vendor source code), so choose a provider explicitly and block the rest. The hosted routes are not uniformly zero-retention. On Zen, OpenAI and Anthropic requests are retained for 30 days; Mistral and Jev data follow those providers' own retention policies; several free models may use data to improve the model; NVIDIA free endpoints log use; and Muse Spark Contributor trains Meta models. On Go, the Grok, GPT Luna and Claude Haiku routes retain for 30 days, the Muse Spark Contributor models train, and the DeepSeek ZDR agreement is renewed monthly. The V2 Console gateway records each request and its cost; its content retention is not documented. The Terms allow Content from unpaid accounts on the hosted Services to be used to improve them. V1 session sharing uploads conversations to opencode.ai; V2 has no sharing yet. Both lines can send web searches to third parties (V1 when the OpenCode or Go provider is used, or with the Exa/Parallel flags; V2 through five search providers or Console-hosted search), and the webfetch tool, allowed by default, can reach any URL. Disable sharing, web search and webfetch for private work, and review every selected provider.
proposed_changes.new: The client keeps sessions, logs and credentials on the local machine (~/.local/share/opencode). The vendor states that it does not store code or context data and that prompts go directly to the selected provider. With no OpenCode key set, V1 and V2 offer the hosted OpenCode free models by default (V1 source; V2 docs and 2.2.1 release notes), so choose a provider explicitly and block the rest (V2: OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS=1 or a provider policy). The hosted routes are not uniformly zero-retention. On OpenCode Models (formerly Zen), OpenAI and Anthropic requests are retained for 30 days, Mistral data follow Mistral's retention policy, several free models may use data to improve the model or retain it for 30 days, and NVIDIA free endpoints log use. On Go, the Grok 4.7, GPT Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Beam Free routes retain for 30 days; the Muse Spark Contributor models train Meta models and are blocked unless an admin allows paid training endpoints; Iceman Contributor Free uses prompts to improve the model; the DeepSeek ZDR agreement is renewed monthly. The V2 Console gateway records each request and its cost; its content retention is not documented. Console-hosted web search is stated to be zero-retention. The Terms allow Content from unpaid accounts on the hosted Services to be used to improve them. Session sharing was discontinued in 1.19.1 (15 Oct 2026), and V2 has no sharing. Both lines can send web searches to third parties (V1 with the OpenCode or Go provider or the Exa/Parallel flags; V2 through five search providers or Console search), and webfetch, allowed by default, can reach any URL. Disable web search and webfetch for private work, and review every selected provider.
proposed_changes.why: Sharing discontinued in 1.19.1; Models privacy exceptions changed (Muse Spark Contributor and Jev no longer listed there; new free models with 30-day retention or improvement use); Go now blocks paid training endpoints by default and adds Iceman Contributor Free; Console web search stated zero-retention; V2 OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS documented.

proposed_changes.old: Open-source coding agent for the terminal, desktop, web and IDE, with local, direct-provider and hosted Zen, Go and Console routes. OpenCode 2 (2.0.0 published on npm on 11 September 2026; the opencode.ai installer now installs v2 and replaces the V1 binary) is developed in parallel with the maintained 1.x line. V2 does not yet support session sharing or run language servers, always runs a local background service, offers web search through five third-party providers (Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, Tavily, TinyFish) or Console-hosted search, and accepts provider and permission policies from the Console. The Zen docs say models are hosted in the US and EU; the Zen landing page says the US. Advisory GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 (September 2026, high severity) affected `opencode serve` on npm/pnpm/Bun installs and was fixed in 1.18.22. Keep the client patched and do not expose the local server.
proposed_changes.new: Open-source coding agent for the terminal, desktop, web and IDE, with local, direct-provider and hosted OpenCode Models, Go and Console routes. OpenCode 2 (@opencode/cli; 2.0.0 on npm 11 Sep 2026, 2.2.5 on 30 Oct) is now the default from the opencode.ai installer and Homebrew core; the 1.x line (opencode-ai, 1.19.5 on 28 Oct) is maintained, no longer installs updates automatically (1.19.0) and stays on 1.x. Session sharing was discontinued in 1.19.1. V2 runs a shared local background service by default (it can be disabled, or --standalone used), does not run language servers, allows access outside the project directory by default, offers web search through five third-party providers or Console search, and accepts policies from system config, macOS MDM and a connected Console workspace. The Models docs say models are hosted in the US and EU; Go workspaces allow Europe and US regions by default. No new advisory since GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 (September 2026, fixed in 1.18.22). Keep the client patched and do not expose the local server.

old: Run inference only through a local model runtime (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM) on controlled infrastructure; do not use the separate Ollama Cloud provider.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Block all other providers, including the built-in "opencode" provider whose hosted free models are enabled when no key is set: V1 enabled_providers/disabled_providers, or a V2 experimental.policies provider.use deny "*" followed by an allow for the local provider. Check the log, because invalid policy statements are dropped with a warning.

Set every model role explicitly to the local provider (V1 model and small_model), and confirm sessions do not switch models (V2 falls back to the newest available supported model when the configured one is unavailable). Keep no cloud API keys in the environment or .env files, and remove stored hosted-provider credentials from ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json.
Set share to "disabled" (V1 default is manual; V2 does not yet support sharing).

Disable web search (V2 "websearch": false; on V1 avoid the OpenCode/Go providers and leave OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA/PARALLEL off) and deny webfetch (V1 permission webfetch deny; V2 policy permission "webfetch:*" deny). Review MCP servers, plugins and LSP downloads for egress.

Enforce the settings: on V1 through managed config (/etc/opencode, /Library/Application Support/opencode, %ProgramData%\opencode, or a macOS MDM profile). V2 (2.0.26) has no documented system managed config, so pin to 1.x where enforcement is required, or protect the V2 config files with OS controls; Console-delivered policy needs a vendor-cloud connection.

Check the effective configuration before sensitive sessions, because project config files, remote .well-known config and the OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT variable are also loaded and may set providers, tools or permissions.

Disable auto-update or manage updates centrally (V1 autoupdate false or OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE; V2 update "disable"). On offline hosts also disable the remote model-catalog fetch and LSP downloads (documented V1 flags: OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH, OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD).
Restrict host network egress to the local model endpoint, because shell commands run with the user's network access, and confirm with egress monitoring before processing special-category data.
Keep clients at or above the patched versions; do not expose opencode serve/web or the V2 background service beyond localhost, and set a server password.
new: Run inference only through a local model runtime (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM) on controlled infrastructure; do not use the separate Ollama Cloud provider.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in ~/.ollama/server.json of the account that runs the server), confirm the log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Block all other providers, including the built-in "opencode" free tier: V1 enabled_providers/disabled_providers; V2 a top-level policies provider.use deny "*" followed by an allow for the local provider, plus OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS=1 on the server process. Check the log, because invalid policy statements are dropped with a warning.

On V2 2.2.3 or later, use managed policies to deny integration.connect for the Console and web-search integrations and to deny mcp.use, skill.use and plugin.use except reviewed items, so a Console workspace cannot deliver providers, MCP servers or web search.

Set every model role explicitly to the local provider (V1 model and small_model; V2 model and agents.title.model), and confirm sessions do not switch models (V2 falls back to the newest available supported model when the configured one is unavailable). Keep no cloud API keys in the environment or .env files, and remove stored hosted-provider credentials from ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json.

Disable web search (V2 "websearch": false, because websearch.use policies need 2.2.6, unreleased on 6 Nov 2026; on V1 avoid the OpenCode/Go providers and leave OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA/PARALLEL off) and deny webfetch (V1 permission webfetch deny; V2 policy tool.use "webfetch:*" deny). Review MCP servers, plugins and LSP downloads for egress.
On V2, add an external_directory ask or deny rule, because V2 allows reads and edits outside the project without a prompt by default.

Enforce the settings through managed configuration that users cannot override: the system config directory (/etc/opencode, /Library/Application Support/opencode, %ProgramData%\opencode) or macOS MDM managed preferences (ai.opencode.managed), now documented for both 1.x and V2. Express restrictions as V2 policies, because ordinary settings cannot stop users adding providers, MCP servers or plugins.

Check the effective configuration before sensitive sessions, because project config files, remote .well-known config and environment variables are also loaded and may set providers, tools or permissions.

Manage updates centrally (V1 1.19.0 or later no longer installs updates automatically; V1 autoupdate false or OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE; V2 update "disable"). On offline hosts also disable the remote model-catalog fetch and LSP downloads (documented V1 flags: OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH, OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD).
Restrict host network egress to the local model endpoint, because shell commands run with the user's network access, and confirm with egress monitoring before processing special-category data.

Keep clients at or above the patched versions (1.x at least 1.19.1, where sharing is discontinued); do not expose opencode serve/web or the V2 background service beyond localhost, and set a server password (V2 OPENCODE_PASSWORD).
proposed_changes.why: V2 managed config and top-level policies (integration.connect/use, mcp.use, plugin.use from 2.2.3; websearch.use only from 2.2.6, not yet released), OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS, V2 external_directory default allow, V1 no longer auto-installs updates, sharing discontinued.

old: Local sessions, logs, credentials (auth.json) and the session database under ~/.local/share/opencode need institutional access, retention and egress controls.

Out of the box, V1 and V2 enable the hosted OpenCode free models, and V2 falls back to the newest available model when the configured one is unavailable; a missing deny rule or a stopped local runtime can route prompts to hosted models, some of which permit data use for improvement or training.
A signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost provider setting alone does not show that inference stays local.
V2 provider policies are experimental, invalid statements are dropped with a warning, and policies do not sandbox plugin code.
V2 has no documented system managed config; users can change their own global config unless OS controls prevent it.
The local HTTP server and web UI have had high or critical advisories (most recently GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4, September 2026); V2 always runs a local background service.
OpenCode 2 is a new major line; V2 equivalents of some V1 egress flags were not verified.
Third-party MCP servers, plugins and LSP servers can send data outside the controlled boundary.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Mistral's training, ZDR, Privacy Policy and DPA terms and the prices are the same as in October. The CLI moved to v3.x: the Rust TUI is now the only interface and is licensed Apache-2.0, which removes the earlier proprietary-component caveat. Some October local-route controls no longer work: enable_auto_update now does nothing (use enable_update_checks), browser sign-in is on by default, and unset utility models go to a Mistral model. Special-category use stays config-required, but researchers following the October settings must update their config.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Classification is unchanged: personal data only through a governed Kiro Enterprise profile, and special-category data not appropriate because inference is cloud-only with no local or customer-controlled model endpoint. Since October, Kiro CLI 3.0.0 made the V3 harness the default and retired the desktop app and shell autocomplete; most models (including Fable 5.1 for Enterprise and GPT-5.6) left Experimental/Preview, and a new US-only Kimi K3 model needs admin approval. Pricing changed: teams and new Enterprise customers now buy credit-pooling seats ($20/seat, 500 shared credits), and individuals get a first-upgrade trial. For researchers, the Enterprise route still requires model governance (block GPT-5.6, Fable 5.1, Kimi K3 and Auto where the approved list must bind) and cloud sessions kept off unless assessed; CLI Memory is confirmed to be stored locally.

proposed_changes.old: Managed cloud catalog; Kiro states it is powered by Amazon Bedrock. Includes Anthropic Claude models, OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, open-weight models (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Qwen) and an Auto router; several models (including Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, all GPT-5.6 tiers and some open-weight models) are labelled Experimental, and Claude Fable 5.1 is an Enterprise-only Preview that admins must add through model governance. Per the models page (updated 8 Oct 2026), GPT-5.6 has Global inference scope and uses the US endpoint even for Frankfurt profiles; other models have Geography scope (the enterprise profile's US or EU geography; Free and individual users use the US endpoint); Fable 5.1 runs only in us-east-1. AWS GovCloud (US) has a separate catalog with inference kept in GovCloud. The docs index lists no local or bring-your-own model option. Models and credit multipliers change often.

Students-tier accounts use the same sign-in methods and the Students FAQ points them to the same training opt-out; Kiro does not state whether they count as individual subscribers. Enterprise users (IAM Identity Center or external IdP) are excluded from service improvement and automatically opted out of telemetry/content collection, but content may be stored in the profile Region (US East (N. Virginia), Europe (Frankfurt) or AWS GovCloud (US)) to run the service; prompt logs and daily activity reports, when enabled, go to a customer-chosen S3 bucket in the customer's AWS account. Kiro may also collect operational signals (error logs and metrics based on instructions, feedback and responses). Model-specific abuse retention applies to all users: OpenAI GPT classifier-flagged traffic up to 30 days; all Claude Fable 5.1 Preview traffic up to 30 days, with possible human review of flagged traffic by AWS. GPT-5.6 uses Global cross-region inference (possibly outside the profile geography). Optional --cloud sessions keep conversation history, cloned repositories and sandbox files in a Kiro-managed cloud sandbox (us-east-1 only for Identity Center organisations; off for Enterprise until an admin enables it). Running the CLI locally does not make inference local.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Classification is unchanged (no-train via Business/Enterprise; nonsensitive ok, personal cfg, special no), but two things changed since October. Warp disclosed a security incident involving a vendor in its infrastructure (CEO post, 26 Oct 2026; GPG signing subkey rotated 4 Nov 2026), and its docs and legal pages do not say which stored data was affected. Before using Warp with personal data, researchers should get Warp's account of the incident. A new Enterprise private-networking option lets Warp's hosted backend reach a private or on-premises LLM gateway. The Warp Agent harness and control plane still run in Warp's cloud, so special-category data stays not appropriate. Pricing now states included usage in dollars, with annual prices and a separate Warp Factories plan ladder.

proposed_changes.old: Desktop client (macOS, Linux, Windows) and Warp Agent CLI, with Warp-cloud agent harness, control plane and run-data storage. Enterprise can self-host cloud-agent execution workers and map cloud-agent run transcripts, artifacts and attachments to its own AWS S3 bucket; orchestration, run records and Warp Agent inference still route through Warp.
proposed_changes.new: Desktop client (macOS, Linux, Windows) and Warp Agent CLI, with Warp-cloud agent harness, control plane and run-data storage. Enterprise can self-host cloud-agent execution workers (Docker, Kubernetes, Direct or Command backends) and map cloud-agent run transcripts, artifacts and prompt attachments to its own AWS S3 bucket (Azure Blob Storage on request). Enterprise private networking (Private Service Connect, AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link, on-premises interconnect or IPsec VPN) lets Warp's hosted backend reach a private team-managed LLM gateway or MCP server. Orchestration, run records and the Warp Agent harness still run in Warp's cloud.
proposed_changes.why: Data-storage page now lists Azure Blob Storage alongside S3; self-hosting page lists four managed backends; new Enterprise private-networking page connects private LLM gateways to Warp's hosted backend, which still originates the model requests.

proposed_changes.old: Warp-managed models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and open-weights models hosted by Fireworks AI (e.g. GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek); BYOK (OpenAI, Anthropic or Google keys), ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscription, and OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints (public URL only, e.g. OpenRouter, LiteLLM), all relayed through Warp's server-side agent harness; Enterprise BYOLLM via AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex AI.
proposed_changes.new: Warp-managed models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI and open-weights models hosted by Fireworks AI (e.g. GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek, MiniMax), plus Auto and custom routers. Customer-supplied inference: personal BYOK (OpenAI, Anthropic or Google keys), ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscription and OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints (public URL only, e.g. OpenRouter, LiteLLM, z.ai), limited to individuals and organisations with 10 or fewer employees; team-managed keys and endpoints on Business and Enterprise; Enterprise BYOLLM via AWS Bedrock (Claude and OpenAI models) or Gemini Enterprise (Vertex AI; Gemini and Claude partner models). All Warp Agent routes are relayed through Warp's server-side harness; Claude consumer subscriptions are not supported.
proposed_changes.why: Model page adds Auto (Open-weights), custom routers and MiniMax via Fireworks; BYOK/endpoint pages restate the 10-employee limit and add z.ai; BYOLLM docs now name Gemini Enterprise (Vertex AI) and the models each route supports; team-managed keys documented for Business/Enterprise.

proposed_changes.old: Tier-specific. Business and Enterprise: Warp's privacy docs say these plans are covered by its ZDR agreement and no AI interaction or console data is collected; data collection is off by default and admin-enforceable. Free: telemetry must stay on to use AI features, and Warp's agent FAQ reserves the right to use collected data to train models (the privacy notice, last modified 18 Aug 2026, also lists model training as a purpose). Other paid plans (docs: 'paid teams'): data collection is on by default; users can opt out and keep AI. Provider ZDR (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Fireworks AI) covers Warp-managed inference only and excludes Claude Fable 5/5.1, which Anthropic retains (off by default for Enterprise teams; Business default not stated). With customer-supplied inference (BYOK, custom endpoints, ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscriptions, team-managed keys, BYOLLM) provider retention and training follow the user's or team's own provider terms; Warp says it cannot enforce ZDR for subscription requests. Product-level retention remains: cloud-synced conversations (per-user setting; Enterprise can disable org-wide) and cloud-agent transcripts, artifacts and attachments sit in Warp-managed storage; only the cloud-agent run data can be mapped to an Enterprise-owned S3 bucket, which Warp's control plane still reads and writes. Codebase Context keeps embeddings; telemetry, when collected, is kept indefinitely; shared sessions expire after about one week. First-party pages conflict: the privacy page requires telemetry for AI on Free while the security pages say opt-out keeps full functionality, and www.warp.dev/legal/security says ZDR is available on the Enterprise plan while the model page says ZDR applies across all plans.
proposed_changes.new: Tier-specific. Business and Enterprise: Warp's privacy docs (last updated 3 Nov 2026) say these plans are covered by its ZDR agreement and no AI interaction or console data is collected; data collection is off by default and admin-enforceable. Free: telemetry must stay on to use AI features, and Warp's agent FAQ reserves the right to use collected data to train models (the privacy notice, last modified 18 Aug 2026, also lists model training as a purpose). Other paid plans (docs: 'paid teams'): data collection is on by default; users can opt out and keep AI. Provider ZDR (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Fireworks AI) covers Warp-managed inference only and excludes Claude Fable 5/5.1, which Anthropic retains (off by default for Enterprise teams; Business default not stated). With customer-supplied inference (BYOK, custom endpoints, ChatGPT or SuperGrok subscriptions, team-managed keys, BYOLLM) provider retention and training follow the user's or team's own provider terms and Warp says it cannot enforce ZDR; its BYOK and endpoint pages say Warp does not train on that relayed content. Team-managed keys fall back to Warp-managed inference when a member has no key, if allowed. Product-level retention remains: cloud-synced conversations (per-user setting, admin-configurable; cloud-agent conversations are always stored) and cloud-agent transcripts, artifacts and attachments sit in Warp-managed storage; only the cloud-agent run data can be mapped to an Enterprise-owned S3 or Azure bucket, which Warp's control plane still reads, writes and periodically accesses for maintenance. Codebase Context keeps embeddings; telemetry, when collected, is kept indefinitely; shared sessions expire after about one week. Warp disclosed a security incident involving a vendor in its infrastructure on 26 Oct 2026; Warp has not published the scope on its docs or legal pages. First-party pages conflict: the privacy page requires telemetry for AI on Free while the security pages and pricing FAQ say any user can opt out (the FAQ calls this 'full ZDR'), and www.warp.dev/legal/security says ZDR is available on the Enterprise plan while the model page says ZDR applies across all plans.
proposed_changes.why: Adds the October 2026 security incident (first-party CEO post and Warp blog), the BYOK/endpoint no-training statement, team-key fallback, Azure storage and maintenance access, and the pricing FAQ's 'full ZDR' wording as a further docs conflict. Classification stays no-train (Business/Enterprise route).

retained_reviews.appraisal: No policy, pricing, training or retention change since 2026-10-10: terms v1.9 and privacy policy v1.2 are unchanged and the pricing page has the same three plans. The Harness takeover is now visible on the site: augmentcode.com is '© 2026 Harness, Inc.', Harness's Cosmos page sends sign-ups to cosmos.augmentcode.com, and Harness's public subprocessor list covers 'Augment Code'. The models page states that models other than eligible OpenAI GPT and Prism options require the organisation to approve provider data retention, a useful control for personal data. Special-category data stays 'no': inference is still Augment-cloud only.

Product retention: the Context Engine stores indexed code (every workspace file not excluded by .gitignore/.augmentignore); Cosmos session snapshots are kept 14 days; Cosmos Files (Expert outputs and memory) persist on Augment with version history (at least one weekly version kept beyond 30 days; deletions recorded as tombstones); the privacy policy (v1.2, 2025-08-28) gives no fixed periods ('as long as necessary'). Model use is gated by provider data retention: the models page says only eligible OpenAI GPT models and the Prism options can be used without approving provider data retention in the organisation's model settings, and Enterprise admins can allow-list models by retention policy. Default storage and processing in the US; EU tenants can enforce EU-inference-only; data residency and CMEK are Enterprise-only on the pricing page, and BYOK is documented in the Enterprise admin guide. DPA and subprocessor list on request (privacy policy). Harness's public subprocessor list now tags Google (US and EU data centres) and AWS as subprocessors for 'Augment Code' but names no model provider, so it is incomplete for this product. proposed_changes.old: Deepnote states AI-processed content is not used for model training and that its provider agreements prohibit training. The AI privacy page says AI context can be processed in the US and worldwide, allows provider safety retention (OpenAI up to 30 days) and cites zero-retention only for some real-time code suggestions; the security overview separately states ZDR for Anthropic. Product-level retention of prompts, agent history and AI-action logs is not published. The security overview also states that an encrypted temporary copy of workspace data can be stored on other compute providers' machines, with AWS used for long-term storage. Sharing block outputs (which can include row-level data) with the LLM is a separate switch, and admins can disable Deepnote AI. The terms let Deepnote use usage statistics (not Customer Data) to improve the product. Enterprise custom endpoints cover Agent, edits and suggestions but not code completions.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Genie Code remains a pure-cloud Databricks agent (special-category data: no); training, ZDR, retention and deployment claims are unchanged. Databricks has withdrawn the 2026-11-01 date for removing the partner-powered AI features setting: the toggle still exists, still cannot be switched off in the UI, and the Settings API still changes it, with removal now 'at a later date'. Genie Code tasks in Lakeflow Jobs went GA on 2026-10-21 and always run with auto-approve, so researchers handling personal data should keep both scheduled and job tasks away from it. Pricing is re-confirmed; the 25% promotion applies to Genie Code only, and the Genie One/Agents free promotion does not cover it.

proposed_changes.old: Databricks-selected models. With the partner-powered AI features setting on (default for non-CSP workspaces), Agent mode uses Azure OpenAI Service, OpenAI on Databricks and Anthropic on Databricks (Databricks states the Anthropic endpoints are hosted by Databricks within its security perimeter), and other Genie Code chat uses Azure OpenAI Service and OpenAI on Databricks. With it off (default for CSP workspaces), Genie Code runs on a Databricks-hosted open model without agentic capabilities; in CSP workspaces this fallback exists only under the HIPAA, FedRAMP Moderate (US), PCI-DSS or HITRUST (US/ANZ) standards. Autocomplete always uses a Databricks-hosted model. Since 2026-09-08 the setting can no longer be switched off in the settings UI, but the Settings API can still change it until 2026-11-01. On that date the toggle is removed and existing values persist; after that, changes go through the Databricks account team. The CLI (Beta) uses a Databricks-selected model via Unity Gateway.
proposed_changes.new: Databricks-selected models. With the partner-powered AI features setting on (default for non-CSP workspaces), Genie Code's agentic capabilities use Azure OpenAI Service, OpenAI on Databricks and Anthropic on Databricks (Databricks states the Anthropic endpoints are hosted by Databricks within its security perimeter), and non-agentic chat uses Azure OpenAI Service and OpenAI on Databricks. With it off (default for CSP workspaces), Genie Code runs on a Databricks-hosted open-source model without agentic capabilities; in CSP workspaces this fallback exists only under the HIPAA, FedRAMP Moderate (US), PCI-DSS or HITRUST (US/ANZ) standards. Autocomplete always uses a Databricks-hosted model. Since 2026-09-08 the setting can no longer be switched off in the settings UI (it can still be switched on), and the Settings API can still change it in either direction. Databricks now says the setting will be removed 'at a later date' (the earlier 2026-11-01 date is no longer stated); existing values persist, and after removal changes go through the Databricks account team. The CLI (Beta) uses a Databricks-selected model via Unity Gateway (GPT 5.6 during Beta per the CLI docs; can change).
proposed_changes.why: The partner-powered page (updated 2026-11-03) and the 2026-09-08 release note now give no removal date ('At a later date, Databricks will fully remove the setting'); the 2026-11-01 date in the record is no longer supported and, as of 2026-11-03, the Settings API still works. CLI docs name the Beta model. 'Agent mode' is now documented as 'agentic capabilities'.

proposed_changes.old: Databricks states it does not use prompts, responses or submitted data to train generative foundation models it makes available to third parties; partner-powered features use partner zero-data-retention endpoints. Provider ZDR is therefore not end-to-end deletion. These commitments are stated for the workspace AI assistive features; the Genie Code CLI (Beta) sends prompts and local file content as Unity Gateway model usage, and the trust page does not separately document how that traffic is handled.

proposed_changes.old: Local/self-hosted: marimo's default config sets no model or key and copilot completion off, and marimohub managed AI is off by default. When AI is used, notebook code, @-referenced variable values and whatever the chat's Ask/Agent/Code-mode tools read from the notebook or kernel go to the configured provider under that provider's terms; if no model is set, marimo falls back to openai/gpt-4o and uses OPENAI_API_KEY from the server environment or .env files when present. Paired agent CLIs send notebook context to their own backends. Core telemetry: no usage analytics found in a source search; OpenTelemetry tracing is opt-in (MARIMO_TRACING) and writes to a local file by default; the CLI checks marimo.io for a new release once a day unless --skip-update-check or MARIMO_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1 is set (per the source code, a plain request without notebook content). molab is a separate hosted service: notebooks are 'public but undiscoverable by default'; built-in AI uses free hosted models (Weights & Biases subprocessor); the subprocessor list for molab, Community Cloud and marimo's websites also names Sentry (error/performance tracing) and PostHog (product analytics). molab terms (last updated 2022-09-22) prohibit HIPAA PHI and GDPR Article 9(1) data and grant Marimo a licence to use submitted content to operate, improve and provide the services; after account cancellation (molab terms) or an honoured deletion request (marimo data-requests page), content is deleted from active systems within 30 days and from backups within 60 days. Marimo's privacy URL redirects to CoreWeave's privacy policy (updated 2026-02-24), which permits AI/ML processing to improve and develop services; no molab-specific statement on training with notebook content or AI prompts was found.
proposed_changes.new: Local/self-hosted: marimo's default config sets no model or key and copilot completion off, and marimohub managed AI is off by default. When AI is used, notebook code, @-referenced variable values and whatever the chat assistant reads at its Notebook access level (Read only, Suggest edits or Full access; Full access can run arbitrary Python) from the notebook or kernel go to the configured provider under that provider's terms; if no model is set, marimo falls back to openai/gpt-4o and uses OPENAI_API_KEY from the server environment or .env files when present. Paired agent CLIs send notebook context to their own backends. With marimohub managed AI on, a per-user project Chat is also on by default (MARIMOHUB_AI_CHAT=on); conversations are stored by the hub with redacted tool previews, but saved resumable tasks keep tool payloads with credential-like fields masked. marimohub problem reports are off by default and, per its docs, exclude notebook content. Since October, ChatGPT for Academic Researchers closed to new applications (waitlist only), and OpenAI launched the Rosalind Academic Plan (2026-10-15): free Business Standard seats for U.S. university life-sciences labs, with standard retention and no ZDR, so it is not open to European researchers. proposed_changes.old: Business, Enterprise, Edu and ChatGPT for Academic Researchers workspaces are excluded from model training by default. Individual plans (Free/Go/Plus/Pro) may be used for training unless 'Improve the model for everyone' is off; thumbs feedback can still submit the whole conversation. On personal accounts, content on shared Space pages can be used for training through a collaborator's settings even if the owner opted out. Product-level retention applies regardless: saved chats persist until deleted or removed by a workspace retention policy (then scheduled for deletion within 30 days); Library files persist until deleted separately, and deleting a chat does not delete them; in Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare workspaces Library files follow the workspace retention policy. From 2026-09-29 Space replaces Library for eligible Pro/Business/Enterprise accounts; Space file retention is not separately documented. Eligible new Enterprise/Edu workspaces can keep in-scope content (including Code Interpreter & Data Analysis artifacts) at rest in-region, with optional GPU inference residency (help centre: EEA+CH, US, UAE); CPU processing, metadata and external integrations may be outside the region, and the residency article does not say where the Python data-analysis environment runs. ZDR is documented for eligible API endpoints; the Business overview lists ZDR only as an unspecified sales-led option, and no ZDR terms for ChatGPT chats or files were found.
proposed_changes.new: Business, Enterprise, Edu and ChatGPT for Academic Researchers workspaces are excluded from model training by default; on Business/Enterprise/Edu, thumbs feedback does not permit training unless the organization signs a separate agreement. Individual plans (Free/Go/Plus/Pro) may be used for training unless 'Improve the model for everyone' is off; thumbs feedback can still submit the whole conversation. On personal accounts, content on shared Space pages can be used for training through a collaborator's settings even if the owner opted out. Business data may be run through automated content classifiers and safety tools. Product-level retention applies regardless: saved chats persist until deleted or removed by a workspace retention policy (then scheduled for deletion within 30 days); temporary chats may be kept up to 30 days. retained_reviews.appraisal: Classification is unchanged (nonsensitive ok, personal cfg via an organisation ZDR key on a pinned Standard model, special no), and the ToS has not changed since 2026-10-09. Muse Code now implements the subscription training default as an in-app Contributor mode setting, on by default and saved per computer; an organisation's managed configuration keeps it off, and builds before 1.4.8 did not fully opt out background requests. New since October: the Muse Wonder model (preview; Wonder Full only on Power and Maximum subscriptions), a $200/month Maximum Usage plan, and the self-hostable open-weight Muse Spark Open, which is not documented for use with Muse Code, so inference for Muse Code stays Meta-cloud only.

proposed_changes.old: Meta-hosted Muse Spark models: Standard muse-spark-1.1/1.2/1.3 and Contributor muse-spark-1.2/1.3-contributor (1,048,576-token context). Muse Code docs name muse-spark-1.2 as the default model; the API docs recommend 1.3 for new work. The client is provider-aware: the configuration docs and changelog refer to other providers, a --provider flag for muse serve and a keyless custom endpoint, and Meta's MIT SDK quickstart sets an endpoint_transport base URL to a loopback test endpoint. No first-party page documents serving a self-hosted or local model to Muse Code. Meta's open-weight Muse Glimmer runs on your own hardware; its docs do not mention Muse Code.
proposed_changes.new: Meta-hosted Muse models. In Muse Code: Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3 (Standard) and their Contributor variants muse-spark-1.2/1.3-contributor, Muse Wonder (muse-wonder-1.0, in preview; Standard model) and, on Power and Maximum Usage subscriptions only, Muse Wonder Full; all 1,048,576-token context. Muse Spark 1.1 is not available in Muse Code. Muse Code docs name muse-spark-1.2 as the default model; the API docs recommend 1.3 for new work. The client is provider-aware: the configuration docs and changelog refer to other providers, a --provider flag for muse serve and a keyless custom endpoint, and Meta's MIT SDK quickstart sets an endpoint_transport base URL to a loopback test endpoint. Changelog entries (1.4.3-1.4.12) also mention 'offline sessions', 'local-model setup' and Claude and GPT models served through a Meta gateway; none of these is documented for public use. Meta's open-weight models (Muse Spark Open, 816B-parameter MoE under the Muse Model License, and Muse Glimmer) can be self-hosted, but no first-party page documents connecting Muse Code to them.
proposed_changes.why: New models since October: Muse Wonder (muse-wonder-1.0, preview) in Muse Code on pay-as-you-go and every plan; Muse Wonder Full on Power/Maximum subscriptions only; Muse Spark 1.1 not available in Muse Code. New open-weight Muse Spark Open (816B MoE, self-hostable, Muse Model License) whose docs do not mention Muse Code. Changelog 1.4.3-1.4.12 mentions offline sessions, local-model setup and Claude/GPT models through a Meta gateway without public docs.

proposed_changes.old: The no-train label applies to the personal-data route in tier_gate (organisation API key on a pinned Standard model); a Muse Code subscription on default settings runs under Contributor (training) terms. Terms depend on account route and model tier (Meta Model API Terms of Service, last updated 2026-10-09). Standard models (muse-spark-1.1/1.2/1.3): Meta acts as processor under the Meta Global Processor Terms and does not train on Content. Contributor models (1.2/1.3-contributor) permit training, and the ToS forbids sending personal, sensitive or confidential data (including confidential code) to them. Since the 2026-10-09 ToS, a Muse Code subscription counts as Contributor (training) by default whatever model is selected; Standard terms require changing an Account setting and apply prospectively only. Pay-as-you-go API-key use of the default model (muse-spark-1.2) is Standard. The ToS also warns that the system may route requests to a Contributor model. On every tier Meta may retain and process Content for policy enforcement and to develop safety and security systems, and the Data Commitments page also lists improving and maintaining the Model API. Without ZDR, Content and Usage Data (tool-call sequences, logs, telemetry) are retained 'as needed' with no stated period, and Usage Data may be used to develop and improve Meta products. The Data Commitments page says Content can be viewed and deleted through the account. ZDR is available only to qualified organisations, enabled by Meta through sales; personal accounts are not covered, support may vary by model, ZDR turns off stateful and background requests, file uploads and web search, and flagged content may still be kept up to 2 years. CLI: changelog 1.4.0 refers to a saved opt-out for 'feedback and diagnostic upload', so it appears to be on unless disabled; what it sends is undocumented. A local session event log is kept by default (--no-session-log disables it); voice input is on by default on macOS; four background observer agents make extra model calls by default. By default Muse Code also loads skills from ~/.claude/skills and $CODEX_HOME/skills (or ~/.codex/skills) and from repo-local .claude/.codex skill folders, so other agents' skill files can enter the context sent to Meta; a user preference can disable the personal foreign skill roots. Client guardrails are on by default: approvals (default Auto-review profile, where an automated judge clears eligible requests), OS sandbox, proxy-only network with per-destination approval, workspace-scoped writes.
proposed_changes.new: The no-train label applies to the personal-data route in tier_gate (organisation API key on a pinned Standard model); a Muse Code subscription on default settings runs in Contributor (training) mode. Standard models (Muse Spark 1.1/1.2/1.3, Muse Wonder, Muse Wonder Full): Meta acts as processor under the Meta Global Processor Terms and does not train on Content. Contributor models (muse-spark-1.2/1.3-contributor) permit training, and the ToS forbids sending personal, sensitive or confidential data (including confidential code) to them. A Muse Code subscription counts as Contributor by default whatever model is selected (ToS 3.3); switching to Standard applies prospectively only. Contributor mode is now a Muse Code setting (/settings > Model > Contributor mode), saved per computer and switched on by the first interactive session on each new computer; --contributor-mode on|off or MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE overrides it per run, and a headless run with an existing settings file but no saved value can run in Contributor mode. In Contributor mode requests are routed to the -contributor model variant. Changelog 1.4.8 says turning the setting off 'now fully opts out, including background requests', so earlier builds did not fully opt out. The setting is hidden, and Contributor mode stays off, on pay-as-you-go, on ZDR accounts and where an organisation's managed configuration controls it. On every tier Meta may retain and process Content for policy enforcement and to develop safety and security systems, and the Data Commitments page also lists improving and maintaining the Model API. Without ZDR, Content and Usage Data (tool-call sequences, logs, telemetry) are retained 'as needed' with no stated period, and Usage Data may be used to develop and improve Meta products. The Data Commitments page says Content can be viewed and deleted through the account.
