retained_reviews.appraisal: Ante is still actively maintained, with ten releases from v0.2.10 to v0.3.3 (2026-11-05), and its core still ships only as a closed preview binary under unchanged terms. Two changes matter for researchers. The v0.3.3 changelog states that published builds send telemetry through the Ante telemetry gateway, so official binaries export metrics and unscrubbed logs by default unless ANTE_TELEMETRY=off is set. Since v0.3.0, Antix (which records request and response bodies) is the first auto-detected provider. The special-data route stays config-required and local-only, with controls tightened to pin the local provider, clear stored cloud credentials and exclude remote MCP servers.

proposed_changes.old: When an OTLP endpoint is set at runtime or embedded in the binary at build time, Ante exports metrics and application logs. The docs do not say whether official release binaries embed an endpoint, so treat them as possibly exporting by default. Exported log bodies are not scrubbed and may contain paths or tool arguments. ANTE_TELEMETRY=off disables export. Local logs, sessions (including copies kept on rewind) and auto-memory persist under ~/.ante; background Bash job output stays under ~/.ante/run/jobs/ for 24 hours after the job ends. Since v0.2.0, WebFetch spill files and staging downloads sit in the OS cache and temp directories, outside ~/.ante. Local GGUF inference keeps model traffic on the machine. With cloud presets, the provider's terms govern. The optional Antix proxy records request and response bodies on every call; Antigma states this traffic is not used to train its models, and the upstream model provider's policy still applies.
proposed_changes.new: Published builds send telemetry by default: since v0.3.3 (2026-11-05) the changelog states they export through the Ante telemetry gateway. The export covers metrics and application logs; log bodies are not scrubbed and may contain home paths or tool arguments. Exports carry no username or hostname, but do carry a random installation id stored in ~/.ante/installation-id. ANTE_TELEMETRY=off disables export. Since v0.3.0, Antix is first in provider auto-detection, and Ante starts on Antix when nothing is authenticated. Stored API keys and sign-ins sit under ~/.ante/auth/credentials/. Local logs, sessions (including copies kept on rewind) and auto-memory persist under ~/.ante; session saving and auto-memory can be switched off. Background Bash job output stays under ~/.ante/run/jobs/ for 24 hours after the job ends. WebFetch spill files and staging downloads sit in the OS cache and temp directories, outside ~/.ante. Local GGUF inference keeps model traffic on the machine. With cloud presets, the provider's terms govern. The optional Antix proxy records request and response bodies on every call; Antigma states this traffic is not used to train its models, and the upstream model provider's policy still applies.
proposed_changes.why: The v0.3.3 changelog (2026-11-05) states published builds send telemetry through the Ante telemetry gateway, which settles the October open question: official binaries export by default. v0.3.0 made Antix first in provider auto-detection and the fallback when nothing is authenticated. Added the credential store, the anonymous-identity details (random installation id) and the session_save/auto-memory switches.

adversarial_field_verdicts.correct_value: The v0.3.3 changelog (2026-11-05) states that published builds send telemetry through the Ante telemetry gateway, so official binaries export by default; utility commands send no telemetry. The export covers metrics and application logs; log bodies are not scrubbed and may contain home paths or tool arguments. Exports carry no username or hostname, but do carry a random installation id stored in ~/.ante/installation-id. ANTE_TELEMETRY=off disables export. Since v0.3.0, Antix is first in provider auto-detection, and Ante starts on Antix when nothing is authenticated. Stored API keys and sign-ins sit under ~/.ante/auth/credentials/. Local logs, sessions (including copies kept on rewind), TUI prompt history and auto-memory persist under ~/.ante; session saving and auto-memory can be switched off. Background Bash job output stays under ~/.ante/run/jobs/ for 24 hours after the job ends. WebFetch spill files and staging downloads sit in the OS cache and temp directories, outside ~/.ante. Local GGUF inference keeps model traffic on the machine. With cloud presets, the provider's terms govern. The optional Antix proxy records request and response bodies on every call; Antigma states this traffic is not used to train its models, and the upstream model provider's policy still applies.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Nanocoder released v1.32.0 on 2026-11-04 and remains active, MIT-licensed and free, so the local-only special-data route stands. The automatic npm version check can now be switched off (NANOCODER_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1), and both security bugs cited in October (ACP file_op auto-accept, fetch_url DNS SSRF) are closed. The release also adds new egress paths a research IT team must control: a released headless browser tool, voice mode with opt-in OpenAI cloud speech, a CI daemon that can post to GitHub, and per-session MCP servers injected by ACP editors. The directory-trust fingerprint now covers project provider baseUrls but not disabledTools or modeProviders, so per-directory config checks remain necessary.

required_controls: Point Qwen Code only at an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio) on the workstation or on institution-owned hardware inside the institutional network, configured via modelProviders; no commercial cloud provider or Alibaba Model Studio entry or key in the configuration.

Pin every model role to that endpoint: set model.name to a local model, leave fastModel, advisorModel, visionModel and compactionModel empty (they then use the main model or, for vision, a same-provider model) or set them only to local models, leave imageModel empty, and do not configure subagents to use any other model. The settings docs state that advisorModel and visionModel send conversation content to the named model even when it uses another provider.
Keep cloud provider API keys out of the shell environment, .env files (Qwen Code auto-loads the first .env file it finds) and the env field of settings.json.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Disable usage statistics in two places: privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false in the system settings file and QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED=false in the system-wide environment (default is enabled; events go to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; the environment variable takes precedence over the setting, so a stray value of true re-enables collection).
Keep OpenTelemetry off (default) or export only to an institution-controlled collector with logPrompts=false.

Block the built-in web_fetch tool with a permissions.deny rule or tools.disabled (it is registered by default and only asks for confirmation in default approval mode); keep web search off; do not enable Browser Use, Channels, Mem0 or remote MCP servers for these sessions.
Keep artifact publishing at its default local mode (artifact.publisher=local); the source code also offers 'host' (user upload command) and 'oss' (Alibaba Cloud OSS upload) modes.

Set general.enableAutoUpdate=false (default true: update checks and installations on startup) and manage upgrades centrally; set QWEN_CODE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH=off in the shell environment to stop the daily models.dev download. On air-gapped hosts, install from a verified release archive (--archive with SHA256SUMS).

Enforce these settings in the system settings file (Linux /etc/qwen-code/settings.json, Windows C:\ProgramData\qwen-code\settings.json, macOS /Library/Application Support/QwenCode/settings.json), which overrides user and project settings. Before sensitive sessions, check the effective configuration: a project .qwen/settings.json overrides user settings, environment variables (including those loaded from .env files) override all settings files, and QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH can redirect the system file.

Block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the model endpoint and verify the block before processing special-category data; on Linux, tools.executionSandbox with network "closed" can additionally confine tool commands.
residual_risks: Prompts and file contents go to whichever endpoint is configured; adding a cloud provider, switching models with /model or pointing a side-model setting (fastModel, advisorModel, visionModel, compactionModel) at another provider sends data off-host.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost baseUrl alone does not show that inference stays local.
Usage statistics default to on and include the configured base URL; a missed setting discloses endpoint metadata to Alibaba Cloud.
web_fetch is available by default and auto-approval modes can approve it without a prompt, so a missing deny rule lets the model fetch external URLs.
Browser Use operates in the signed-in Chrome profile and can capture page text, screenshots and cookies.
Local sessions, logs, memory and tool outputs under ~/.qwen require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Fast release cadence: defaults and integrations change often, so settings need re-checking after each upgrade.

Pin every model role to that endpoint: set model.name to a local model, leave fastModel, advisorModel, visionModel and compactionModel empty (they then use the main model) or set them only to local models, leave imageModel empty, keep agents.builtin.exploreModel at inherit, and do not configure subagents to use any other model. Keep cloud provider API keys out of the shell environment, .env files (Qwen Code auto-loads the first .env file it finds) and the env field of settings.json.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the server config of the account that runs it), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.

Disable usage statistics in two places: privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled=false in the system settings file and QWEN_USAGE_STATISTICS_ENABLED=false in the system-wide environment (default is enabled for every authentication method; events go to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint; the environment variable takes precedence, and a trusted project's .qwen/settings.json can otherwise switch it back on).
Keep OpenTelemetry off (default) or export only to an institution-controlled collector with logPrompts=false.

Block the built-in web_fetch tool with a permissions.deny rule or tools.disabled; keep web search off; do not enable Browser Use, Computer Use (node-repl MCP server), Channels, Mem0 or remote MCP servers for these sessions.
Keep artifact publishing at its default local mode (artifact.publisher=local); the source code also offers 'host' (user upload command) and 'oss' (Alibaba Cloud OSS upload) modes.

Set general.enableAutoUpdate=false (default true: update checks and installations on startup) and manage upgrades centrally; set model.catalogRefresh=false in the system settings file or QWEN_CODE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH=off in the shell environment to stop the daily models.dev download. Do not use the experimental Managed Agent mode (qwen serve --managed), which downloads a server JAR on first launch. On air-gapped hosts, install from a verified release archive (--archive with SHA256SUMS).

Enforce these settings in the system settings file (Linux /etc/qwen-code/settings.json, Windows C:\ProgramData\qwen-code\settings.json, macOS /Library/Application Support/QwenCode/settings.json), which overrides user and project settings. Before sensitive sessions, check the effective configuration: a project .qwen/settings.json overrides user settings, environment variables (including those loaded from .env files) override all settings files, and QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH can redirect the system file.

Block outbound traffic at host or network level except to the model endpoint and verify the block before processing special-category data; on Linux, tools.executionSandbox with network "closed" can additionally confine tool commands.
residual_risks: Prompts and file contents go to whichever endpoint is configured; adding a cloud provider, signing in with a Qwen account, switching models with /model or pointing a side-model setting (fastModel, advisorModel, visionModel, compactionModel) at another provider sends data off-host.
With cloud features on, a signed-in Ollama server can serve ':cloud' models through the same localhost endpoint, so a localhost baseUrl alone does not show that inference stays local.
Usage statistics default to on and include the configured base URL; a missed setting discloses endpoint metadata to Alibaba Cloud.
web_fetch is available by default and auto-approval modes can approve it without a prompt, so a missing deny rule lets the model fetch external URLs.
Browser Use operates in the signed-in Chrome profile and can capture page text, screenshots and cookies; Computer Use can capture desktop window screenshots and accessibility text.
Local sessions, logs, memory and tool outputs under ~/.qwen require institutional access, retention and egress controls.
Fast release cadence (nine stable releases in four weeks): defaults and integrations change often, so settings need re-checking after each upgrade.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Factory has redefined Factory Private: Factory still hosts the control plane by default, and only Droid sandboxes run in the customer VPC through the new OpenCompute orchestrator (private preview). The docs now tie the airgap build to Custom Deployments and no longer describe a customer-operated hybrid pattern, so for special-category research data the only documented customer-controlled route is a sales-gated airgap Custom Deployment. The legal side got stronger for personal data: the DPA (2 Nov 2026) now covers individuals inside code and prompts and bars training and product improvement, and the organisation terms (27 Oct 2026) bar training without consent. The rewritten privacy policy no longer states a storage region or retention cap, and the public BAA template is gone. Ratings are unchanged.

proposed_changes.old: cloud-managed (Factory-operated control plane in the US, or in a Factory-operated EEA region on Enterprise; Droid runs on local or customer machines, CI or Factory-hosted Droid Computers) / enterprise customer-operated hybrid or fully air-gapped build / Factory Private: control plane in customer VPC or on-premises, air-gapped configurations available (private preview)
proposed_changes.new: Factory Managed: Factory-hosted control plane (US, or a Factory-operated EU deployment on Enterprise); Droid runs on local machines, CI/CD, machines connected through Remote Control, or Factory-hosted Droid Computers / Factory Private (private preview): Factory-hosted control plane by default, with Droid sandboxes in the customer's VPC or data centre through the self-hosted OpenCompute orchestrator (private preview); a customer-hosted control plane only by arrangement / Custom Deployment: all of Factory inside the customer network with the sales-gated airgap build

Airgap builds are now tied to Custom Deployments, and the docs no longer describe a separate 'hybrid' pattern.

proposed_changes.old: Factory states customer code is not used as training data. Individual terms (14 Jul 2026) let Factory use Customer Data internally to provide the service and to generate aggregated de-identified data, which it may freely use and retain for business purposes including improving its products. Product-level retention: CLI sessions are mirrored to Factory cloud by default (cloudSessionSync true; users can switch it off, org admins can pin it); forked sessions and AutoWiki content (wikiCloudSync, on by default) also sync to Factory cloud. Orgs can turn on auto-deletion of synced sessions after 14-365 days (sessionRetentionDays); no default deletion period is published. Factory-hosted operational logs follow Trust Center terms, which are not publicly readable. Personal data (privacy policy, 20 Aug 2026) is primarily stored on AWS US West and deleted no later than 10 years after last use unless contracted otherwise. ZDR is listed for Business and above; its scope relative to session sync is a contract question. Mythos-class Anthropic models (Claude Fable 5/5.1) carry 30-day trust-and-safety retention where org admins opt in. Telemetry: in connected deployments OTEL metrics (with user, session and repo attributes unless aggregate granularity is pinned) also go to Factory's collector; message-content spans are off by default and go only to a customer collector. Airgap builds send no runtime data to Factory.
proposed_changes.new: Factory states customer code is not used as training data. Organisation SaaS Product Terms (27 Oct 2026) bar using Customer Data to develop or train AI models without prior consent; the DPA (2 Nov 2026) bars processing for model training or product improvement and requires return or deletion within 60 days after termination, apart from encrypted backup archives. old.personal: Use a Business/Enterprise contract with the DPA (EU SCCs; EU-region deployment for residency on Enterprise), and confirm its annex covers the research data subjects and data categories: the public annex lists only customers' end-users, staff and contractors, with contact and service-generated data. Switch off cloud session sync and AutoWiki cloud sync, or turn on a short sessionRetentionDays; restrict models to ZDR-covered endpoints and avoid opt-in Mythos-class retention; keep message-content telemetry off or on an institutional collector. Inference-layer ZDR alone is insufficient.
old.special: Qualifying routes are the sales-gated enterprise airgap build, or a hybrid deployment with in-network models and collectors and cloud sync off; in connected (non-airgap) builds, OTEL metrics still reach Factory's collector. Factory Private (customer VPC/on-prem; announced 18 Sep 2026, private preview, no docs page) may qualify only once documentation or the contract places the control plane, inference and collectors inside institution-controlled infrastructure. Factory states Airgap Mode is cooperative, so isolation must come from institutional network controls. retained_reviews.appraisal: Training, retention, ZDR and self-hosted boundary statements are unchanged, so the classification stays no-train with nonsensitive ok, personal cfg, special cfg. Three things changed since October: GitLab's sub-processor list now names LangChain, Inc. for AI logging (scope undocumented), so personal-data users should ask what it receives; GitLab Dedicated for Government now authorizes Agentic Chat and foundational agents; and the docs now say flow isolation holds only when the SRT sandbox actually runs, with silent fallback otherwise. For special-category data, the institution must therefore block runner egress itself (or, from 19.6, require the sandbox).

proposed_changes.old: GitLab.com (SaaS); GitLab Dedicated (vendor-operated single-tenant SaaS); Self-Managed (customer-operated) with GitLab-managed, hybrid or fully self-hosted AI Gateway and models, including offline licences. Not available on GitLab Dedicated for Government.
proposed_changes.new: GitLab.com (SaaS); GitLab Dedicated (vendor-operated single-tenant SaaS); Self-Managed (customer-operated) with GitLab-managed, hybrid or fully self-hosted AI Gateway and models, including offline licences. GitLab Dedicated for Government (US public sector, self-hosted AI architecture only) now authorizes Agentic Chat and foundational agents per capability; flows and external agents are not authorized there.
proposed_changes.why: Dedicated for Government page changed after the October review (mirror commits 2026-10-19/22): Agent Platform moved from 'not available' to per-capability authorization of Agentic Chat and foundational agents; flows and external agents remain unauthorized.

proposed_changes.old: GitLab does not train generative AI models; AI model sub-processors are barred from training on input/output. Product retention: chat and workflow history (chats user-deletable), also kept on GitLab.com for anti-abuse; expanded logging keeps traces; opt-in usage-data collection logs full prompts, responses and tool calls (with a self-hosted gateway these logs stay on customer infrastructure). GitLab documents a ZDR policy only with Fireworks AI, and it does not hold when prompt caching is on, which is the default (vendor holds prompts temporarily in memory; cannot be turned off for OpenAI models). Certain Anthropic and OpenAI models have limited vendor-side retention. Prompt-injection scanning via HiddenLayer runs on GitLab's AI Gateway and defaults to Log only on GitLab.com; 'No checks' sends no prompt data to third parties. Telemetry: aggregated or de-identified Snowplow usage metrics. A self-hosted AI Gateway keeps code, prompts and responses in the customer network; online licences still send billing metadata to GitLab, offline licences do not connect.
proposed_changes.new: GitLab does not train generative AI models; AI model sub-processors are barred from training on input/output. Product retention: chat and workflow history (chats user-deletable), also kept on GitLab.com for anti-abuse; expanded logging keeps traces; opt-in usage-data collection logs full prompts, responses and tool calls (with a self-hosted gateway these logs stay on customer infrastructure); AI audit event storage (beta, off by default) records agent sessions, which can include prompts and responses. GitLab documents a ZDR policy only with Fireworks AI, and it does not hold when prompt caching is on, which is the default (vendor holds prompts temporarily in memory; cannot be turned off for OpenAI models). Certain Anthropic and OpenAI models have limited vendor-side retention. Prompt-injection scanning via HiddenLayer runs on GitLab's AI Gateway and defaults to Log only on GitLab.com; 'No checks' sends no prompt data to third parties. Since October GitLab's sub-processor list adds LangChain, Inc. for 'Logging for AI-Powered Product Features' (GitLab.com, Dedicated, Self-Managed); what it logs and how to switch it off is not documented. Telemetry: aggregated or de-identified Snowplow usage metrics. A self-hosted AI Gateway keeps code, prompts and responses in the customer network; online licences still send billing metadata to GitLab, offline licences do not connect.
proposed_changes.why: Added LangChain, Inc. (AI logging sub-processor; absent from the 2026-10-11 archived list, present on 2026-11-06) and the AI audit event storage setting (off by default; stores agent session data). Training, retention, ZDR and caching statements re-read unchanged.

correct_value: Self-Managed Premium/Ultimate with a fully self-hosted AI Gateway on institution infrastructure; every model endpoint it calls is served on institution-controlled hardware inside the network (same host or separate inference servers, e.g. vLLM); no hybrid GitLab-managed features, no Bedrock/Azure OpenAI or other external model endpoints.

Runner hosts for flows restrict outbound traffic at the network level (firewall or Kubernetes NetworkPolicy) to the institution's GitLab instance and self-hosted AI Gateway; from GitLab 19.6, also require the execution-environment sandbox (needs privileged runner mode and a working SRT in the image) so flows fail instead of running unsandboxed.

adversarial_field_verdicts.why: The new control is well founded. The sandbox page says that without SRT the flow runs unsandboxed and network-policy settings do not apply. It recommends a runner-host firewall or a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, and documents the 19.6 require-sandbox setting for Self-Managed. Three corrections. (1) 'Block outbound traffic' is too absolute: flows must still reach the GitLab instance and the Duo Workflow Service, which are always on the sandbox allow-list. The control should be an egress allow-list. (2) The sandbox prerequisites state 'Privileged runner mode enabled. It is required for sandboxing to function', so requiring the sandbox means running privileged runners. Institutions must know this trade-off. (3) Dedicated for Government is now described as using the 'Duo Self-Hosted architecture'. Naming it in the not-acceptable list prevents it being misread as customer-controlled; it is vendor-operated. status config-required, boundary customer-controlled and inference local-only stay valid.
adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: To limit what these jobs can reach, restrict outbound network traffic where the jobs run. For example, use a firewall on the runner host or a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy

adversarial_field_verdicts.why: The new residual risk matches the sandbox page word for word in substance. adversarial_field_verdicts.excerpt: If a project uses a custom image or a setup_script , the project controls which srt command runs, so the requirement cannot guarantee isolation for flows in that project.

Portal's 'dedicated deployment in your own cloud account' does not apply to the notebook agent, so suitability stays ok/no/no. retained_reviews.appraisal: The project changed character since October (about 580 commits since 2026-10-10, GitHub releases v0.3.0 to v0.7.0, PyPI package automated-data-analyst 0.7.0). It is now a local Python package, command line, MCP server and Claude Code/Codex skill that computes and checks numbers from CSV/Excel deterministically, with `ada chat` driving a local open-weight model (Ollama by default) as the caller; on 2026-11-01 the Streamlit browser app, the optional OpenAI layer and the research/modelling workflow moved to a separate repository, ADA Lab, which also serves the public demo. For researchers this makes the qualifying route cleaner (no Streamlit, no OpenAI code in the package; only `ada chat` to a configured model server and an opt-in localhost MCP listener make network contact), but a new leak path appears: when ADA runs as a tool inside a cloud assistant or MCP host, its results, which can name data values, reach that host's model. Classification is unchanged (local, special = config-required); the record now describes the package and treats ADA Lab as a companion with its own controls. Editorial note for the maintainer: ADA is now partly a tool for other agents; scope still fits a data agent through `ada chat`, but this is worth a glance.

A new security page states that customer data never trains any model, which moves data_handling from unknown to no-train; retention, ZDR and managed model-provider terms are still undocumented, and the statement is not contractual. The special-category route is unchanged (cfg via Enterprise Self-Managed with an institution-operated gateway to institution-hosted models). Researchers should note the finance repositioning and the new external channels (Slack, Telegram, X) on superagents.

proposed_changes.old: The Terms of Service (effective 9 Jan 2026) let Zerve use Customer Data only as needed to provide, operate and maintain the product. Product improvement may use statistical data derived from use of the product, but not Customer Data itself. No AI-specific training, prompt-retention or ZDR statement was found, and training and retention by the managed model providers are undocumented, so data handling stays unknown. The privacy policy (effective 22 Jan 2024) says the Services are hosted in the US and that personal data is kept while the account is open. It names analytics subprocessors and lists OpenAI and Exafunction (Codeium) as AI subprocessors; Anthropic, a model provider named in the product docs, is not listed. The Terms reserve Zerve's right to keep residual copies of Customer Data for backup purposes. BYOC keeps execution and storage in the customer cloud but uses the Zerve-hosted control plane (the AWS BYOC doc places it in eu-west-1). Hosting location is inconsistent across first-party sources: the 2024 privacy policy says the Services are hosted in the US; the AWS BYOC doc puts the control plane in eu-west-1. retained_reviews.appraisal: No rename, licence change, paid plan or privacy policy since October; Juggler shipped v0.7.7-v0.7.9 and is rewriting its network stack to one server per machine on the develop branch. v0.7.9 removed the cdnjs.cloudflare.com script, closing one default egress path, while v0.7.8 added an optional hosted decision model (Jev/TypeSafe) for Auto-approve and v0.7.7 a reverse-proxy option. The updated SECURITY.md now states that any account on the machine can drive the agent and that an approved agent command can switch on LAN or tunnel exposure, so researchers should use a single-user machine or VM. Classification is unchanged (special = cfg, local inference only), with controls updated for the decision model, LAN/WAN-on-launch settings and the minimum version.

proposed_changes.why: Material changes: cdnjs script dropped (v0.7.9), new hosted decision-model provider (Jev/TypeSafe, v0.7.8), reverse-proxy and persisted LAN/WAN-on-launch options, and a documented cross-account and agent-widens-exposure risk in the develop SECURITY.md.

proposed_changes.old: Per the README, no Juggler service sits in the model path: prompts, code and keys go straight to the chosen provider, and Juggler keeps copies only on local disk. Project state (conversations, session, bash output) is written to <project>/.juggler/, API keys to ~/.juggler/credentials.json (0600), and logs to the platform log directory (10 MB x 5 rotation, 14-day sweep, configurable). Default-on outbound traffic besides the model provider: with Updates on Automatic (the default) the server polls juggler.studio at start and every 6 h, sending version, OS and architecture plus a first-of-day/month mark used to count installs, source builds included (Updates can be set to Off, but a manual 'Check for updates' still contacts juggler.studio; official macOS desktop builds also auto-download found updates); the web UI loads a diff script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com on each page load; and the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch tools run without approval in the Default and Read-only strategies unless disabled. No privacy policy or telemetry statement was found. Hosted backends, background 'cheap model' jobs, ACP agents, MCP servers, extensions and the official binaries' WAN modes each add separate boundaries.
proposed_changes.new: Per the README, no Juggler service sits in the model path: prompts, code and keys go straight to the chosen provider, and Juggler keeps copies only on local disk. Project state (conversations, session, bash output, per-project env files) is written to <project>/.juggler/, API keys to ~/.juggler/credentials.json (0600), and logs to the platform log directory (10 MB x 5 rotation, 14-day sweep, configurable). Default-on outbound traffic besides the model provider: with Updates on Automatic (the default) the server polls juggler.studio at start and every 6 h, sending version, OS, architecture, any package manager that installed it, and a first-of-day/month mark used to count installs, source builds included (Settings > Updates discloses all but the install mark; Updates can be set to Off, but a manual 'Check for updates' still contacts juggler.studio; official macOS and Windows builds also download found updates in the background); and the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch tools run without approval in the Default and Read-only strategies unless disabled. Up to v0.7.8 the web UI also loaded a diff script from cdnjs.cloudflare.com; v0.7.9 (28 Oct 2026) removed it. All of Juggler's own connections follow one outbound-proxy setting (System, Direct or Manual); loopback always goes direct. No privacy policy or telemetry statement was found. Hosted backends, background 'cheap model' and decision-model jobs (Jev is hosted), ACP agents, MCP servers, extensions and the official binaries' WAN modes each add separate boundaries.

old: Run a reviewed source build on researcher- or institution-controlled hardware (an official binary only with Updates Off, accepting its unauditable private components), with inference only through local runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI) under the same control.

If Ollama serves the model, run it in local-only mode (OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in the config of the account that runs the server), confirm the server log reports cloud disabled, and serve no :cloud models.
Point the background 'cheap model' (tab naming, reply suggestions, auto-approve reviewer, extension text generation) at the same local model, or switch it off.
Store no hosted-provider credentials (Settings or ~/.juggler/credentials.json) and keep cloud API keys out of the environment, so no model role can reach a hosted provider.

Keep the default loopback-only access; never enable the passwordless LAN mode (p or --public) on shared networks (over HTTPS, LAN mode also uses Google's public STUN server for WebRTC); in Docker, where --public is used, publish the port only to localhost or an isolated network; do not use the official binaries' WAN modes.

Set Settings > Updates to Off (default Automatic polls juggler.studio at start and every 6 h with version, OS, architecture and an install-count mark; official macOS desktop builds also auto-download updates) or block that egress, and confirm with egress monitoring after each upgrade. With Updates Off, a manual 'Check for updates' still contacts juggler.studio (without the install mark), so do not use it where that egress is not accepted.

Disable the built-in Web Search (DuckDuckGo) and Web Fetch capabilities in Settings > Extensions for every project (stored as plugins.disabled in <project>/.juggler/config.json), or deny the WebSearch and WebFetch tools globally with a beforeTool hook in ~/.juggler/hooks; both run without approval in the Default and Read-only strategies.
Block or explicitly accept outbound requests to cdnjs.cloudflare.com: the web UI loads diff_match_patch from it on each page load (allowed by the CSP, no integrity attribute).

Use the Default or Read-only strategy so writes and shell commands need manual approval; do not use YOLO, the Auto-approve reviewer, or `juggler run` without an explicit --strategy (it defaults to yolo); do not use ACP agents (they bypass Juggler's strategies and their permission requests are auto-allowed by default); keep the Exa extension (ships disabled) and remote MCP servers off; install only reviewed extensions.

Before each sensitive session, check the effective settings of the project in use (providers, cheap model, strategy, disabled tools); the web-tool disable list is stored per project, so a new project starts with the web tools enabled unless the global beforeTool hook denies them.

Block outbound network traffic at host or network level, allowing only the local model runtime and any host explicitly accepted under these controls, and verify that the block holds; shell commands and extensions run with the user's privileges, so in-app settings alone do not stop egress.

Apply institutional access, retention and backup controls to <project>/.juggler/, ~/.juggler/credentials.json and the platform log directory, and keep .juggler/ out of shared repositories and sync folders.
new: Run a reviewed source build (v0.7.9 or later) on a single-user, researcher- or institution-controlled machine or a dedicated VM/container (an official binary only with Updates Off, accepting its unauditable private components), with inference only through local runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or LocalAI) under the same control.

Store no hosted-provider credentials (Settings, ~/.juggler/credentials.json) and keep cloud API keys out of the environment Juggler starts in (it reads provider keys such as TYPESAFE_API_KEY from it), so no model role can reach a hosted provider.

Keep the default loopback-only access: never enable LAN access (p or --public up to v0.7.9; Start LAN access, `juggler server lan on` or `juggler serve --lan` on the develop branch) on shared networks, leave 'Start whenever Juggler starts' (connectivity.lanOnLaunch) and connectivity.wanOnLaunch unset, add no --allow-host names or reverse proxies, and do not use the official binaries' WAN modes (Direct P2P, Cloudflare Tunnel; WebRTC peer links default to Google's public STUN server). The Docker image starts with LAN access on, so publish its port only to localhost or an isolated network.

Block outbound network traffic at host or network level, allowing only the local model runtime and any host explicitly accepted under these controls, and verify that the block holds; shell commands and extensions run with the user's privileges, so in-app settings alone do not stop egress.

Apply institutional access, retention and backup controls to <project>/.juggler/ (including per-project env files), ~/.juggler/ (credentials.json, env.json, server.json) and the platform log directory, and keep .juggler/ out of shared repositories and sync folders.

proposed_changes.old: Configuration, sessions, logs, memory, scheduler state and caches stay on the user's machine. Prompts, tool results and selected files go to the configured provider. Per the policy, web search, channels, browser automation and other integrations contact external services when enabled. Since v0.5.5 (2026-09-23), one default-on Network reporting switch with no consent prompt covers V1 install and daily turn/token counts plus V2 reliability diagnostics and product/growth analytics. V2 events carry a hashed OS-machine-ID device token; V1 events carry a hashed MAC/IP-derived install ID. The policy excludes prompts, file contents and paths from these uploads; servers can see the source IP. OPENSQUILLA_PRIVACY_DISABLE_NETWORK_OBSERVABILITY=true stops all statistics uploads and update checks but does not erase queued events. The retention period and controller of the telemetry server are not documented. The install-ID provider header is retired, but the code still attaches session, turn and execution correlation IDs to TokenRhythm Studio requests unless that variable is set. TokenRhythm Studio's privacy policy (version dated 2026-09-03) allows de-identified training on calls to its own models and processes those calls in China. It forwards other calls to third-party model vendors, and the account keeps call logs and conversation records.
proposed_changes.new: Configuration, sessions, logs, memory, scheduler state and caches stay on the user's machine. Prompts, tool results and selected files go to the configured provider. Per the policy, web search, channels, browser automation and other integrations contact external services when enabled. V2 events carry a hashed OS-machine-ID device token; V1 events carry a hashed MAC/IP-derived install ID. The policy excludes prompts, file contents and paths from these uploads; servers can see the source IP. OPENSQUILLA_PRIVACY_DISABLE_NETWORK_OBSERVABILITY=true stops all statistics uploads and update checks but does not erase queued events. The retention period and controller of the telemetry server are not documented. Since v0.5.8, when OpenRouter or TokenRhythm is the primary provider, model recommendations are fetched from an Alibaba Cloud OSS (Beijing) bucket at each Gateway start and every 24 hours unless the same switch is set. The install-ID provider header is retired, but the code still attaches session, turn, execution and call-kind correlation IDs to TokenRhythm Studio requests unless the environment variable is set. TokenRhythm Studio's user agreement (updated 2026-10-12) says platform-key calls are relayed to third-party models, inputs and outputs are recorded, and de-identified data may be used for model optimisation unless the user opts out by contacting the company; BYOK calls through Studio are not stored long-term or used for training. Its privacy policy (updated 2026-09-28) stores personal information collected in China in China; no retention period is stated.
proposed_changes.why: TokenRhythm Studio terms changed after the October review: the user agreement (updated 2026-10-12, effective 2026-10-13) applies de-identified optimisation to all platform-key calls with an opt-out by contact, and records inputs/outputs; the privacy policy now carries update date 2026-09-28 (not 2026-09-03). v0.5.8 adds background recommendation fetches from an Alibaba OSS Beijing bucket gated by the privacy switch. Correlation headers now also include call kind and check only the environment variable.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Pi remains an actively maintained MIT terminal agent (1.2.0 to 1.5.0 between 12 Oct and 2 Nov 2026) with unchanged telemetry defaults, offline mode and local llama.cpp/models.json routes, so the local-only special-category route still holds. Changes are around the edges: provider attribution headers now target OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM and OpenCode; /share gained a sessionShareDestination setting; Radius login also installs the Radius MCP server. Radius terms and privacy policy were re-dated 2 November 2026: still not a DPA, now explicitly forbid special-category data, state no Radius-side retention or training, and route inference through OpenRouter with per-model provider retention. Ratings ok/cfg/cfg unchanged.

proposed_changes.old: Local JSONL sessions persist under ~/.pi/agent/sessions by default; --no-session disables persistence. Install/update telemetry (a ping to pi.dev carrying version, OS, runtime and architecture in the User-Agent, plus provider attribution headers for OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM and Cloudflare) is on by default; analytics defaults off. Set enableInstallTelemetry false or PI_TELEMETRY=0; the telemetry setting does not control the pi.dev version check. --offline or PI_OFFLINE=1 stops automatic network activity (version check, pi.dev model-catalog refresh, package update checks, telemetry, /bug upload), not model, tool or MCP traffic. /share uploads a session to an organization-visible Radius artifact when Radius sign-in is configured, otherwise to a secret GitHub gist that anyone with the link can view; /bug can upload a report to radius.pi.dev. Built-in MCP client, extensions and tools can add external traffic. Provider terms govern cloud inference.
proposed_changes.new: Local JSONL sessions persist under ~/.pi/agent/sessions by default; --no-session disables persistence. Install/update telemetry (a ping to pi.dev carrying version, OS, runtime and architecture in the User-Agent) and provider attribution headers for OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM and OpenCode are on by default; analytics defaults off. Set enableInstallTelemetry false or PI_TELEMETRY=0; this setting does not control the pi.dev version check or the detailed User-Agent sent to model endpoints. --offline or PI_OFFLINE=1 stops automatic network activity (version check, pi.dev model-catalog refresh, package update checks, telemetry, /bug upload), not model, tool or MCP traffic. /share uploads a session to an organization-visible Radius artifact when Radius sign-in is configured, otherwise to a secret GitHub gist that anyone with the link can view; the sessionShareDestination setting can force gist or radius. /bug can upload a report to radius.pi.dev without login. Signing in to Radius also adds the Radius MCP server. Built-in MCP client, extensions and tools can add external traffic. Provider terms govern cloud inference.

proposed_changes.old: Snowflake states that AI inputs and outputs, including Usage Data, are not used to train models made available to other customers. CoCo inputs are classified as Usage Data and outputs as Customer Data. On all three surfaces, CoCo writes every prompt and response trace to SNOWFLAKE.LOCAL.AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS in the customer account; rows cannot be modified, only an AI_OBSERVABILITY_ADMIN role can delete them, and no automatic expiry is stated. CLI and Desktop also keep full conversations (file content, tool output, SQL) under ~/.snowflake/cortex/conversations/. The CLI --private flag disables conversation persistence and server-side logging. Ratings and feedback comments go to Snowflake. CoCo requires cross-region inference: prompts and outputs go transiently to the processing region and are not persisted there. Routing is an account parameter (any region, one cloud, or a region group such as AWS_EU or AZURE_EU). The documented default differs between pages and by account age, so check the effective value. Retention at the cloud-provider model endpoints and for Snowsight chat history is not stated. By default, Cloud Agents sandboxes have read-only HTTPS egress to package registries; admins can disable non-Snowflake egress.
proposed_changes.new: Snowflake states that AI inputs and outputs, including Usage Data, are not used to train models made available to other customers. CoCo inputs are classified as Usage Data and outputs as Customer Data; Snowflake describes Usage Data as accessible to its operations personnel. On all three surfaces, CoCo writes every prompt and response trace to SNOWFLAKE.LOCAL.AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS in the customer account; rows cannot be modified, only an AI_OBSERVABILITY_ADMIN role can delete them, and no automatic expiry is stated. CLI, Desktop and automation runs also keep conversations as Cortex threads in the account, with no stated retention. CLI and Desktop keep full conversations (file content, tool output, SQL) under ~/.snowflake/cortex/conversations/; Desktop memory is stored under ~/.snowflake/cortex/memory/. The CLI --private flag disables conversation persistence and server-side logging. Ratings and feedback comments go to Snowflake as product feedback; per Snowflake, it receives the request ID and comment, not the prompt or response. Desktop Artifacts and Cloud automations (both Preview, Desktop v1.24.0, Nov 2026) publish agent-written files to the account and can email run reports. CoCo requires cross-region inference: prompts and outputs go transiently to the processing region and are not persisted there. Routing is an account parameter (any region, one cloud, or a region group such as AWS_EU or AZURE_EU). The documented default differs between pages and by account age, so check the effective value. Retention at the cloud-provider model endpoints and for Snowsight chat history is not stated, and client-side telemetry from CLI and Desktop is not described. By default, Cloud Agents sandboxes have read-only HTTPS egress to package registries; admins can disable non-Snowflake egress.

proposed_changes.old: Provider-dependent. Default mode supports four providers: GitHub Copilot; OpenAI- or LiteLLM-compatible endpoints, cloud or self-hosted (e.g. vLLM/TGI); and Ollama, local or on a host set through OLLAMA_HOST at server launch. Claude mode uses the Claude Code CLI for chat and the Anthropic API (or a configured Base URL) for inline chat and auto-complete. An experimental ACP mode, off by default, runs OpenAI Codex as its only agent type. Launcher tiles open the Claude Code, opencode, Pi, GitHub Copilot CLI or Codex CLIs in a terminal when they are installed.
proposed_changes.new: Provider-dependent. Default mode supports four providers: GitHub Copilot; OpenAI- or LiteLLM-compatible endpoints, cloud or self-hosted (e.g. vLLM/TGI); and Ollama, local or on a host set through OLLAMA_HOST at server launch. Claude mode uses the Claude Code CLI for chat and the Anthropic API (or a configured Base URL) for inline chat and auto-complete. An experimental ACP mode, off by default, runs OpenAI Codex as its only agent type; since v6.3.0 it needs an administrator-preinstalled codex-acp adapter and no longer downloads one from npm at startup. Launcher tiles open the Claude Code, opencode, Pi, GitHub Copilot CLI or Codex CLIs in a terminal when they are installed.
proposed_changes.why: v6.3.0 changelog/README/docs/acp.md: ACP launches a preinstalled codex-acp executable; NBI does not download an adapter at startup.

proposed_changes.old: NBI runs inside the user's Jupyter Server and has no central server of its own. It documents no external telemetry: its in-process usage events go nowhere unless an administrator registers a listener. retained_reviews.appraisal: No change to deployment model, training default, plans or suitability since October: SaaS remains no-train with in-memory payload handling and US East admin data, and the self-hosted air-gapped route is still the only special-category option. retained_reviews.appraisal: The CLI remains an actively maintained MIT project (2.5.2 released today) and its institution-endpoint route for regulated data is unchanged. The material change is on the managed route: Moonshot's 2026-11-05 policy update scopes the kimi.com policy (with its customer-service training opt-out) to mainland-China users, and the kimi.ai policy that now governs European researchers uses user content for model training with no stated opt-out, so data_handling moves from opt-out to trains. New remote environments let the agent operate on an SSH or Docker research server while model calls stay local, which helps HPC-style setups without changing the egress controls.

proposed_changes.why: The kimi.ai policy (updated 2026-11-05) governs users outside mainland China and uses user content for training and optimising AI models with no training-specific opt-out; the kimi.com policy whose customer-service opt-out supported 'opt-out' now applies only to mainland-China users.

proposed_changes.old: Default managed route: the kimi.com privacy policy (Beijing Moonshot, effective 2026-08-31, linked from the Kimi Code page) uses de-identified input/output to optimise models; users can opt out of training by contacting customer service; storage in the PRC. API-key route: the Kimi Open Platform policy (Moonshot AI Pte. Ltd., Singapore, last update 2025-04-30) lists training among uses with no training-specific opt-out stated; terms for platform.kimi.com keys were not assessed. Which policy governs global-region logins (kimi login --region global) is not established. No DPA found. CLI: anonymous telemetry on by default, with or without sign-in (telemetry=false or KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to disable); per source code it sends device ID, model, session ID, crash and API-error events with paths, emails, URLs and tokens scrubbed, to a Kimi collector (default mainland-cn region profile); the opt-out was ignored in print mode until 0.41.0 (2026-09-04). Auto-update on by default; signed-in users' web fetches use the managed Kimi fetch service unless an endpoint is set; /feedback can attach diagnostic logs and codebase context; Remote Control (paid membership, signed in) relays sessions through Kimi's relay. Sessions, logs and credentials are stored under ~/.kimi-code.
proposed_changes.new: Default managed route. Users outside mainland China fall under the kimi.ai privacy policy (NOVASCENT PRIVATE LIMITED, last updated 2026-11-05): user content (prompts, files, generated content) is processed to provide and improve the services, including training and optimising AI models, on legitimate-interest or consent grounds; no training-specific opt-out is described, and data may be stored on servers outside the user's country. The kimi.com policy (Beijing Moonshot; new version updated 2026-11-05, effective 2026-11-12) now states it applies only to users in mainland China; there, de-identified input/output is used to optimise models, training can be stopped by contacting customer service, and storage is in the PRC. API-key route: the Kimi Open Platform policy (Moonshot AI Pte. Ltd., Singapore, last update 2025-04-30) lists training among uses with no training-specific opt-out; platform terms were not assessed. No DPA found. CLI: anonymous telemetry on by default, with or without sign-in (telemetry=false or KIMI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to disable); per source code it sends device ID, model, session ID and crash/API-error events with paths, emails, URLs and tokens scrubbed, to a region-specific Kimi collector (telemetry-logs.kimi.com for the default mainland-cn profile, telemetry-logs.kimi.ai for global); the opt-out was ignored in print mode until 0.41.0 (2026-09-04). Auto-update on by default (KIMI_CODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 disables checks); signed-in users' web fetches use the managed Kimi fetch service unless an endpoint is set; /feedback can attach diagnostic logs and codebase context; Remote Control (paid membership, signed in) relays sessions through Kimi's relay. Sessions, logs and credentials are stored under ~/.kimi-code.
proposed_changes.why: Region scope of the two consumer policies now established; kimi.com policy new version (updated 2026-11-05, effective 2026-11-12); region-specific telemetry collectors per source; KIMI_CODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE documented.

retained_reviews.appraisal: Deep Agents Code remains active MIT software (0.2.5, 2026-11-05; Beta; now Python 3.14) and its classification is unchanged: local Ollama under a managed allowlist still gives a customer-controlled route for special-category data. Three data-flow changes since October matter: 0.2.2 stopped the bundled server uploading usage metadata to LangSmith (so pin >=0.2.2), 0.2.3 removed silent model auto-selection from cloud keys in the environment, and 0.2.3 preconfigures the official plugin marketplace. The LangGraph CLI analytics ping is still on by default and undocumented in dcode docs, and the providers docs lag the code on model selection.

proposed_changes.old: BYOK: no dcode-hosted inference service is documented, so provider terms govern inference. If no model is set, startup falls back to an OPENAI, ANTHROPIC or GOOGLE key found in the environment. It sends agent operations and tool calls to LangSmith. --no-tracing or DEEPAGENTS_CODE_LANGSMITH_TRACING=false disables it. Default-on network calls: a PyPI update check and auto-install at session start, and an hourly pricing-catalog refresh from raw.githubusercontent.com. Also, on each launch, langgraph-cli sends a usage ping (OS, OS version, Python and CLI version, command name, anonymised flags) to a Supabase endpoint unless LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1. The dcode docs do not mention this ping. Optional cloud services: Tavily web search, remote sandboxes, MCP servers. Sessions, history and credentials live under ~/.deepagents. retained_reviews.appraisal: Still active and MIT-licensed, but every one of its 37 releases is a pre-release, and the vendor still calls it an unaudited developer preview; the privacy policy is unchanged (20 Sept 2026). Two telemetry/egress points matter for researchers: Desktop product analytics are on by default with no user-facing switch (the October record wrongly said the default was unstated), and the 0.2.2 pre-releases send web-search queries plus up to 128 characters of the latest prompt to the DeepSeek Search API whenever a DeepSeek credential is present, even next to a self-hosted model. Suitability stays nonsensitive-only; special stays not-appropriate.

proposed_changes.old: DeepSeek API key (official model services); built-in third-party providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM) and custom OpenAI Chat Completions/Responses or Anthropic Messages endpoints, including company gateways and self-hosted servers.
proposed_changes.new: DeepSeek official model services via a DeepSeek API key or a signed-in DeepSeek account route; built-in third-party providers (e.g. Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM) and custom OpenAI Chat Completions/Responses or Anthropic Messages endpoints, including company gateways and self-hosted servers.
proposed_changes.why: First-party docs describe a separate signed-in DeepSeek account route (llm-deepseek-account) next to the API-key route; the October text listed only the API key.

proposed_changes.old: The Harness privacy policy (last update 2026-09-20) separates official model services from custom model services. On the official route DeepSeek collects session logs (inputs, uploaded files, model outputs, tool invocations, plugin configuration), uses personal data to train and improve its models, keeps input data for as long as the account exists, and stores data in the PRC; a training opt-out is listed only among rights that may be available depending on jurisdiction. With custom model services no login is needed and DeepSeek Harness does not store or process inputs/outputs server-side; the chosen provider's terms govern. Desktop analytics add available login identity and follow an application-owned collection switch with no user settings surface (default not stated); ordinary Web clients collect no product events; session telemetry defaults to feedback-only. Whether the Web UI's DeepSeek API-key route falls under this Harness policy or separate DeepSeek Open Platform terms was not checked; both send data to DeepSeek. The vendor labels the project an unaudited developer preview.
proposed_changes.new: The Harness privacy policy (last update 2026-09-20, unchanged on 2026-11-06) separates official model services from custom model services. On the official route DeepSeek collects session logs (inputs, uploaded files, model outputs, tool invocations, plugin configuration), uses personal data to train and improve its models, keeps input data for as long as the account exists, and stores data in the PRC; a training opt-out is listed only among rights that may be available depending on jurisdiction. With custom model services no login is needed and DeepSeek Harness does not store or process inputs/outputs server-side; the chosen provider's terms govern. Desktop product analytics are on by default (the `enabled` setting defaults to true) with no user-facing control; they carry available device and user IDs, app version and hardware/OS fields, and exclude prompts, responses and API keys; switching them off requires editing configuration. Ordinary Web clients collect no product events; session telemetry defaults to feedback-only. In the 0.2.2 pre-releases (npm latest 0.2.2-rc.1) the default web-search provider is the DeepSeek Search API: whenever a DeepSeek credential is available, each search sends the query and, unless `sendOriginalQuestion` is set to false, the latest prompt cut to 128 characters to DeepSeek, also when the chat model is a custom endpoint. Whether the Web UI's DeepSeek API-key route falls under this Harness policy or separate DeepSeek Open Platform terms was not checked; both send data to DeepSeek. The vendor labels the project an unaudited developer preview.
proposed_changes.why: Correction plus new behaviour: (1) the October note said the Desktop analytics default was not stated, but the first-party package README says it defaults to true with no user-facing control (wording present since 2026-09-25); (2) the 0.2.2 pre-releases make the DeepSeek Search API the default search provider, which sends the query and up to 128 characters of the latest prompt to DeepSeek when a DeepSeek credential is available.

discovery_decisions.name: ThinkRail
discovery_decisions.reason: New open-source agentic IDE from JetBrains (Apache-2.0 confirmed; v0.2.0 on 2026-10-18, v0.3.0 on 2026-10-29, v0.3.2 on 2026-11-06; daily nightlies; commits on the review date), with a researcher-relevant privacy route: a documented 'Custom servers' setting connects any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, LiteLLM), and ThinkRail has no accounts of its own. It is held for four reasons. (a) By its own description it is 'on purpose a thin layer on top of Pi' (rca-pi): models, permissions and context belong to Pi. That puts it near the excluded workspace-layer category, and its privacy route adds nothing beyond Pi's. (b) Basic usage events and error reports go to PostHog tied to an installation ID and are 'always sent'. Only additional sharing can be switched off, so a special-category route would require network-level blocking that the vendor does not document. (c) There is no product documentation ('Docs: Coming soon'); the only privacy statement is a README section, and it has no DPA. (d) It is pre-1.0 with weekly feature churn. Its GUI over a terminal agent is relevant for researchers who avoid the CLI, so the owner should decide whether a GUI IDE over a catalogued agent counts as distinct (compare JetBrains Air and AgentsDock, not added in October).
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: First-party product documentation and a privacy statement beyond the README exist (docs currently 'Coming soon'); a stable 1.0 (or an explicit stability statement) is released; the basic analytics and error reports can be fully disabled, or a documented offline/no-egress mode exists; and the owner rules that a GUI IDE over a catalogued agent (Pi) is in scope rather than an excluded workspace layer. If added, it should probably be an alias or route on rca-pi, unless ThinkRail gains its own agent runtime.

discovery_decisions.name: CodeGPT (VS Code, JetBrains and Visual Studio extension)
discovery_decisions.reason: An established multi-IDE agent extension that the catalog never assessed. It has a documented local route: Ollama and LM Studio providers, pointed at http://localhost:11434. It also has BYOK and paid tiers (Free $0, Professional $10/month, Teams $30/user/month on the home page). No in-window material change was found. It is held for evidence gaps. The privacy notice (Effective Date March 4th, 2025, v1.2) covers website and account data and usage metrics (number of prompts, time spent, tokens), but it says nothing about retention or model training on prompts and code sent through CodeGPT-hosted credits/models. The extension's telemetry is not documented, and neither is whether local-provider mode works without sign-in. No DPA or trust page was found, and no software licence was established (treat as proprietary/unconfirmed). The marketing claim 'Your code never leaves your control unless you explicitly choose to use cloud AI models' is not backed by product-level terms.
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: CodeGPT publishes product-level terms for prompts and code (retention, training default, sub-processors) for CodeGPT-hosted models, documents extension telemetry and an off switch, and states whether the Ollama/LM Studio mode works without account sign-in or other egress; a licence or EULA for the extension is identified.

discovery_decisions.name: OpenAI Dots (always-on ChatGPT agents)
discovery_decisions.reason: The reconsider condition is now answerable. Three OpenAI Help Center articles were readable in the in-app browser (HTTP 200; curl and WebFetch still get 403). Findings: dots are general-purpose, always-on personal agents in ChatGPT. Each has its own cloud computer, connected apps, memory shared with ChatGPT, and optional local-computer access (off by default). Coding is one example use case, and work a dot delegates to ChatGPT Work or Codex threads is billed separately. Availability: Pro (18+, excluding the EEA, Switzerland and the UK) and Business Premium, rolling out. Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare get an admin preview 2026-11-04 to 11-18, then default-on unless the admin opts out. Not available with UAE residency. Data: dot context is retained for as long as the dot exists. Individual memories cannot be viewed or deleted; only deleting the dot does that. Disconnecting an app does not delete what was already absorbed. Human review can occur even with model improvement off. Personal plans train by default unless 'Improve the model for everyone' is turned off; Business/Enterprise/Edu do not train by default. HIPAA-eligible under a BAA. Enterprise model controls do not apply to dots. Agent-security network policies for dot cloud tasks are still in development. Pure OpenAI cloud: special = no in any case. Decision: not a separate catalog record. A dot is a general personal assistant agent, not a coding or data-analysis agent, and its coding path runs through Codex, which the catalog already covers (rca-openai-codex). Recommended follow-up for the rca-openai-codex re-verifier (not done here): add a one-line note that ChatGPT dots can create Codex cloud tasks and share plugin permissions and ChatGPT memory, and that Enterprise dots become default-on on 2026-11-18 unless admins opt out. That would alert institutional admins.
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: Re-open only if OpenAI positions dots as a coding or data-analysis product with terms distinct from ChatGPT/Codex (e.g. a developer-facing dot with its own data controls), or if the rca-openai-codex re-verifier decides the delegation path needs its own row.

discovery_decisions.name: Claude for Excel (Claude for M365 add-ins)
discovery_decisions.reason: Add. On scope: the catalog already lists spreadsheet and office data-analysis agents (rca-microsoft-365-copilot-analyst, rca-chatgpt-advanced-data-analysis), so an Office add-in that analyses workbooks fits the data lane. Only the Excel add-in is proposed; the PowerPoint, Word and Outlook add-ins are not data-analysis tools. The plan-specific terms the October hold asked for are now collected from first-party sources. Consumer Pro/Max: training is opt-out (pricing page), with up to 5 years of de-identified retention if model improvement is on. Commercial Team/Enterprise: no training on Customer Content (Commercial Terms) and 30-day deletion of API data, with Usage Policy exceptions. Third-party platforms: on Bedrock and Vertex AI, Anthropic has no access and does not train; on Azure AI Foundry, Anthropic acts as an independent processor. The add-in's own documentation (Data storage and retention) is unusually detailed about device-local storage, telemetry, Sentry and file expiry. Inference is cloud-only, so special-category data is 'no'. The GA date is still not established (the docs say only that it 'is generally available'), which does not block a record. Note for integration: the pricing page now also lists an Ultra plan that includes Claude for Microsoft 365.

Met: the Connect Models docs now document 'Use API Key' as an alternative to Z.ai or BigModel sign-in, and custom Anthropic- or OpenAI-compatible providers, including 'self-hosted services on a private network'. That is a documented route to institution-controlled inference. Not met: (1) Public development is still not visible. The repo has 8 commits, all source drops ('chore: sync ZCode source'), from 2 named contributors; issues are disabled, there are no pull requests, and the docs send bug reports elsewhere. discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: ZCode documents its client telemetry (what is sent, where, default and an opt-out that also covers API-key-only use without sign-in), and public development becomes visible (issue tracker or PRs, beyond periodic source drops). discovery_decisions.reason: Partly improved; the main conditions are unmet. Still no privacy policy: magnitude.dev/privacy and /privacy-policy both return 404, and the site links none. discovery_decisions.name: Forge Code (ForgeCode)
discovery_decisions.reason: Drop. (1) Vendor pivot: forgecode.dev now sells 'Your software factory', a cloud product in which agents on vendor cloud machines take work from Slack, alerts and issues and open PRs. That is an autonomous cloud dev platform, out of scope here. (2) The open-source CLI is in maintenance-only mode: every commit since 2026-10-01 (100 in the API page) is an automated dependency bump, the last functional commit was 2026-10-01 and the last release v2.14.0 on 2026-10-01. (3) Telemetry in the CLI source is worse than recorded in October. Release builds always track (can_track is false only for 'dev' or '0.1.0' versions). The UI dispatches a 'prompt' event whose value is the full prompt text, plus tool-call payloads and the conversation, to PostHog (us.i.posthog.com). FORGE_TRACKER=false only stops email/identity enrichment. The new privacy policy (2 Nov 2026) confirms 'Agent telemetry may include conversation text' and offers an opt-out 'in the settings of the agent's telemetry extension', but no such switch exists in the CLI source on main. With prompt text sent by default and no documented CLI opt-out, it would be nonsensitive-only, and the vendor's direction is out of scope.
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: Only if Tailcall resumes functional development of the open-source CLI as a standalone local agent and ships a documented, CLI-level switch that stops prompt, tool-call and conversation telemetry.

discovery_decisions.name: Step Code
discovery_decisions.reason: The reconsider condition (an either/or) is now formally met, but adding is not yet warranted. Met: StepFun's Step Code docs now document custom endpoints through ~/.stepcode/models.json, 'including Ollama, vLLM, and LM Studio', plus third-party API-key providers, and StepFun publishes a User Privacy policy (effective 7 Aug 2026), a DPA (effective 28 Nov 2025) and a Step Plan Paid Service Agreement (effective 16 Mar 2026). Still open: (a) Scope/overlap: LICENSE-STATUS.md says Step Code 'is derived from the MIT-licensed Pi project', and Pi (rca-pi) is already catalogued with the same local route; the main difference is the bundled StepFun cloud provider plus StepPage publishing and a Lark remote connection. (b) Step route data terms: the privacy policy lists 'To evaluate and improve our models, products, and services, where permitted by applicable law' as a general purpose. It does not state whether Step Plan prompts are used for training, gives no prompt retention period and no training opt-out; explicit training use is stated only for Startup/early-access programmes. (c) Telemetry: the docs show only how to disable it ([telemetry] enabled = false); the default (the sample config shows true) and the content collected are not documented. (d) Maturity: 0.1.x (v0.1.6 on 23 Oct 2026), no GitHub releases, ~1k stars; the README still says the default entrypoint exposes one built-in provider, which conflicts with the docs. Provisional classification if added: openness open-source (MIT confirmed); data_handling unknown; nonsensitive ok, personal cfg (local or separately approved provider, telemetry off), special cfg only via a local Ollama/vLLM/LM Studio endpoint with telemetry off, Step login removed and egress blocked.
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: Integration rules whether vendor-branded derivatives of an already-catalogued agent (Pi) get their own record; and StepFun documents the telemetry default and payload plus whether Step Plan prompts are used for training (with retention and opt-out). If both resolve favourably, add with the provisional classification in the assessment; if Step Code remains 0.1.x with undocumented telemetry at the next sweep, drop as a Pi derivative.

discovery_decisions.name: Freebuff (formerly Codebuff)
discovery_decisions.reason: Add as a warning record (precedent: rca-deepseek-harness, data_handling 'trains'). The October hold had two conditions. The privacy-policy review is now done, and the policy is explicit. The integration ruling on ad-funded tools is the owner's call. My default is to list it, because it is a widely used free agent (about 14k GitHub stars; npm 0.2.36 on 2026-11-03) that students and researchers are likely to meet, and the catalog's purpose is to warn about exactly this trade-off. Key facts: prompt and project data feed ad personalisation and ad-model training on all routes. Data from models labelled for AI training may be sold, including agent traces. Freebuff Cloud repositories may undergo 'Codebase Evaluation' of their commercial value. Retention has no fixed period. No BYOK or local route is documented for the CLI. Paid plans ($8/$25/$60 per month) are not stated to remove ads or change data use. The repo is Apache-2.0, but npm metadata says MIT and the repo is a synced snapshot of a private repo; recorded in notes. If the owner rules against listing ad-funded tools, treat this as drop.
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: Re-check when the privacy policy changes (the reviewed version takes effect 2026-11-12), if an ad-free or no-training paid tier is documented, or if a BYOK/local model route appears for the CLI.

discovery_decisions.name: Letta Code
discovery_decisions.reason: Drop as out of scope. The scope question has resolved against inclusion. The repository description is now 'Agents that self-improve with experience', and the README presents Letta Code as 'a stateful agent harness for creating agents that are more like people than tools'. Its headline features are long-horizon memory, self-rewriting prompts and harness, always-on agents with crons and heartbeats, chat through Telegram, Slack, Discord and chat.letta.com, and agents roaming across remote computers. That is a general-purpose persistent-agent platform, not a coding or data-analysis agent. Privacy posture also argues against: 'Letta Cloud is the default' for agent memory, identity and conversations, bundled system prompts become Cloud-managed on resume, and remote computers and secrets require a Letta sign-in. A local backend exists but was not reviewed. Maintenance is healthy (v0.34.41 on 2026-11-05, Apache-2.0), so this is a scope drop, not an abandonment drop.
discovery_decisions.reconsider_when: Only if Letta repositions Letta Code (or ships a distinct product) as a coding/data-analysis agent with a documented local-only backend and reviewed Letta Cloud privacy/retention terms.
