issues.problem: Verifiers returned confirm_with_corrections with precise field-level replacements (e.g. Factory 'product is unchanged' unsupported; Kilo '14 model providers' unsupported, entries have blank purpose; IBM Bob 'client 2.3.0' is IDE-only and 'policies IDE only' partly contradicted; Junie 'downloaded from JetBrains' unconfirmed and project config.json can route to cloud; Jules export is a changelog script not a CLI command; Data Formulator 5-row cap does not bound model exposure; Freebuff 'no local endpoint documented' wrong (BYOK in source); Crush PAYG ZDR needs the Shred-credit qualifier; Warp private-networking plan label; Coder project memory on by default). None of these changes a suitability/special_route classification.
issues.proposed_resolution: Merge each verifier's corrected value into the final record (for adds, use verify/add-*.json corrected_record, not the discovery/holds stub). No classification change is implied.

issues.problem: data_handling is scoped by three different conventions for the same situation (product with a vendor-managed cloud route AND a documented local/self-hosted route, special=cfg): (a) best/local route -> 'local' (Crush, Qwen Code, Mistral Vibe, Zed, Kilo, OpenCode, Oh My Pi, Ante, Tabnine, Zencoder, Junie, Datalore, MLJAR, OpenHands, Coder); (b) best commercial cloud route -> 'no-train' (Copilot, GitLab Duo, IBM Bob, Factory, Antigravity, Posit, Codex, Deepnote, Roomote); (c) default vendor route -> 'trains'/'opt-out' (Kimi Code CLI, Grok Build, Poolside). Clearest pairs: Kimi Code CLI 'trains' vs Qwen Code 'local' (both OSS CLIs whose vendor-managed route trains, both with self-hosted endpoints); Tabnine 'local' vs IBM Bob/GitLab 'no-train' (all enterprise self-hosted + vendor SaaS); Datalore 'local' vs Deepnote 'no-train'; Roomote 'no-train' vs OpenHands/Coder 'local'. Verifiers flagged Ante, OpenCode, Oh My Pi, Zencoder, MLJAR, Tabnine and Crush as 'local' while their default path is vendor cloud. The portal legend defines Local as 'supports local/self-hosted inference', which convention (b)/(c) records also satisfy.
issues.proposed_resolution: Owner decision (default proposed): write one rule into MAINTENANCE.md - data_handling describes the route a new user gets by default; use 'local' only when the product has no vendor-operated inference or storage on by default (pure BYO-model/local tools: Aider, Goose, Ollama, Tabby, marimo, Jupyter AI, etc.); the local/self-hosted route is carried by suitability.special, special_route and tier_gate. Under that rule relabel the (a) records whose default is vendor cloud, and keep Kimi/Grok/Poolside as is. If she prefers the legend's 'best route' meaning instead, relabel Kimi Code CLI, Grok Build, Poolside and the (b) group to 'local'. Either way apply it to all rows in one migration; this is a multi-record change, so state it before applying.

issues.problem: DeepSeek Harness is personal=no/special=no although it documents custom self-hosted endpoints that DeepSeek says it does not store or process; Kimi Code CLI (same pattern: PRC vendor, default route trains, self-hosted endpoint) is personal=cfg/special=cfg. The difference rests on Harness's vendor statements (developer preview, unaudited, not production-ready; policy says not intended for sensitive personal data). Other pre-1.0 tools (ADA 0.7, Juggler 0.7.9, OpenSquilla 0.5.8, Codewhale) and Antigravity's special route (Antigravity SDK, PyPI 'Alpha') get cfg. The rule behind the split is not written down.
issues.proposed_resolution: Keep current ratings and codify the criterion in MAINTENANCE.md: special/personal = no when the vendor itself states the software is not production-ready or not intended for sensitive data; version number or package 'Alpha' classifier alone does not trigger it. Add to Antigravity's tier_gate/residual_risks that the only qualifying route is the Antigravity SDK (alpha, separate Apache-2.0 package), not the App/CLI/IDE, so the portal 'special: configurable' badge is not read as covering the IDE.

issues.problem: special_route.inference 'local-only' is used for routes whose required_controls explicitly allow an endpoint on institution-owned hardware elsewhere in the institutional network (e.g. Aider, Cline, Qwen Code, Copilot, GitLab Duo, mini-swe-agent, Codewhale, Datalore, Factory in-network customModels), while comparable routes elsewhere use 'customer-controlled-endpoint' (Coder, Deepnote, IBM Bob, JASP, Kimi, MLJAR, Notebook Intelligence, Poolside, Roomote, Zerve, Data Formulator, Open WebUI). Verifiers raised it for Qwen Code and Factory. Not rendered in the HTML portal; visible in the published JSON. 'local-only' over-states the boundary when networked servers are allowed.
issues.proposed_resolution: Default: define local-only = model server on the same host as the agent (loopback); customer-controlled-endpoint = any institution-operated server or gateway reached over the network. Relabel routes whose controls permit networked endpoints to customer-controlled-endpoint (or narrow the control text to same-host). Data-only change; suitability unchanged.

issues.problem: Among 'trains' tools, Freebuff is nonsensitive=cfg while Kimi Code CLI and DeepSeek Harness are nonsensitive=ok. The difference (Freebuff uses prompts for ad profiling/ad-model training and may sell submissions for some models) is a real distinction but only stated in suitability_notes.
issues.proposed_resolution: Keep; make the rationale explicit in Freebuff's tier_gate ('ad-funded: prompts used for ad profiling'). Freebuff inclusion itself is an owner call (verifier: ad-funded tool policy not established).

issues.problem: Personal-data gating for weakly documented cloud tools varies: Clusy and Runcell personal=no (no DPA / China routing), while KNIME K-AI (data_handling unknown) and Zerve (unknown) are personal=cfg conditional on a DPA, and Julius (now opt-out by email, DPA referenced but text not public) is personal=cfg. Defensible (a DPA is offered by KNIME/Zerve/Julius), but 'unknown' training + personal cfg is the least conservative combination in the catalog.
issues.proposed_resolution: Keep, but require tier_gate for every unknown/opt-out personal=cfg record to name the executed DPA and the confirmed training opt-out as preconditions (KNIME and Julius already do; check Zerve after applying verifier text).

issues.problem: Claude Code is the only 'zdr' record, although its ZDR is per-organisation, Anthropic-approved and excludes Covered Models; Warp (Business/Enterprise ZDR), Amp (Enterprise ZDR for eligible models), Factory (Business/Enterprise ZDR) and Hex (provider ZDR by default) carry 'no-train'. The 'Zero-retention' pill is therefore applied to the narrowest gated route for one tool only.
issues.proposed_resolution: Default: relabel Claude Code to 'no-train' (commercial default) and keep the ZDR scope in tier_gate, matching peers; alternatively, if 'zdr' is to mean 'a documented ZDR route exists', apply it to Warp, Amp and Factory too. One rule for all.

issues.problem: Jules is status 'discontinued' (read-only after 11 Nov 2026, shutdown 31 Dec 2026) but keeps nonsensitive=ok, so it still appears in the 'non-sensitive' suitable view. MAINTENANCE says discontinued products are not current and should be removed.
issues.proposed_resolution: Default: keep the row for this release only, marked discontinued, so researchers see the export deadline; set nonsensitive to 'no' (no new work possible after 11 Nov) or make sure the portal excludes discontinued rows from suitability filters; remove at the first refresh after 31 Dec 2026. Export guidance should note the script can run without a third-party AI agent.

issues.problem: Overlapping records: the Kiro record now describes 'Kiro IDE and CLI (standalone kiro-cli since CLI 3.0)', and Kiro CLI 3.0 uses the same V3 harness; both carry identical judgments (no-train, ok/cfg/no). Same vendor product split twice.
issues.proposed_resolution: Owner call (structural). Default: keep both IDs this release (no safety conflict) but scope rca-kiro to IDE/Web/Mobile/Crew and point to rca-kiro-cli for the CLI; consider status 'merged' with aliases next cycle.

issues.problem: rca-windsurf is now 'Devin Desktop' (Cognition) and rca-devin covers Devin cloud plus 'devin --cloud' in the Devin CLI; the beta air-gapped build is described in both records ('Devin Desktop and CLI'). Judgments agree (opt-out, ok/cfg/no).

issues.proposed_resolution: Add 'DeepSeek TUI' as an alias on rca-codewhale and say 'not affiliated with DeepSeek' in its notes.

issues.problem: 'open-core' vs 'open-source' is applied inconsistently to fully OSI-licensed clients whose vendor also sells a hosted service: Codewhale (MIT), Mistral Vibe (whole client Apache-2.0), Kilo and Cline are open-core; OpenCode (vendor sells Zen/Go), Qwen Code, Kimi Code CLI, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, gptme (gptme.ai) and Freebuff are open-source.
issues.proposed_resolution: Default rule: open-core only when part of the shipped product is under a non-OSI or closed licence (e.g. Coder's enterprise/ directory, Crush under FSL); a separately sold hosted service does not make an OSI client open-core. Re-check the four open-core OSS clients against that rule (low severity; no privacy effect).

issues.problem: software_license values are not SPDX expressions: Coder carries a prose sentence; Open WebUI 'Open WebUI License' (BSD-3 text plus branding clause, GitHub NOASSERTION); JASP and Warp 'AGPL-3.0', Notebook Intelligence 'GPL-3.0' are deprecated SPDX ids. Schema accepts them; validator only requires non-empty.
issues.proposed_resolution: Coder: 'AGPL-3.0-only' or '-or-later' per LICENSE plus a LicenseRef for enterprise/ (move the prose to notes); Open WebUI: LicenseRef-style id with explanation in notes; replace deprecated ids with the -only/-or-later variant after reading each LICENSE header (do not guess).

issues.problem: tier_gate is empty for six BYO-model tools rated personal=cfg/special=cfg, while comparable tools (gptme, OpenCode, Crush, Qwen Code, Nanocoder) carry a short gate text that the portal shows under the rating.
issues.proposed_resolution: Add a one-line gate (e.g. 'fully local model, telemetry off, egress blocked for special-category data; DPA-covered provider for personal data') for consistency.

issues.problem: type 'cloud' (portal label 'Cloud / autonomous') is used for products now offered only self-hosted (Coder: no SaaS; OpenHands pricing lists only self-hosted plans; Roomote Cloud no longer listed). Readers may take 'Cloud' as vendor cloud.

issues.problem: Scope calls flagged by verifiers: Zerve Superagents (long-running multi-agent missions; site and docs now target finance) overlap the autonomous-agent exclusion; Open WebUI is borderline (general chat UI, Jan was excluded in October) though Open Terminal adds execution; Freebuff is ad-funded.
issues.proposed_resolution: Owner decision; defaults: keep Zerve (Workspace remains in scope, note Superagents as out-of-scope surface), add Open WebUI (distinct self-hosted multi-user route), add Freebuff only if ad-funded tools are acceptable in a privacy-first catalog (otherwise hold).

integration.consistency_summary: Checked 71 reverify updated_records, 50 verify verdicts (39 re-verifications, 11 additions), 6 discovery lanes and 5 hold batches; JSON Schema 2020-12 (jsonschema, format checker) plus the catalog's special_route/openness rules from validate_catalog.py were run on 90 records. All 71 updated_records and all 8 add corrected_records (SageMaker Data Agent, Claude for Excel, Codewhale, Data Formulator, Freebuff, KNIME K-AI, MATLAB Copilot, Open WebUI) are schema-valid and pass the special_route rules; only the 3 rejected carryover stubs fail. Core privacy rule holds everywhere: every runs_locally=false/pure-cloud record has special=no with not-appropriate/none/none; every special=cfg route is config-required/customer-controlled with local or institution-run inference; vendor VPC/dedicated tenancy (Factory Private, Zerve BYOC, Deepnote/Datalore managed dedicated, Devin dedicated, Amp orbs) and managed model APIs in a customer cloud account (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) are never treated as customer-controlled; no 'ready' status. Main inconsistencies are labelling conventions, not ratings: data_handling scoped three ways (best route vs commercial route vs default route), 'zdr' used for Claude Code only, 'local-only' inference used for networked institutional endpoints, undocumented preview rule (DeepSeek Harness vs Kimi/Antigravity), open-core usage. Classification changes: Julius no-train->opt-out and Kimi opt-out->trains stand (verified); Zerve no-train refuted -> keep unknown. Three carryover adds rejected (Rovo Dev invented self-hosted route, Continue sunset, Kimi CLI duplicate). No web fetches were made.
